# Overview – Stage 3 of 6

Stage 3 is the only stage that both loads point clouds **and** does heavy
computation on them. It:

1. reloads `las_1`/`las_2` exactly as Stage 1 read them – no filtering, so the
   points are the same ones every Stage 1 and Stage 2 measurement was made on,
2. applies the Stage 2 rotation `R_xyz` to `las_1` **about `pivot1`** – the
   first time any transform touches a cloud in this workflow,
3. rotates the kept Stage-1 stem axis vectors through the same transform,
   storing the result in a **new** object `vecs_axis_1_rot`,
4. refits RANSAC ellipses on planes perpendicular to each pair's average stem
   axis, cleans them, and filters pairs on stem coverage,
5. matches per-pair ellipse-property curves across epochs to estimate the
   vertical offset, and **records** it as `t_trans_z`.

What this stage does not do

Stage 3 **does not apply the Z-shift**. `t_trans_z` is solved, inspected and
written to the checkpoint; Stage 4 is where it is actually applied to the
ellipse centres and to `pivot1`.

Memory

The point clouds are released from memory (`rm()` + `gc()`) as soon as the
axis-perpendicular ellipse fit is finished and checkpointed. Everything from
Step 3.2 onward operates on fitted ellipse geometry alone, so the second half
of this stage runs in a small fraction of the memory the first half needs.

Checkpoints

Stage 3 writes **two**:

- `save-load_Stage3_1` – straight after the ellipse fit, so the expensive
  RANSAC pass never has to be repeated while tuning the curve-matching
  parameters downstream.
- `save-load_Stage3_2` – the full stage output consumed by Stage 4.

# Stage 0 - Setup


## 0.1 Load libraries
```{r}
#| label: setup
#| code-summary: "Load libraries and set plot theme"

library(lidR)       # LAS I/O and point cloud processing
library(ggplot2)    # Plotting
library(dplyr)      # Data wrangling
library(plotly)     # Interactive 3D axis/ellipse figures
library(base64enc)  # Embed rendered plots into HTML galleries
library(htmltools)  # Assemble the HTML gallery output

# ── Driver-supplied parameter overrides ──────────────────────────────────────
# Every params-* chunk in this file ends with .par_apply("<its label>"). Run the
# file by hand and that call does nothing: the values the chunk just assigned
# stand. Run it under the batch driver, which puts a .batch_params list in the
# environment before the first chunk, and any entry keyed to that chunk label is
# assigned here - AFTER the defaults, so the driver's value is the one that
# survives into the functional chunk that follows.
#
# Why this exists. Parameters used to sit in the same chunk as the code that
# consumed them, so the driver's overrides - which land after a chunk finishes -
# arrived too late to matter, and every pair silently used the .qmd's hardcoded
# value. Splitting each chunk in two fixes the ordering; this helper is what the
# driver reaches through.
#
# The defaults stay in this file rather than moving into the driver. They are
# the single definition, the driver names only what a batch changes, and there
# is no second copy of ~670 parameters to drift out of step with this one.
#
# envir = parent.frame() so a call at chunk top level lands in the environment
# the chunk is being evaluated in - globalenv by hand, the pair environment
# under the driver - without needing .stage_env(), which is defined further down.
.par_apply <- function(label, envir = parent.frame()) {
  bp <- mget(".batch_params", envir = envir, ifnotfound = list(NULL),
             inherits = TRUE)[[1]]
  if (is.null(bp) || is.null(bp[[label]])) return(invisible(character(0)))
  vals <- bp[[label]]
  if (!length(vals)) return(invisible(character(0)))
  if (is.null(names(vals)) || any(!nzchar(names(vals))))
    stop(sprintf("[.par_apply] .batch_params[['%s']] must be a fully NAMED list.", label))
  # A name the chunk did not define is almost always a typo or a rename in the
  # .qmd that the driver has not caught up with. Silence there would mean the
  # batch runs on the default while looking like it was overridden, so it stops.
  unknown <- names(vals)[!vapply(names(vals), exists, logical(1),
                                 envir = envir, inherits = FALSE)]
  if (length(unknown))
    stop(sprintf(paste0("[.par_apply] %s: %d override(s) name nothing this chunk assigns:\n  %s\n",
                        "  Fix the name in the driver's .build_params(), or remove it."),
                 label, length(unknown), paste(unknown, collapse = "\n  ")))
  for (nm in names(vals)) assign(nm, vals[[nm]], envir = envir)
  cat(sprintf("  [params] %s <- driver (%s)\n", label, paste(names(vals), collapse = ", ")))
  invisible(names(vals))
}
```

## 0.2 Global Helpers
```{r}
#| label: params-helpers
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Colours, ggplot theme, thinning, stage save/load utilities, and the on-demand point-cloud loader"

# ============================================================
# Colours
# ============================================================
COL_1     <- "#2196F3"
COL_2     <- "#FF5722"
COL_MATCH <- "#D9F9A5"

# ============================================================
# Progress bars
#
# Thin wrappers around cli, using EXACTLY the idiom Stage 3's axis-RANSAC fit
# has always used, because that one works when these documents are run on their
# own. Their only job is to save repeating the same six lines at every long
# loop.
#
# THE ONE THING THAT MUST NOT BE CHANGED HERE is `.envir = parent.frame()`.
# cli ties a progress bar's lifetime to a frame and tears the bar down when
# that frame exits. .pb_new() is a function, so a bar created with cli's
# default `.envir` would be created and immediately destroyed the moment
# .pb_new returned - the loop then ticks a bar that no longer exists and
# nothing is ever drawn. parent.frame() hands the bar to the CALLER's frame,
# which is the loop, and is the difference between this working and silently
# doing nothing. (An earlier revision passed globalenv() here, which is why the
# bars added through this helper never appeared while the hand-written ones in
# 3.3, 3.6 and 3.9 did.)
#
# Under the batch driver these will NOT be visible: cli draws on stderr, and
# the driver holds a message sink, which cannot be split. That is expected and
# is not worked around here - the driver prints its own progress instead.
# ============================================================
# Progress bars
# ============================================================
# One set of helpers, two renderers, chosen at the moment a bar is created.
#
#   cli    a redrawing bar, when there is a terminal able to show one
#   lines  one ordinary printed line per update, when there is not
#
# The choice is not cosmetic. cli draws on STDERR, and the batch driver holds a
# sink(type = "message"), which cannot split - so under the driver a cli bar
# goes to the log file and nowhere else, arriving as carriage returns and
# escape codes wrapped around each other. That is what the last run's log shows
# for every fitting step except the library's own: minutes of work with nothing
# on screen, and an unreadable smear in the log afterwards.
#
# The printed-line renderer is what the RANSAC library's cat handler already
# does, and it is the one visible line in that log. Same format here, so a fit
# reports identically whether the progress comes from the library or from a
# loop in this file.
show_progress_bars <- TRUE

# Print at most one line per 5% of the total or per 15 seconds, whichever comes
# first, plus always the first and last. A 20-stem fit gives ~20 lines; a
# 5000-slice loop does not give 5000.
progress_step_frac    <- 0.05
progress_min_seconds  <- 15

.par_apply("params-helpers")
```

```{r}
#| label: helpers
#| code-summary: "Colours, ggplot theme, thinning, stage save/load utilities, and the on-demand point-cloud loader"

# ============================================================
# ggplot theme
# ============================================================
theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position  = "bottom"
    )
)
# ============================================================
# Thinning for visualisation
# ============================================================
thin <- function(mat, every = 20) mat[seq(1, nrow(mat), by = every), ]
.filter_min_ellipses <- function(raw, label, min_count = 5L) {
  counts  <- sapply(raw, function(df)
    if (is.null(df)) 0L else
      sum(!is.na(df$center_x) & !is.na(df$semi_a) & !is.na(df$semi_b)))
  keep    <- counts >= min_count
  removed <- names(raw)[!keep]
  if (length(removed) > 0)
    cat(sprintf(
      "[%s] Pre-clean filter: removed %d tree(s) with fewer than %d fitted ellipses: %s\n",
      label, length(removed), min_count, paste(removed, collapse = ", ")
    ))
  else
    cat(sprintf(
      "[%s] Pre-clean filter: all %d trees have >= %d fitted ellipses.\n",
      label, length(raw), min_count
    ))
  raw[keep]
}
.write_las_snapshot <- function(las_template, xyz_mat, output_path, stage_label) {
  las_snap        <- las_template
  las_snap@data$X <- xyz_mat[, 1]
  las_snap@data$Y <- xyz_mat[, 2]
  las_snap@data$Z <- xyz_mat[, 3]

  # Make output_path unique if the file already exists (appends _001, _002, ...)
  if (file.exists(output_path)) {
    base_noext <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(output_path)
    ext        <- tools::file_ext(output_path)
    counter    <- 1L
    repeat {
      candidate <- sprintf("%s_%03d.%s", base_noext, counter, ext)
      if (!file.exists(candidate)) { output_path <- candidate; break }
      counter <- counter + 1L
    }
    cat(sprintf("Output file already exists - using unique name: %s\n", output_path))
  }

  writeLAS(las_snap, output_path)
  cat(sprintf("[%s] Saved %s points -> %s\n",
              stage_label, format(nrow(xyz_mat), big.mark = ","), output_path))
  invisible(output_path)
}

.apply_4x4_transform <- function(xyz, M) {
  xyz   <- as.matrix(xyz)
  homog <- cbind(xyz, 1)
  out   <- t(M %*% t(homog))
  out[, 1:3, drop = FALSE]
}

# ============================================================
# Stage save/load utilities – shared by every stage file.
#
# Contract (identical in all six stage files):
# SAVE → hard ERROR if any *required* object is missing from the
# environment, so a checkpoint can never be written half-empty.
# A *warning* is raised for any missing *optional* object
# (diagnostic products that may legitimately not have been run);
# those are simply omitted from the file.
# LOAD → never errors on content. A *warning* is raised for each
# requested object that is absent from the RDS. Objects present in
# the RDS but not requested are COUNTED in the summary line and
# never listed. Everything found in the file is loaded either way,
# so nothing is silently discarded.
# PATHS → a save never overwrites: if the target path exists, a numeric
# suffix (_001, _002, ...) is appended until the name is free.
# ============================================================

#' Return `path` if free, otherwise path_001 / path_002 / ... (first free one).
.unique_path <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(path)
  base_noext <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(path)
  ext        <- tools::file_ext(path)
  counter    <- 1L
  repeat {
    candidate <- sprintf("%s_%03d.%s", base_noext, counter, ext)
    if (!file.exists(candidate)) {
      cat(sprintf("Target already exists - using unique name: %s\n", candidate))
      return(candidate)
    }
    counter <- counter + 1L
  }
}

#' Which environment do the stage helpers read and write?
#'
#' A .qmd rendered or run by hand evaluates its chunks in the global
#' environment. The batch driver does not: it gives every LAS pair a fresh
#' environment of its own, so that a leftover object from the previous pair
#' cannot be picked up by one of the exists() guards this pipeline is full of.
#' Under the driver, everything the stages assign therefore lives THERE, and
#' not in globalenv.
#'
#' parent.env(environment()) is the environment this chunk was evaluated in:
#' globalenv() by hand, the pair environment under the driver. It is resolved
#' from where .stage_env was DEFINED rather than from where it is called, so it
#' returns the same environment inside a function as it does at chunk top
#' level, and nothing has to be told which mode it is in.
#'
#' This replaced a hardcoded .stage_env() throughout. Under the driver that
#' pointed at an environment the pipeline had never written to, so every object
#' in a save manifest read as missing and the checkpoint refused to write - the
#' Stage 1 failure that reported 30 missing required objects after a 64-minute
#' fit. (`run_counts` was the one it did find, and only because .tally()'s `<<-`
#' walked past the pair environment into globalenv. That is fixed below too.)
.stage_env <- function() parent.env(environment())

#' Is a batch driver running this file?
#'
#' The driver assigns .batch_mode <- TRUE into the pair environment before the
#' first chunk runs. It changes one thing, and only for the checkpoints: in a
#' batch, every stage runs in ONE session, so Stage N+1 already holds in memory
#' everything Stage N computed and never has to read it back off disk. The
#' checkpoints stop being load-bearing and become a record of the run.
#'
#' So under a batch: nothing in a manifest is required (a missing object is
#' reported and left out, and the pair carries on), a failed write is reported
#' rather than thrown, and .stage_load is a no-op. Run the same .qmd by hand and
#' every one of those is an error again, which is what it should be when the
#' checkpoint is the only thing carrying the stage forward.
.in_batch <- function() {
  isTRUE(mget(".batch_mode", envir = .stage_env(),
              ifnotfound = list(FALSE), inherits = FALSE)[[1]])
}

#' Read one of the driver's batch settings out of the pair environment.
#' Absent - i.e. this file is being run by hand - gives `default`.
.batch_opt <- function(name, default = NULL) {
  v <- mget(name, envir = .stage_env(), ifnotfound = list(NULL), inherits = FALSE)[[1]]
  if (is.null(v)) default else v
}

#' Where a checkpoint goes when a batch is running.
#'
#' Every save chunk in this pipeline assigns its .rds path and then USES it a
#' few lines later, in the same chunk. The driver applies its overrides AFTER a
#' chunk has run, so an override of stage1_rds_path arrives after the file has
#' already been written to the path hardcoded here - which means, without this,
#' every sample in a batch writes over the same hardcoded name.
#'
#' So in batch mode the destination is derived instead, from two values the
#' driver puts in the environment before anything runs: .batch_rds_dir and
#' .batch_sample. The label the save chunk already passes supplies the rest, so
#' "Stage 3.2" becomes <dir>/<sample>_Stage3_2.rds with nothing to keep in sync.
#'
#' NULL means: not in a batch, or the driver did not set the directory - use the
#' path the chunk asked for.
.batch_rds_path <- function(label) {
  dir <- .batch_opt(".batch_rds_dir")
  smp <- .batch_opt(".batch_sample")
  if (is.null(dir) || is.null(smp)) return(NULL)
  file.path(dir, sprintf("%s_%s.rds", smp,
                         gsub("\\.", "_", gsub("\\s+", "", label))))
}

#' Save a stage checkpoint. Errors on missing required objects - unless the
#' batch driver is running this file, in which case nothing is required, the
#' destination is the per-sample one derived above, and a failure to write is
#' reported rather than thrown. See .in_batch() above.
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a

.stage_save <- function(path, required, optional = character(0),
                        label = "stage", envir = .stage_env(),
                        strict = !.in_batch()) {

  required <- unique(required)
  optional <- setdiff(unique(optional), required)

  # A batch may switch an individual checkpoint off by label - the driver's
  # keep_stage3_fit_checkpoint does exactly this for "Stage 3.1", whose chunk
  # must still RUN (the final Stage 3 manifest inherits from it) but need not
  # write a second large file per sample.
  if (!strict && label %in% .batch_opt(".batch_skip_saves", character(0))) {
    cat(sprintf("[%s save] Skipped - switched off for this batch.\n", label))
    return(invisible(NA_character_))
  }

  # inherits = FALSE, matching the mget() below, which has always been strict.
  # With inheritance on, an object could be FOUND in a parent environment and
  # then fail to be FETCHED, and under the driver the parent is globalenv -
  # i.e. the previous pair's leftovers.
  .have <- function(x)
    if (!length(x)) logical(0)
    else vapply(x, exists, logical(1), envir = envir, inherits = FALSE)

  missing_req <- required[!.have(required)]
  if (length(missing_req) > 0L) {
    if (strict)
      stop(sprintf(
        "[%s save] Cannot save - %d required object(s) missing from the environment:\n  %s",
        label, length(missing_req), paste(missing_req, collapse = "\n  ")))
    cat(sprintf(
      "[%s save] %d required object(s) missing - treated as optional and omitted (batch mode):\n  %s\n",
      label, length(missing_req), paste(missing_req, collapse = "\n  ")))
  }

  missing_opt <- optional[!.have(optional)]
  if (length(missing_opt) > 0L) {
    msg <- sprintf(
      "[%s save] %d optional object(s) missing - omitted from the checkpoint:\n  %s",
      label, length(missing_opt), paste(missing_opt, collapse = "\n  "))
    if (strict) warning(msg) else cat(msg, "\n", sep = "")
  }

  present  <- c(setdiff(required, missing_req), setdiff(optional, missing_opt))
  n_opt_in <- length(setdiff(optional, missing_opt))
  dat      <- mget(present, envir = envir, inherits = FALSE)

  # ── The checkpoint describes itself ────────────────────────────────────────
  # The manifest travels INSIDE the file. Without it, loading a checkpoint means
  # first reconstructing the exact `required`/`optional` vectors it was written
  # with - and those are built by chunks, so a later checkpoint could only be
  # loaded after running the chunks that define an earlier one's manifest. That
  # made resuming from an arbitrary point in a fresh session impossible: the
  # Stage 3.2 chunk, for instance, stops outright unless .stage3_1_required is
  # already in scope.
  #
  # Stored under a name no manifest can collide with, and stripped again on
  # load, so it never reaches the session as an object.
  dat[[".__manifest__"]] <- list(
    required = setdiff(required, missing_req),
    optional = setdiff(optional, missing_opt),
    label    = label,
    saved_utc = format(Sys.time(), tz = "UTC", usetz = TRUE))

  .write <- function() {
    p <- path
    if (!strict) {
      bp <- .batch_rds_path(label)
      if (!is.null(bp)) p <- bp
    }
    dir.create(dirname(p), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    # .unique_path only interactively. A batch path already carries the sample
    # name, so it cannot collide with another sample, and a re-run of the same
    # sample should REPLACE its checkpoint rather than leave _001, _002 behind
    # for the next reader to guess between.
    if (strict) p <- .unique_path(p)
    saveRDS(dat, p)
    cat(sprintf("[%s save] Saved %d object(s) (%d required, %d optional) -> %s\n",
                label, length(dat), length(present) - n_opt_in, n_opt_in, p))
    p
  }

  if (strict) return(invisible(.write()))

  out <- tryCatch(.write(), error = function(e) {
    cat(sprintf("[%s save] Checkpoint NOT written: %s\n", label, conditionMessage(e)))
    cat(sprintf("[%s save] Batch mode - the objects are still in this session, so the run continues.\n",
                label))
    NA_character_
  })
  invisible(out)
}

#' Load a stage checkpoint. Warns (never errors) on content mismatches, and
#' under the batch driver does not read at all - see .in_batch() above.
.stage_load <- function(path, required, optional = character(0),
                        label = "stage", envir = .stage_env(),
                        strict = !.in_batch()) {

  # In a batch the objects this would read are already live in `envir`, put
  # there by the stage that just ran. Reading them back would at best be a
  # no-op. At worst it would be wrong: checkpoint paths are per-sample and
  # .unique_path() means a re-run writes _001 rather than replacing the
  # original, so the path named here can easily be an EARLIER run's file. And
  # if the write failed or was partial, there would be nothing to read and the
  # pair would die at the start of the next stage having done all the work.
  if (!strict) {
    cat(sprintf("[%s load] Skipped - batch mode: this stage's objects are already in the session.\n",
                label))
    return(invisible(character(0)))
  }

  if (!file.exists(path))
    stop(sprintf("[%s load] File not found:\n  %s", label, path))

  dat <- readRDS(path)

  # ── Prefer the manifest the file carries ───────────────────────────────────
  # A checkpoint written by .stage_save records what it holds, so a load needs
  # nothing from the session - no earlier chunk, no earlier checkpoint, no
  # reconstructed name vectors. `required` and `optional` become a CHECK against
  # what the caller expected rather than the definition of what to read, which
  # is what lets any stage be resumed from any checkpoint in a fresh session.
  #
  # Files written before manifests existed simply have none; those fall back to
  # the caller's vectors, exactly as before.
  mf <- dat[[".__manifest__"]]
  dat[[".__manifest__"]] <- NULL
  caller_req <- unique(required)
  caller_opt <- setdiff(unique(optional), caller_req)

  if (!is.null(mf)) {
    required <- unique(mf$required)
    optional <- setdiff(unique(mf$optional), required)
    src <- sprintf("its own manifest (written %s)", mf$saved_utc %||% "?")
  } else {
    required <- caller_req; optional <- caller_opt
    src <- "the caller's manifest - this file predates self-describing checkpoints"
  }
  expected <- c(required, optional)

  cat(sprintf("[%s load] Reading %d object(s) from: %s\n",
              label, length(dat), path))
  cat(sprintf("[%s load] Manifest: %s\n", label, src))

  # Named by the caller but absent from the file: the real incompatibility, and
  # the only one worth a warning when the file describes itself.
  if (!is.null(mf)) {
    unmet <- setdiff(caller_req, names(dat))
    if (length(unmet))
      warning(sprintf(
        "[%s load] %d object(s) this stage expects are not in the checkpoint:\n  %s",
        label, length(unmet), paste(unmet, collapse = "\n  ")))
  }

  missing_req <- required[!required %in% names(dat)]
  if (length(missing_req) > 0L)
    warning(sprintf(
      "[%s load] %d REQUIRED object(s) absent from the RDS - downstream chunks that use them will fail:\n  %s",
      label, length(missing_req), paste(missing_req, collapse = "\n  ")))

  missing_opt <- optional[!optional %in% names(dat)]
  if (length(missing_opt) > 0L)
    warning(sprintf(
      "[%s load] %d optional object(s) absent from the RDS:\n  %s",
      label, length(missing_opt), paste(missing_opt, collapse = "\n  ")))

  # Unrequested objects are COUNTED, never listed. Every checkpoint from Stage 2
  # onward is cumulative, so this set is routinely hundreds of names long and
  # printing it buried the two messages that actually matter - an absent
  # required object, and an absent optional one - under a wall of text. The
  # count still appears in the summary line below, which is the only part of it
  # anyone reads.
  extra <- setdiff(names(dat), expected)

  # ── Publish what was loaded, for the next stage's save manifest ────────────
  # Every stage's SAVE manifest is built as "the previous stage's manifest, plus
  # my own objects", and the previous manifest is a vector defined by that
  # stage's LOAD chunk. Load a LATER checkpoint directly and that chunk never
  # runs, so the save dies on a missing .stageN_required - which is exactly the
  # resume-from-anywhere case these checkpoints now exist to support.
  #
  # Recording the manifest here breaks the dependency: .manifest_from() below
  # falls back to whatever was actually loaded, whichever chunk did it.
  assign(".stage_last_manifest",
         list(required = required, optional = optional,
              names = names(dat), label = label, path = path),
         envir = envir)

  list2env(dat, envir = envir)

  cat(sprintf("[%s load] Loaded %d object(s) | required present: %d/%d | optional present: %d/%d | unrequested: %d\n",
              label, length(dat),
              length(required) - length(missing_req), length(required),
              length(optional) - length(missing_opt), length(optional),
              length(extra)))
  invisible(names(dat))
}

#' The manifest a save chunk inherits from the stage before it.
#'
#' Looks for the named vector first - that is the normal path, when this
#' session's own load chunk built it. Falls back to the manifest carried by
#' whichever checkpoint was last loaded, which is what makes it possible to load
#' any checkpoint and still save the next one.
#'
#' `which` is "required" or "optional". Stops with something actionable rather
#' than returning character(0): a save that silently inherits nothing writes a
#' checkpoint missing every object from every earlier stage, and nothing would
#' notice until a later stage failed to find them.
.manifest_from <- function(name, which = c("required", "optional"),
                           envir = .stage_env()) {
  which <- match.arg(which)
  if (exists(name, envir = envir, inherits = FALSE))
    return(get(name, envir = envir, inherits = FALSE))

  lm <- if (exists(".stage_last_manifest", envir = envir, inherits = FALSE))
          get(".stage_last_manifest", envir = envir, inherits = FALSE) else NULL

  if (!is.null(lm)) {
    cat(sprintf("[manifest] %s not in the session - inheriting from the %s checkpoint that was loaded.\n",
                name, lm$label))
    # For "required", everything the loaded file actually held is the honest
    # inheritance: it is what this session has, regardless of how the file that
    # produced it split required from optional.
    return(if (identical(which, "required")) lm$names else character(0))
  }

  # ── Last resort: the session itself ────────────────────────────────────────
  # No named vector and no checkpoint loaded. That is the ordinary case for a
  # session built by RUNNING chunks rather than by loading - Stage 1 through
  # Stage 3 straight down the document, or an interactive session where the
  # objects were produced rather than read. There is nothing wrong with it, and
  # a save must not refuse.
  #
  # So fall back to what Stages 4 and 5 have always done: take the manifest from
  # the environment. Every non-function, non-dotted object in scope is what this
  # stage inherited, by definition - it is the same rule, just applied later.
  #
  # Only "required" gets this. Optional means "save it if it happens to exist",
  # which is meaningless once the list IS everything that exists.
  if (identical(which, "required")) {
    nm <- setdiff(ls(envir = envir), lsf.str(envir = envir))
    nm <- nm[!startsWith(nm, ".")]
    if (length(nm)) {
      cat(sprintf(paste0("[manifest] %s not found and no checkpoint was loaded - taking the manifest\n",
                         "           from the session instead (%d object(s)). This is the normal path\n",
                         "           when the stage was RUN rather than loaded.\n"), name, length(nm)))
      return(nm)
    }
  } else {
    return(character(0))
  }

  stop(sprintf(paste0("[manifest] %s not found, no checkpoint has been loaded, and the session is\n",
                      "  empty - there is nothing to save. Run this stage's chunks, or load a\n",
                      "  checkpoint, before the save chunk."), name))
}

#' Print the Stage 1 pivot point.
.report_pivot1 <- function() {
  if (exists("pivot1")) {
    cat(sprintf("pivot1 (Stage 1 footprint centre): (%.4f, %.4f, %.4f)\n",
                pivot1[1], pivot1[2], pivot1[3]))
  } else {
    cat("pivot1 NOT available.\n")
  }
}

# ============================================================
# Stages 2, 4 and 5 deliberately never load point clouds - they work purely on
# fitted ellipse geometry, which is what keeps them cheap to re-run. A handful
# of 3-D figures in those stages genuinely need raw points, so each of those
# chunks carries its own loader at the top, controlled by one toggle.
#
# Stage 3 carries it too, for a different reason: it DOES load the clouds at the
# top, but releases them again part-way through, and resuming from the Stage 3
# post-fit checkpoint skips the load entirely.
#
# Stages 1 and 6 do NOT have this block at all - they load the clouds up front
# and keep them for the whole stage, so nothing there would ever call it.
#
#   vis_load_clouds <- TRUE    read las_1 / las_2 from disk
#   vis_load_clouds <- FALSE   reuse whatever is already resident in memory
#
# Set it FALSE when the clouds are already loaded - you just ran Stage 3 in the
# same session, or an earlier figure in this stage already loaded them. Reading
# a multi-gigabyte LAS once per figure is slow and pointless. Leave it TRUE when
# running the stage standalone from its checkpoint, which is the normal case.
#
# ── FRAMES: why las_1 needs a rotation the moment it comes off disk ────────────
# las_1 sits on disk in the ORIGINAL scan frame. Stage 1A's rough vertical
# alignment (R_align_1 about align_pivot_1) was applied to las_1 IN MEMORY in
# Stage 1 and never written back - there is no writeLAS anywhere in Stage 1. So
# every measurement made downstream of Stage 1A - ellipse centres, per-stem axis
# vectors, pivot1, and the Stage 2 rotation solve R_xyz - live in the ALIGNED
# frame, not the disk frame. A figure that reads las_1 off disk and overlays any
# of that geometry is mixing two frames unless it first reapplies R_align_1.
#
# This loader therefore reconstructs the pipeline frame for las_1 as a stack of
# rigid steps, matching the Stage 2 composition (R_align_xyz_1) exactly:
#
#   x_aligned = R_align_1 (x_raw     - align_pivot_1) + align_pivot_1   (apply_align, Stage 1A)
#   x_final   = R_xyz     (x_aligned - pivot1)        + pivot1          (apply_rot,   Stage 2)
#   x_final  += t_trans_z                                              (apply_zshift, Stage 4)
#   x_final   = R_z-only  about pivot2 in XY                            (apply_zrot,   Stage 5)
#
# apply_align is the default-ON baseline: everything above stacks on the
# aligned frame, so leaving it on is what makes las_1 line up with the ellipses
# and vectors. Turn it OFF only to inspect the raw disk cloud deliberately.
# las_2 is the REFERENCE cloud - Stage 1 never rotates it and its ellipses are in
# the disk frame - so it is never transformed here.
#
# Transforms are applied to the RETURNED point frame, never baked back into the
# LAS object, so repeated calls (or a load = FALSE reuse) can never compound.
# ============================================================

#' Make point clouds available to one visualisation chunk.
#'
#' @param load         TRUE to read from disk; FALSE to reuse las_1 / las_2
#'                     already in the global environment.
#' @param las_1_path,las_2_path
#'                     Optional explicit source paths. When NULL (default) the
#'                     paths are taken from the global environment, so a caller
#'                     can either pass them or rely on the checkpoint. Only used
#'                     when load = TRUE.
#' @param apply_align  reapply the Stage 1A rough vertical alignment to las_1
#'                     (R_align_1 about align_pivot_1). Default TRUE: this is the
#'                     baseline frame every Stage 1/2 measurement lives in, so
#'                     without it the returned las_1 points do NOT match the
#'                     ellipses or axis vectors. Set FALSE only to see the raw
#'                     on-disk cloud. No-op (identity) when rough alignment was
#'                     not run; skipped with a note if the checkpoint lacks the
#'                     objects.
#' @param apply_rot    rebuild the Stage 2 XYZ rotation R_xyz (about pivot1),
#'                     stacked on the aligned frame.
#' @param apply_zshift rebuild the Stage 4 Z-translation.
#' @param apply_zrot   rebuild the Stage 5 Z-only rotation (about pivot2 in XY).
#' @param need_las2    FALSE to skip the reference cloud entirely.
#'
#' @return list(las_1, las_2, pts_1, pts_2, xyz_1, state). pts_* are plain data
#'   frames of X/Y/Z/TreeID with TreeID 0 and NA dropped (figures show stems).
#'   xyz_1 / pts_1 are in the transformed frame; the LAS objects stay on-disk.
.vis_point_clouds <- function(load,
                              las_1_path   = NULL,
                              las_2_path   = NULL,
                              apply_align  = TRUE,
                              apply_rot    = FALSE,
                              apply_zshift = FALSE,
                              apply_zrot   = FALSE,
                              need_las2    = TRUE,
                              quiet        = FALSE,
                              envir        = .stage_env()) {

  .say <- function(...) if (!quiet) cat(...)
  .g   <- function(nm) get(nm, envir = envir)
  .has <- function(nm) exists(nm, envir = envir)

  # Resolve source paths: explicit argument wins, else the global/checkpoint.
  .p1 <- if (!is.null(las_1_path)) las_1_path else
         if (.has("las_1_path")) .g("las_1_path") else NULL
  .p2 <- if (!is.null(las_2_path)) las_2_path else
         if (.has("las_2_path")) .g("las_2_path") else NULL

  if (isTRUE(load)) {

    if (is.null(.p1))
      stop("[vis loader] las_1_path not supplied and not in the environment - ",
           "pass it or load this stage's checkpoint first.")

    .say(sprintf("[vis loader] Reading las_1 from disk: %s\n", basename(.p1)))
    l1 <- lidR::readLAS(.p1)
    if (lidR::is.empty(l1)) stop("[vis loader] las_1 read as empty: ", .p1)
    l1 <- lidR::add_lasattribute(l1, x = seq_len(nrow(l1@data)),
                                 name = "point_id", desc = "Unique ID for las_1 points")
    l2 <- NULL
    if (need_las2) {
      if (is.null(.p2))
        stop("[vis loader] las_2_path not supplied and not in the environment.")
      .say(sprintf("[vis loader] Reading las_2 from disk: %s\n", basename(.p2)))
      l2 <- lidR::readLAS(.p2)
      if (lidR::is.empty(l2)) stop("[vis loader] las_2 read as empty: ", .p2)
      l2 <- lidR::add_lasattribute(l2, x = seq_len(nrow(l2@data)),
                                   name = "point_id", desc = "Unique ID for las_2 points")
    }

    assign("las_1", l1, envir = envir)
    if (!is.null(l2)) assign("las_2", l2, envir = envir)

  } else {

    if (!.has("las_1"))
      stop("[vis loader] vis_load_clouds = FALSE but las_1 is not in memory. Set it TRUE.")
    if (need_las2 && !.has("las_2"))
      stop("[vis loader] vis_load_clouds = FALSE but las_2 is not in memory. Set it TRUE.")

    l1 <- .g("las_1")
    l2 <- if (need_las2) .g("las_2") else NULL
    .say("[vis loader] Reusing the point clouds already in memory (no disk read).\n")
  }

  # ── Rebuild the transform state (las_1 only; las_2 is never transformed) ──────
  # The stack runs in pipeline order on the RETURNED frame: Stage 1A align first,
  # then the Stage 2 rotation, then the Stage 4/5 shifts. Each step is a rigid
  # transform about the pivot the corresponding stage used, matching the Stage 2
  # composition. IDENTICAL in Stages 2, 3, 4 and 5 - if it is edited, edit all four.
  xyz   <- as.matrix(l1@data[, c("X", "Y", "Z")])
  state <- character(0)

  # ── Stage 1A: rough vertical alignment (raw disk -> aligned frame) ────────────
  if (isTRUE(apply_align)) {
    if (!.has("R_align_1") || !.has("align_pivot_1")) {
      .say("[vis loader] R_align_1 / align_pivot_1 not in the checkpoint - ",
           "las_1 left in the raw disk frame (no Stage 1A alignment).\n")
    } else {
      Ra <- .g("R_align_1"); pa <- as.numeric(.g("align_pivot_1"))
      xyz <- sweep(t(Ra %*% t(sweep(xyz, 2, pa))), 2, -pa)
      # Angle of the rigid rotation, for the log only: acos((tr(R) - 1) / 2).
      .ang_a <- acos(max(-1, min(1, (sum(diag(Ra)) - 1) / 2))) * 180 / pi
      state  <- c(state, sprintf("stage-1A align %.4f deg about align_pivot_1", .ang_a))
    }
  }

  # ── Stage 2: XYZ rotation R_xyz about pivot1 (aligned -> final) ───────────────
  if (isTRUE(apply_rot)) {
    if (!.has("R_xyz") || !.has("pivot1"))
      stop("[vis loader] apply_rot = TRUE but R_xyz / pivot1 not found - run the ",
           "Stage 2 rotation solve first, or reload a checkpoint that carries them.")
    R  <- .g("R_xyz"); pv <- as.numeric(.g("pivot1"))
    xyz <- sweep(t(R %*% t(sweep(xyz, 2, pv))), 2, -pv)
    .ang_x <- if (.has("angle_xyz")) .g("angle_xyz") else
              acos(max(-1, min(1, (sum(diag(R)) - 1) / 2))) * 180 / pi
    state <- c(state, sprintf("xyz-rot %.4f deg about pivot1", .ang_x))
  }

  if (isTRUE(apply_zshift)) {
    tz <- if (.has("t_trans_z_applied")) .g("t_trans_z_applied") else .g("t_trans_z")
    xyz[, 3] <- xyz[, 3] + tz
    state <- c(state, sprintf("z-shift %+.4f m", tz))
  }

  if (isTRUE(apply_zrot)) {
    # Same sign flip the Stage 5 / Stage 6 builders use: z_rotation_deg is held
    # in the standard CCW-positive convention, the 2x2 fill below evaluates to
    # the matrix for -a, so the angle is negated exactly once here.
    a  <- -.g("z_rotation_deg") * pi / 180
    Rz <- matrix(c(cos(a), -sin(a), sin(a), cos(a)), 2, 2)
    pv <- if (.has("pivot2")) .g("pivot2") else .g("pivot1")
    xc <- xyz[, 1] - pv[1]; yc <- xyz[, 2] - pv[2]
    xyz[, 1] <- Rz[1, 1] * xc + Rz[1, 2] * yc + pv[1]
    xyz[, 2] <- Rz[2, 1] * xc + Rz[2, 2] * yc + pv[2]
    state <- c(state, sprintf("z-rot %+.4f deg", .g("z_rotation_deg")))
  }

  pts_1 <- data.frame(X = xyz[, 1], Y = xyz[, 2], Z = xyz[, 3], TreeID = l1@data$TreeID)
  pts_1 <- pts_1[!is.na(pts_1$TreeID) & pts_1$TreeID != 0L, ]

  pts_2 <- NULL
  if (!is.null(l2)) {
    pts_2 <- data.frame(X = l2@data$X, Y = l2@data$Y, Z = l2@data$Z, TreeID = l2@data$TreeID)
    pts_2 <- pts_2[!is.na(pts_2$TreeID) & pts_2$TreeID != 0L, ]
  }

  .say(sprintf("[vis loader] las_1 state: %s\n",
               if (length(state)) paste(state, collapse = " + ") else "as loaded (no transform)"))
  .say(sprintf("[vis loader] stem points available - las_1: %s | las_2: %s\n",
               format(nrow(pts_1), big.mark = ","),
               if (is.null(pts_2)) "not loaded" else format(nrow(pts_2), big.mark = ",")))

  invisible(list(las_1 = l1, las_2 = l2, pts_1 = pts_1, pts_2 = pts_2,
                 xyz_1 = xyz, state = state))
}

# ============================================================
# Run tally - one cumulative record of how many things survived each filter
#
# Every stage prints its own counts, but those printouts vanish with the render
# and cannot be compared across runs. .tally() writes the same numbers into a
# single named list, `run_counts`, that travels in the checkpoints and is read
# out whole by the Stage 6 error report. A run then answers "how many pairs
# reached the Z-translation" without anyone re-reading five HTML files.
#
# Cumulative and idempotent: each call updates only the keys it names, so
# re-running one chunk refreshes that chunk's numbers and leaves the rest alone.
# It never errors - a tally is bookkeeping, and a missing count must not be able
# to stop a stage from saving.
# ============================================================
.tally <- function(...) {
  vals <- list(...)
  e    <- .stage_env()
  base <- if (exists("run_counts", envir = e, inherits = FALSE))
            get("run_counts", envir = e) else list()
  assign("run_counts", utils::modifyList(base, vals), envir = e)
  invisible(get("run_counts", envir = e))
}


#' TRUE when a cli bar can actually be seen.
#'
#' All four conditions matter: cli absent, output being knitted, a message sink
#' in the way (the batch driver), or a terminal that cannot redraw - any one of
#' them and the bar is invisible, mangled, or both.
.pb_cli_usable <- function() {
  isNamespaceLoaded("cli") || requireNamespace("cli", quietly = TRUE)
  requireNamespace("cli", quietly = TRUE) &&
    !isTRUE(getOption("knitr.in.progress")) &&
    sink.number(type = "message") == 0L &&
    isTRUE(try(cli::is_dynamic_tty(), silent = TRUE))
}

.pb_fmt_dur <- function(s) {
  if (!is.finite(s)) return("--")
  if (s < 90) sprintf("%.0fs", s) else if (s < 5400) sprintf("%.1fm", s / 60)
  else sprintf("%.1fh", s / 3600)
}

#' Start a bar. Returns an opaque handle for .pb_tick()/.pb_done(), or NULL.
#'
#' .envir = parent.frame() is load-bearing for the cli branch: cli ties a bar's
#' lifetime to a frame, so a bar created with the default .envir would be torn
#' down the instant this function returned and every later tick would silently
#' do nothing. That was a real bug here once.
.pb_new <- function(total, label) {
  total <- as.integer(total)
  if (!isTRUE(show_progress_bars) || is.na(total) || total < 1L) return(NULL)

  if (.pb_cli_usable()) {
    id <- cli::cli_progress_bar(
      name   = label,
      total  = total,
      format = paste0(label,
                      " {cli::pb_bar} {cli::pb_current}/{cli::pb_total}",
                      " | {cli::pb_elapsed} | {cli::pb_eta} left"),
      .envir = parent.frame())
    return(structure(list(kind = "cli", id = id), class = ".pb"))
  }

  # An ENVIRONMENT, not a list: a tick inside lapply() has to update the
  # caller's counter, and a list passed by value would not.
  st <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
  st$i <- 0L; st$total <- total; st$label <- label
  st$t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]; st$last_t <- -Inf; st$last_i <- -1L
  structure(list(kind = "lines", st = st), class = ".pb")
}

.pb_tick <- function(pb, by = 1L) {
  if (is.null(pb)) return(invisible(NULL))
  if (identical(pb$kind, "cli")) {
    cli::cli_progress_update(id = pb$id, inc = by)
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  st <- pb$st
  st$i <- st$i + by
  now <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  step <- max(1L, as.integer(ceiling(st$total * progress_step_frac)))
  due  <- st$i >= st$total || st$i == 1L ||
          (st$i - st$last_i) >= step ||
          (now - st$last_t) >= progress_min_seconds
  if (!due) return(invisible(NULL))
  st$last_i <- st$i; st$last_t <- now
  el   <- now - st$t0
  frac <- st$i / st$total
  eta  <- if (st$i > 0L) el / st$i * (st$total - st$i) else NA_real_
  nfill <- as.integer(round(20 * frac))
  cat(sprintf("  %s [%s%s] %d/%d %3.0f%% | %s elapsed | ~%s left\n",
              st$label, strrep("#", nfill), strrep("-", 20L - nfill),
              st$i, st$total, 100 * frac, .pb_fmt_dur(el), .pb_fmt_dur(eta)))
  flush.console()
  invisible(NULL)
}

.pb_done <- function(pb) {
  if (is.null(pb)) return(invisible(NULL))
  if (identical(pb$kind, "cli")) {
    cli::cli_progress_done(id = pb$id)
  } else if (pb$st$i < pb$st$total) {
    # The loop ended early (an epoch with nothing to do, say). Say so rather
    # than leaving a bar stopped at 12/25 as though something had hung.
    cat(sprintf("  %s: finished after %d of %d | %s\n", pb$st$label, pb$st$i,
                pb$st$total, .pb_fmt_dur(proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - pb$st$t0)))
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}
```

## 0.3 Load the Stage 2 Checkpoint

```{r}
#| label: params-load_Stage3
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Load the Stage 2 checkpoint"


# ── Source checkpoint ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# This is the STAGE 2 checkpoint. It was previously held in a variable called
# stage3_1_rds_path, which is also the name the Stage 3.1 save/load chunk uses
# for its OWN checkpoint further down - so whichever ran last silently decided
# where the other one pointed. Two checkpoints, two names.
#
# .stage_save never overwrites: it appends _001, _002 ... when the target
# exists, so the file Stage 2 actually wrote may carry a numeric suffix. Check
# the path Stage 2 printed rather than assuming this one.
stage2_rds_path <- "C:/Users/ascsh/Documents/1_Artemis/11_PaqLab/115_TreeTimeAlign/SaveLoad/Stage2_BOS_F1_4m_15mS1.rds"

.par_apply("params-load_Stage3")
```

```{r}
#| label: load_Stage3
#| code-summary: "Load the Stage 2 checkpoint"
#| code-fold: false

# ── What Stage 2 writes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# This list mirrors the Stage 2 save chunk. Requesting the full set rather than
# only what Stage 3 consumes is deliberate: .stage_load warns about objects
# present in the RDS but not requested, so a short list buys a wall of warnings
# and hides the ones that matter.
.stage2_required <- c(
  # ==== Inherited from the Stage 1 checkpoint (carried by Stage 2) ====
  "las_1_path", "las_2_path", "ransac_ellipse_script", "second_run",
  "ransac_seed", "ransac_track_history", "ransac_slice_bot", "ransac_slice_top",
  "treeids_1", "treeids_2", "pivot1",
  "fp", "ellipses_zt_1_all", "ellipses_zt_2_all",
  "mad_minor_mult", "mad_major_mult", "cp",
  "ellipses_zt_1_valid_all", "ellipses_zt_2_valid_all", "pairs_stage1",
  # Rough vertical alignment (Stage 1A), carried through the Stage 2
  # checkpoint. Required here (not just optional) because the Step 0.2 vis
  # loader's apply_align defaults TRUE - a raw las_1 needs this leg PLUS
  # R_xyz to reach the frame this stage's ellipses/vectors were measured in,
  # so a vis chunk run without it would be silently wrong rather than loudly
  # missing an object.
  "R_align_1", "align_pivot_1",
  # ==== Stage 2's own products ====================================
  "pf", "sp", "gold_count_basis", "gate_tests", "gate_min_votes",
  "gold_length", "gold_n_use",
  "pairs_axis", "vecs_xy_1", "vecs_xy_2", "ax",
  "ellipses_zt_1_valid", "ellipses_zt_2_valid",
  "angular_diag",
  # R_xyz is the second leg of the composed rotation the Step 0.2 vis loader
  # reconstructs (align then rot); Step 3.0a below applies it to las_1 too.
  "R_xyz", "angle_xyz", "yaw_in_R_xyz", "xy_tilt_in_rot_xyz_deg",
  "tilt_dir_deg", "tilt_consistency", "pairs_stage2",
  # Step 2.4 Z-translation pair set + the 2.1.3 straightness ranking behind it
  "pairs_ztrans", "ztrans_mode", "ztrans_rank", "ztrans_topup",
  "ztrans_target_pairs"
)

.stage2_optional <- c(
  # Carried from Stage 1: post-refit / pass-2 survivor sets + slice-fate ledger.
  "ellipses_zt_1_refit_all", "ellipses_zt_2_refit_all",
  "ellipses_zt_1_valid2_all", "ellipses_zt_2_valid2_all",
  "slice_fates_1", "slice_fates_2", "slice_fates_all",
  "slice_fate_summary_1", "slice_fate_summary_2",
  # Carried from Stage 1A.1b: the density regime and the fit settings it chose.
  # Step 3.2's axis-aligned fit adopts them so it runs on the same slice
  # thickness and inlier band Step 1.1 did.
  "density_stats", "density_stats_by_tree",
  "density_probe_width", "density_probe_step", "density_regime",
  "density_scarcity", "density_centre_scatter", "density_apply_regime",
  "density_max_frac_centre", "density_max_frac_minor", "density_max_frac_major",
  "density_slice_width_reco", "density_distance_threshold_reco"
)

.stage_load(stage2_rds_path, .stage2_required, .stage2_optional, label = "Stage 2")

# ── Hard requirements for the first half of this stage ────────────────────────
# .stage_load only WARNS on an absent object, which is right for diagnostics and
# wrong for these four: without them Stage 3 cannot read a cloud and cannot
# rotate it. Failing here names the missing object; failing later names a line
# of lidR internals.
.need <- c("las_1_path", "las_2_path", "pivot1", "R_xyz")
# exists() must be told WHERE to look. Called bare inside vapply it resolves
# from the frame vapply builds for it, whose enclosure is exists()'s own
# namespace - so the search runs base -> globalenv -> the search path and never
# reaches the environment these chunks are evaluating in. Run a .qmd by hand and
# that happens to be globalenv, so the check passes; run it under the batch
# driver, where chunks are evaluated in a per-pair environment, and all four
# objects report missing however plainly they are sitting there. This is the
# same trap as the old envir = .GlobalEnv defaults, wearing a different hat: a
# bare exists() inside an apply is not the same as a bare exists() at chunk top
# level, where the calling frame IS the evaluation environment.
.gone <- .need[!vapply(.need, exists, logical(1),
                       envir = .stage_env(), inherits = FALSE)]
if (length(.gone))
  stop(sprintf("[Stage 3 load] Stage 2 checkpoint is missing %d object(s) Stage 3 cannot run without:\n  %s",
               length(.gone), paste(.gone, collapse = "\n  ")))

cat("\n\u2500\u2500 Carried in from Stages 1-2 \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n")
.report_pivot1()       # <- the rotation origin Step 3.0a rotates about
cat(sprintf("XYZ rotation to apply (R_xyz): %.4f deg (yaw %.4f, tilt %.4f)\n",
            angle_xyz, yaw_in_R_xyz * 180 / pi, xy_tilt_in_rot_xyz_deg))
cat(sprintf("Straightness gate: %d of %d votes (%s) at a %.1f m window | %d straight %s\n",
            gate_min_votes, length(gate_tests), paste(gate_tests, collapse = ", "),
            gold_length, gold_n_use,
            if (identical(gold_count_basis, "pairs")) "pair(s)" else "stem(s)"))
cat(sprintf("Pairs: %d gated (pairs_axis) -> %d after the IRLS outlier drop (pairs_stage2)\n",
            nrow(pairs_axis), nrow(pairs_stage2)))
```


## 0.4 Input Parameters

Only the parameters Stage 3 introduces are set here. Stage 1 RANSAC geometry arrives in the checkpoint and are never redeclared,
so the two halves of the workflow cannot drift apart.

The two LAS paths are the exception, and they are re-stated deliberately: the
checkpoint carries the paths the files sat at when Stage 1 ran, which is not
necessarily where they sit now. Setting them here overrides the inherited
values, and the chunk reports whenever the two disagree so a silent substitution
of one collection for another is visible rather than assumed.

```{r}
#| label: params-stage3
#| code-summary: "User-defined input parameters (Stage 3)"
#| code-fold: false

# Stage 3 does not choose the clouds. It re-reads the two Stage 1 already
# measured, and every ellipse, axis and pair in the checkpoint was derived from
# those files - so pointing this stage at a different collection does not switch
# samples, it just measures one sample's clouds against another sample's
# geometry. INHERIT is therefore the default, and the paths below are a manual
# escape hatch rather than the normal route.
#
#   "inherit"  use whatever Stage 1 measured (from the checkpoint, or from the
#              session when the pipeline runs end to end). No path is typed
#              twice, so none can fall out of step with the sample being run.
#   "custom"   use s3_las_*_path_custom below. For the rare case of a relocated
#              or re-exported file, where the geometry still applies.
#
# This chunk used to assign the two hardcoded paths unconditionally. Renaming a
# sample in the driver and not here meant Stage 3 silently swapped in another
# collection - and once the old files were gone it stopped the run outright,
# after Stages 1 and 2 had done an hour of work.
s3_paths <- "inherit"

s3_las_1_path_custom <- "C:/Users/ascsh/Documents/1_Artemis/11_PaqLab/115_TreeTimeAlign/Neighbor_Collection/1_i_b_BOS_2020_Schoen/Focal_1_with_neighbors_5m.las"
s3_las_2_path_custom <- "C:/Users/ascsh/Documents/1_Artemis/11_PaqLab/115_TreeTimeAlign/Neighbor_Collection/1_ii_2024_5m_Schoen/Focal_191_with_neighbors_5m.las"

# Inherited values, kept so an override can be reported against them.
.las_1_path_ckpt <- if (exists("las_1_path")) las_1_path else NA_character_
.las_2_path_ckpt <- if (exists("las_2_path")) las_2_path else NA_character_

if (identical(s3_paths, "custom")) {
  las_1_path <- s3_las_1_path_custom
  las_2_path <- s3_las_2_path_custom
} else {
  if (is.na(.las_1_path_ckpt) || is.na(.las_2_path_ckpt))
    stop("[Stage 3 params] s3_paths = \"inherit\", but no las path came from the ",
         "checkpoint or the session. Run the load chunk above first, or set ",
         "s3_paths <- \"custom\".")
  las_1_path <- .las_1_path_ckpt
  las_2_path <- .las_2_path_ckpt
}

# Applied HERE, not at the end of the chunk: the checks below read these paths,
# so a driver value arriving after them would be validated too late - which is
# exactly how a run died on a stale hardcoded path that the driver had already
# replaced everywhere else.
.par_apply("params-stage3")

# A moved file is routine; a DIFFERENT file is not. Comparing the basenames
# separates the two: same name at a new location is a relocation, a new name
# means the epoch being aligned has changed and every measurement in the
# checkpoint was made on something else.
for (.e in list(c("las_1", .las_1_path_ckpt, las_1_path),
                c("las_2", .las_2_path_ckpt, las_2_path))) {
  if (is.na(.e[2]) || identical(.e[2], .e[3])) next
  cat(sprintf("%s path overridden here:\n  checkpoint: %s\n  this stage: %s\n",
              .e[1], .e[2], .e[3]))
  if (!identical(basename(.e[2]), basename(.e[3])))
    warning(sprintf("[Stage 3 params] %s FILENAME differs from the one Stage 1 measured (%s vs %s) - check this is the same epoch.",
                    .e[1], basename(.e[2]), basename(.e[3])), call. = FALSE)
}

.miss <- c(las_1_path, las_2_path)[!file.exists(c(las_1_path, las_2_path))]
if (length(.miss))
  stop("[Stage 3 params] LAS file not found:\n  ", paste(.miss, collapse = "\n  "))
```

## 0.6 Load Point Clouds
```{r}
#| label: load
#| code-summary: "Read LAS files and report point + TreeID counts"

# Step 0.6 - Load Point Clouds

# Read as-is. No stage filters its points: every ellipse centre, stem vector
# and rotation in the checkpoint was measured on the full cloud, and filtering
# here would refit 3.3's ellipses against a different population of points
# than the axes they are perpendicular to.
las_1 <- readLAS(las_1_path)
las_2 <- readLAS(las_2_path)
if (lidR::is.empty(las_1) || lidR::is.empty(las_2))
  stop("[Step 0.6] One or both clouds read as empty - check the paths in Step 0.4.")

las_1 <- lidR::add_lasattribute(
  las_1,
  x    = seq_len(nrow(las_1@data)),
  name = "point_id",
  desc = "Unique ID for las_1 points"
)

las_2 <- lidR::add_lasattribute(
  las_2,
  x    = seq_len(nrow(las_2@data)),
  name = "point_id",
  desc = "Unique ID for las_2 points"
)

xyz_1 <- as.matrix(las_1@data[, c("X", "Y", "Z")])
xyz_2 <- as.matrix(las_2@data[, c("X", "Y", "Z")])

# Unique TreeID counts (excluding NA and 0)
treeids_1 <- unique(las_1@data$TreeID)
treeids_1 <- treeids_1[!is.na(treeids_1) & treeids_1 != 0L]

treeids_2 <- unique(las_2@data$TreeID)
treeids_2 <- treeids_2[!is.na(treeids_2) & treeids_2 != 0L]

cat(sprintf("las_1: %s points | %d unique TreeID values (NA and 0 not counted)\n",
            format(nrow(xyz_1), big.mark = ","), length(treeids_1)))
cat(sprintf("las_2: %s points | %d unique TreeID values (NA and 0 not counted)\n",
            format(nrow(xyz_2), big.mark = ","), length(treeids_2)))

# The stems this stage can actually work on are the ones that survived Stage 2
# AND are still present in the cloud. A TreeID in pairs_stage2 with no points
# here means the two are out of step - almost always a different collection.
# Checked against pairs_ztrans when it is present, since that (not pairs_stage2)
# is the set Step 3.1 actually works through.
.pairs_chk <- if (exists("pairs_ztrans") && !is.null(pairs_ztrans)) pairs_ztrans else pairs_stage2
.want_1 <- setdiff(as.character(.pairs_chk$TreeID_1), as.character(treeids_1))
.want_2 <- setdiff(as.character(.pairs_chk$TreeID_2), as.character(treeids_2))
if (length(.want_1) || length(.want_2)) {
  warning(sprintf("[Step 0.6] %d las_1 and %d las_2 paired TreeID(s) have no points in the loaded cloud.",
                  length(.want_1), length(.want_2)), call. = FALSE)
  cat(sprintf("  missing las_1: %s\n  missing las_2: %s\n",
              paste(utils::head(.want_1, 10), collapse = ", "),
              paste(utils::head(.want_2, 10), collapse = ", ")))
} else {
  cat(sprintf("All %d paired stem(s) present in both clouds.\n", nrow(.pairs_chk)))
}


```


# Stage 3 - Axis-Perpendicular Ellipses and Z-Translation

This stage estimates the Z-translation offset. Slices are taken perpendicular to
each pair's average stem axis vector – the mean of the two Stage 2 stem vectors,
with `las_1`'s already rotated in Step 3.0b by the IRLS-solved rotation. The
shared direction is positioned on each stem separately, through that stem's own
kept ellipse centres, and the slice column starts where that fitted axis meets
the perpendicular plane through the stem's own lowest point – so stem-length 0
is the base of each stem, not a shared global base and not the middle of the
Stage 1 fitting window.
The resulting ellipse curves are plotted against stem-length position (projection
onto the pair axis) rather than raw Z.

## 3.0 Helpers

```{r}
#| label: stage3-helpers
#| code-summary: "Stage 3 helper functions"

# ─── RANSAC axis-aligned fitting ─────────────────────────────────────────────

# ── 4x4 homogeneous-matrix builders (Step 3 items 2/4: full-matrix transform
# with an exact algebraic inverse, rather than a basis-projection shortcut) ───
.transl_4x4 <- function(t) {
  M <- diag(4)
  M[1:3, 4] <- t
  M
}
.rot_4x4 <- function(R) {
  M <- diag(4)
  M[1:3, 1:3] <- R
  M
}

#' Build the exact full 4x4 rigid transform for one stem such that:
#'   - `axis_point` (that stem's own best-fit axis position, Step 3.1b) maps
#'     to the origin, and the shared pair-axis direction `ax` maps exactly
#'     onto the global Z axis -- i.e. the stem axis passes perfectly through
#'     the (temporary) z-axis for every Z, not merely parallel to it.
#'   - the lowest point of THIS stem's own point cloud (`pts`) is shifted to
#'     sit exactly on the temporary XY (Z = 0) plane.
#' M is a genuine 4x4 homogeneous matrix (rotation + translation); M_inv is
#' its exact algebraic inverse (built from R^T and negated translations, not
#' a numerical solve()), so back-projection via M_inv is a perfect round trip.
build_stem_axis_transform <- function(pts, axis_point, ax) {
  ax    <- ax / sqrt(sum(ax^2))
  basis <- make_perp_basis(ax)
  R     <- rbind(basis$u, basis$v, ax)   # orthonormal rotation: rows u, v, ax

  M_center  <- .transl_4x4(-axis_point)
  M_rot     <- .rot_4x4(R)
  M_partial <- M_rot %*% M_center         # translate to axis_point, then rotate

  pts_rot <- .apply_4x4_transform(pts, M_partial)
  z_min   <- min(pts_rot[, 3])

  M_z    <- .transl_4x4(c(0, 0, -z_min))
  M_full <- M_z %*% M_partial

  # Exact inverse: T(axis_point) %*% R^T %*% Tz(z_min)
  M_inv <- .transl_4x4(axis_point) %*% .rot_4x4(t(R)) %*% .transl_4x4(c(0, 0, z_min))

  list(M = M_full, M_inv = M_inv, R = R, axis_point = axis_point,
       ax = ax, z_min = z_min)
}

#' Build a temporary LAS object transformed with the exact full 4x4 stem-axis
#' transform (see build_stem_axis_transform()). The transform used is stashed
#' as the "axis_transform" attribute for back-projection later.
.make_axis_aligned_las <- function(las, tid, ax, axis_point) {
  idx <- which(las@data$TreeID == as.integer(tid))
  if (length(idx) < 5L) return(NULL)
  sub <- las[idx]
  ax  <- ax / sqrt(sum(ax^2))

  pts <- as.matrix(sub@data[, c("X", "Y", "Z")])
  tr  <- build_stem_axis_transform(pts, axis_point, ax)

  pts_new <- .apply_4x4_transform(pts, tr$M)
  sub@data$X <- pts_new[, 1]
  sub@data$Y <- pts_new[, 2]
  sub@data$Z <- pts_new[, 3]

  attr(sub, "axis_transform") <- tr
  sub
}
build_rings_axis <- function(ell_df, ax, n = 60L) {
  if (is.null(ell_df) || nrow(ell_df) == 0L) return(NULL)
  ax    <- ax / sqrt(sum(ax^2))
  basis <- make_perp_basis(ax)
  u_vec <- basis$u; v_vec <- basis$v
  theta <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n + 1L)
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(ell_df)), function(i) {
    Cx <- ell_df$center_x[i]; Cy <- ell_df$center_y[i]; Cz <- ell_df$center_z[i]
    a  <- ell_df$semi_a[i];   b  <- ell_df$semi_b[i]
    angle <- ell_df$angle_deg[i] * pi / 180
    if (any(is.na(c(Cx, Cy, Cz, a, b, angle)))) return(NULL)
    cos_a <- cos(angle); sin_a <- sin(angle)
    u_rot <- cos_a * u_vec - sin_a * v_vec
    v_rot <- sin_a * u_vec + cos_a * v_vec
    X <- Cx + a * cos(theta) * u_rot[1] + b * sin(theta) * v_rot[1]
    Y <- Cy + a * cos(theta) * u_rot[2] + b * sin(theta) * v_rot[2]
    Z <- Cz + a * cos(theta) * u_rot[3] + b * sin(theta) * v_rot[3]
    rbind(data.frame(X = X, Y = Y, Z = Z),
          data.frame(X = NA_real_, Y = NA_real_, Z = NA_real_))
  }))
}

# ─── Gallery renderer ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

#' Render a scrollable gallery of named ggplot panels as HTML with lightbox.
render_panel_gallery <- function(panel_list, lb_id, ncols = 2L) {
  encode_plot <- function(p, w = 10, h = 4.5, dpi = 180) {
    tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
    on.exit(unlink(tmp), add = TRUE)
    ggsave(tmp, plot = p, width = w, height = h, dpi = dpi)
    paste0("data:image/png;base64,", base64enc::base64encode(tmp))
  }
  img_tag <- function(src) sprintf(
    '<img src="%s"
          style="width:100%%;border-radius:6px;
                 box-shadow:0 2px 10px rgba(0,0,0,.18);
                 cursor:zoom-in;display:block;"
          onclick="openLb_%s(this.src)" />', src, lb_id)
  grid_css <- sprintf(
    "display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(%d,1fr);gap:18px;margin-bottom:24px;",
    ncols)
  blocks <- paste(
    vapply(names(panel_list), function(nm) {
      p <- panel_list[[nm]]
      if (is.null(p)) return("")
      b64 <- tryCatch(encode_plot(p), error = function(e) NULL)
      if (is.null(b64)) return("")
      sprintf(
        '<div>%s<p style="text-align:center;font-size:11px;color:#555;margin:4px 0 0 0;">%s</p></div>',
        img_tag(b64), nm)
    }, character(1)),
    collapse = "\n"
  )
  HTML(sprintf('
<style>
  #lbOv_%s{display:none;position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:9999;
    background:rgba(0,0,0,.82);align-items:center;justify-content:center;}
  #lbOv_%s.open{display:flex;}
  #lbOv_%s img{max-width:95vw;max-height:95vh;border-radius:6px;
    box-shadow:0 4px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.6);}
  #lbCl_%s{position:fixed;top:16px;right:20px;font-size:32px;color:#fff;
    cursor:pointer;line-height:1;user-select:none;z-index:10000;}
</style>
<div id="lbOv_%s" onclick="if(event.target===this)closeLb_%s()">
  <span id="lbCl_%s" onclick="closeLb_%s()">&#x2715;</span>
  <img id="lbIm_%s" src=""/>
</div>
<div style="%s padding:20px;">%s</div>
<script>
  window.openLb_%s  = s => {
    document.getElementById("lbIm_%s").src = s;
    document.getElementById("lbOv_%s").classList.add("open");
  };
  window.closeLb_%s = () =>
    document.getElementById("lbOv_%s").classList.remove("open");
</script>',
    lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id,
    lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id,
    grid_css, blocks,
    lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id
  ))
}
make_perp_basis <- function(ax) {
  ax   <- ax / sqrt(sum(ax^2))
  seed <- if (abs(ax[1]) < 0.9) c(1, 0, 0) else c(0, 1, 0)
  u    <- seed - sum(seed * ax) * ax
  u    <- u / sqrt(sum(u^2))
  v    <- c(ax[2]*u[3] - ax[3]*u[2],
            ax[3]*u[1] - ax[1]*u[3],
            ax[1]*u[2] - ax[2]*u[1])
  list(u = u, v = v)
}
```

## 3.0a Apply the Stage 1A Alignment + `R_xyz` to las_1 (Raw Disk Frame -> Final Frame)

```{r}
#| label: params-apply-xyz-rotation-stage3
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Apply the Stage 2 XYZ rotation to las_1, about pivot1"


# ── Automatic vs. custom transform ────────────────────────────────────────────
# apply_mode_rot = "auto" → use R_xyz, the FULL 3D rotation solved by the
# Stage 2 IRLS-SVD (yaw included). Default.
# apply_mode_rot = "custom" → override with a user-supplied 4x4 homogeneous
# matrix. Its top-left 3x3 replaces R_xyz (applied
# about pivot1); its rightmost column (rows 1:3) is
# an optional extra XYZ translation applied on top
# of the pivot-based rotation. Bottom row must stay
# c(0, 0, 0, 1).
apply_mode_rot <- "auto"    # "auto" or "custom"

.par_apply("params-apply-xyz-rotation-stage3")
```

```{r}
#| label: apply-xyz-rotation-stage3
#| code-summary: "Apply the Stage 2 XYZ rotation to las_1, about pivot1"
#| code-fold: false

# ── The Stage 2 solve, preserved across re-runs ───────────────────────────────
# A custom override REPLACES R_xyz and angle_xyz in the environment. Run this
# chunk twice in custom mode and the second run starts from the override rather
# than from the solve; switch back to "auto" afterwards and it quietly keeps
# using the custom matrix, because the solved one is gone. Stash it on first
# entry and start every run from there.
if (!exists("R_xyz_solved")) {
  R_xyz_solved     <- R_xyz
  angle_xyz_solved <- angle_xyz
}
R_xyz     <- R_xyz_solved
angle_xyz <- angle_xyz_solved

# ── Custom-matrix validation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Defined here because it exists nowhere else in the workflow - the custom
# branch below called it and failed on its first line. The three checks are the
# conditions the code downstream assumes: a 4x4 homogeneous matrix, a bottom row
# that does not project, and a 3x3 block that is a rotation rather than a scale,
# shear or reflection. A scale would resize every stem; a reflection would mirror
# the stand and still satisfy R'R = I, which is why the determinant is checked
# separately.
.validate_4x4_transform <- function(M, nm) {
  if (!is.matrix(M) || !identical(dim(M), c(4L, 4L)))
    stop(sprintf("[3.1] %s must be a 4x4 matrix.", nm))
  if (!isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(M[4, ]), c(0, 0, 0, 1))))
    stop(sprintf("[3.1] %s bottom row must be c(0, 0, 0, 1).", nm))
  R <- M[1:3, 1:3]
  if (!isTRUE(all.equal(t(R) %*% R, diag(3), tolerance = 1e-8, check.attributes = FALSE)))
    stop(sprintf("[3.1] the 3x3 block of %s is not a rotation (R'R != I) - a scale or shear here would resize the stems.", nm))
  if (det(R) < 0)
    stop(sprintf("[3.1] the 3x3 block of %s has determinant %.4f - a reflection, not a rotation.", nm, det(R)))
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# Rodrigues' rotation formula: a rotation of `magnitude_deg` about a horizontal
# axis perpendicular to `direction_deg`. A convenience for building a custom
# matrix by hand.
#
# WHAT THE TWO ARGUMENTS MEAN. Verified against the matrix rather than asserted:
#     R %*% c(0, 0, 1) = (sin m cos d, sin m sin d, cos m)
# so `magnitude_deg` is exactly the tilt away from vertical, and `direction_deg`
# is exactly the azimuth the +Z AXIS tips toward, CCW from +X. Those are the same
# two quantities .rot_specs() reports as tilt / tilt_dir in Stage 2, so a value
# entered here comes back out of the reports under the same name and meaning.
#
# An earlier version of this comment said points lying in `direction_deg` from
# the pivot move in +Z. They move in -Z: a point at azimuth d has
# R %*% (cos d, sin d, 0) = (..., ..., -sin m), so the ground on the
# `direction_deg` side goes DOWN while the axis leans that way. The matrix was
# always right; only the sentence was wrong, so nothing computed from it needs
# revisiting - but a custom matrix built by hand from the old reading would have
# been tilted 180 degrees out.
.tilt_rotation_matrix <- function(magnitude_deg, direction_deg) {
  m <- magnitude_deg * pi / 180
  d <- direction_deg * pi / 180
  axis <- c(-sin(d), cos(d), 0)          # horizontal axis, perpendicular to direction
  ax <- axis[1]; ay <- axis[2]; az <- axis[3]
  K <- matrix(c(  0, -az,  ay,
                 az,   0, -ax,
                -ay,  ax,   0), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)
  diag(3) + sin(m) * K + (1 - cos(m)) * (K %*% K)
}

# Only used when apply_mode_rot == "custom".
custom_transform_matrix_rot <- rbind(
  cbind(.tilt_rotation_matrix(0.5916, 20.85), c(0, 0, 0)),
  c(0, 0, 0, 1)
)

if (identical(apply_mode_rot, "custom")) {
  .validate_4x4_transform(custom_transform_matrix_rot, "custom_transform_matrix_rot")
  cat("XYZ rotation OVERRIDDEN with a custom 4x4 transform:\n")
  print(custom_transform_matrix_rot)
  cat(sprintf("  (Stage 2 auto-solved value was %.4f deg)\n", angle_xyz))
  R_xyz     <- custom_transform_matrix_rot[1:3, 1:3]
  angle_xyz <- acos(pmax(-1, pmin(1, (sum(diag(R_xyz)) - 1) / 2))) * 180 / pi
} else {
  cat(sprintf("Using the Stage 2 XYZ rotation: magnitude = %.4f deg\n", angle_xyz))
}

# ── Rotate about pivot1 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# pivot1 is the footprint centre of the filtered las_1 measured in Stage 1. It
# is used rather than the raw UTM origin because rotating about a far-off origin
# converts even a fraction of a degree into a large spurious translation. It is
# also the exact same point Stage 6 rotates about, so the transform applied here
# for fitting purposes and the transform written to the exported cloud agree.
cat(sprintf("Reconstructing Stage 1A alignment about align_pivot_1 = (%.4f, %.4f, %.4f) [%s]\n",
            align_pivot_1[1], align_pivot_1[2], align_pivot_1[3],
            if (isTRUE(run_rough_alignment)) "R_align_1 applied" else "R_align_1 = identity"))
cat(sprintf("Rotating (aligned frame) about pivot1 = (%.4f, %.4f, %.4f)\n",
            pivot1[1], pivot1[2], pivot1[3]))

# Centre, rotate and un-centre through ONE object. The previous version held
# xyz_1_raw, xyz_1_centered and xyz_1_rot simultaneously - three full copies of
# a multi-million-row matrix, plus las_1 and las_1_rot - in the one stage where
# memory is the binding constraint. Nothing downstream reads the intermediates.
#
# ── TWO LEGS, not one ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# las_1 here is freshly read from disk in Step 0.6 - the RAW, ORIGINAL-SCAN
# frame. Stage 1A's rough vertical alignment (R_align_1 about align_pivot_1)
# was only ever applied to las_1 IN MEMORY back in Stage 1 and was never
# written back to disk. But pivot1, the Stage 2 axis vectors and R_xyz were
# all measured AFTER that alignment, i.e. in the aligned frame. So a raw disk
# las_1 needs BOTH legs applied, in order, before R_xyz means what Stage 2
# solved it to mean:
#
#   x_aligned = R_align_1 (x_raw     - align_pivot_1) + align_pivot_1
#   x_final   = R_xyz     (x_aligned - pivot1)         + pivot1
#
# Applying R_xyz straight to the raw cloud (skipping the align leg) silently
# lands las_1_rot in neither the aligned frame nor the raw frame - exactly the
# mismatch the Step 0.2 vis loader's two-step reconstruction warns about.
# R_align_1 / align_pivot_1 are always defined (identity / pivot1 if rough
# alignment was not run in Stage 1), so this leg is always safe to apply.
xyz_1_rot <- sweep(as.matrix(las_1@data[, c("X", "Y", "Z")]), 2, align_pivot_1)
xyz_1_rot <- t(R_align_1 %*% t(xyz_1_rot))
xyz_1_rot <- sweep(xyz_1_rot, 2, -align_pivot_1)

xyz_1_rot <- sweep(xyz_1_rot, 2, pivot1)
xyz_1_rot <- if (identical(apply_mode_rot, "custom")) {
  .apply_4x4_transform(xyz_1_rot, custom_transform_matrix_rot)
} else {
  t(R_xyz %*% t(xyz_1_rot))
}
xyz_1_rot <- sweep(xyz_1_rot, 2, -pivot1)

las_1_rot        <- las_1
las_1_rot@data$X <- xyz_1_rot[, 1]
las_1_rot@data$Y <- xyz_1_rot[, 2]
las_1_rot@data$Z <- xyz_1_rot[, 3]

# A rotation is rigid, so no pairwise distance may change. Checking a sample of
# pairs catches a malformed matrix that passed validation - or an override with
# a scale hidden in it - before the ellipse refit inherits the error.
.chk <- sample.int(nrow(xyz_1_rot), min(2000L, nrow(xyz_1_rot)))
.d0  <- dist(as.matrix(las_1@data[.chk, c("X", "Y", "Z")]))
.d1  <- dist(xyz_1_rot[.chk, , drop = FALSE])
if (max(abs(.d1 - .d0)) > 1e-6)
  warning(sprintf("[3.1] rotation changed inter-point distances by up to %.3g m - the transform is not rigid.",
                  max(abs(.d1 - .d0))), call. = FALSE)

cat(sprintf("Applied XYZ rotation to %s las_1 points | largest point displacement %.4f m | rigid to %.2g m\n",
            format(nrow(xyz_1_rot), big.mark = ","),
            max(sqrt(rowSums((xyz_1_rot - as.matrix(las_1@data[, c("X", "Y", "Z")]))^2))),
            max(abs(.d1 - .d0))))
cat("las_2 is the fixed reference cloud and is never transformed.\n")

# ── The same transform, for anything that is not the cloud ────────────────────
# Defined here rather than in Step 3.0 so it sits beside the transform it
# mirrors and is available to Step 3.0a, which runs first. Whichever branch was
# taken above - auto R_xyz or a custom 4x4 - this applies it to an arbitrary
# Nx3 of XYZ about pivot1, so ellipse centres and axis vectors can never drift
# out of the frame the cloud is in.
.apply_R_xyz_about_pivot1 <- function(xyz) {
  xyz   <- as.matrix(xyz)
  xyz_c <- sweep(xyz, 2, pivot1)
  if (identical(apply_mode_rot, "custom")) {
    sweep(.apply_4x4_transform(xyz_c, custom_transform_matrix_rot), 2, -pivot1)
  } else {
    sweep(t(R_xyz %*% t(xyz_c)), 2, -pivot1)
  }
}
```

## 3.0b Rotate the Kept Stem Axis Vectors

```{r}
#| label: rotate-stem-axis-vectors
#| code-summary: "Rotate the Stage 2 per-stem axis vectors into the post-rotation frame -> vecs_axis_1_rot"

# ── Why this chunk exists ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# vecs_xy_1 holds the RAW, pre-rotation per-stem axis vectors – fitted in Stage
# 2.4 by Theil-Sen regression of x and y on z over the bottom axis_window_m, and
# the very vectors Stage 2.5 used to SOLVE R_xyz. Now that the rotation has been applied to
# the las_1 cloud (las_1_rot, above), those raw vectors describe stem
# orientation in the OLD frame and no longer match the cloud. Step 3.1 builds
# pair_axis_list – the axis each stem is re-sliced perpendicular to – so it must
# be built from the ROTATED axis or every axis-perpendicular slice for las_1 is
# subtly mis-oriented relative to the cloud it is cut from.
#
# The rotated vectors are written to a NEW object, vecs_axis_1_rot; vecs_xy_1 is
# left untouched so the Stage 2 solve inputs remain inspectable.
#
# A stem axis is a direction (unit vector), not a point, so rotating it strictly
# only needs the rotation part: translating both endpoints by the same amount
# cancels in the difference, whatever pivot is used. It is nonetheless routed
# through the identical pivot1-centred machinery used for the cloud above (same
# pivot, same auto/custom branch) so the axis transform can never silently drift
# from the point-cloud transform.

.rotate_stem_axis <- function(v, pivot) {
  if (any(is.na(v))) return(rep(NA_real_, 3L))

  p0 <- matrix(pivot,     nrow = 1L)   # a point AT the shared pivot
  p1 <- matrix(pivot + v, nrow = 1L)   # a second point, one axis-unit away

  if (identical(apply_mode_rot, "custom")) {
    p0_rot <- sweep(.apply_4x4_transform(sweep(p0, 2, pivot), custom_transform_matrix_rot), 2, -pivot)
    p1_rot <- sweep(.apply_4x4_transform(sweep(p1, 2, pivot), custom_transform_matrix_rot), 2, -pivot)
  } else {
    p0_rot <- sweep(t(R_xyz %*% t(sweep(p0, 2, pivot))), 2, -pivot)
    p1_rot <- sweep(t(R_xyz %*% t(sweep(p1, 2, pivot))), 2, -pivot)
  }

  v_rot <- as.numeric(p1_rot - p0_rot)
  norm  <- sqrt(sum(v_rot^2))
  if (norm < 1e-10) return(rep(NA_real_, 3L))
  v_rot / norm
}

# New object – vecs_xy_1 itself is never modified.
vecs_axis_1_rot <- vecs_xy_1

.rot_mat <- t(vapply(
  seq_len(nrow(vecs_xy_1)),
  function(i) .rotate_stem_axis(as.numeric(vecs_xy_1[i, c("vx", "vy", "vz")]), pivot1),
  numeric(3L)
))
vecs_axis_1_rot$vx_rot <- .rot_mat[, 1]
vecs_axis_1_rot$vy_rot <- .rot_mat[, 2]
vecs_axis_1_rot$vz_rot <- .rot_mat[, 3]

# las_2 is never rotated (fixed reference cloud), so vecs_xy_2 is used as-is
# downstream with no rotated counterpart.

cat(sprintf(
  "Rotated %d / %d las_1 stem axis vectors about pivot1 (%.4f, %.4f, %.4f) -> vecs_axis_1_rot\n",
  sum(!is.na(vecs_axis_1_rot$vx_rot)), nrow(vecs_axis_1_rot),
  pivot1[1], pivot1[2], pivot1[3]
))

# ── Sanity check ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The expected reorientation is NOT angle_xyz. A rotation by alpha about axis n
# moves a unit vector v through theta, where
# cos(theta) = cos^2(phi) + sin^2(phi) * cos(alpha), phi = angle(v, n)
# so a vector lying ALONG the axis does not move at all, and only one
# perpendicular to it moves by the full alpha. Stems are near vertical, and
# R_xyz retains the yaw it was solved with, whose axis is near vertical too -
# so the stems move a good deal less than angle_xyz. The old check compared the
# mean against angle_xyz and would have reported a failure on a correct
# rotation. Comparing each stem against its OWN predicted angle tests the thing
# that should actually hold: that the axes moved exactly as the cloud did.
.rot_axis <- function(R) {
  a <- acos(pmax(-1, pmin(1, (sum(diag(R)) - 1) / 2)))
  if (a < 1e-9) return(list(axis = c(0, 0, 1), angle = 0))
  n <- c(R[3, 2] - R[2, 3], R[1, 3] - R[3, 1], R[2, 1] - R[1, 2]) / (2 * sin(a))
  list(axis = n / sqrt(sum(n^2)), angle = a)
}
.ra <- .rot_axis(R_xyz)

.ang <- t(vapply(seq_len(nrow(vecs_axis_1_rot)), function(i) {
  a <- as.numeric(vecs_axis_1_rot[i, c("vx", "vy", "vz")])
  b <- as.numeric(vecs_axis_1_rot[i, c("vx_rot", "vy_rot", "vz_rot")])
  if (any(is.na(a)) || any(is.na(b))) return(c(NA_real_, NA_real_))
  cp <- sum(a * .ra$axis)                      # cos of the angle to the axis
  c(acos(pmax(-1, pmin(1, sum(a * b)))) * 180 / pi,
    acos(pmax(-1, pmin(1, cp^2 + (1 - cp^2) * cos(.ra$angle)))) * 180 / pi)
}, numeric(2)))
.obs <- .ang[, 1]; .pred <- .ang[, 2]

cat(sprintf("Rotation axis: (%.3f, %.3f, %.3f), %.2f deg from vertical | rotation %.4f deg\n",
            .ra$axis[1], .ra$axis[2], .ra$axis[3],
            acos(pmin(1, abs(.ra$axis[3]))) * 180 / pi, angle_xyz))
cat(sprintf("Axis reorientation: observed %.4f deg (median) | predicted %.4f deg | worst disagreement %.2g deg\n",
            median(.obs, na.rm = TRUE), median(.pred, na.rm = TRUE),
            max(abs(.obs - .pred), na.rm = TRUE)))
if (isTRUE(max(abs(.obs - .pred), na.rm = TRUE) > 1e-6))
  warning("[3.1] rotated axes do not match the rotation applied to the cloud - the two transforms have drifted apart.",
          call. = FALSE)
```
