```{r}
#| label: export-rotated-cloud-stage3
#| code-summary: "Optionally export las_1 with the XYZ rotation applied (diagnostic)"

# In a batch this is OFF unless asked for. It is an eyeballing aid, and a batch
```

## 3.0c Rotate the Kept Ellipse Centres

Stage 1 and Stage 2 measured every ellipse in the **pre-rotation** frame. Step
3.0a rotated the `las_1` cloud and Step 3.0b rotated its axis vectors; this step
does the same for `las_1`'s kept ellipse centres, so all three describe the same
stand. `las_2` is never rotated and is used as it stands.

```{r}
#| label: rotate-kept-ellipse-centres
#| code-summary: "Rotate the las_1 kept ellipse centres into the post-rotation frame -> ellipses_zt_1_valid_rot"

# ── Frame note ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# slice_z is an ABSOLUTE world Z. The RANSAC library no longer re-bases each
# tree to its own lowest point before slicing, so center_x, center_y and
# slice_z together are already a world XYZ point and need no reconstruction.
# (Earlier revisions of this step added each tree's min(Z) back onto slice_z to
# undo a per-tree re-basing that no longer happens - which added the stem's
# base elevation a second time and put every anchor point hundreds of metres
# out. That reconstruction is gone.)
#
# The rotated coordinates are written to center_x / center_y / center_z in a
# NEW list. slice_z is left exactly as it was: it records the height the slice
# was CUT at in the original frame, which is not the same quantity as the
# rotated centre's Z and should not be silently overwritten with it.
.centres_of <- function(d)
  cbind(d$center_x, d$center_y, d$slice_z)

ellipses_zt_1_valid_rot <- lapply(ellipses_zt_1_valid, function(d) {
  if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L) return(d)
  ok <- !is.na(d$center_x) & !is.na(d$center_y) & !is.na(d$slice_z)
  d$center_z <- NA_real_
  if (any(ok)) {
    r <- .apply_R_xyz_about_pivot1(.centres_of(d)[ok, , drop = FALSE])
    d$center_x[ok] <- r[, 1]
    d$center_y[ok] <- r[, 2]
    d$center_z[ok] <- r[, 3]
  }
  d
})

# las_2 keeps its own frame, but gains the same column so both sides can be
# read with one accessor downstream.
ellipses_zt_2_valid_rot <- lapply(ellipses_zt_2_valid, function(d) {
  if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L) return(d)
  d$center_z <- d$slice_z
  d
})

# One accessor, both epochs: an Nx3 of world XYZ in the WORKING frame (rotated
# for las_1, untouched for las_2), NA rows dropped.
.stem_centres <- function(tid, epoch) {
  d <- if (identical(epoch, "las_1")) ellipses_zt_1_valid_rot[[as.character(tid)]]
       else                           ellipses_zt_2_valid_rot[[as.character(tid)]]
  if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L) return(NULL)
  m <- cbind(d$center_x, d$center_y, d$center_z)
  m <- m[stats::complete.cases(m), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(m) == 0L) NULL else m
}

# How far the rotation actually moved the centres, and a check that it moved
# them the same way it moved the cloud: a centre and the points it was fitted
# to must land in the same place.
.n_ell_1 <- sum(vapply(ellipses_zt_1_valid_rot, function(d) if (is.null(d)) 0L else nrow(d), integer(1)))
.disp <- unlist(lapply(names(ellipses_zt_1_valid), function(k) {
  a <- ellipses_zt_1_valid[[k]]; b <- ellipses_zt_1_valid_rot[[k]]
  if (is.null(a) || nrow(a) == 0L) return(numeric(0))
  sqrt((b$center_x - a$center_x)^2 + (b$center_y - a$center_y)^2 +
       (b$center_z - a$slice_z)^2)
}))
cat(sprintf("Rotated %s kept las_1 ellipse centre(s) across %d stem(s) | displacement %.4f - %.4f m\n",
            format(.n_ell_1, big.mark = ","), length(ellipses_zt_1_valid_rot),
            min(.disp, na.rm = TRUE), max(.disp, na.rm = TRUE)))

.probe <- .apply_R_xyz_about_pivot1(matrix(pivot1, nrow = 1L))
cat(sprintf("Transform check: pivot1 maps to itself to within %.2g m\n",
            max(abs(as.numeric(.probe) - pivot1))))
```

## 3.1 Per-Pair Average Stem Axis Vectors

```{r}
#| label: pair-axis-vectors
#| code-summary: "Compute unweighted average stem axis per temporal pair (from Step 2)"

# ── Pairs entering Stage 3 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Stage 3 measures the Z-TRANSLATION, so it takes the Z-translation pair set
# Step 2.4 assembled - pairs_ztrans - NOT the rotation set.
#
# The two differ deliberately. pairs_stage2 is the rotation set: gate survivors
# minus the IRLS residual outliers, kept tight because a bent stem biases a
# rotation rather than merely adding noise to it. pairs_ztrans is that same set,
# topped up on the 2.1.3 straightness ranking when the gate left fewer than
# ztrans_target_pairs, because the Z-translation averages a per-pair feature
# match and its precision falls off directly with the pair count - and a mildly
# bent stem still carries perfectly matchable bumps and hollows up its length.
# In the "gate" and "irls_all" modes the two sets are identical.
#
# Falling back to pairs_stage2 keeps this runnable against a checkpoint written
# before Step 2.4 existed.
if (exists("pairs_ztrans") && !is.null(pairs_ztrans) && nrow(pairs_ztrans) > 0L) {
  pairs_stage3_in <- pairs_ztrans
  .src_lab <- sprintf("pairs_ztrans, mode %s",
                      if (exists("ztrans_mode")) ztrans_mode else "unknown")
} else {
  pairs_stage3_in <- pairs_stage2
  .src_lab <- "pairs_stage2 (pairs_ztrans absent - pre-2.4 checkpoint)"
  warning("[3.1] pairs_ztrans not found - falling back to the rotation pair set ",
          "pairs_stage2. Any Step 2.4 top-up is NOT in this run.", call. = FALSE)
}

# From here Stage 3 produces its own newly named lists rather than overwriting
# the input:
#
#   pairs_stage3_in -> pairs_axis_ok   (drop pairs with an NA average axis)
#                   -> pairs_ax_fitted (drop pairs with no fitted ellipses)
#                   -> pairs_stage3    (final Stage 3 pair set)
cat(sprintf("Pairs entering Stage 3 (%s): %d\n", .src_lab, nrow(pairs_stage3_in)))
cat(sprintf("  rotation set (pairs_stage2): %d | Stage 1 produced %d\n",
            nrow(pairs_stage2), nrow(pairs_stage1)))
if (!is.null(pairs_stage3_in$source))
  cat(sprintf("  of these, %d came from the gate and %d were topped up on rank\n",
              sum(pairs_stage3_in$source == "gate"),
              sum(pairs_stage3_in$source == "topup")))
.tally(n_pairs_stage3_in = nrow(pairs_stage3_in))
rm(.src_lab)

# ── Build per-pair average axis vector ───────────────────────────────────────
# Uses a simple unweighted average of the two unit stem vectors.
# Both vectors are flipped to point upward (vz > 0) before averaging.
# An additional dot-product check flips v2 if it points away from v1,
# which handles nearly-horizontal stems correctly where the Z-sign guard
# alone is insufficient.
#
# IMPORTANT: v1 (las_1) uses the ROTATED axis (vecs_axis_1_rot$vx_rot/vy_rot/
# vz_rot, from the "Rotate the Kept Stem Axis Vectors" chunk in Step 3.1) –
# NOT the raw pre-rotation vecs_xy_1 vectors that were only computed to SOLVE
# the rotation in the first place. pair_axis_list is used below to re-slice
# las_1_rot (the ALREADY-rotated las_1 cloud), so the axis must live in that
# same rotated frame or every axis-aligned/axis-perpendicular slice for las_1
# is subtly mis-oriented relative to the cloud it's cut from. las_2 is never
# rotated, so v2 correctly keeps using the raw vecs_xy_2 axis.

pairs_axis_ok <- pairs_stage3_in   # new object; the input set is never mutated

# Every list built in this section - pair_axis_list, pair_axis_point_1,
# pair_axis_point_2 - is keyed by TreeID_1 alone, and Step 3.3 looks the axis
# and both anchors up by that key. That is only sound if a las_1 stem appears
# in at most one pair: if one appeared twice, the second would overwrite the
# first and both pairs would silently be fitted about the same axis. Cheap to
# assert, expensive to discover later.
if (anyDuplicated(pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_1))
  stop(sprintf("[3.2] TreeID_1 is not unique across pairs (%s) - the axis and anchor lists are keyed by it.",
               paste(unique(pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_1[duplicated(pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_1)]),
                     collapse = ", ")))

pair_axis_list <- setNames(
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs_axis_ok)), function(i) {
    tid1 <- pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_1[i]; tid2 <- pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_2[i]
    rows1 <- which(vecs_axis_1_rot$TreeID == tid1)
    rows2 <- which(vecs_xy_2$TreeID == tid2)
    if (length(rows1) == 0L || length(rows2) == 0L) return(rep(NA_real_, 3L))
    v1 <- as.numeric(vecs_axis_1_rot[rows1[1L], c("vx_rot", "vy_rot", "vz_rot")])
    v2 <- as.numeric(vecs_xy_2[rows2[1L], c("vx", "vy", "vz")])
    if (any(is.na(v1)) || any(is.na(v2))) return(rep(NA_real_, 3L))
    # Ensure both point upward
    if (v1[3L] < 0) v1 <- -v1
    if (v2[3L] < 0) v2 <- -v2
    # If vectors still point away from each other, flip v2
    if (sum(v1 * v2) < 0) v2 <- -v2
    avg  <- v1 + v2
    norm <- sqrt(sum(avg^2))
    if (norm < 1e-10) return(rep(NA_real_, 3L))
    avg / norm
  }),
  as.character(pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_1)
)

valid_axes <- sum(sapply(pair_axis_list, function(v) !any(is.na(v))))
cat(sprintf("Valid pair axis vectors: %d / %d\n", valid_axes, nrow(pairs_axis_ok)))

# Drop pairs whose axis vector is NA
na_axis_tids <- as.integer(names(Filter(function(v) any(is.na(v)), pair_axis_list)))
if (length(na_axis_tids) > 0L) {
  cat(sprintf(
    "Dropping %d pair(s) with NA axis vector: %s\n",
    length(na_axis_tids), paste(na_axis_tids, collapse = ", ")
  ))
  pairs_axis_ok       <- pairs_axis_ok[!pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_1 %in% na_axis_tids, ]
  pair_axis_list <- pair_axis_list[!names(pair_axis_list) %in% as.character(na_axis_tids)]
}

cat(sprintf("Pairs carried forward: %d\n", nrow(pairs_axis_ok)))
```

## 3.2 Per-Stem Axis Anchor Points

```{r}
#| label: params-per-stem-axis-position
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Per-stem axis anchor: shared pair direction, positioned on that stem's own kept centres, pinned to the stem base"


# ── What an anchor is, and why the direction alone is not enough ──────────────
# pair_axis_list gives ONE shared direction per pair. A direction is not a line:
# each stem sits at its own place in space, and the two stems of a pair are not
# collinear. Two more things are needed, and they are separate questions.
#
# WHERE the line sits. For a FIXED direction, the line minimising the summed
# squared perpendicular distance to a set of points passes through their
# centroid - sliding a line along its own direction changes no perpendicular
# distance - so the centroid of that stem's own kept ellipse centres is the
# best-fit position for the shared direction. This is a fit, and the
# perpendicular RMS below says how good it is.
#
# WHERE ALONG the line to measure from. Step 3.3 slices from
# s5_slice_bot to s5_slice_top measured along the axis FROM THE ANCHOR, so
# the anchor sets the origin of the stem-length coordinate. The centroid is
# the wrong origin for that: it sits in the middle of the Stage 1 fitting
# window, roughly 1.8 m up, so a 0.8 - 5.8 m window measured from it actually
# samples about 2.6 - 7.6 m of stem. The anchor is therefore slid down the
# fitted line to the plane perpendicular to the axis through the stem's own
# lowest point:
#
# p = c + ((b - c) . a_hat) * a_hat
#
# with c the centroid, b the stem base point and a_hat the unit pair axis.
# That is the foot of the axis at the stem base - on the fitted line, and on
# the perpendicular plane level with the base - so stem-length 0 means the
# bottom of the stem on both sides of the pair.
#
# The anchor depends only on Stage 1/2 kept centres and the cloud, never on
# Step 3.3's own output, so it does not move between fitting passes.

# ── The stem base point ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The lowest point of the stem, in the WORKING frame (las_1_rot for epoch 1,
# las_2 for epoch 2). A single stray low point - a ground return that kept the
# stem's TreeID - would drag the anchor down with it, so the quantile below can
# be lifted off the true minimum. It defaults to 0, the literal lowest point,
# and the report says how far the 0.1% quantile sits above it: a large gap
# means the minimum is an outlier rather than the stem base.
anchor_base_quantile <- 0

.par_apply("params-per-stem-axis-position")
```

```{r}
#| label: per-stem-axis-position
#| code-summary: "Per-stem axis anchor: shared pair direction, positioned on that stem's own kept centres, pinned to the stem base"

.stem_base_point <- function(las, tid, q = anchor_base_quantile) {
  idx <- which(las@data$TreeID == as.integer(tid))
  if (!length(idx)) return(rep(NA_real_, 3L))
  z  <- las@data$Z[idx]
  zt <- if (q <= 0) min(z) else as.numeric(stats::quantile(z, q, names = FALSE))
  j  <- idx[which.min(abs(z - zt))]
  c(las@data$X[j], las@data$Y[j], las@data$Z[j])
}

# ── Anchor, and how well the shared direction suits this stem ────────────────
.axis_anchor <- function(centres, axis, base_pt) {
  cen <- colMeans(centres)
  if (any(is.na(base_pt))) return(list(p = rep(NA_real_, 3L), cen = cen,
                                       rms = NA_real_, slide = NA_real_))
  slide <- sum((base_pt - cen) * axis)
  d     <- sweep(centres, 2, cen)
  perp  <- d - outer(as.vector(d %*% axis), axis)
  list(p     = cen + slide * axis,
       cen   = cen,
       rms   = sqrt(mean(rowSums(perp^2))),   # centres about the fitted line
       slide = slide)                          # centroid -> base, along axis
}

pair_axis_point_1 <- setNames(vector("list", nrow(pairs_axis_ok)), as.character(pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_1))
pair_axis_point_2 <- setNames(vector("list", nrow(pairs_axis_ok)), as.character(pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_1))
axis_anchor_diag  <- NULL

for (i in seq_len(nrow(pairs_axis_ok))) {
  tid1     <- pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_1[i]
  tid2     <- pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_2[i]
  tid1_chr <- as.character(tid1)
  ax       <- pair_axis_list[[tid1_chr]]

  c1 <- .stem_centres(tid1, "las_1")
  c2 <- .stem_centres(tid2, "las_2")

  a1 <- if (is.null(c1) || is.null(ax) || any(is.na(ax)))
          list(p = rep(NA_real_, 3L), cen = rep(NA_real_, 3L), rms = NA_real_, slide = NA_real_)
        else .axis_anchor(c1, ax, .stem_base_point(las_1_rot, tid1))
  a2 <- if (is.null(c2) || is.null(ax) || any(is.na(ax)))
          list(p = rep(NA_real_, 3L), cen = rep(NA_real_, 3L), rms = NA_real_, slide = NA_real_)
        else .axis_anchor(c2, ax, .stem_base_point(las_2, tid2))

  pair_axis_point_1[[tid1_chr]] <- a1$p
  pair_axis_point_2[[tid1_chr]] <- a2$p

  # Along-axis span of the kept centres MEASURED FROM THE ANCHOR - i.e. in the
  # same coordinate Step 3.3 slices in. Read against s5_slice_bot/top to see
  # whether the fitting window covers the stem the ellipses actually came from.
  .s <- function(cc, p) if (is.null(cc) || any(is.na(p))) c(NA_real_, NA_real_) else
          range(as.vector(sweep(cc, 2, p) %*% ax))
  s1 <- .s(c1, a1$p); s2 <- .s(c2, a2$p)

  axis_anchor_diag <- rbind(axis_anchor_diag, data.frame(
    TreeID_1 = tid1, TreeID_2 = tid2,
    n_cen_1 = if (is.null(c1)) 0L else nrow(c1),
    n_cen_2 = if (is.null(c2)) 0L else nrow(c2),
    fit_rms_1_cm = a1$rms * 100, fit_rms_2_cm = a2$rms * 100,
    base_slide_1 = a1$slide,     base_slide_2 = a2$slide,
    cen_lo_1 = s1[1], cen_hi_1 = s1[2],
    cen_lo_2 = s2[1], cen_hi_2 = s2[2],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
}
rownames(axis_anchor_diag) <- NULL

n_valid_pts <- sum(vapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs_axis_ok)), function(i) {
  k <- as.character(pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_1[i])
  !any(is.na(pair_axis_point_1[[k]])) && !any(is.na(pair_axis_point_2[[k]]))
}, logical(1)))

cat(sprintf("Axis anchors: %d / %d pair(s) with a valid anchor on both sides\n",
            n_valid_pts, nrow(pairs_axis_ok)))
cat(sprintf("  centroid -> base slide: %.2f to %.2f m (las_1) | %.2f to %.2f m (las_2)\n",
            min(axis_anchor_diag$base_slide_1, na.rm = TRUE),
            max(axis_anchor_diag$base_slide_1, na.rm = TRUE),
            min(axis_anchor_diag$base_slide_2, na.rm = TRUE),
            max(axis_anchor_diag$base_slide_2, na.rm = TRUE)))
# A large negative slide is expected - the centroid sits above the base by
# roughly half the Stage 1 window - and it is exactly the offset the old
# centroid anchor was missing.
cat(sprintf("  kept centres, along-axis from the anchor: %.2f to %.2f m (las_1) | %.2f to %.2f m (las_2)\n",
            min(axis_anchor_diag$cen_lo_1, na.rm = TRUE),
            max(axis_anchor_diag$cen_hi_1, na.rm = TRUE),
            min(axis_anchor_diag$cen_lo_2, na.rm = TRUE),
            max(axis_anchor_diag$cen_hi_2, na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("  shared direction vs each stem's own centres, perpendicular RMS: median %.2f cm (las_1) | %.2f cm (las_2) | worst %.2f cm\n",
            median(axis_anchor_diag$fit_rms_1_cm, na.rm = TRUE),
            median(axis_anchor_diag$fit_rms_2_cm, na.rm = TRUE),
            max(c(axis_anchor_diag$fit_rms_1_cm, axis_anchor_diag$fit_rms_2_cm), na.rm = TRUE)))

# A stray low return would show up here as a base far below the lowest kept
# centre. Reported rather than corrected: raising anchor_base_quantile is a
# decision about the data, not something to do silently.
.q_gap_1 <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs_axis_ok)), function(i) {
  tid <- pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_1[i]
  idx <- which(las_1_rot@data$TreeID == as.integer(tid))
  if (!length(idx)) return(NA_real_)
  z <- las_1_rot@data$Z[idx]
  as.numeric(stats::quantile(z, 0.001, names = FALSE)) - min(z)
}, numeric(1))
cat(sprintf("  las_1 stem base: the 0.1%% quantile sits %.3f m above the minimum at the median, %.3f m at worst (anchor_base_quantile = %g)\n",
            median(.q_gap_1, na.rm = TRUE), max(.q_gap_1, na.rm = TRUE),
            anchor_base_quantile))

cat("\nPer-pair anchor diagnostics:\n")
print(axis_anchor_diag, row.names = FALSE, digits = 4)
```

### Vis - 3D pair vector and anchor
```{r}
#| label: params-fig-3D-axes-anchors
#| code-summary: "Parameters - 3D: kept stem points with the centred pair-axis vector (gold) and each stem's anchor point"


# ── What this shows ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# One scene, both epochs. For every pair carried forward: the stem points, the
# shared pair-axis direction drawn as the line it actually is – positioned on
# that stem's own kept ellipse centres – and the anchor as a sphere at the foot
# of that line.
#
# The thing to look for is where the gold line MEETS the sphere: the anchor
# should sit at the bottom of the stem points, not in the middle of them. An
# anchor floating mid-stem is the centroid bug returning, and it would shift
# every slice in Step 3.3 by the same amount.
#
# The line is drawn over the interval Step 3.3 will actually slice, so the gold
# segment is a preview of the fitting window rather than a decoration: if it
# runs out past the top of the points, or starts below them, the window and the
# stem disagree.

vis_axes_max_pairs <- 13L    # pairs drawn; NULL or Inf for all
vis_axes_max_pts   <- 2000L   # points per stem after thinning
vis_axes_anchor_sz <- 5      # anchor sphere size

.par_apply("params-fig-3D-axes-anchors")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-3D-axes-anchors
#| code-summary: "3D: kept stem points with the centred pair-axis vector (gold) and each stem's anchor point"
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7

if (params$make_plots) {

  # Step 3.3's window if it has been run, otherwise the span of the kept
  # centres, padded. Either way the gold segment is measured along the axis
  # from the anchor, which is the coordinate the slicing uses.
  .ax_lo <- if (exists("s5_slice_bot")) s5_slice_bot else
              max(0, min(axis_anchor_diag$cen_lo_1, axis_anchor_diag$cen_lo_2,
                         na.rm = TRUE) - 0.5)
  .ax_hi <- if (exists("s5_slice_top")) s5_slice_top else
              max(axis_anchor_diag$cen_hi_1, axis_anchor_diag$cen_hi_2,
                  na.rm = TRUE) + 0.5

  .keys <- as.character(pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_1)
  .ok   <- vapply(.keys, function(k)
             !is.null(pair_axis_list[[k]])     && !any(is.na(pair_axis_list[[k]])) &&
             !any(is.na(pair_axis_point_1[[k]])) && !any(is.na(pair_axis_point_2[[k]])),
             logical(1))
  .use <- which(.ok)
  if (is.finite(vis_axes_max_pairs %||% Inf) && length(.use) > vis_axes_max_pairs)
    .use <- .use[seq_len(vis_axes_max_pairs)]

  if (length(.use) == 0L) {
    cat("No pair has a valid axis and anchors on both sides - nothing to draw.\n")
  } else {

    # ── Gather ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    .thin <- function(d) if (nrow(d) > vis_axes_max_pts)
                           d[sample.int(nrow(d), vis_axes_max_pts), , drop = FALSE] else d

    .pts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(.use, function(i) {
      t1 <- pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_1[i]; t2 <- pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_2[i]
      d1 <- las_1_rot@data[las_1_rot@data$TreeID == as.integer(t1), c("X", "Y", "Z")]
      d2 <- las_2@data[    las_2@data$TreeID     == as.integer(t2), c("X", "Y", "Z")]
      rbind(
        if (nrow(d1)) data.frame(.thin(as.data.frame(d1)), epoch = "las_1", TreeID = t1),
        if (nrow(d2)) data.frame(.thin(as.data.frame(d2)), epoch = "las_2", TreeID = t2)
      )
    }))

    # Axis segments and anchors, both epochs, in one pass.
    .seg <- NULL; .anc <- NULL
    for (i in .use) {
      k  <- as.character(pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_1[i])
      ax <- pair_axis_list[[k]]
      for (e in c("las_1", "las_2")) {
        p   <- if (e == "las_1") pair_axis_point_1[[k]] else pair_axis_point_2[[k]]
        tid <- if (e == "las_1") pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_1[i] else pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_2[i]
        a   <- p + .ax_lo * ax
        b   <- p + .ax_hi * ax
        # NA row breaks the polyline so one trace can carry every segment.
        .seg <- rbind(.seg, data.frame(X = c(a[1], b[1], NA),
                                       Y = c(a[2], b[2], NA),
                                       Z = c(a[3], b[3], NA)))
        .anc <- rbind(.anc, data.frame(X = p[1], Y = p[2], Z = p[3],
                                       epoch = e, TreeID = tid))
      }
    }

    # ── Local frame ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Plotly loses precision on raw UTM coordinates, and a scene centred on the
    # origin is unreadable. Everything is shifted by one common offset, so the
    # relative geometry - which is the whole point of the figure - is untouched.
    .cx <- mean(.pts$X, na.rm = TRUE); .cy <- mean(.pts$Y, na.rm = TRUE)
    for (nm in c(".pts", ".seg", ".anc")) {
      d <- get(nm); d$X <- d$X - .cx; d$Y <- d$Y - .cy; assign(nm, d)
    }

    .anc$lab <- sprintf("%s | TreeID %s | anchor", .anc$epoch, .anc$TreeID)

    p3d <- plot_ly() |>
      add_trace(data = .pts, x = ~X, y = ~Y, z = ~Z,
                color = ~epoch, colors = c(las_1 = COL_1, las_2 = COL_2),
                type = "scatter3d", mode = "markers",
                marker = list(size = 1.6, opacity = 0.45),
                hoverinfo = "none") |>
      add_trace(data = .seg, x = ~X, y = ~Y, z = ~Z,
                type = "scatter3d", mode = "lines",
                name = sprintf("pair axis (%.1f-%.1f m)", .ax_lo, .ax_hi),
                line = list(color = "#E8B10A", width = 7),
                hoverinfo = "none", inherit = FALSE) |>
      add_trace(data = .anc, x = ~X, y = ~Y, z = ~Z,
                type = "scatter3d", mode = "markers",
                name = "anchor point", text = ~lab, hoverinfo = "text",
                marker = list(size = vis_axes_anchor_sz, color = "#566E3D",
                              opacity = 0.95,
                              line = list(color = "#D9F9A5", width = 1)),
                inherit = FALSE)

    p3d <- p3d |> layout(
      title = sprintf("Pair axes and stem anchors - %d of %d pair(s), %s pts/stem",
                      length(.use), sum(.ok), format(vis_axes_max_pts, big.mark = ",")),
      scene = list(
        xaxis = list(title = "X local (m)"),
        yaxis = list(title = "Y local (m)"),
        zaxis = list(title = "Z (m)"),
        aspectmode = "data",
        camera = list(eye = list(x = 1.6, y = 1.6, z = 0.7))
      ),
      legend = list(title = list(text = "Cloud / geometry"))
    )

    cat(sprintf("Drawing %d of %d valid pair(s) | axis segment %.2f - %.2f m along the axis from each anchor\n",
                length(.use), sum(.ok), .ax_lo, .ax_hi))
    p3d
  }
}
```

## 3.3 Axis-aligned Ellipse Fitting - pass 1

For each kept-pair tree, the cloud is temporarily rotated so that the pair's average stem
axis aligns with the fitting frame's Z-axis. The full-range `ransac_ellipse_fit_one()` (same
RANSAC pipeline as Step 1) is then run on ALL original points – no inlier
pre-filtering, no PCA approximation.

The structure mirrors Stage 1 exactly: fit, clean, masked refit of what cleaning
removed, then a second cleaning pass over the refit set. Everything runs in each
stem's own axis-aligned frame, where `slice_z` is distance along the stem axis
and `center_x` / `center_y` are perpendicular offsets from it. Results are
back-projected to world coordinates once, at the end, so no intermediate step has
to reason in two frames at once.

```{r}
#| label: params-axis-aligned-ransac-fit
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Run RANSAC axis-aligned ellipse fitting for all paired trees"


# ── Axis-perpendicular RANSAC ellipse fitting (Step 3.2) ──────────────────────
# Height range is stem-length along each pair's own axis, measured from that
# stem's own axis origin – not world Z.
s3_slice_bot   <- 0.0    # m
s3_slice_top   <- NULL    # m  
s3_slice_step  <- 0.05   # m  
s3_slice_width <- 0.05   # m
s3_ransac_distance_threshold <- 0.005
s3_ransac_iter_per_point       <- 1.0
s3_ransac_iter_max             <- 750L
s3_ransac_iter_min             <- 1L     # raise this if very sparse slices need a floor
                                       # (res_1/res_2/ellipses_zt_*_all/etc.). NULL → use the first value.
ransac_seed                 <- 33L    # RNG seed for reproducible sampling

.par_apply("params-axis-aligned-ransac-fit")
```

```{r}
#| label: axis-aligned-ransac-fit
#| code-summary: "Run RANSAC axis-aligned ellipse fitting for all paired trees"

# ── Where the local frame's zero sits ─────────────────────────────────────────
# build_stem_axis_transform() puts the stem's own lowest PROJECTED point on the
# local Z = 0 plane, so s3_slice_bot is measured from the base of the stem in
# the axis frame. The Step 3.2 anchor still decides where the axis LINE sits
# laterally; its along-axis component is superseded here, which is the right
# division of labour - the anchor is a fit through the ellipse centres, and the
# base is a property of the points.
#
# s3_slice_top = NULL means each stem is sliced to its own highest point rather
# than to a shared ceiling.

# ── Fit settings from the Stage 1A.1b density probe ──────────────────────────
# Both epochs were measured in Stage 1 and a regime was chosen there; this
# adopts it, so Stage 3 slices at the same thickness and accepts the same inlier
# band Step 1.1 used. A NO-OP when the probe did not run or was set to report
# only, in which case the params chunk's own values stand.
#
# It sits here rather than in the params chunk because fp_s3 is built from these
# two values immediately below - the params chunk is a separate chunk, so a
# driver override there would still land in time, but a reader editing this
# chunk would not see where the values came from.
if (exists("density_slice_width_reco") && !is.null(density_slice_width_reco) &&
    is.finite(density_slice_width_reco)) {
  s3_slice_width <- density_slice_width_reco
  cat(sprintf("[3.2] density probe (%s, t = %.2f): slice width %.0f cm\n",
              density_regime, density_scarcity, s3_slice_width * 100))
}
if (exists("density_distance_threshold_reco") && !is.null(density_distance_threshold_reco) &&
    is.finite(density_distance_threshold_reco)) {
  s3_ransac_distance_threshold <- density_distance_threshold_reco
  cat(sprintf("[3.2] density probe (%s, t = %.2f): distance threshold %.1f mm\n",
              density_regime, density_scarcity, s3_ransac_distance_threshold * 1000))
}

fp_s3 <- ransac_ellipse_fit_params(
  bot                = s3_slice_bot,
  top                = s3_slice_top,
  height_min         = NULL,          # pairing already decided which stems are fitted
  step               = s3_slice_step,
  width              = s3_slice_width,
  distance_threshold = s3_ransac_distance_threshold,
  n_iterations       = 1000L,         # ignored while iter_per_point is set
  iter_per_point     = s3_ransac_iter_per_point,
  iter_max           = s3_ransac_iter_max,
  iter_min           = s3_ransac_iter_min,
  early_exit         = FALSE,
  track_history      = if (exists("ransac_track_history")) ransac_track_history else FALSE
)

# ── Fit one stem in its own axis frame ────────────────────────────────────────
# The points are transformed, the SAME ransac_ellipse_fit_one() Stage 1 uses is
# run on them, and the result is returned in the LOCAL frame together with the
# transform that produced it. Back-projection is deliberately NOT done here:
# cleaning and the masked refit both need to work in the frame the slicing
# happened in, and converting back and forth between them is how a frame error
# gets in. .s3_backproject() does it once, after the second cleaning pass.
.s3_fit_stem_local <- function(las, tid, ax, axis_point, fp, seed) {
  idx <- which(las@data$TreeID == as.integer(tid))
  if (length(idx) < 5L) return(NULL)
  sub <- las[idx]
  pts <- as.matrix(sub@data[, c("X", "Y", "Z")])
  tr  <- tryCatch(build_stem_axis_transform(pts, axis_point, ax),
                  error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(tr)) return(NULL)

  loc <- .apply_4x4_transform(pts, tr$M)
  sub@data$X <- loc[, 1]; sub@data$Y <- loc[, 2]; sub@data$Z <- loc[, 3]

  raw <- tryCatch(
    ransac_ellipse_fit_one(las = sub, tree_ids = as.integer(tid), params = fp,
                           label = as.character(tid), show_progress = FALSE,
                           seed = seed)[[as.character(tid)]],
    error = function(e) {
      warning(sprintf("[axis-RANSAC] tree %s failed: %s", tid, conditionMessage(e)),
              call. = FALSE)
      NULL
    })
  if (is.null(raw) || nrow(raw) == 0L) return(NULL)
  list(raw = as.data.frame(raw), tr = tr)
}

# ── The local-frame point set for one stem ────────────────────────────────────
# Recomputed from the stored transform rather than cached: the masked refit is
# the only thing that needs it, and holding every paired stem's points in a
# second frame would double the memory this stage already spends on clouds.
.s3_pts_local <- function(las, tid, tr) {
  idx <- which(las@data$TreeID == as.integer(tid))
  if (!length(idx)) return(NULL)
  d   <- las@data[idx, ]
  loc <- .apply_4x4_transform(as.matrix(d[, c("X", "Y", "Z")]), tr$M)
  data.frame(point_id = if ("point_id" %in% names(d)) d$point_id else seq_along(idx),
             X = loc[, 1], Y = loc[, 2], Z = loc[, 3])
}

# Only the fitting RUN is skipped on a reload; the parameters and helpers above
# are always defined, because the cleaning, refit and protrusion chunks below
# use them whether or not the fit was re-executed this session.
if (!second_run) {

cat(sprintf("Step 3.3 fitting: %.2f m to %s | step %.3f m | width %.3f m | threshold %.4f m\n",
            s3_slice_bot, if (is.null(s3_slice_top)) "each stem's own top"
                          else sprintf("%.2f m", s3_slice_top),
            s3_slice_step, s3_slice_width, s3_ransac_distance_threshold))
cat(sprintf("  iteration budget: %.1f per candidate point, clamped to [%d, %d]\n",
            s3_ransac_iter_per_point, s3_ransac_iter_min, s3_ransac_iter_max))

n_pairs_s3 <- nrow(pairs_axis_ok)
t0_s3      <- proc.time()["elapsed"]

.s3_fit_epoch <- function(las, id_col, epoch, label) {
  # .pb_* rather than cli directly: under the batch driver a cli bar is drawn on
  # stderr into an unsplittable message sink, so this fit - the longest step in
  # Stage 3 - reported nothing on screen and a smear of escape codes in the log.
  pb <- .pb_new(n_pairs_s3, label)
  on.exit(.pb_done(pb), add = TRUE)

  out <- lapply(seq_len(n_pairs_s3), function(i) {
    .pb_tick(pb)
    k   <- as.character(pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_1[i])
    tid <- pairs_axis_ok[[id_col]][i]
    ax  <- pair_axis_list[[k]]
    apt <- if (identical(epoch, "las_1")) pair_axis_point_1[[k]] else pair_axis_point_2[[k]]
    if (is.null(ax) || any(is.na(ax)) || is.null(apt) || any(is.na(apt))) return(NULL)
    .s3_fit_stem_local(las, tid, ax, apt, fp_s3, ransac_seed)
  })
  setNames(out, as.character(pairs_axis_ok[[id_col]]))
}

.fit_1 <- .s3_fit_epoch(las_1_rot, "TreeID_1", "las_1", "las_1 axis-RANSAC")
.fit_2 <- .s3_fit_epoch(las_2,     "TreeID_2", "las_2", "las_2 axis-RANSAC")

# Split into the two things the rest of the stage needs: the local-frame
# ellipse tables, and the per-stem transforms that put them back in the world.
ellipses_ax_1_raw <- lapply(.fit_1, function(x) if (is.null(x)) data.frame() else x$raw)
ellipses_ax_2_raw <- lapply(.fit_2, function(x) if (is.null(x)) data.frame() else x$raw)
axis_tr_1 <- lapply(.fit_1, function(x) if (is.null(x)) NULL else x$tr)
axis_tr_2 <- lapply(.fit_2, function(x) if (is.null(x)) NULL else x$tr)

elapsed_s3 <- round((proc.time()["elapsed"] - t0_s3) / 60, 1)
cat(sprintf("\nAxis-RANSAC fitting complete - las_1: %d stems | las_2: %d stems | %.1f min\n",
            sum(vapply(ellipses_ax_1_raw, nrow, integer(1)) > 0L),
            sum(vapply(ellipses_ax_2_raw, nrow, integer(1)) > 0L), elapsed_s3))
cat(sprintf("  slices fitted: las_1 %d | las_2 %d\n",
            sum(vapply(ellipses_ax_1_raw, function(d) sum(!is.na(d$center_x)), integer(1))),
            sum(vapply(ellipses_ax_2_raw, function(d) sum(!is.na(d$center_x)), integer(1)))))

ee_ax_1 <- ransac_ellipse_summarise_early_exit(ellipses_ax_1_raw, label = "las_1 axis")
ee_ax_2 <- ransac_ellipse_summarise_early_exit(ellipses_ax_2_raw, label = "las_2 axis")

}
```

## 3.4 Ellipse Cleaning - pass 1

```{r}
#| label: params-s3-clean-pass1
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Neighbour-slice consensus (adaptive) + MAD semi-minor + MAD semi-major, in the axis frame"


# ── Stage A: consensus parameters ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Each fitted slice is compared with the nearest fitted slice above and below it
# along the stem axis. Unfitted slices are skipped over, so a gap does not break
# the chain. Two slices i, j AGREE if ALL of:
# perpendicular centre distance <= frac_centre * mean(minor_i, minor_j)
# |delta semi-minor| <= frac_minor * min(minor_i, minor_j)
# |delta semi-major| <= frac_major * min(major_i, major_j)
# A slice with no agreeing neighbour is removed.
#
# The tolerances are the Stage 1 defaults. They may want to be TIGHTER here:
# these slices are cut perpendicular to the stem axis rather than horizontally,
# so a leaning stem no longer produces the elongated sections that forced Stage
# 1's tolerances open. Read the first run's removal counts before deciding.
s3_consensus_frac_centre <- 0.20   # of the MEAN semi-minor of the two slices
s3_consensus_frac_minor  <- 0.20   # of the SMALLER semi-minor
s3_consensus_frac_major  <- 0.20   # of the SMALLER semi-major

s3_consensus_tol_floor <- NULL     # optional absolute floor on any tolerance (m)
s3_consensus_tol_cap   <- NULL     # optional absolute cap on any tolerance (m)
s3_consensus_max_gap   <- NULL     # max along-axis gap to count as neighbours (m)
s3_consensus_sort_axes <- TRUE     # compare max-to-max / min-to-min, not a-to-a

# ── Stage B / C: MAD outlier parameters ───────────────────────────────────────
s3_mad_minor_mult  <- 3.0
s3_mad_minor_min_n <- 5L
s3_run_mad_minor   <- TRUE

s3_mad_major_mult  <- 3.0
s3_mad_major_min_n <- 5L
s3_run_mad_major   <- TRUE

s3_run_cleaning <- TRUE            # FALSE = pass the raw fit through as-is

.par_apply("params-s3-clean-pass1")
```

```{r}
#| label: s3-clean-pass1
#| code-summary: "Neighbour-slice consensus (adaptive) + MAD semi-minor + MAD semi-major, in the axis frame"

# ── Consensus fractions from the Stage 1A.1b scarcity ramp ───────────────────
# Same t Stage 1 used, but interpolated from STAGE 3's OWN bases (0.20, tighter
# than Stage 1's 0.30 because these slices are cut perpendicular to each stem's
# own axis, so the stem's tilt is already out of the residual). A NO-OP at
# t = 0, and when the probe did not run or was set to report only.
#
# Pass 2 follows automatically - s3_consensus2_frac_* are NULL and inherit these.
if (exists("density_scarcity") && isTRUE(density_scarcity > 0) &&
    isTRUE(density_apply_regime)) {
  .dscale <- function(base, cap) base + density_scarcity * (cap - base)
  .old_c  <- c(s3_consensus_frac_centre, s3_consensus_frac_minor, s3_consensus_frac_major)

  s3_consensus_frac_centre <- .dscale(s3_consensus_frac_centre, density_max_frac_centre)
  s3_consensus_frac_minor  <- .dscale(s3_consensus_frac_minor,  density_max_frac_minor)
  s3_consensus_frac_major  <- .dscale(s3_consensus_frac_major,  density_max_frac_major)

  cat(sprintf(paste0("[3.5] scarcity t = %.2f: frac_centre %.2f -> %.2f | ",
                     "frac_minor %.2f -> %.2f | frac_major %.2f -> %.2f\n"),
              density_scarcity,
              .old_c[1], s3_consensus_frac_centre,
              .old_c[2], s3_consensus_frac_minor,
              .old_c[3], s3_consensus_frac_major))
  rm(.dscale, .old_c)
}


# ── Implementation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The same three flagging functions Stage 1 uses, defined here because they live
# in the Stage 1 document rather than in the RANSAC library. Kept byte-identical
# in behaviour on purpose: if the two stages cleaned by different rules, a
# difference between the Stage 1 and Stage 3 ellipse sets could not be
# attributed to the axis-perpendicular slicing, which is the whole point of
# fitting them twice.
.s3_consensus_flag_one <- function(df, frac_c, frac_maj, frac_min,
                                   max_gap = NULL, sort_axes = TRUE,
                                   tol_floor = NULL, tol_cap = NULL) {
  n <- nrow(df)
  if (n == 0L) return(df)

  fitted <- !is.na(df$center_x) & !is.na(df$center_y) &
            !is.na(df$semi_a)   & !is.na(df$semi_b)   & !is.na(df$slice_z)

  maj  <- if (sort_axes) pmax(df$semi_a, df$semi_b) else df$semi_a
  min_ <- if (sort_axes) pmin(df$semi_a, df$semi_b) else df$semi_b

  .clamp <- function(t) {
    if (!is.null(tol_floor)) t <- max(t, tol_floor)
    if (!is.null(tol_cap))   t <- min(t, tol_cap)
    t
  }

  agrees  <- rep(FALSE, n); n_agree <- rep(0L, n)
  tol_c_used <- tol_min_used <- tol_maj_used <- rep(NA_real_, n)

  idx <- which(fitted)
  if (length(idx) >= 2L) {
    ord <- idx[order(df$slice_z[idx])]
    for (k in seq_len(length(ord) - 1L)) {
      i <- ord[k]; j <- ord[k + 1L]
      gap <- abs(df$slice_z[j] - df$slice_z[i])
      if (!is.null(max_gap) && gap > max_gap) next

      tol_c   <- .clamp(frac_c   * mean(c(min_[i], min_[j])))
      tol_min <- .clamp(frac_min * min(min_[i], min_[j]))
      tol_maj <- .clamp(frac_maj * min(maj[i],  maj[j]))

      tol_c_used[c(i, j)]   <- pmax(tol_c_used[c(i, j)],   tol_c,   na.rm = TRUE)
      tol_min_used[c(i, j)] <- pmax(tol_min_used[c(i, j)], tol_min, na.rm = TRUE)
      tol_maj_used[c(i, j)] <- pmax(tol_maj_used[c(i, j)], tol_maj, na.rm = TRUE)

      d_centre <- sqrt((df$center_x[j] - df$center_x[i])^2 +
                       (df$center_y[j] - df$center_y[i])^2)

      if (d_centre <= tol_c && abs(min_[j] - min_[i]) <= tol_min &&
          abs(maj[j] - maj[i]) <= tol_maj) {
        agrees[i] <- TRUE; agrees[j] <- TRUE
        n_agree[i] <- n_agree[i] + 1L; n_agree[j] <- n_agree[j] + 1L
      }
    }
  }

  df$minor_len    <- ifelse(fitted, min_, NA_real_)
  df$major_len    <- ifelse(fitted, maj,  NA_real_)
  df$n_agreeing   <- n_agree
  df$tol_centre   <- tol_c_used
  df$tol_minor    <- tol_min_used
  df$tol_major    <- tol_maj_used
  df$no_consensus <- fitted & !agrees
  df$unfitted     <- !fitted

  if (!"ell_ecc" %in% names(df)) {
    a_ <- pmax(df$semi_a, df$semi_b); b_ <- pmin(df$semi_a, df$semi_b)
    df$ell_ecc <- sqrt(pmax(0, 1 - (b_ / a_)^2))
  }
  df
}

.s3_mad_minor_flag_one <- function(df, mult, min_n) {
  n <- nrow(df)
  df$mad_minor_z <- NA_real_; df$mad_minor_out <- rep(FALSE, n)
  if (n == 0L) return(df)
  eligible <- !df$unfitted & !df$no_consensus & !is.na(df$minor_len)
  if (sum(eligible) < min_n) return(df)
  b   <- df$minor_len[eligible]
  med <- median(b, na.rm = TRUE)
  m   <- mad(b, center = med, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.na(m) || m < 1e-12) return(df)
  df$mad_minor_z[eligible]   <- (b - med) / m
  df$mad_minor_out[eligible] <- abs(b - med) > mult * m
  df
}

.s3_mad_major_flag_one <- function(df, mult, min_n) {
  n <- nrow(df)
  df$mad_major_z <- NA_real_; df$mad_major_out <- rep(FALSE, n)
  if (n == 0L) return(df)
  minor_out <- if ("mad_minor_out" %in% names(df)) df$mad_minor_out else rep(FALSE, n)
  eligible <- !df$unfitted & !df$no_consensus & !minor_out & !is.na(df$major_len)
  if (sum(eligible) < min_n) return(df)
  a   <- df$major_len[eligible]
  med <- median(a, na.rm = TRUE)
  m   <- mad(a, center = med, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.na(m) || m < 1e-12) return(df)
  df$mad_major_z[eligible]   <- (a - med) / m
  df$mad_major_out[eligible] <- abs(a - med) > mult * m
  df
}

.s3_consensus_clean <- function(raw_list, frac_c, frac_maj, frac_min,
                                max_gap = NULL, sort_axes = TRUE,
                                tol_floor = NULL, tol_cap = NULL,
                                do_mad = TRUE, mad_mult = 3.0, mad_min_n = 5L,
                                do_mad_maj = TRUE, mad_maj_mult = 3.0,
                                mad_maj_min_n = 5L) {
  lapply(raw_list, function(df) {
    if (is.null(df)) df <- data.frame()
    flagged <- .s3_consensus_flag_one(df, frac_c, frac_maj, frac_min,
                                      max_gap, sort_axes, tol_floor, tol_cap)
    flagged <- if (do_mad && nrow(flagged) > 0L)
      .s3_mad_minor_flag_one(flagged, mad_mult, mad_min_n) else {
        flagged$mad_minor_z <- NA_real_
        flagged$mad_minor_out <- rep(FALSE, nrow(flagged)); flagged }
    flagged <- if (do_mad_maj && nrow(flagged) > 0L)
      .s3_mad_major_flag_one(flagged, mad_maj_mult, mad_maj_min_n) else {
        flagged$mad_major_z <- NA_real_
        flagged$mad_major_out <- rep(FALSE, nrow(flagged)); flagged }

    if (nrow(flagged) > 0L) {
      flagged$spike_cx    <- flagged$no_consensus
      flagged$spike_cy    <- flagged$no_consensus
      flagged$spike_xy    <- flagged$no_consensus
      flagged$spike_b     <- flagged$mad_minor_out
      flagged$spike_a     <- flagged$mad_major_out
      flagged$spike_radii <- flagged$mad_minor_out | flagged$mad_major_out
      flagged$spike       <- flagged$no_consensus | flagged$unfitted |
                             flagged$mad_minor_out | flagged$mad_major_out
      flagged$isolated    <- FALSE
    }

    valid  <- if (nrow(flagged)) flagged[!flagged$spike, , drop = FALSE] else flagged
    before <- nrow(flagged)

    list(flagged = flagged, valid = valid,
         ellipses_before = before, ellipses_after = nrow(valid),
         n_removed_unfitted = if (before) sum(flagged$unfitted,      na.rm = TRUE) else 0L,
         n_removed_orphan   = if (before) sum(flagged$no_consensus,  na.rm = TRUE) else 0L,
         n_removed_mad      = if (before) sum(flagged$mad_minor_out, na.rm = TRUE) else 0L,
         n_removed_mad_maj  = if (before) sum(flagged$mad_major_out, na.rm = TRUE) else 0L,
         med_tol_centre     = if (before) median(flagged$tol_centre, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
         prop_kept          = if (before > 0L) nrow(valid) / before else NA_real_)
  })
}

.s3_print_clean_summary <- function(clean_result, label, frac_c, frac_min, frac_maj,
                                    madB_on, madB_mult, madB_n,
                                    madA_on, madA_mult, madA_n) {
  cat(sprintf(paste0("\n[%s] Cleaning - consensus (adaptive), MAD semi-minor, MAD semi-major\n",
                     "      centre <= %.0f%% of mean semi-minor | minor <= %.0f%% of lower semi-minor | major <= %.0f%% of lower semi-major\n",
                     "      MAD semi-minor: %s (mult = %.1f, min n = %d) | MAD semi-major: %s (mult = %.1f, min n = %d)\n"),
              label, frac_c * 100, frac_min * 100, frac_maj * 100,
              if (madB_on) "on" else "off", madB_mult, madB_n,
              if (madA_on) "on" else "off", madA_mult, madA_n))

  tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(clean_result), function(tid) {
    r <- clean_result[[tid]]
    data.frame(TreeID = tid, before = r$ellipses_before,
               unfit = r$n_removed_unfitted, orphan = r$n_removed_orphan,
               madB = r$n_removed_mad, madA = r$n_removed_mad_maj,
               kept = r$ellipses_after,
               pct  = round(100 * r$prop_kept, 1),
               tol_cm = round(100 * r$med_tol_centre, 2),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
  if (is.null(tab) || nrow(tab) == 0L) { cat("  (no trees)\n"); return(invisible(NULL)) }
  print(tab, row.names = FALSE)
  cat(sprintf("  TOTAL: %d in -> %d kept (%.1f%%) | %d unfitted, %d orphaned, %d MAD semi-minor, %d MAD semi-major\n",
              sum(tab$before), sum(tab$kept),
              100 * sum(tab$kept) / max(1L, sum(tab$before)),
              sum(tab$unfit), sum(tab$orphan), sum(tab$madB), sum(tab$madA)))
  invisible(tab)
}

# ── Run ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
.s3_clean_args <- list(
  frac_c    = s3_consensus_frac_centre,
  frac_maj  = s3_consensus_frac_major,
  frac_min  = s3_consensus_frac_minor,
  max_gap   = s3_consensus_max_gap,
  sort_axes = s3_consensus_sort_axes,
  tol_floor = s3_consensus_tol_floor,
  tol_cap   = s3_consensus_tol_cap,
  do_mad        = s3_run_mad_minor,
  mad_mult      = s3_mad_minor_mult,
  mad_min_n     = s3_mad_minor_min_n,
  do_mad_maj    = s3_run_mad_major,
  mad_maj_mult  = s3_mad_major_mult,
  mad_maj_min_n = s3_mad_major_min_n
)

if (s3_run_cleaning) {

  windowed_ax_1 <- .filter_min_ellipses(ellipses_ax_1_raw, "las_1")
  windowed_ax_2 <- .filter_min_ellipses(ellipses_ax_2_raw, "las_2")

  clean1_result_ax_1 <- do.call(.s3_consensus_clean, c(list(windowed_ax_1), .s3_clean_args))
  clean1_result_ax_2 <- do.call(.s3_consensus_clean, c(list(windowed_ax_2), .s3_clean_args))

  clean1_summary_ax_1 <- .s3_print_clean_summary(
    clean1_result_ax_1, "las_1 axis", s3_consensus_frac_centre, s3_consensus_frac_minor,
    s3_consensus_frac_major, s3_run_mad_minor, s3_mad_minor_mult, s3_mad_minor_min_n,
    s3_run_mad_major, s3_mad_major_mult, s3_mad_major_min_n)
  clean1_summary_ax_2 <- .s3_print_clean_summary(
    clean1_result_ax_2, "las_2 axis", s3_consensus_frac_centre, s3_consensus_frac_minor,
    s3_consensus_frac_major, s3_run_mad_minor, s3_mad_minor_mult, s3_mad_minor_min_n,
    s3_run_mad_major, s3_mad_major_mult, s3_mad_major_min_n)

  ellipses_ax_1_valid1 <- lapply(clean1_result_ax_1, `[[`, "valid")
  ellipses_ax_2_valid1 <- lapply(clean1_result_ax_2, `[[`, "valid")

} else {
  cat("\nPass-1 cleaning SKIPPED (s3_run_cleaning = FALSE).\n")
  clean1_result_ax_1 <- clean1_result_ax_2 <- NULL
  ellipses_ax_1_valid1 <- ellipses_ax_1_raw
  ellipses_ax_2_valid1 <- ellipses_ax_2_raw
}

cp_s3 <- list(
  method         = "consensus_adaptive_then_mad_minor_then_mad_major",
  frac_centre    = s3_consensus_frac_centre,
  frac_minor     = s3_consensus_frac_minor,
  frac_major     = s3_consensus_frac_major,
  tol_floor      = s3_consensus_tol_floor,
  tol_cap        = s3_consensus_tol_cap,
  max_gap        = s3_consensus_max_gap,
  sort_axes      = s3_consensus_sort_axes,
  mad_minor      = s3_run_mad_minor,
  mad_minor_mult = s3_mad_minor_mult,
  mad_minor_n    = s3_mad_minor_min_n,
  mad_major      = s3_run_mad_major,
  mad_major_mult = s3_mad_major_mult,
  mad_major_n    = s3_mad_major_min_n
)
```

### Diag - MAD Select

```{r}
#| label: params-diag-s3-mad-minor-multiplier
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Diagnostic: MAD z-scores of semi-minor axis per axis-aligned slice, to choose s3_mad_minor_mult"


# ── Parameters ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
s3mad_diag_treeids_1 <- NULL                  # NULL = every tree; else c(1, 13, ...)
s3mad_diag_mult_grid <- c(1, 1.5, 2, 3, 6)    # multipliers to compare in the table

s3mad_diag_ref_lines <- c(3, 6)               # multipliers drawn on the plots
s3mad_diag_pad       <- 0.1                   # y-axis padding beyond min/max z
s3mad_diag_plot      <- TRUE                  # FALSE = sweep table only

.par_apply("params-diag-s3-mad-minor-multiplier")
```

```{r}
#| label: diag-s3-mad-minor-multiplier
#| code-summary: "Diagnostic: MAD z-scores of semi-minor axis per axis-aligned slice, to choose s3_mad_minor_mult"
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4

s3mad_diag_show      <- if (exists("s3_mad_minor_mult")) s3_mad_minor_mult else 2.0

# ── Build the per-slice score frame from the cleaning output ──────────────────
# Scores are computed on the CONSENSUS SURVIVORS only, matching where the MAD
# stage actually runs. Slices already dropped by consensus are excluded from the
# median and MAD, so the reference distribution here is the same one the filter
# sees – not the raw spread.
#
# One difference from the Stage 1 version worth expecting in the numbers: these
# slices are cut perpendicular to the stem axis, so a leaning stem no longer
# produces the elongated sections that widen its semi-minor spread. The MAD
# should be TIGHTER here than at Stage 1 for the same tree, which means a
# multiplier carried over from Stage 1 will cut harder than it did there.
.s3mad_diag_frame <- function(clean_result, label) {
  if (is.null(clean_result) || length(clean_result) == 0L) return(NULL)

  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(clean_result), function(tid) {
    df <- clean_result[[tid]]$flagged
    if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0L) return(NULL)
    df <- as.data.frame(df)

    # minor_len is written by .s3_consensus_flag_one() and respects sort_axes,
    # so this scores exactly the value the filter scores.
    b <- if ("minor_len" %in% names(df)) df$minor_len else
           pmin(df$semi_a, df$semi_b)

    elig <- !df$unfitted & !df$no_consensus & !is.na(b)
    if (sum(elig) < 2L) return(NULL)

    med  <- median(b[elig], na.rm = TRUE)
    madr <- mad(b[elig], center = med, na.rm = TRUE)   # includes 1.4826
    if (is.na(madr) || madr < 1e-12) madr <- NA_real_

    data.frame(
      epoch   = label,
      TreeID  = tid,
      slice_z = df$slice_z[elig],
      # slice_z already IS distance along the pair axis from this stem's own
      # base – build_stem_axis_transform() put that base at local zero – so
      # unlike Stage 1 there is no per-tree minimum to subtract. Subtracting one
      # would silently re-base each tree on its lowest SCORED slice and shift
      # every panel by a different amount.
      s       = df$slice_z[elig],
      minor   = b[elig],
      z       = (b[elig] - med) / madr,
      med     = med,
      madr    = madr,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}

if (!exists("clean1_result_ax_1") || is.null(clean1_result_ax_1))
  stop("clean1_result_ax_1 not found – run the s3-clean-pass1 chunk first.")

s3mad_diag_1 <- .s3mad_diag_frame(clean1_result_ax_1, "las_1")
s3mad_diag_2 <- .s3mad_diag_frame(clean1_result_ax_2, "las_2")
s3mad_diag   <- dplyr::bind_rows(s3mad_diag_1, s3mad_diag_2)

if (is.null(s3mad_diag) || nrow(s3mad_diag) == 0L)
  stop("No scoreable slices – every stem has fewer than 2 consensus survivors.")

# ── Multiplier sweep: what each choice would remove ───────────────────────────
s3sweep <- do.call(rbind, lapply(s3mad_diag_mult_grid, function(k) {
  d <- s3mad_diag[!is.na(s3mad_diag$z), ]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(split(d, d$epoch), function(dd) {
    flag <- abs(dd$z) > k
    data.frame(
      mult        = k,
      epoch       = dd$epoch[1],
      n_slices    = nrow(dd),
      n_flagged   = sum(flag),
      pct_flagged = round(100 * mean(flag), 2),
      n_trees_hit = length(unique(dd$TreeID[flag])),
      # A tree losing most of its slices to this filter is the failure mode to
      # watch: it means the stem's own spread, not a few bad fits, is driving it.
      worst_tree_pct = round(100 * max(c(0, sapply(split(dd, dd$TreeID),
                              function(t) mean(abs(t$z) > k)))), 1),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}))

cat("── MAD semi-minor multiplier sweep (Step 3.3, pass 1) ──\n")
cat("z = (b - median(b)) / MAD  [MAD includes the 1.4826 constant]\n\n")
print(s3sweep[order(s3sweep$epoch, s3sweep$mult), ], row.names = FALSE)

cat(sprintf("\nScore range: las_1 |z| max %.2f | las_2 |z| max %.2f\n",
            suppressWarnings(max(abs(s3mad_diag$z[s3mad_diag$epoch == "las_1"]), na.rm = TRUE)),
            suppressWarnings(max(abs(s3mad_diag$z[s3mad_diag$epoch == "las_2"]), na.rm = TRUE))))
cat(sprintf("Currently set: s3_mad_minor_mult = %.1f", s3mad_diag_show))
if (exists("s3_mad_major_mult"))
  cat(sprintf(" | s3_mad_major_mult = %.1f (scored on the semi-MAJOR axis, not shown here)",
              s3_mad_major_mult))
cat("\n")

# ── Per-tree dual-axis plots ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Left axis : z score. The y range is clipped to that tree's own observed range
# (+/- s3mad_diag_pad), so the shape of the series is readable
# rather than squashed by the threshold lines – which means a
# reference line above the highest score simply does not appear on
# that tree's panel.
# Right axis : semi-minor axis length, which is z rescaled by that tree's own
# median and MAD (b = med + z * MAD). The mapping is exact and
# linear, so one series carries both readings – the right axis is a
# second way of reading the same points, not a second variable.
if (s3mad_diag_plot) {

  wanted_1 <- if (is.null(s3mad_diag_treeids_1)) unique(s3mad_diag_1$TreeID) else
                as.character(s3mad_diag_treeids_1)

  mk_s3mad_plot <- function(d, epoch_label, colour) {
    if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L || all(is.na(d$z))) return(NULL)
    d   <- d[order(d$s), ]
    med <- d$med[1]; madr <- d$madr[1]
    if (is.na(madr)) return(NULL)

    d$flagged <- abs(d$z) > s3mad_diag_show

    z_lo <- min(d$z, na.rm = TRUE) - s3mad_diag_pad
    z_hi <- max(d$z, na.rm = TRUE) + s3mad_diag_pad

    ggplot(d, aes(s, z)) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = c(-1, 1) * rep(s3mad_diag_ref_lines, each = 2),
                 linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.3) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = c(-1, 1) * s3mad_diag_show,
                 linetype = "dashed", colour = "#D7263D", linewidth = 0.6) +
      geom_line(colour = colour, alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.4) +
      geom_point(aes(shape = flagged, size = flagged), colour = colour, alpha = 0.85) +
      scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 16, `TRUE` = 4), guide = "none") +
      scale_size_manual(values  = c(`FALSE` = 2.2, `TRUE` = 3.6), guide = "none") +
      scale_y_continuous(
        name     = "MAD z-score of semi-minor axis",
        sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . * madr + med, name = "Semi-minor axis b (m)")
      ) +
      # coord_cartesian clips the view without dropping rows, so the connecting
      # line still runs to an off-panel point instead of breaking. It must do
      # the clipping rather than scale_y_continuous(limits=), which would set
      # out-of-range values to NA and also recompute the secondary axis breaks
      # from the truncated data.
      coord_cartesian(ylim = c(z_lo, z_hi)) +
      labs(
        title    = sprintf("[%s] Tree %s \u2014 axis-aligned", epoch_label, d$TreeID[1]),
        subtitle = sprintf("median b %.4f m | MAD %.4f | %d of %d flagged at mult %.1f",
                           med, madr, sum(d$flagged), nrow(d), s3mad_diag_show),
        x        = "Stem length along the pair axis from the stem base (m)",
        caption  = sprintf("dashed = current mult (%.1f) | dotted = %s | y clipped to observed z \u00b1 %.1f",
                           s3mad_diag_show,
                           paste(s3mad_diag_ref_lines, collapse = ", "),
                           s3mad_diag_pad)
      ) +
      theme_bw(base_size = 11)
  }

  for (tid in wanted_1) {
    p <- mk_s3mad_plot(s3mad_diag_1[s3mad_diag_1$TreeID == tid, ], "las_1", COL_1)
    if (!is.null(p)) print(p)
  }
  for (tid in unique(s3mad_diag_2$TreeID)) {
    p <- mk_s3mad_plot(s3mad_diag_2[s3mad_diag_2$TreeID == tid, ], "las_2", COL_2)
    if (!is.null(p)) print(p)
  }
}
```




### Vis - slice x thresh inliers

```{r}
#| label: fig-s3-clean1-slice-status
#| standalone: true
#| fig: false
#| results: asis
#| column: page
#| code-summary: "Per-slice panels after the first cleaning pass; red = consensus removal, orange = MAD removal"

if (!second_run && params$make_plots) {

  if (!exists("clean1_result_ax_1") || is.null(clean1_result_ax_1))
    stop("clean1_result_ax_1 not found – run the s3-clean-pass1 chunk first.")

  # ── User input ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  vis_s3c1_treeids_1 <- NULL     # NULL = every pair carried into Step 3.3
  n_s3c1_rows        <- NULL     # NULL = every slice; k = first k from the base
  slice_match_eps    <- 1e-6

  # ── Appearance ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  s3c1_col_consensus <- "#D7263D"   # red    - dropped by neighbour consensus
  s3c1_col_mad       <- "#F07C10"   # orange - dropped by either MAD stage
  s3c1_px            <- 6

  # ── The panel, drawn in the LOCAL axis frame ───────────────────────────────
  # Stage 1's make_threshold_panel() works in world XY, which is the frame its
  # ellipses are fitted in. Stage 3's are not: at this point in the pipeline
  # center_x / center_y are perpendicular offsets from the stem axis and
  # slice_z is distance along it. Drawing world points against a local ellipse
  # would show a scatter that has nothing to do with the ring on top of it, so
  # the points are transformed with the same per-stem matrix the fit used.
  #
  # Points are selected by the slice WINDOW rather than by slice_point_ids,
  # because for a refit slice that column holds only the masked candidate set –
  # and the whole reason to look at these panels is to see what the fit did NOT
  # take. The mask ring is drawn so the two can be told apart by eye.
  .s3_mask_scale_vis <- if (exists("s3_prot_mask_scale")) s3_prot_mask_scale else 1.5

  .s3_pts_cache <- local({
    e <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
    function(las, tid, tr, key) {
      if (is.null(e[[key]])) e[[key]] <- .s3_pts_local(las, tid, tr)
      e[[key]]
    }
  })

  .s3_slice_panel <- function(row_data, pts_local, width,
                              colour_inlier  = "#82B211",
                              colour_outlier = if (exists("LOSER")) LOSER else "#B0413E",
                              colour_masked  = "#CFCFCF",
                              colour_ellipse = "gold",
                              colour_mask    = "#8A8A8A",
                              pt_size = 0.35, line_width = 0.5) {

    if (is.null(row_data) || nrow(row_data) == 0L) return(NULL)
    if (is.na(row_data$center_x[1]) || is.na(row_data$semi_a[1])) return(NULL)
    if (is.null(pts_local) || nrow(pts_local) == 0L) return(NULL)

    cx <- row_data$center_x[1]; cy <- row_data$center_y[1]
    a  <- row_data$semi_a[1];   b  <- row_data$semi_b[1]
    ang <- row_data$angle_deg[1] * pi / 180

    z_lo <- row_data$slice_z[1] - width / 2
    p <- pts_local[pts_local$Z >= z_lo & pts_local$Z < z_lo + width, , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(p) == 0L) return(NULL)

    # Same normalised radius the protrusion signal uses, so "inside the mask"
    # means the same thing in the picture and in the number.
    dx <- p$X - cx; dy <- p$Y - cy
    u  <-  dx * cos(ang) + dy * sin(ang)
    v  <- -dx * sin(ang) + dy * cos(ang)
    r  <- sqrt((u / a)^2 + (v / b)^2)

    inl <- if ("inlier_ids" %in% names(row_data) && !is.null(row_data$inlier_ids[[1]]))
             p$point_id %in% row_data$inlier_ids[[1]] else rep(FALSE, nrow(p))

    p$Status <- ifelse(r > .s3_mask_scale_vis, "Beyond mask",
                       ifelse(inl, "Inlier", "Outlier"))

    theta <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 121)
    ring <- function(s) data.frame(
      X = s * a * cos(theta) * cos(ang) - s * b * sin(theta) * sin(ang) + cx,
      Y = s * a * cos(theta) * sin(ang) + s * b * sin(theta) * cos(ang) + cy)

    ggplot(p, aes(X, Y)) +
      geom_point(aes(color = Status), size = pt_size, alpha = 0.85, show.legend = FALSE) +
      geom_path(data = ring(.s3_mask_scale_vis), aes(X, Y), colour = colour_mask,
                linetype = "dashed", linewidth = line_width * 0.8, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
      geom_path(data = ring(1), aes(X, Y), colour = colour_ellipse,
                linewidth = line_width, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
      scale_color_manual(values = c(Inlier = colour_inlier, Outlier = colour_outlier,
                                    `Beyond mask` = colour_masked)) +
      coord_equal() + theme_void() + theme(plot.margin = margin(1, 1, 1, 1))
  }

  # ── Per-slice verdict, read from the stored result ─────────────────────────
  # Not recomputed. The pass-1 flags are already on the frame, and a second
  # implementation of the same rule is a second thing to keep in step.
  .s3c1_status_frame <- function(clean_result, tid) {
    f <- clean_result[[as.character(tid)]]$flagged
    if (is.null(f) || nrow(f) == 0L) return(NULL)
    f <- as.data.frame(f)
    status <- ifelse(f$unfitted, NA_character_,
              ifelse(f$no_consensus, "consensus",
              ifelse(f$mad_minor_out | f$mad_major_out, "mad", "kept")))
    data.frame(slice_z = f$slice_z, status = status,
               row_idx = seq_len(nrow(f)), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }

  pairs_vis <- pairs_axis_ok[, c("TreeID_1", "TreeID_2")]
  pairs_vis$TreeID_1 <- as.character(pairs_vis$TreeID_1)
  pairs_vis$TreeID_2 <- as.character(pairs_vis$TreeID_2)
  pairs_vis <- pairs_vis[pairs_vis$TreeID_1 %in% names(clean1_result_ax_1) &
                         pairs_vis$TreeID_2 %in% names(clean1_result_ax_2), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!is.null(vis_s3c1_treeids_1))
    pairs_vis <- pairs_vis[pairs_vis$TreeID_1 %in% as.character(vis_s3c1_treeids_1), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(pairs_vis) == 0L) stop("No renderable pairs.")

  cat(sprintf("Rendering %d pair(s) after the first cleaning pass.\n", nrow(pairs_vis)))

  # ── One grid per pair: rows = stem length, columns = epoch ─────────────────
  make_s3c1_grid <- function(tid_1, tid_2) {

    st_1 <- .s3c1_status_frame(clean1_result_ax_1, tid_1)
    st_2 <- .s3c1_status_frame(clean1_result_ax_2, tid_2)
    if (is.null(st_1) && is.null(st_2)) return(NULL)

    # Rows are stem length directly: the local frame already measures from each
    # stem's own base, so no per-stem offset has to be subtracted the way it
    # does in Stage 1.
    sl_all <- sort(unique(round(c(if (!is.null(st_1)) st_1$slice_z,
                                  if (!is.null(st_2)) st_2$slice_z), 6)))
    keep <- c(if (!is.null(st_1)) st_1$slice_z[!is.na(st_1$status)],
              if (!is.null(st_2)) st_2$slice_z[!is.na(st_2$status)])
    if (length(keep) == 0L) return(NULL)
    sl_all <- sl_all[sl_all <= max(keep) + slice_match_eps]
    if (!is.null(n_s3c1_rows) && length(sl_all) > n_s3c1_rows)
      sl_all <- sl_all[seq_len(n_s3c1_rows)]

    cols <- list(
      list(label = "las_1", st = st_1, tid = tid_1, las = las_1_rot,
           tr = axis_tr_1[[tid_1]], cr = clean1_result_ax_1, key = paste0("1|", tid_1)),
      list(label = "las_2", st = st_2, tid = tid_2, las = las_2,
           tr = axis_tr_2[[tid_2]], cr = clean1_result_ax_2, key = paste0("2|", tid_2))
    )

    panel_matrix <- status_matrix <- vector("list", length(sl_all))

    for (r in seq_along(sl_all)) {
      cells <- stats <- vector("list", length(cols))
      for (k in seq_along(cols)) {
        cc <- cols[[k]]
        if (is.null(cc$st) || is.null(cc$tr)) { cells[[k]] <- NULL
                                                stats[[k]] <- NA_character_; next }
        hit <- which(abs(cc$st$slice_z - sl_all[r]) <= slice_match_eps)
        if (length(hit) != 1L || is.na(cc$st$status[hit])) {
          cells[[k]] <- NULL; stats[[k]] <- NA_character_; next
        }
        row_data <- as.data.frame(cc$cr[[cc$tid]]$flagged)[cc$st$row_idx[hit], , drop = FALSE]
        cells[[k]] <- .s3_slice_panel(row_data,
                                      .s3_pts_cache(cc$las, cc$tid, cc$tr, cc$key),
                                      fp_s3$width)
        stats[[k]] <- cc$st$status[hit]
      }
      panel_matrix[[r]] <- cells; status_matrix[[r]] <- stats
    }

    list(matrix = panel_matrix, status = status_matrix,
         row_labels = sprintf("s \u2248 %.3f m", sl_all),
         col_labels = vapply(cols, function(x) x$label, character(1)))
  }

  # ── Renderer ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  render_s3c1_grid <- function(grid_obj, lb_id, w = 3.2, h = 3.2, dpi = 140) {

    panel_matrix <- grid_obj$matrix; status_matrix <- grid_obj$status
    row_labels <- grid_obj$row_labels; col_labels <- grid_obj$col_labels
    n_col <- length(col_labels)

    if (!any(vapply(panel_matrix, function(rw)
          any(!vapply(rw, is.null, logical(1))), logical(1))))
      return(HTML("<p>No data.</p>"))

    encode_plot <- function(p) {
      if (is.null(p)) return(NA_character_)
      tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".png"); on.exit(unlink(tmp), add = TRUE)
      ggsave(tmp, plot = p, width = w, height = h, dpi = dpi, bg = "white")
      paste0("data:image/png;base64,", base64enc::base64encode(tmp))
    }

    border_for <- function(status)
      sprintf("border:%dpx solid %s;", s3c1_px,
              switch(as.character(status),
                     "consensus" = s3c1_col_consensus,
                     "mad"       = s3c1_col_mad,
                     "transparent"))

    img_tag <- function(src, status) {
      if (is.na(src))
        return('<div style="background:#f4f4f4;border-radius:6px;min-height:120px;"></div>')
      sprintf('<img src="%s" style="width:100%%;border-radius:4px;%s
                box-shadow:0 1px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.18);cursor:zoom-in;
                display:block;box-sizing:border-box;" onclick="openLb_%s(this.src)" />',
              src, border_for(status), lb_id)
    }

    header_row <- sprintf(
      '<div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:90px repeat(%d,1fr);gap:6px;margin-bottom:4px;"><div></div>%s</div>',
      n_col, paste(vapply(col_labels, function(lbl)
        sprintf('<div style="font-size:12px;font-weight:600;text-align:center;padding:2px;">%s</div>', lbl),
        character(1)), collapse = ""))

    swatch <- function(col, txt)
      sprintf('<span style="display:inline-block;width:14px;height:14px;border:%dpx solid %s;
               vertical-align:-3px;margin:0 5px 0 14px;box-sizing:border-box;"></span>%s',
              s3c1_px, col, txt)

    legend <- sprintf('<div style="font-size:12px;margin:0 0 8px 2px;">%s%s%s</div>',
      swatch(s3c1_col_consensus, "removed by neighbour consensus"),
      swatch(s3c1_col_mad,       "removed by a MAD filter"),
      '<span style="margin-left:14px;">no outline = kept | grey points and dashed ring = beyond the protrusion mask</span>')

    body_rows <- paste(vapply(seq_along(panel_matrix), function(r) {
      cells <- vapply(panel_matrix[[r]], encode_plot, character(1))
      stats <- status_matrix[[r]]
      imgs  <- paste(vapply(seq_along(cells),
                            function(k) img_tag(cells[k], stats[[k]]), character(1)),
                     collapse = "")
      sprintf('<div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:90px repeat(%d,1fr);gap:6px;align-items:center;margin-bottom:6px;">
                 <div style="font-size:11px;font-weight:600;">%s</div>%s</div>',
              n_col, row_labels[r], imgs)
    }, character(1)), collapse = "\n")

    HTML(sprintf('
<style>
  #lbOv_%s{display:none;position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:9999;
    background:rgba(0,0,0,.82);align-items:center;justify-content:center;}
  #lbOv_%s.open{display:flex;}
  #lbOv_%s img{max-width:95vw;max-height:95vh;border-radius:6px;
    box-shadow:0 4px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.6);}
  #lbCl_%s{position:fixed;top:16px;right:20px;font-size:32px;color:#fff;
    cursor:pointer;line-height:1;user-select:none;z-index:10000;}
</style>
<div id="lbOv_%s" onclick="if(event.target===this)closeLb_%s()">
  <span id="lbCl_%s" onclick="closeLb_%s()">&#x2715;</span>
  <img id="lbIm_%s" src=""/>
</div>
<div style="padding:10px;overflow-x:auto;">%s%s%s</div>
<script>
  window.openLb_%s  = s => {
    document.getElementById("lbIm_%s").src = s;
    document.getElementById("lbOv_%s").classList.add("open");
  };
  window.closeLb_%s = () =>
    document.getElementById("lbOv_%s").classList.remove("open");
</script>',
      lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id,
      legend, header_row, body_rows,
      lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id))
  }

  pair_blocks <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs_vis)), function(i) {
    tid_1 <- pairs_vis$TreeID_1[i]; tid_2 <- pairs_vis$TreeID_2[i]
    grid_obj <- make_s3c1_grid(tid_1, tid_2)
    if (is.null(grid_obj)) return(NULL)
    n_of <- function(v) sum(vapply(grid_obj$status, function(rw)
      sum(vapply(rw, function(s) !is.na(s) && s == v, logical(1))), integer(1)))
    tagList(
      h3(sprintf("Pair %d of %d \u2014 las_1 TreeID %s \u2194 las_2 TreeID %s",
                 i, nrow(pairs_vis), tid_1, tid_2)),
      h4(sprintf("kept %d | consensus %d | MAD %d",
                 n_of("kept"), n_of("consensus"), n_of("mad"))),
      render_s3c1_grid(grid_obj, sprintf("s3c1_%s_%s", tid_1, tid_2))
    )
  })

  browsable(tagList(
    h3("Axis-aligned slice status after the first cleaning pass"),
    h4("Rows = stem length along the pair axis from each stem's own base \u2014 columns = epoch"),
    h4("Red = neighbour consensus removal \u2014 orange = MAD removal \u2014 no outline = kept"),
    pair_blocks
  ))
}
```

## 3.5 Ellipse Refit – masked second pass

```{r}
#| label: params-s3-refit-masked
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Second-pass RANSAC on cleaning-removed slices, masked by a circle projected from the nearest kept slice"


# ── Parameters ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
s3_run_refit <- TRUE

# Which removals get a second attempt.
# "consensus" -> only slices dropped by the neighbour-consensus filter
# "consensus_mad" -> those plus slices dropped by either MAD filter
s3_refit_targets <- "consensus"

# Mask: a circle centred on the anchor ellipse's centre, radius = anchor
# semi-MAJOR axis x this factor. Points outside are invisible to the refit.
s3_refit_mask_scale <- 1.3
s3_refit_min_pts    <- 5L
s3_refit_seed       <- 42L

# NULL inherits the pass-1 setting, so the refit uses the same threshold and the
# same iteration rule - but on the MASKED point count, which is smaller, so a
# refit slice gets a smaller budget than its first pass did.
s3_refit_distance_threshold <- NULL
s3_refit_iter_per_point     <- NULL
s3_refit_iter_max           <- NULL
s3_refit_iter_min           <- NULL
s3_refit_early_exit         <- FALSE

.par_apply("params-s3-refit-masked")
```

```{r}
#| label: s3-refit-masked
#| code-summary: "Second-pass RANSAC on cleaning-removed slices, masked by a circle projected from the nearest kept slice"

# ── Refit one stem ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Targets are processed from the BOTTOM UP. Each one looks for the nearest
# available slice BELOW it; only if none exists does it look above. "Available"
# means kept by pass-1 cleaning OR successfully refit earlier in this same loop,
# so a refit cascades upward through a run of consecutive failures.
#
# The projection is straight up the LOCAL Z axis, and here that is exact rather
# than approximate: the local Z axis IS the stem axis, so carrying the anchor's
# centre up to the focal slice introduces no lean error at all. Stage 1 has to
# absorb that error in the mask factor because it has no axis yet; Stage 3 does
# not, which is one of the things fitting in this frame buys.
.s3_refit_one_stem <- function(pts_local, tid, flagged, width,
                               mask_scale, min_pts, seed,
                               dist_thr, n_iter, early_exit, include_mad,
                               track_hist, iter_pp, iter_mx, iter_mn) {

  df <- as.data.frame(flagged); n <- nrow(df)
  df$refit          <- rep(FALSE, n)
  df$refit_status   <- rep(NA_character_, n)   # ok | no_anchor | too_few_pts | fit_failed
  df$refit_anchor_z <- rep(NA_real_, n)
  df$refit_mask_r   <- rep(NA_real_, n)
  df$refit_n_masked <- rep(NA_integer_, n)
  if (n == 0L || is.null(pts_local)) return(df)

  available <- !df$spike & !is.na(df$center_x)

  target <- df$no_consensus & !df$unfitted
  if (include_mad && "mad_minor_out" %in% names(df))
    target <- target | (df$mad_minor_out & !df$unfitted)
  if (include_mad && "mad_major_out" %in% names(df))
    target <- target | (df$mad_major_out & !df$unfitted)
  if (!any(target)) return(df)

  for (t in order(df$slice_z)[order(df$slice_z) %in% which(target)]) {

    z_t <- df$slice_z[t]

    avail_idx <- which(available)
    if (length(avail_idx) == 0L) { df$refit_status[t] <- "no_anchor"; next }

    below <- avail_idx[df$slice_z[avail_idx] <  z_t]
    above <- avail_idx[df$slice_z[avail_idx] >  z_t]
    anchor <- if (length(below) > 0L) below[which.max(df$slice_z[below])] else
              if (length(above) > 0L) above[which.min(df$slice_z[above])] else NA_integer_
    if (is.na(anchor)) { df$refit_status[t] <- "no_anchor"; next }

    cx_m <- df$center_x[anchor]
    cy_m <- df$center_y[anchor]
    r_m  <- df$semi_a[anchor] * mask_scale
    df$refit_anchor_z[t] <- df$slice_z[anchor]
    df$refit_mask_r[t]   <- r_m

    # ransac_ellipse_fit_one() takes Z in [zi, zi + width) and records
    # slice_z = zi + width/2, so the window is recovered as below.
    z_lo  <- z_t - width / 2
    pts_i <- pts_local[pts_local$Z >= z_lo & pts_local$Z < z_lo + width, , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(pts_i) == 0L) { df$refit_status[t] <- "too_few_pts"
                             df$refit_n_masked[t] <- 0L; next }

    inside <- (pts_i$X - cx_m)^2 + (pts_i$Y - cy_m)^2 <= r_m^2
    pts_m  <- pts_i[inside, , drop = FALSE]
    df$refit_n_masked[t] <- nrow(pts_m)
    if (nrow(pts_m) < min_pts) { df$refit_status[t] <- "too_few_pts"; next }

    set.seed(as.integer(seed) + as.integer(tid) * 1000L + t)

    rr <- tryCatch(
      custom_ransac_ellipse_fit(
        pts_m[, c("X", "Y")],
        n_iterations       = n_iter,
        iter_per_point     = iter_pp,
        iter_max           = iter_mx,
        iter_min           = iter_mn,
        distance_threshold = dist_thr,
        early_exit         = early_exit,
        track_history      = track_hist),
      error = function(e) list(ellipse = rep(NA_real_, 5), inliers = integer(0),
                               inlier_history = integer(0), segs_history = integer(0),
                               n_points = nrow(pts_m)))

    ell <- rr$ellipse
    if (length(ell) < 5L || is.na(ell[3])) { df$refit_status[t] <- "fit_failed"; next }

    df$center_x[t]  <- ell[1]; df$center_y[t] <- ell[2]
    df$semi_a[t]    <- ell[3]; df$semi_b[t]   <- ell[4]
    df$angle_deg[t] <- ell[5]

    if ("inlier_ids" %in% names(df))
      df$inlier_ids[[t]] <- if (length(rr$inliers) > 0L)
        pts_m$point_id[rr$inliers] else integer(0)
    # NOTE: slice_point_ids now holds the MASKED candidate set for this slice,
    # not the full slice - the same caveat Stage 1 carries.
    if ("slice_point_ids" %in% names(df)) df$slice_point_ids[[t]] <- pts_m$point_id
    if ("n_cand_pts" %in% names(df))      df$n_cand_pts[t]        <- nrow(pts_m)
    if ("inlier_history" %in% names(df))
      df$inlier_history[[t]] <- if (is.null(rr$inlier_history)) integer(0) else rr$inlier_history
    if ("segs_history" %in% names(df))
      df$segs_history[[t]]   <- if (is.null(rr$segs_history)) integer(0) else rr$segs_history

    df$refit[t] <- TRUE; df$refit_status[t] <- "ok"
    available[t] <- TRUE       # this slice can now anchor the one above
  }
  df
}

# ── Run ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if (s3_run_refit && s3_run_cleaning) {

  .s3_rf_dist <- if (is.null(s3_refit_distance_threshold)) fp_s3$distance_threshold else s3_refit_distance_threshold
  .s3_rf_pp   <- if (is.null(s3_refit_iter_per_point))     fp_s3$iter_per_point     else s3_refit_iter_per_point
  .s3_rf_mx   <- if (is.null(s3_refit_iter_max))           fp_s3$iter_max           else s3_refit_iter_max
  .s3_rf_mn   <- if (is.null(s3_refit_iter_min))           fp_s3$iter_min           else s3_refit_iter_min
  .s3_incl_mad <- identical(s3_refit_targets, "consensus_mad")

  cat(sprintf("Masked refit: targets = %s | mask = %.2f x anchor semi-major | threshold = %.4f m | %.1f iterations/point, clamped to [%d, %d]\n",
              s3_refit_targets, s3_refit_mask_scale, .s3_rf_dist, .s3_rf_pp, .s3_rf_mn, .s3_rf_mx))

  .s3_refit_epoch <- function(clean_result, las, tr_list, label) {
    if (is.null(clean_result) || length(clean_result) == 0L) return(NULL)
    pb <- .pb_new(length(clean_result), label)
    on.exit(.pb_done(pb), add = TRUE)

    out <- lapply(names(clean_result), function(tid) {
      .pb_tick(pb)
      tr <- tr_list[[tid]]
      if (is.null(tr)) return(clean_result[[tid]]$flagged)
      .s3_refit_one_stem(
        .s3_pts_local(las, tid, tr), tid, clean_result[[tid]]$flagged,
        width      = fp_s3$width,
        mask_scale = s3_refit_mask_scale,
        min_pts    = s3_refit_min_pts,
        seed       = s3_refit_seed,
        dist_thr   = .s3_rf_dist,
        n_iter     = fp_s3$n_iterations,
        early_exit = s3_refit_early_exit,
        include_mad = .s3_incl_mad,
        track_hist = isTRUE(fp_s3$track_history),
        iter_pp = .s3_rf_pp, iter_mx = .s3_rf_mx, iter_mn = .s3_rf_mn)
    })
    setNames(out, names(clean_result))
  }

  refit_flagged_ax_1 <- .s3_refit_epoch(clean1_result_ax_1, las_1_rot, axis_tr_1, "las_1 refit")
```
