```{r}
  refit_flagged_ax_2 <- .s3_refit_epoch(clean1_result_ax_2, las_2,     axis_tr_2, "las_2 refit")

  .s3_refit_summary <- function(refit_flagged, label) {
    if (is.null(refit_flagged)) { cat(sprintf("[%s] nothing to refit.\n", label)); return(invisible(NULL)) }
    tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(refit_flagged), function(tid) {
      d  <- refit_flagged[[tid]]
      st <- if ("refit_status" %in% names(d)) d$refit_status[!is.na(d$refit_status)] else character(0)
      data.frame(TreeID = tid, attempted = length(st),
                 ok = sum(st == "ok"), no_anchor = sum(st == "no_anchor"),
                 few_pts = sum(st == "too_few_pts"), fit_failed = sum(st == "fit_failed"),
                 med_masked = suppressWarnings(median(d$refit_n_masked, na.rm = TRUE)),
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }))
    tab <- tab[tab$attempted > 0L, , drop = FALSE]
    cat(sprintf("\n[%s] Masked refit results\n", label))
    if (nrow(tab) == 0L) { cat("  (no target slices)\n"); return(invisible(NULL)) }
    print(tab, row.names = FALSE)
    cat(sprintf("  TOTAL: %d attempted -> %d refit (%.1f%%) | %d no anchor, %d too few points, %d fit failed\n",
                sum(tab$attempted), sum(tab$ok),
                100 * sum(tab$ok) / max(1L, sum(tab$attempted)),
                sum(tab$no_anchor), sum(tab$few_pts), sum(tab$fit_failed)))
    invisible(tab)
  }

  refit_summary_ax_1 <- .s3_refit_summary(refit_flagged_ax_1, "las_1 axis")
  refit_summary_ax_2 <- .s3_refit_summary(refit_flagged_ax_2, "las_2 axis")

} else {
  cat("\nMasked refit SKIPPED.\n")
  refit_flagged_ax_1 <- refit_flagged_ax_2 <- NULL
}
```

## 3.6 Ellipse Reclean – pass 2

```{r}
#| label: params-s3-clean-pass2
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Second consensus + MAD pass over the refit slice set"


# NULL = inherit the pass-1 value, so this pass is identical unless deliberately
# changed. The refit slices were fitted against a masked point set anchored on
# their neighbour, so they are biased TOWARD agreeing with it - running the same
# tolerances here is the conservative choice, not a lenient one.
s3_consensus2_frac_centre <- NULL
s3_consensus2_frac_minor  <- NULL
s3_consensus2_frac_major  <- NULL
s3_consensus2_tol_floor   <- NULL
s3_consensus2_tol_cap     <- NULL
s3_consensus2_max_gap     <- NULL
s3_consensus2_sort_axes   <- NULL

s3_mad2_minor_mult  <- NULL
s3_mad2_minor_min_n <- NULL
s3_run_mad2_minor   <- NULL

s3_mad2_major_mult  <- NULL
s3_mad2_major_min_n <- NULL
s3_run_mad2_major   <- NULL

s3_run_cleaning_2 <- TRUE

.par_apply("params-s3-clean-pass2")
```

```{r}
#| label: s3-clean-pass2
#| code-summary: "Second consensus + MAD pass over the refit slice set"

.c2s3 <- function(x, fallback) if (is.null(x)) fallback else x
.c2s3_frac_centre <- .c2s3(s3_consensus2_frac_centre, s3_consensus_frac_centre)
.c2s3_frac_minor  <- .c2s3(s3_consensus2_frac_minor,  s3_consensus_frac_minor)
.c2s3_frac_major  <- .c2s3(s3_consensus2_frac_major,  s3_consensus_frac_major)
.c2s3_tol_floor   <- if (is.null(s3_consensus2_tol_floor)) s3_consensus_tol_floor else s3_consensus2_tol_floor
.c2s3_tol_cap     <- if (is.null(s3_consensus2_tol_cap))   s3_consensus_tol_cap   else s3_consensus2_tol_cap
.c2s3_max_gap     <- if (is.null(s3_consensus2_max_gap))   s3_consensus_max_gap   else s3_consensus2_max_gap
.c2s3_sort_axes   <- .c2s3(s3_consensus2_sort_axes, s3_consensus_sort_axes)
.c2s3_madB_on     <- .c2s3(s3_run_mad2_minor,   s3_run_mad_minor)
.c2s3_madB_mult   <- .c2s3(s3_mad2_minor_mult,  s3_mad_minor_mult)
.c2s3_madB_n      <- .c2s3(s3_mad2_minor_min_n, s3_mad_minor_min_n)
.c2s3_madA_on     <- .c2s3(s3_run_mad2_major,   s3_run_mad_major)
.c2s3_madA_mult   <- .c2s3(s3_mad2_major_mult,  s3_mad_major_mult)
.c2s3_madA_n      <- .c2s3(s3_mad2_major_min_n, s3_mad_major_min_n)

# Candidates are the slices standing after the refit: kept by pass 1, or
# successfully refit. Pass-1 verdict columns are stripped first - for a refit
# slice they describe the ellipse that was REPLACED, and .s3_consensus_flag_one()
# only recomputes minor_len / major_len / ell_ecc when they are absent.
.s3_strip_pass1 <- function(d) {
  drop <- c("minor_len", "major_len", "ell_ecc", "n_agreeing",
            "tol_centre", "tol_minor", "tol_major", "no_consensus", "unfitted",
            "mad_minor_z", "mad_minor_out", "mad_major_z", "mad_major_out",
            "spike_cx", "spike_cy", "spike_xy", "spike_a", "spike_b",
            "spike_radii", "spike", "isolated")
  d[, setdiff(names(d), drop), drop = FALSE]
}

.s3_refit_candidates <- function(refit_flagged) {
  if (is.null(refit_flagged)) return(NULL)
  lapply(refit_flagged, function(d) {
    if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L) return(d)
    keep <- (!d$spike) | (d$refit & !is.na(d$refit_status) & d$refit_status == "ok")
    .s3_strip_pass1(d[keep, , drop = FALSE])
  })
}

# A stem whose every slice failed pass 1 and could not be refit arrives here
# with zero rows. The MAD helpers assign whole columns by value, which R rejects
# on a zero-row frame, so those stems are held back and reinstated afterwards -
# keeping their TreeID present downstream rather than silently vanishing.
.s3_empty_clean_entry <- function(d) {
  list(flagged = d, valid = d, ellipses_before = 0L, ellipses_after = 0L,
       n_removed_unfitted = 0L, n_removed_orphan = 0L, n_removed_mad = 0L,
       n_removed_mad_maj = 0L, med_tol_centre = NA_real_, prop_kept = NA_real_)
}

.s3_clean2_with_empties <- function(cand, args, label) {
  if (is.null(cand) || length(cand) == 0L) return(NULL)
  n_rows  <- vapply(cand, function(d) if (is.null(d)) 0L else nrow(d), integer(1))
  empties <- names(cand)[n_rows == 0L]
  if (length(empties) > 0L)
    cat(sprintf("[%s] %d stem(s) enter pass 2 with no surviving slices: %s\n",
                label, length(empties), paste(empties, collapse = ", ")))
  res <- if (any(n_rows > 0L))
           do.call(.s3_consensus_clean, c(list(cand[n_rows > 0L]), args)) else list()
  for (tid in empties) res[[tid]] <- .s3_empty_clean_entry(cand[[tid]])
  res[names(cand)]
}

if (s3_run_cleaning_2 && !is.null(refit_flagged_ax_1)) {

  .s3_clean2_args <- list(
    frac_c = .c2s3_frac_centre, frac_maj = .c2s3_frac_major, frac_min = .c2s3_frac_minor,
    max_gap = .c2s3_max_gap, sort_axes = .c2s3_sort_axes,
    tol_floor = .c2s3_tol_floor, tol_cap = .c2s3_tol_cap,
    do_mad = .c2s3_madB_on, mad_mult = .c2s3_madB_mult, mad_min_n = .c2s3_madB_n,
    do_mad_maj = .c2s3_madA_on, mad_maj_mult = .c2s3_madA_mult, mad_maj_min_n = .c2s3_madA_n)

  cand_ax_1 <- .s3_refit_candidates(refit_flagged_ax_1)
  cand_ax_2 <- .s3_refit_candidates(refit_flagged_ax_2)

  clean_result_ax_1 <- .s3_clean2_with_empties(cand_ax_1, .s3_clean2_args, "las_1 axis")
  clean_result_ax_2 <- .s3_clean2_with_empties(cand_ax_2, .s3_clean2_args, "las_2 axis")

  # Split by provenance: how many refit slices survive is the number that says
  # whether the second pass is earning its place.
  .s3_print_clean2 <- function(clean_result, label) {
    cat(sprintf("\n[%s] Post-refit cleaning\n", label))
    if (is.null(clean_result) || length(clean_result) == 0L) { cat("  (no trees)\n"); return(invisible(NULL)) }
    tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(clean_result), function(tid) {
      r <- clean_result[[tid]]; f <- r$flagged
      if (is.null(f) || nrow(f) == 0L)
        return(data.frame(TreeID = tid, in_slices = 0L, of_which_new = 0L, orphan = 0L,
                          madB = 0L, madA = 0L, kept = 0L, new_kept = 0L,
                          new_pct = NA_real_, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
      is_refit <- if ("refit" %in% names(f)) f$refit else rep(FALSE, nrow(f))
      dropped  <- f$no_consensus | f$mad_minor_out | f$mad_major_out
      data.frame(TreeID = tid, in_slices = r$ellipses_before,
                 of_which_new = sum(is_refit), orphan = r$n_removed_orphan,
                 madB = r$n_removed_mad, madA = r$n_removed_mad_maj,
                 kept = r$ellipses_after, new_kept = sum(is_refit & !dropped),
                 new_pct = if (sum(is_refit) > 0L)
                             round(100 * sum(is_refit & !dropped) / sum(is_refit), 1)
                           else NA_real_,
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }))
    print(tab, row.names = FALSE)
    cat(sprintf("  TOTAL: %d in -> %d kept (%.1f%%) | %d orphaned, %d MAD semi-minor, %d MAD semi-major\n",
                sum(tab$in_slices), sum(tab$kept),
                100 * sum(tab$kept) / max(1L, sum(tab$in_slices)),
                sum(tab$orphan), sum(tab$madB), sum(tab$madA)))
    cat(sprintf("  Refit slices: %d entered -> %d survived (%.1f%%) | stems left with no slices: %d\n",
                sum(tab$of_which_new), sum(tab$new_kept),
                100 * sum(tab$new_kept) / max(1L, sum(tab$of_which_new)),
                sum(tab$kept == 0L)))
    invisible(tab)
  }

  clean2_summary_ax_1 <- .s3_print_clean2(clean_result_ax_1, "las_1 axis")
  clean2_summary_ax_2 <- .s3_print_clean2(clean_result_ax_2, "las_2 axis")

} else {
  cat("\nPost-refit cleaning SKIPPED - the pass-1 result is used as-is.\n")
  clean_result_ax_1 <- clean1_result_ax_1
  clean_result_ax_2 <- clean1_result_ax_2
}

cp2_s3 <- list(
  method         = "post_refit_consensus_adaptive_then_mad_minor_then_mad_major",
  frac_centre    = .c2s3_frac_centre, frac_minor = .c2s3_frac_minor,
  frac_major     = .c2s3_frac_major,  tol_floor  = .c2s3_tol_floor,
  tol_cap        = .c2s3_tol_cap,     max_gap    = .c2s3_max_gap,
  sort_axes      = .c2s3_sort_axes,
  mad_minor      = .c2s3_madB_on, mad_minor_mult = .c2s3_madB_mult, mad_minor_n = .c2s3_madB_n,
  mad_major      = .c2s3_madA_on, mad_major_mult = .c2s3_madA_mult, mad_major_n = .c2s3_madA_n
)
```

### Vis - slice x thresh inliers Reclean

```{r}
#| label: fig-s3-clean2-slice-status
#| standalone: true
#| fig: false
#| results: asis
#| column: page
#| code-summary: "Per-slice panels after refit and second cleaning; tinted background = refit, borders = removal stage"

if (!second_run && params$make_plots) {

  if (!exists("refit_flagged_ax_1") || is.null(refit_flagged_ax_1))
    stop("refit_flagged_ax_1 not found – run the s3-refit-masked chunk first.")
  if (!exists("clean_result_ax_1") || is.null(clean_result_ax_1))
    stop("clean_result_ax_1 not found – run the s3-clean-pass2 chunk first.")
  if (!exists(".s3_slice_panel"))
    stop(".s3_slice_panel not found – run the fig-s3-clean1-slice-status chunk first; it defines the panel builder both figures share.")

  # ── User input ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  vis_s3c2_treeids_1 <- NULL
  n_s3c2_rows        <- NULL
  slice_match_eps    <- 1e-6

  # ── Appearance ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Background carries PROVENANCE (was this slice refit?), border carries
  # VERDICT (what removed it, if anything). The two are independent: a refit
  # slice that then failed second-pass consensus shows both.
  s3c2_bg_refit       <- "#ECCCCC"   # tint  - slice was refit
  s3c2_bg_plain       <- "white"
  s3c2_col_consensus2 <- "#D7263D"   # red    - removed by 2nd-pass consensus
  s3c2_col_mad2       <- "#F07C10"   # orange - removed by 2nd-pass MAD
  s3c2_col_mad1       <- "purple"    #        - removed by 1st-pass MAD
  s3c2_col_unrefit    <- "blue"      #        - 1st-pass consensus, refit failed
  s3c2_px             <- 6
  s3c2_px_mad1        <- 10

  # ── Per-slice status, read from the stored results ─────────────────────────
  # Priority order matters: a slice removed at pass 1 never reached pass 2, so
  # its verdict stands regardless of what the pass-2 frame does or does not
  # contain.
  #   mad1       - dropped by a first-pass MAD stage (never a refit target
  #                unless s3_refit_targets includes them)
  #   unrefit    - dropped by first-pass consensus, refit did not succeed
  #   consensus2 - entered pass 2, dropped by consensus
  #   mad2       - entered pass 2, dropped by MAD
  #   kept       - survived everything
  .s3c2_status_frame <- function(refit_flagged, clean2_result, tid) {
    base <- refit_flagged[[as.character(tid)]]
    if (is.null(base) || nrow(base) == 0L) return(NULL)
    base <- as.data.frame(base)

    c2 <- clean2_result[[as.character(tid)]]$flagged
    c2 <- if (is.null(c2) || nrow(c2) == 0L) NULL else as.data.frame(c2)

    n <- nrow(base); status <- rep(NA_character_, n)

    for (i in seq_len(n)) {
      if (isTRUE(base$unfitted[i])) next
      if (isTRUE(base$mad_minor_out[i]) ||
          isTRUE(base$mad_major_out[i])) { status[i] <- "mad1"; next }

      hit <- if (is.null(c2)) integer(0) else
               which(abs(c2$slice_z - base$slice_z[i]) <= slice_match_eps)
      if (length(hit) != 1L) { status[i] <- "unrefit"; next }

      status[i] <-
        if (isTRUE(c2$no_consensus[hit])) "consensus2" else
        if (isTRUE(c2$mad_minor_out[hit]) ||
            isTRUE(c2$mad_major_out[hit])) "mad2" else "kept"
    }

    data.frame(slice_z = base$slice_z, status = status,
               refit = if ("refit" %in% names(base)) base$refit else rep(FALSE, n),
               row_idx = seq_len(n), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }

  # Geometry comes from the pass-2 frame when the slice reached it – that is
  # the frame the second cleaning judged. Both carry post-refit geometry, so
  # they agree; the fallback matters only for mad1 and unrefit slices, which
  # pass 2 never saw.
  .s3c2_row <- function(refit_flagged, clean2_result, tid, row_idx, slice_z) {
    c2 <- clean2_result[[as.character(tid)]]$flagged
    if (!is.null(c2) && nrow(c2) > 0L) {
      c2  <- as.data.frame(c2)
      hit <- which(abs(c2$slice_z - slice_z) <= slice_match_eps)
      if (length(hit) == 1L) return(c2[hit, , drop = FALSE])
    }
    as.data.frame(refit_flagged[[as.character(tid)]])[row_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  }

  pairs_vis <- pairs_axis_ok[, c("TreeID_1", "TreeID_2")]
  pairs_vis$TreeID_1 <- as.character(pairs_vis$TreeID_1)
  pairs_vis$TreeID_2 <- as.character(pairs_vis$TreeID_2)
  pairs_vis <- pairs_vis[pairs_vis$TreeID_1 %in% names(refit_flagged_ax_1) &
                         pairs_vis$TreeID_2 %in% names(refit_flagged_ax_2), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!is.null(vis_s3c2_treeids_1))
    pairs_vis <- pairs_vis[pairs_vis$TreeID_1 %in% as.character(vis_s3c2_treeids_1), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(pairs_vis) == 0L) stop("No renderable pairs.")

  cat(sprintf("Rendering %d pair(s) after refit + second cleaning.\n", nrow(pairs_vis)))

  make_s3c2_grid <- function(tid_1, tid_2) {

    st_1 <- .s3c2_status_frame(refit_flagged_ax_1, clean_result_ax_1, tid_1)
    st_2 <- .s3c2_status_frame(refit_flagged_ax_2, clean_result_ax_2, tid_2)
    if (is.null(st_1) && is.null(st_2)) return(NULL)

    sl_all <- sort(unique(round(c(if (!is.null(st_1)) st_1$slice_z,
                                  if (!is.null(st_2)) st_2$slice_z), 6)))
    keep <- c(if (!is.null(st_1)) st_1$slice_z[!is.na(st_1$status)],
              if (!is.null(st_2)) st_2$slice_z[!is.na(st_2$status)])
    if (length(keep) == 0L) return(NULL)
    sl_all <- sl_all[sl_all <= max(keep) + slice_match_eps]
    if (!is.null(n_s3c2_rows) && length(sl_all) > n_s3c2_rows)
      sl_all <- sl_all[seq_len(n_s3c2_rows)]

    cols <- list(
      list(label = "las_1", st = st_1, tid = tid_1, las = las_1_rot,
           tr = axis_tr_1[[tid_1]], rf = refit_flagged_ax_1, c2 = clean_result_ax_1,
           key = paste0("1|", tid_1)),
      list(label = "las_2", st = st_2, tid = tid_2, las = las_2,
           tr = axis_tr_2[[tid_2]], rf = refit_flagged_ax_2, c2 = clean_result_ax_2,
           key = paste0("2|", tid_2))
    )

    panel_matrix <- status_matrix <- refit_matrix <- vector("list", length(sl_all))

    for (r in seq_along(sl_all)) {
      cells <- stats <- rfs <- vector("list", length(cols))
      for (k in seq_along(cols)) {
        cc <- cols[[k]]
        if (is.null(cc$st) || is.null(cc$tr)) {
          cells[[k]] <- NULL; stats[[k]] <- NA_character_; rfs[[k]] <- FALSE; next
        }
        hit <- which(abs(cc$st$slice_z - sl_all[r]) <= slice_match_eps)
        if (length(hit) != 1L || is.na(cc$st$status[hit])) {
          cells[[k]] <- NULL; stats[[k]] <- NA_character_; rfs[[k]] <- FALSE; next
        }
        row_data <- .s3c2_row(cc$rf, cc$c2, cc$tid,
                              cc$st$row_idx[hit], cc$st$slice_z[hit])
        cells[[k]] <- .s3_slice_panel(row_data,
                                      .s3_pts_cache(cc$las, cc$tid, cc$tr, cc$key),
                                      fp_s3$width)
        stats[[k]] <- cc$st$status[hit]
        rfs[[k]]   <- isTRUE(cc$st$refit[hit])
      }
      panel_matrix[[r]] <- cells; status_matrix[[r]] <- stats; refit_matrix[[r]] <- rfs
    }

    list(matrix = panel_matrix, status = status_matrix, refit = refit_matrix,
         row_labels = sprintf("s \u2248 %.3f m", sl_all),
         col_labels = vapply(cols, function(x) x$label, character(1)))
  }

  # ── Renderer ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # The tint sits on the wrapping div, not the image, so it shows around a
  # panel whose own plot area is transparent.
  render_s3c2_grid <- function(grid_obj, lb_id, w = 3.2, h = 3.2, dpi = 140) {

    panel_matrix <- grid_obj$matrix; status_matrix <- grid_obj$status
    refit_matrix <- grid_obj$refit
    row_labels <- grid_obj$row_labels; col_labels <- grid_obj$col_labels
    n_col <- length(col_labels)

    if (!any(vapply(panel_matrix, function(rw)
          any(!vapply(rw, is.null, logical(1))), logical(1))))
      return(HTML("<p>No data.</p>"))

    encode_plot <- function(p) {
      if (is.null(p)) return(NA_character_)
      tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".png"); on.exit(unlink(tmp), add = TRUE)
      ggsave(tmp, plot = p, width = w, height = h, dpi = dpi, bg = NA)
      paste0("data:image/png;base64,", base64enc::base64encode(tmp))
    }

    border_spec <- function(status)
      switch(as.character(status),
             "consensus2" = c(s3c2_col_consensus2, s3c2_px),
             "mad2"       = c(s3c2_col_mad2,       s3c2_px),
             "mad1"       = c(s3c2_col_mad1,       s3c2_px_mad1),
             "unrefit"    = c(s3c2_col_unrefit,    s3c2_px),
             c("transparent", s3c2_px_mad1))   # kept: reserve the widest gutter

    cell_tag <- function(src, status, is_refit) {
      if (is.na(src))
        return('<div style="background:#f4f4f4;border-radius:6px;min-height:120px;"></div>')
      bs <- border_spec(status)
      bg <- if (isTRUE(is_refit)) s3c2_bg_refit else s3c2_bg_plain
      sprintf('<div style="background:%s;border:%spx solid %s;border-radius:6px;
                 box-sizing:border-box;padding:2px;">
                 <img src="%s" style="width:100%%;display:block;border-radius:4px;
                      cursor:zoom-in;" onclick="openLb_%s(this.src)" /></div>',
              bg, bs[2], bs[1], src, lb_id)
    }

    header_row <- sprintf(
      '<div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:90px repeat(%d,1fr);gap:6px;margin-bottom:4px;"><div></div>%s</div>',
      n_col, paste(vapply(col_labels, function(lbl)
        sprintf('<div style="font-size:12px;font-weight:600;text-align:center;padding:2px;">%s</div>', lbl),
        character(1)), collapse = ""))

    swatch <- function(col, px, txt, bg = "white")
      sprintf('<span style="display:inline-block;width:16px;height:16px;background:%s;
               border:%dpx solid %s;vertical-align:-3px;margin:0 5px 0 14px;
               box-sizing:border-box;"></span>%s', bg, px, col, txt)

    legend <- sprintf(
      '<div style="font-size:12px;margin:0 0 10px 2px;line-height:1.9;">%s%s%s%s%s</div>',
      swatch("#cccccc", 1, "refit slice (tinted background)", s3c2_bg_refit),
      swatch(s3c2_col_consensus2, s3c2_px,      "2nd-pass consensus removal"),
      swatch(s3c2_col_mad2,       s3c2_px,      "2nd-pass MAD removal"),
      swatch(s3c2_col_mad1,       s3c2_px_mad1, "1st-pass MAD removal"),
      swatch(s3c2_col_unrefit,    s3c2_px,      "consensus removal, refit failed"))

    body_rows <- paste(vapply(seq_along(panel_matrix), function(r) {
      cells <- vapply(panel_matrix[[r]], encode_plot, character(1))
      stats <- status_matrix[[r]]; rfs <- refit_matrix[[r]]
      imgs  <- paste(vapply(seq_along(cells),
                            function(k) cell_tag(cells[k], stats[[k]], rfs[[k]]),
                            character(1)), collapse = "")
      sprintf('<div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:90px repeat(%d,1fr);gap:6px;align-items:center;margin-bottom:6px;">
                 <div style="font-size:11px;font-weight:600;">%s</div>%s</div>',
              n_col, row_labels[r], imgs)
    }, character(1)), collapse = "\n")

    HTML(sprintf('
<style>
  #lbOv_%s{display:none;position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:9999;
    background:rgba(0,0,0,.82);align-items:center;justify-content:center;}
  #lbOv_%s.open{display:flex;}
  #lbOv_%s img{max-width:95vw;max-height:95vh;border-radius:6px;background:#fff;
    box-shadow:0 4px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.6);}
  #lbCl_%s{position:fixed;top:16px;right:20px;font-size:32px;color:#fff;
    cursor:pointer;line-height:1;user-select:none;z-index:10000;}
</style>
<div id="lbOv_%s" onclick="if(event.target===this)closeLb_%s()">
  <span id="lbCl_%s" onclick="closeLb_%s()">&#x2715;</span>
  <img id="lbIm_%s" src=""/>
</div>
<div style="padding:10px;overflow-x:auto;">%s%s%s</div>
<script>
  window.openLb_%s  = s => {
    document.getElementById("lbIm_%s").src = s;
    document.getElementById("lbOv_%s").classList.add("open");
  };
  window.closeLb_%s = () =>
    document.getElementById("lbOv_%s").classList.remove("open");
</script>',
      lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id,
      legend, header_row, body_rows,
      lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id))
  }

  pair_blocks <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs_vis)), function(i) {
    tid_1 <- pairs_vis$TreeID_1[i]; tid_2 <- pairs_vis$TreeID_2[i]
    grid_obj <- make_s3c2_grid(tid_1, tid_2)
    if (is.null(grid_obj)) return(NULL)
    n_of <- function(v) sum(vapply(grid_obj$status, function(rw)
      sum(vapply(rw, function(s) !is.na(s) && s == v, logical(1))), integer(1)))
    n_refit <- sum(vapply(grid_obj$refit, function(rw)
      sum(vapply(rw, isTRUE, logical(1))), integer(1)))
    tagList(
      h3(sprintf("Pair %d of %d \u2014 las_1 TreeID %s \u2194 las_2 TreeID %s",
                 i, nrow(pairs_vis), tid_1, tid_2)),
      h4(sprintf("%d refit | kept %d | consensus2 %d | mad2 %d | mad1 %d | unrefit %d",
                 n_refit, n_of("kept"), n_of("consensus2"),
                 n_of("mad2"), n_of("mad1"), n_of("unrefit"))),
      render_s3c2_grid(grid_obj, sprintf("s3c2_%s_%s", tid_1, tid_2))
    )
  })

  browsable(tagList(
    h3("Axis-aligned slice status after refit and second cleaning"),
    h4("Rows = stem length along the pair axis from each stem's own base \u2014 columns = epoch"),
    h4("Tinted background = refit | red = 2nd-pass consensus | orange = 2nd-pass MAD | purple = 1st-pass MAD | blue = refit failed"),
    pair_blocks
  ))
}
```

## 3.7 Ellipse Stack Trimming

Cleaning judges each slice against its neighbours, which is the right question
in the body of a stem and the wrong one at its ends. Near the base and up in the
crown the surviving ellipses thin out into a scatter: long runs of nothing,
broken by the occasional slice that happened to find enough points to agree with
something. Those stragglers pass every filter so far – a slice is not removed
for being lonely – but a handful of ellipses separated from the stem by a metre
of gap describe nothing continuous, and a curve fitted through them is fitting
noise at the exact place where it has least support.

This step cuts them off. It finds the long gaps, and where one side of a gap
holds only a few kept ellipses, that whole side goes.

```{r}
#| label: params-s3-trim-ends
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Cut noisy leading and trailing ends off each cleaned ellipse stack"

# ── Parameters ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
s3_run_trim <- TRUE

# A gap is a run of consecutive slices carrying no kept ellipse. It does not
# matter WHY each slice is empty - never fitted, dropped by pass-1 consensus, by
# either MAD stage, or refit and dropped again - only that nothing survived
# there. What is being detected is a break in continuity, and a break is a break
# whatever produced it.
s3_trim_run_min <- 5L      # consecutive empty slices that make a gap

# A side of a gap is cut when it holds this many kept ellipses OR FEWER. The
# comparison is on the count of survivors, not on the span they cover: five
# ellipses scattered over three metres are less evidence of a stem than five
# packed into 25 cm, and neither is enough to anchor a curve.
s3_trim_side_max <- 10L

s3_trim_max_iter <- 50L    # guard on the cascade below

.par_apply("params-s3-trim-ends")
```

```{r}
#| label: s3-trim-ends
#| code-summary: "Cut noisy leading and trailing ends off each cleaned ellipse stack"

# ── Re-runnable ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# This chunk is written to be run repeatedly at different settings. It never
# trims an already-trimmed stack: each run first rebuilds the UNTRIMMED kept set
# from the flagged frame, then applies the current parameters to that. So a
# second run with a looser threshold genuinely loosens the cut rather than
# cutting further into what the first run left, and s3_run_trim <- FALSE
# restores the full cleaning output instead of leaving the last trim in place.
#
# The rebuild is exact rather than a cached copy, which is what makes it safe
# when the chunks above have also been re-run: .s3_consensus_clean() defines
# valid as flagged[!spike], and trimming does not touch flagged, so that
# expression always reconstructs the cleaning verdict as it currently stands.
# A stashed snapshot would go stale the moment pass 2 was re-run at new
# settings, and would do so silently.
#
# NOTE: rebuilding valid discards columns added AFTER cleaning - the prot_*
# signals in particular. Re-run this chunk and the protrusion chunk below it
# together, which is the document order anyway.
.s3_untrimmed_valid <- function(f) {
  if (is.null(f) || nrow(f) == 0L) return(f)
  f <- as.data.frame(f)
  if (!"spike" %in% names(f)) return(f)
  keep <- !f$spike
  keep[is.na(keep)] <- FALSE
  f[keep, setdiff(names(f), "trimmed"), drop = FALSE]
}


# ── The cascade ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Trimming one side changes the counts for every other gap, because an ellipse
# that has been cut no longer counts towards anyone's "five or fewer". So this
# is not a single pass: after each cut the whole stem is re-examined, and the
# process repeats until nothing more qualifies.
#
# That cascade is the point rather than a side effect. A noisy end is usually
# several small clusters separated by several gaps, and cutting only the
# outermost would leave the next one looking like a legitimate group. Working
# inward, each cut exposes the next cluster as the small thing it is, and the
# process stops at the first side substantial enough to survive the test - which
# is the start of the continuous stem.
#
# It stops of its own accord: the body of the stem has far more than
# s3_trim_side_max ellipses on both sides of any gap it contains, so the test
# fails there and the cascade cannot eat into it. A stem thin enough everywhere
# for the cascade to run away had no continuous section to protect.

# ── One stem ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The full slice ladder comes from the flagged frame, which carries EVERY slice
# the fitter attempted, including the NA rows for slices that produced no
# ellipse. The valid list alone would not do: it contains only survivors, so the
# gaps - the thing being measured - would be invisible in it.
.s3_trim_one_stem <- function(all_slices, kept_z, run_min, side_max, max_iter) {

  n <- length(all_slices)
  out <- list(keep_z = kept_z, n_before = length(kept_z), n_after = length(kept_z),
              n_cut = 0L, n_gaps = 0L, cuts = character(0),
              s_lo = NA_real_, s_hi = NA_real_)
  if (n == 0L || length(kept_z) == 0L) return(out)

  ord  <- order(all_slices)
  z    <- all_slices[ord]
  kept <- z %in% kept_z

  for (it in seq_len(max_iter)) {

    if (!any(kept)) break

    # Runs of consecutive empty slices, in ladder order.
    r     <- rle(kept)
    ends  <- cumsum(r$lengths)
    starts<- ends - r$lengths + 1L
    gap   <- which(!r$values & r$lengths >= run_min)
    if (length(gap) == 0L) break

    cut_made <- FALSE
    for (g in gap) {
      lo_i <- starts[g]; hi_i <- ends[g]

      n_below <- sum(kept[seq_len(lo_i - 1L)])
      n_above <- if (hi_i >= n) 0L else sum(kept[(hi_i + 1L):n])

      # A side with nothing on it is already clear - cutting it is a no-op, and
      # counting it as a cut would spin the loop.
      if (n_below > 0L && n_below <= side_max) {
        kept[seq_len(lo_i - 1L)] <- FALSE
        out$n_cut <- out$n_cut + n_below
        out$cuts  <- c(out$cuts, sprintf("below %.3f m (%d)", z[lo_i], n_below))
        cut_made <- TRUE
      }
      if (n_above > 0L && n_above <= side_max) {
        kept[(hi_i + 1L):n] <- FALSE
        out$n_cut <- out$n_cut + n_above
        out$cuts  <- c(out$cuts, sprintf("above %.3f m (%d)", z[hi_i], n_above))
        cut_made <- TRUE
      }
      if (cut_made) break     # counts have changed; re-derive the runs
    }
    if (!cut_made) break
    out$n_gaps <- out$n_gaps + 1L
  }

  out$keep_z  <- z[kept]
  out$n_after <- sum(kept)
  if (out$n_after > 0L) { out$s_lo <- min(z[kept]); out$s_hi <- max(z[kept]) }
  out
}

# ── Run ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
.s3_trim_epoch <- function(clean_result, ladder_src, label, do_trim = TRUE) {
  if (is.null(clean_result) || length(clean_result) == 0L) return(NULL)

  diag <- NULL
  for (tid in names(clean_result)) {
    f <- clean_result[[tid]]$flagged
    # Always start from the untrimmed set, whatever a previous run left behind.
    v <- .s3_untrimmed_valid(f)
    clean_result[[tid]]$valid <- v

    # The ladder: every slice position the fitter attempted for this stem. Taken
    # from the pass-1 / refit frame, which still holds the rows pass 2 dropped,
    # so a slice removed at pass 1 reads as empty rather than as absent.
    lad <- ladder_src[[tid]]
    all_z <- if (!is.null(lad) && nrow(lad) > 0L) as.data.frame(lad)$slice_z else
             if (!is.null(f) && nrow(f) > 0L)     as.data.frame(f)$slice_z else numeric(0)
    all_z <- sort(unique(all_z[!is.na(all_z)]))

    kept_z <- if (is.null(v) || nrow(v) == 0L) numeric(0) else v$slice_z

    r <- if (do_trim)
           .s3_trim_one_stem(all_z, kept_z, s3_trim_run_min, s3_trim_side_max,
                             s3_trim_max_iter)
         else
           # Not trimming: report the untrimmed range, so trim_range_ax_* is
           # populated either way and nothing downstream has to test whether
           # this step ran.
           list(keep_z = kept_z, n_before = length(kept_z), n_after = length(kept_z),
                n_cut = 0L, n_gaps = 0L, cuts = character(0),
                s_lo = if (length(kept_z)) min(kept_z) else NA_real_,
                s_hi = if (length(kept_z)) max(kept_z) else NA_real_)

    # Apply. The valid table is subset; the flagged table gains a column so the
    # figures can draw a trimmed slice differently from one the filters removed
    # - it was not judged unfit, it was judged unsupported.
    if (!is.null(v) && nrow(v) > 0L)
      clean_result[[tid]]$valid <- v[v$slice_z %in% r$keep_z, , drop = FALSE]
    if (!is.null(f) && nrow(f) > 0L) {
      f <- as.data.frame(f)
      f$trimmed <- !is.na(f$slice_z) & (f$slice_z %in% kept_z) &
                   !(f$slice_z %in% r$keep_z)
      clean_result[[tid]]$flagged <- f
    }
    clean_result[[tid]]$trim <- r

    diag <- rbind(diag, data.frame(
      TreeID = tid, n_slices = length(all_z),
      kept_before = r$n_before, trimmed = r$n_cut, kept_after = r$n_after,
      s_lo = r$s_lo, s_hi = r$s_hi,
      span = if (is.na(r$s_lo)) NA_real_ else r$s_hi - r$s_lo,
      cuts = if (length(r$cuts)) paste(r$cuts, collapse = "; ") else "",
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
  }
  rownames(diag) <- NULL
  list(clean = clean_result, diag = diag)
}

# The ladders are built whether or not trimming runs, so the figure below can
# draw the stack either way and a skipped run still leaves a complete picture.
s3_trim_ladder_1 <- if (!is.null(refit_flagged_ax_1)) refit_flagged_ax_1 else
                      lapply(clean1_result_ax_1, `[[`, "flagged")
s3_trim_ladder_2 <- if (!is.null(refit_flagged_ax_2)) refit_flagged_ax_2 else
                      lapply(clean1_result_ax_2, `[[`, "flagged")

if (s3_run_trim) {
  cat(sprintf("Trimming: a gap is %d+ consecutive empty slices | a side is cut at %d kept ellipse(s) or fewer\n",
              s3_trim_run_min, s3_trim_side_max))
} else {
  cat("\nTrimming DISABLED (s3_run_trim = FALSE) - the full cleaning output is restored.\n")
}

.tr1 <- .s3_trim_epoch(clean_result_ax_1, s3_trim_ladder_1, "las_1 axis", s3_run_trim)
.tr2 <- .s3_trim_epoch(clean_result_ax_2, s3_trim_ladder_2, "las_2 axis", s3_run_trim)

clean_result_ax_1 <- .tr1$clean
clean_result_ax_2 <- .tr2$clean
trim_diag_ax_1    <- .tr1$diag
trim_diag_ax_2    <- .tr2$diag

if (s3_run_trim) {

  # ── The surviving range ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Recorded per stem, and this is the object the LOESS fits downstream must be
  # limited to. Fitting outside it would extrapolate across the gap that was
  # just cut - the smoother has no data there, so it would carry the trend of
  # the last real ellipses out into empty stem and return a value that looks
  # like a measurement.
  trim_range_ax_1 <- trim_diag_ax_1[, c("TreeID", "s_lo", "s_hi", "kept_after")]
  trim_range_ax_2 <- trim_diag_ax_2[, c("TreeID", "s_lo", "s_hi", "kept_after")]
  names(trim_range_ax_1)[4] <- names(trim_range_ax_2)[4] <- "n_kept"

  .s3_trim_report <- function(diag, label) {
    if (is.null(diag) || nrow(diag) == 0L) { cat(sprintf("[%s] nothing to trim.\n", label)); return(invisible(NULL)) }
    cat(sprintf("\n[%s] Trimming\n", label))
    print(diag[, c("TreeID", "n_slices", "kept_before", "trimmed", "kept_after",
                   "s_lo", "s_hi", "span")], row.names = FALSE, digits = 4)
    cat(sprintf("  TOTAL: %d kept -> %d after trimming (%d cut, %.1f%%) | %d stem(s) untouched, %d emptied\n",
                sum(diag$kept_before), sum(diag$kept_after), sum(diag$trimmed),
                100 * sum(diag$trimmed) / max(1L, sum(diag$kept_before)),
                sum(diag$trimmed == 0L), sum(diag$kept_after == 0L)))
    # Where the cut happened matters as much as how much came off: a stem
    # trimmed only at the top has a crown problem, one trimmed at both ends has
    # a coverage problem, and one trimmed hard at the bottom may have a base
    # the axis frame is not describing well.
    .cut <- diag[nzchar(diag$cuts), c("TreeID", "trimmed", "cuts"), drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(.cut) > 0L) {
      cat("  cuts made:\n")
      print(.cut, row.names = FALSE)
    }
    invisible(diag)
  }

  .s3_trim_report(trim_diag_ax_1, "las_1 axis")
  .s3_trim_report(trim_diag_ax_2, "las_2 axis")

  # A record of what produced the numbers above, so two runs at different
  # settings can be told apart in a rendered document.
  s3_trim_settings <- list(run_min = s3_trim_run_min, side_max = s3_trim_side_max,
                           max_iter = s3_trim_max_iter,
                           n_cut = sum(trim_diag_ax_1$trimmed) + sum(trim_diag_ax_2$trimmed))

  # A stem trimmed to nothing has no continuous section at all. It is left in
  # place here rather than dropped, so the back-projection chunk removes its
  # pair by the rule it already applies - one place decides which pairs survive.
  .gone <- c(trim_diag_ax_1$TreeID[trim_diag_ax_1$kept_after == 0L],
             trim_diag_ax_2$TreeID[trim_diag_ax_2$kept_after == 0L])
  if (length(.gone) > 0L)
    warning(sprintf("[3.6 trim] %d stem(s) left with no ellipses: %s. Their pairs are dropped at back-projection.",
                    length(.gone), paste(.gone, collapse = ", ")), call. = FALSE)

} else {
  # Ranges are still recorded - they now describe the untrimmed stacks, which
  # is exactly what the LOESS fits should be limited to when trimming is off.
  trim_range_ax_1 <- trim_diag_ax_1[, c("TreeID", "s_lo", "s_hi", "kept_after")]
  trim_range_ax_2 <- trim_diag_ax_2[, c("TreeID", "s_lo", "s_hi", "kept_after")]
  names(trim_range_ax_1)[4] <- names(trim_range_ax_2)[4] <- "n_kept"
  s3_trim_settings <- list(run_min = NA, side_max = NA, max_iter = NA, n_cut = 0L)
}
```

### Vis – what trimming removed

```{r}
#| label: fig-s3-trim
#| code-summary: "Kept ellipse ladder per stem, before and after trimming"
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5

if (params$make_plots && !is.null(trim_diag_ax_1)) {

  # One row per stem, stem length across. Every attempted slice is drawn, so the
  # gaps that drove the decision are visible as gaps rather than inferred from
  # the counts.
  .s3_trim_ladder <- function(clean_result, ladder_src, label) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(names(clean_result), function(tid) {
      lad <- ladder_src[[tid]]
      if (is.null(lad) || nrow(lad) == 0L) return(NULL)
      lad <- as.data.frame(lad)
      v   <- clean_result[[tid]]$valid
      kz  <- if (is.null(v) || nrow(v) == 0L) numeric(0) else v$slice_z
      tz  <- if ("trimmed" %in% names(clean_result[[tid]]$flagged))
               clean_result[[tid]]$flagged$slice_z[clean_result[[tid]]$flagged$trimmed] else numeric(0)
      data.frame(
        epoch = label, TreeID = tid, s = lad$slice_z,
        state = ifelse(lad$slice_z %in% kz, "kept",
                ifelse(lad$slice_z %in% tz, "trimmed", "removed earlier")),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }))
  }

  .lad_plot <- rbind(
    .s3_trim_ladder(clean_result_ax_1, s3_trim_ladder_1, "las_1"),
    .s3_trim_ladder(clean_result_ax_2, s3_trim_ladder_2, "las_2"))

  if (!is.null(.lad_plot) && nrow(.lad_plot) > 0L) {
    .lad_plot$row <- paste(.lad_plot$epoch, .lad_plot$TreeID)
    print(
      ggplot(.lad_plot, aes(s, row, colour = state)) +
        geom_point(shape = 15, size = 1.4) +
        scale_colour_manual(values = c(kept = "#2C7FB8",
                                       trimmed = "#D7263D",
                                       `removed earlier` = "grey85"),
                            name = NULL) +
        labs(title = "Ellipse ladder per stem, after trimming",
             subtitle = sprintf("gap = %d+ empty slices | side cut at <= %d kept | red = cut by trimming, grey = removed by fitting or cleaning",
                                s3_trim_run_min, s3_trim_side_max),
             x = "Stem length along the pair axis (m)", y = NULL) +
        theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
        theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
    )
  }
}
```

## 3.8 Protrusion signals – eight axis-orthogonal sectors

```{r}
#| label: params-s3-protrusion-signals
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Eight cake-slice protrusion signals per ellipse: fraction of slice points falling outside the fitted ellipse, by sector"


# ── What this measures ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The established signals - area, centre offset, semi-minor, semi-major,
# eccentricity - all describe the fitted ellipse. None of them says anything
# about the points the ellipse did NOT capture, and that is where a branch stub,
# a bark plate or a buttress lives. The protrusion signals fill that gap: the
# axis-orthogonal plane is cut into eight sectors, and each records the fraction
# of that sector's points lying outside the fitted ellipse.
#
# Eight signals rather than one because the position of a protrusion around the
# stem is the informative part. A single "fraction outside" would average a
# one-sided bulge away to nothing.
#
# ── The sector frame ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The sectors live in the plane perpendicular to the pair axis, so they are NOT
# horizontal and the labels are NOT compass directions. They are named N, NE, E,
# ... only because eight labelled directions read more easily than indices 1-8.
#
# NORTH is defined as the in-plane direction with the greatest global Z
# component - the direction you would move to gain height fastest without
# leaving the plane. It is the projection of the global Z axis onto the
# orthogonal plane, and it is what makes the frame reproducible: it depends only
# on the pair axis, so both stems of a pair get the SAME sector boundaries and
# their signals can be compared slice for slice. Anchoring on anything derived
# from the points themselves - the widest radius, the first principal direction
# - would let the two epochs rotate independently and destroy that.
#
# In the local frame the axis IS the Z axis, and the local direction of global
# "up" is simply the Z components of the two in-plane basis vectors, so North
# needs no extra computation: theta_N = atan2(v[3], u[3]) where u, v are the
# rows of the stem's own rotation matrix.
#
# The remaining seven directions sit at 45 degree intervals from North, turning
# right-handed about the axis (counter-clockwise seen from the top of the stem
# looking down). The SECTORS are the wedges BETWEEN adjacent directions, so
# sector 1 spans N to NE, sector 2 NE to E, and so on. Each is 45 degrees wide
# and no point can fall in two.

# ── Parameters ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# ── The mask ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Counting every point in the slice window would count LEAVES. A slice cut
# through a crown catches foliage metres from the stem, all of it outside the
# fitted ellipse and all of it landing in whichever sector it happens to fall
# in - so a leafy stem would read as protruding in every direction at once, and
# the signal would measure canopy density rather than stem shape.
#
# The fix is the same device the masked refit uses: restrict the points to a
# neighbourhood of the ellipse before counting. The refit takes a circle at
# 1.5x the anchor's semi-major axis; here each slice is masked by its OWN
# fitted ellipse, scaled by the same factor. The mask is elliptical rather than
# circular because the ellipse is what the points are being scored against - a
# circular mask on a flattened section would admit more of the plane along the
# minor axis than along the major one, and bias the sectors accordingly.
#
# This is applied to EVERY slice, refit or not. A refit slice was fitted inside
# a circle projected from its neighbour, but that circle belongs to the fitting
# step; using it here would mean two slices' protrusion values were computed
# under two different masks and could not be compared.
s3_prot_mask_scale <- 1.3   # multiple of the slice's own fitted ellipse

s3_prot_apex <- "ellipse"   # "ellipse" = wedges radiate from the fitted centre
                            # "axis"    = from the stem axis (local origin)
# The ellipse centre is the default because the signal is about that ellipse:
# a bulge should land in the wedge it bulges into, measured from the shape it is
# bulging out of. The axis apex is offered because it does not move when the fit
# wobbles, which is the better choice if the fits themselves are unstable.

s3_prot_outside_tol <- 0    # m of radial excess before a point counts as OUTSIDE
# 0 is the literal definition and the default. Be aware of what it implies: the
# fit puts the ellipse THROUGH the point cloud, so roughly half the inlier shell
# sits marginally outside it and every sector starts from a baseline near 0.5.
# That is not a fault - the signal is still driven by real protrusions, and a
# baseline shared by both epochs cancels in the comparison - but it does mean
# these values should be read as departures from ~0.5, not from 0. Setting this
# to the fit's own distance_threshold instead measures "outside the fitted
# SHELL", which starts near 0 and responds only to genuine protrusions.

s3_prot_min_pts <- 3L       # points a sector needs before its fraction is kept
# Below this the quotient is one or two points and swings between 0 and 1 on
# noise. Such sectors get NA rather than a number that looks like a measurement.

.s3_sector_names <- c("N_NE", "E_NE", "E_SE", "S_SE", "S_SW", "W_SW", "W_NW", "N_NW")

.par_apply("params-s3-protrusion-signals")
```

```{r}
#| label: s3-protrusion-signals
#| code-summary: "Eight cake-slice protrusion signals per ellipse: fraction of slice points falling outside the fitted ellipse, by sector"

# ── Per-stem computation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Runs on the surviving ellipses only, in the LOCAL frame, before
# back-projection - the sectors are defined in that frame and the points are
# already there.
#
# The point set is the FULL slice window, not the fit's candidate set. For a
# refit slice those differ: the refit only ever saw the masked subset, and
# scoring protrusion against that would ask how much of a deliberately narrowed
# set falls outside, which is a different question and a smaller one. Protrusion
# is a property of the stem, so it is measured against every point present.
.s3_protrusion_one_stem <- function(d, pts_local, R, width,
                                    apex = s3_prot_apex,
                                    tol  = s3_prot_outside_tol,
                                    mask = s3_prot_mask_scale,
                                    min_pts = s3_prot_min_pts) {

  n_col <- paste0("n_",    .s3_sector_names)
  p_col <- paste0("prot_", .s3_sector_names)
  for (cc in c(n_col, p_col)) d[[cc]] <- NA_real_
  d$prot_n_masked <- NA_integer_
  d$prot_n_window <- NA_integer_

  if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L || is.null(pts_local) || nrow(pts_local) == 0L)
    return(d)

  # North: the in-plane direction of greatest global Z. R's rows are u, v, ax,
  # so the local coordinates of the global Z axis are (u[3], v[3], ax[3]) and
  # the in-plane part is the first two.
  theta_N <- atan2(R[2, 3], R[1, 3])

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(d))) {
    cx <- d$center_x[i]; cy <- d$center_y[i]
    a  <- d$semi_a[i];   b  <- d$semi_b[i]
    ang <- d$angle_deg[i]
    if (any(is.na(c(cx, cy, a, b, ang))) || a <= 0 || b <= 0) next

    z_lo <- d$slice_z[i] - width / 2
    p    <- pts_local[pts_local$Z >= z_lo & pts_local$Z < z_lo + width, , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(p) == 0L) next
    d$prot_n_window[i] <- nrow(p)

    # One quantity decides both the mask and the verdict. Rotating into the
    # ellipse's own frame, r = sqrt((u/a)^2 + (v/b)^2) is 1 exactly on the
    # boundary, so r <= mask IS the scaled-ellipse mask and 1 < r is outside.
    # The radial excess in metres is dist * (1 - 1/r), which is what the
    # tolerance is measured in.
    th <- ang * pi / 180
    dx <- p$X - cx; dy <- p$Y - cy
    u  <-  dx * cos(th) + dy * sin(th)
    v  <- -dx * sin(th) + dy * cos(th)
    r  <- sqrt((u / a)^2 + (v / b)^2)

    keep <- r <= mask
    if (!any(keep)) next
    p <- p[keep, , drop = FALSE]; r <- r[keep]; dx <- dx[keep]; dy <- dy[keep]
    d$prot_n_masked[i] <- nrow(p)

    # Sector assignment, on the masked set. The apex choice only shifts where
    # the wedges radiate from; the ANGULAR reference is theta_N either way, so
    # the direction a sector name refers to does not change with it.
    ax_x <- if (identical(apex, "axis")) p$X else dx
    ax_y <- if (identical(apex, "axis")) p$Y else dy
    psi  <- (atan2(ax_y, ax_x) - theta_N) %% (2 * pi)
    sec  <- pmin(8L, floor(psi / (pi / 4)) + 1L)

    dist_c  <- sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2)
    outside <- if (tol <= 0) r > 1 else (r > 1 & dist_c * (1 - 1 / r) > tol)

    n_tot <- tabulate(sec, nbins = 8L)
    n_out <- tabulate(sec[outside], nbins = 8L)
    frac  <- ifelse(n_tot >= min_pts, n_out / n_tot, NA_real_)

    d[i, n_col] <- as.list(as.numeric(n_tot))
    d[i, p_col] <- as.list(frac)
  }

  d
}

.s3_protrusion_epoch <- function(valid_list, tr_list, las, label) {
  if (is.null(valid_list) || length(valid_list) == 0L) return(valid_list)
  pb <- .pb_new(length(valid_list), label)
  on.exit(.pb_done(pb), add = TRUE)

  out <- lapply(names(valid_list), function(tid) {
    .pb_tick(pb)
    d  <- valid_list[[tid]]
    tr <- tr_list[[tid]]
    if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L || is.null(tr)) return(d)
    .s3_protrusion_one_stem(d, .s3_pts_local(las, tid, tr), tr$R, fp_s3$width)
  })
  setNames(out, names(valid_list))
}

.pv_1 <- .s3_protrusion_epoch(lapply(clean_result_ax_1, `[[`, "valid"),
                              axis_tr_1, las_1_rot, "las_1 protrusion")
.pv_2 <- .s3_protrusion_epoch(lapply(clean_result_ax_2, `[[`, "valid"),
                              axis_tr_2, las_2, "las_2 protrusion")

# Write the signals back into the cleaning result, so the back-projection chunk
# below carries them through with everything else and nothing has to be joined
# back on later by slice.
for (tid in names(clean_result_ax_1)) clean_result_ax_1[[tid]]$valid <- .pv_1[[tid]]
for (tid in names(clean_result_ax_2)) clean_result_ax_2[[tid]]$valid <- .pv_2[[tid]]

# ── Report ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
.s3_prot_report <- function(pv, label) {
  d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pv, function(x)
    if (is.null(x) || nrow(x) == 0L) NULL else x[, paste0("prot_", .s3_sector_names), drop = FALSE]))
  if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L) { cat(sprintf("[%s] no ellipses to score.\n", label)); return(invisible(NULL)) }
  cat(sprintf("\n[%s] protrusion by sector over %d ellipse(s)\n", label, nrow(d)))
  cat("           ", paste(sprintf("%8s", .s3_sector_names), collapse = ""), "\n", sep = "")
  cat("  median   ", paste(sprintf("%8.3f", vapply(d, median, numeric(1), na.rm = TRUE)), collapse = ""), "\n", sep = "")
  cat("  p90      ", paste(sprintf("%8.3f", vapply(d, function(x) as.numeric(quantile(x, .9, na.rm = TRUE)), numeric(1))), collapse = ""), "\n", sep = "")
  cat("  NA (thin)", paste(sprintf("%8d", vapply(d, function(x) sum(is.na(x)), integer(1))), collapse = ""), "\n", sep = "")
  # A sector systematically emptier than the others is a scan-geometry effect -
  # the far side of the stem - not a protrusion. Worth seeing beside the values.
  invisible(d)
}
.s3_prot_report(.pv_1, "las_1 axis")
.s3_prot_report(.pv_2, "las_2 axis")

# How much the mask is throwing away. A high discard rate is expected in crown
# slices and near zero on a clean lower stem; if it is high everywhere, the mask
# is too tight or the fits are too small.
.mask_rate <- function(pv) {
  d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pv, function(x)
    if (is.null(x) || nrow(x) == 0L) NULL else x[, c("prot_n_window", "prot_n_masked")]))
  if (is.null(d)) return(NA_real_)
  100 * (1 - sum(d$prot_n_masked, na.rm = TRUE) / max(1, sum(d$prot_n_window, na.rm = TRUE)))
}
cat(sprintf("\nMask (%.2f x each slice's own ellipse) discarded %.1f%% of window points in las_1, %.1f%% in las_2\n",
            s3_prot_mask_scale, .mask_rate(.pv_1), .mask_rate(.pv_2)))
cat(sprintf("Apex: %s | outside tolerance: %.4f m | sector minimum: %d point(s)\n",
            s3_prot_apex, s3_prot_outside_tol, s3_prot_min_pts))
```

## 3.9 Back-projection to world coordinates

```{r}
#| label: s3-backproject
#| code-summary: "Back-project the surviving axis-frame ellipses to world XYZ and drop pairs with nothing left"

# Everything above ran in each stem's own axis frame. This is the single point
# where that is undone, using the exact algebraic inverse stored with the
# transform rather than a numerical solve, so the round trip is exact.
#
# The local coordinates are KEPT alongside the world ones:
# stem_len - distance along the stem axis from the stem's own base. This
# is what every downstream curve is plotted against.
# center_offset - perpendicular distance of the ellipse centre from the axis,
# which is exactly sqrt(x^2 + y^2) in this frame because the
# axis is the local Z axis by construction.
# prot_* / n_* - the eight sector protrusion signals and their masked point
# counts, computed in the chunk above. They are dimensionless
# fractions and sector counts, so the transform does not
# touch them; they simply travel with the row.
# Signals available downstream after this chunk: ell_area, center_offset,
# semi_a, semi_b, ell_ecc, and the eight prot_* fractions.
.s3_backproject <- function(valid_list, tr_list) {
  out <- lapply(names(valid_list), function(tid) {
    d  <- valid_list[[tid]]
    tr <- tr_list[[tid]]
    if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L || is.null(tr)) return(d)

    d$stem_len      <- d$slice_z
    d$center_x_temp <- d$center_x
    d$center_y_temp <- d$center_y
    d$center_z_temp <- d$slice_z
    d$center_offset <- sqrt(d$center_x_temp^2 + d$center_y_temp^2)

    w <- .apply_4x4_transform(
      cbind(d$center_x_temp, d$center_y_temp, d$center_z_temp), tr$M_inv)
    d$center_x <- w[, 1]; d$center_y <- w[, 2]; d$center_z <- w[, 3]

    o <- as.numeric(.apply_4x4_transform(matrix(c(0, 0, 0), nrow = 1L), tr$M_inv))
    d$global_stem_origin_x <- o[1]
    d$global_stem_origin_y <- o[2]
    d$global_stem_origin_z <- o[3]

    ax <- tr$ax
    d$stem_len_origin <- o[3]
    d$stem_len_abs    <- o[3] + d$stem_len * ax[3]

    d$ell_area <- ifelse(!is.na(d$semi_a) & !is.na(d$semi_b), pi * d$semi_a * d$semi_b, NA_real_)
    d$ell_ecc  <- ifelse(!is.na(d$semi_a) & d$semi_a > 0,
                         sqrt(pmax(0, 1 - (d$semi_b / d$semi_a)^2)), NA_real_)
    d
  })
  setNames(out, names(valid_list))
}

ellipses_ax_1_valid <- .s3_backproject(lapply(clean_result_ax_1, `[[`, "valid"), axis_tr_1)
ellipses_ax_2_valid <- .s3_backproject(lapply(clean_result_ax_2, `[[`, "valid"), axis_tr_2)

# The flagged tables travel too, so the cleaning figures can draw removed slices
# in the same frame as the kept ones.
clean_result_ax_1 <- lapply(clean_result_ax_1, function(r) {
  if (!is.null(r$flagged) && nrow(r$flagged) > 0L) r$flagged$stem_len <- r$flagged$slice_z
  r })
clean_result_ax_2 <- lapply(clean_result_ax_2, function(r) {
  if (!is.null(r$flagged) && nrow(r$flagged) > 0L) r$flagged$stem_len <- r$flagged$slice_z
  r })

# ── Drop pairs with nothing left on one side ─────────────────────────────────
# New object; pairs_axis_ok is left intact.
pairs_ax_fitted <- pairs_axis_ok
.has_1 <- vapply(ellipses_ax_1_valid, function(d) !is.null(d) && nrow(d) > 0L, logical(1))
.has_2 <- vapply(ellipses_ax_2_valid, function(d) !is.null(d) && nrow(d) > 0L, logical(1))
.keep  <- .has_1[as.character(pairs_ax_fitted$TreeID_1)] &
          .has_2[as.character(pairs_ax_fitted$TreeID_2)]
.keep[is.na(.keep)] <- FALSE

if (any(!.keep)) {
  cat(sprintf("Dropping %d pair(s) with no surviving ellipses on one side:\n", sum(!.keep)))
  cat(sprintf("  las_1 %s -> las_2 %s\n",
              pairs_ax_fitted$TreeID_1[!.keep], pairs_ax_fitted$TreeID_2[!.keep]))
}
pairs_ax_fitted     <- pairs_ax_fitted[.keep, , drop = FALSE]
ellipses_ax_1_valid <- ellipses_ax_1_valid[as.character(pairs_ax_fitted$TreeID_1)]
ellipses_ax_2_valid <- ellipses_ax_2_valid[as.character(pairs_ax_fitted$TreeID_2)]

cat(sprintf("\nStep 3.3 complete: %d pair(s) carried forward | %d + %d ellipse(s) kept\n",
            nrow(pairs_ax_fitted),
            sum(vapply(ellipses_ax_1_valid, nrow, integer(1))),
            sum(vapply(ellipses_ax_2_valid, nrow, integer(1)))))
cat(sprintf("  stem-length covered: las_1 %.2f - %.2f m | las_2 %.2f - %.2f m\n",
            min(unlist(lapply(ellipses_ax_1_valid, function(d) d$stem_len)), na.rm = TRUE),
            max(unlist(lapply(ellipses_ax_1_valid, function(d) d$stem_len)), na.rm = TRUE),
            min(unlist(lapply(ellipses_ax_2_valid, function(d) d$stem_len)), na.rm = TRUE),
            max(unlist(lapply(ellipses_ax_2_valid, function(d) d$stem_len)), na.rm = TRUE)))
```

### Vis - 3D stem points with axis-aligned fitted ellipse rings

```{r}
#| label: params-fig-ellipses-3D
#| code-summary: "Parameters - fig-ellipses-3D"


# This chunk runs AFTER back-projection, so it draws ellipses_ax_*_valid: the
# set that survived both cleaning passes and the end trimming, in world
# coordinates. An earlier revision drew the raw fit, which is why the objects it
# named no longer exist – the raw tables are ellipses_ax_*_raw and they are in
# each stem's local axis frame, where these world-frame rings cannot be built.
#
# It is also the LAST chunk that needs the point clouds, so it runs before the
# release chunk below.

# ── Point clouds for this figure ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Stage 3 loads point clouds at the top, so this defaults to FALSE. It exists
# because Step 3.10 releases them from memory, and because resuming from the
# save-load_Stage3_1 checkpoint skips the load entirely - in either case set it
# TRUE to make this figure self-sufficient.
# vis_load_clouds <- TRUE read las_1 / las_2 from disk
# vis_load_clouds <- FALSE reuse the clouds already in memory (no disk read)
# The loader also rebuilds the transform state this figure expects, so the
# points shown match the pipeline stage rather than the file on disk.
#
# apply_align = TRUE (the default) plus apply_rot = TRUE reproduces the
# composed rotation from the end of Stage 2: R_align_1 about align_pivot_1,
# then R_xyz about pivot1. That is the frame this stage's ellipse rings
# (ellipses_ax_*_valid) and axis vectors were measured in, so a raw las_1
# needs BOTH legs applied before the points behind the rings line up with
# them - apply_rot alone would rotate from the wrong starting frame.
vis_load_clouds <- FALSE

vis_all_paired_trees_s5 <- TRUE
vis_selected_tids_s5    <- c(1)
vis_full_tree_s5        <- FALSE
s5_vis_max_pts          <- 2000L
s5_ring_n               <- 120L
s5_vis_pad              <- 0.1

.par_apply("params-fig-ellipses-3D")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ellipses-3D
#| fig-cap: "3-D stem points with axis-perpendicular RANSAC ellipse rings (Step 3.3)."

.vpc <- .vis_point_clouds(
  load        = vis_load_clouds,
  apply_align = TRUE,
  apply_rot   = TRUE
)

# Only rebuild las_1_rot when the loader actually produced rotated coordinates.
# On a reuse-from-memory run las_1_rot is already correct, and overwriting it
# from a partially populated .vpc would put the cloud back in the wrong frame.
if (!is.null(.vpc$xyz_1)) {
  las_1_rot <- .vpc$las_1
  las_1_rot@data$X <- .vpc$xyz_1[, 1]
  las_1_rot@data$Y <- .vpc$xyz_1[, 2]
  las_1_rot@data$Z <- .vpc$xyz_1[, 3]
}
if (!is.null(.vpc$las_2)) las_2 <- .vpc$las_2


# ── extract_stem_pts_axis: defined here, used only in this chunk ───────────
# The along-axis window is taken from the ellipse table's OWN origin
# (global_stem_origin_*, written by the back-projection) rather than from
# min(proj) over the sampled points. Those are not the same number: the sample
# is thinned and clipped, so its lowest projected point drifts with
# s5_vis_max_pts, and the window would move with it. The stored origin is the
# local frame's zero, which is exactly what stem_len is measured from.
extract_stem_pts_axis <- function(las, tid, ax, ell_df, pad, max_pts,
                                  full_tree = FALSE) {
  idx <- las@data$TreeID == as.integer(tid)
  if (!any(idx)) return(NULL)
  df <- as.data.frame(las@data[idx, c("X", "Y", "Z")])
  if (nrow(df) < 3L) return(NULL)

  if (!full_tree) {
    if (is.null(ell_df) || nrow(ell_df) == 0L ||
        !"stem_len" %in% names(ell_df)) return(NULL)

    ax_unit <- ax / sqrt(sum(ax^2))
    proj    <- as.matrix(df[, c("X", "Y", "Z")]) %*% ax_unit

    origin <- if (all(c("global_stem_origin_x", "global_stem_origin_y",
                        "global_stem_origin_z") %in% names(ell_df))) {
      sum(c(ell_df$global_stem_origin_x[1], ell_df$global_stem_origin_y[1],
            ell_df$global_stem_origin_z[1]) * ax_unit)
    } else {
      min(proj)          # fallback for a table written before back-projection
    }

    sl_min <- origin + min(ell_df$stem_len, na.rm = TRUE) - pad
    sl_max <- origin + max(ell_df$stem_len, na.rm = TRUE) + pad

    df <- df[proj >= sl_min & proj <= sl_max, ]
    if (nrow(df) < 3L) return(NULL)
  }

  if (nrow(df) > max_pts) df <- df[sample.int(nrow(df), max_pts), ]
  df$TreeID <- as.integer(tid)
  df
}

# pairs_ax_fitted, not pairs_axis_ok: back-projection dropped the pairs left
# with no surviving ellipses on one side, and subset the valid lists to match.
# Iterating the wider table would look up stems that are no longer in them.
.vis_pair_src <- if (exists("pairs_ax_fitted")) pairs_ax_fitted else pairs_axis_ok

if (vis_all_paired_trees_s5) {
  vis_pairs_s5 <- .vis_pair_src
} else {
  vis_pairs_s5 <- .vis_pair_src[.vis_pair_src$TreeID_1 %in% vis_selected_tids_s5, ]
  if (nrow(vis_pairs_s5) == 0L)
    warning("[vis s5] None of vis_selected_tids_s5 matched a fitted pair.")
}

if (params$make_plots && nrow(vis_pairs_s5) > 0L) {

  # One panel builder for both epochs - the two sides differed only in which
  # objects they read, and keeping two copies is how they drift apart.
  .draw_stem <- function(las, tid, ax, ell_df, epoch_lab, colour) {
    sp <- extract_stem_pts_axis(las, tid, ax, ell_df, s5_vis_pad,
                                s5_vis_max_pts, full_tree = vis_full_tree_s5)
    if (is.null(sp)) return(invisible(NULL))

    cx <- mean(sp$X); cy <- mean(sp$Y)
    sp$Xloc <- sp$X - cx; sp$Yloc <- sp$Y - cy

    p <- plot_ly() |>
      add_trace(data = sp, x = ~Xloc, y = ~Yloc, z = ~Z,
                type = "scatter3d", mode = "markers",
                name = paste(epoch_lab, "pts"),
                marker = list(size = 1.5, color = colour, opacity = 0.5))

    rg <- build_rings_axis(ell_df, ax, s5_ring_n)
    if (!is.null(rg) && nrow(rg) > 0L) {
      rg$Xloc <- rg$X - cx; rg$Yloc <- rg$Y - cy
      p <- p |> add_trace(
        data = rg, x = ~Xloc, y = ~Yloc, z = ~Z,
        type = "scatter3d", mode = "lines",
        name = paste("ellipses", epoch_lab),
        line = list(color = "gold", width = 3),
        hoverinfo = "none", inherit = FALSE)
    }

    print(p |> layout(
      title = sprintf("%s Tree %s \u2014 axis-RANSAC ellipses, cleaned and trimmed%s | %d kept, stem length %.2f-%.2f m",
                      epoch_lab, tid,
                      if (vis_full_tree_s5) " (full tree)" else "",
                      nrow(ell_df),
                      min(ell_df$stem_len, na.rm = TRUE),
                      max(ell_df$stem_len, na.rm = TRUE)),
      scene = list(xaxis = list(title = "X local (m)"),
                   yaxis = list(title = "Y local (m)"),
                   zaxis = list(title = "Z (m)"), aspectmode = "data")))
    invisible(NULL)
  }

  .n_drawn <- 0L
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(vis_pairs_s5))) {
    tid1 <- vis_pairs_s5$TreeID_1[i]; tid2 <- vis_pairs_s5$TreeID_2[i]
    ax   <- pair_axis_list[[as.character(tid1)]]
    if (is.null(ax) || any(is.na(ax))) next

    e1 <- ellipses_ax_1_valid[[as.character(tid1)]]
    e2 <- ellipses_ax_2_valid[[as.character(tid2)]]

    # A stem trimmed to nothing has no rings and no window to cut points to.
    # Skipping it quietly would hide the fact, so say which.
    if (is.null(e1) || nrow(e1) == 0L || is.null(e2) || nrow(e2) == 0L) {
      cat(sprintf("Skipping pair las_1 %s / las_2 %s - no surviving ellipses on %s side.\n",
                  tid1, tid2,
                  if (is.null(e1) || nrow(e1) == 0L) "the las_1" else "the las_2"))
      next
    }

    .draw_stem(las_1_rot, tid1, ax, e1, "las_1", COL_1)
    .draw_stem(las_2,     tid2, ax, e2, "las_2", COL_2)
    .n_drawn <- .n_drawn + 1L
  }
  cat(sprintf("Drew %d of %d pair(s).\n", .n_drawn, nrow(vis_pairs_s5)))
}
```

## Save/Load 1 – Stage 3 post ellipse fit

The axis-perpendicular RANSAC fit is by far the most expensive step in the
whole workflow. This checkpoint exists purely so that it never has to be re-run
while tuning the cleaning, coverage-filter and curve-matching parameters that
follow. Set `stage3_1_load <- TRUE` and skip straight past Step 3.3.

```{r}
#| label: params-save-load_Stage3_1
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Save or load the Stage 3 object set as of the completed, cleaned and trimmed ellipse fit"


# ── Path ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# One name, used by both branches. An earlier revision assigned the path to
```

```{r}
#| label: save-load_Stage3_1
#| code-summary: "Save or load the Stage 3 object set as of the completed, cleaned and trimmed ellipse fit"

# A batch decides these itself, whatever they are left set to above. Both are
# read a few lines below, in this same chunk, so the driver's overrides land
# too late to reach them - and a stage left switched to LOAD after an
# interactive session would otherwise make a batch write no checkpoint at all
# and say nothing about it. Saving is what a batch is for; loading is a no-op
# in one, since every stage runs in the same session.
if (.in_batch()) { stage3_1_save <- TRUE; stage3_1_load <- FALSE }

# ── What a reload can and cannot re-tune ──────────────────────────────────────
# The raw fit (ellipses_ax_*_raw) and the per-stem axis transforms (axis_tr_*)
# both travel, so cleaning, the second cleaning pass and trimming can all be
# re-run from a checkpoint without the RANSAC fit - which is the expensive part
# and the reason this file exists.
#
# Two steps still need the POINT CLOUDS and therefore cannot be re-tuned from a
# reload alone: the masked refit calls .s3_pts_local(), and the protrusion
# signals count points per sector. Step 3.10 releases the clouds, so a reload
# session that wants to move s3_refit_* or s3_prot_* must reload them first -
# the loader in Step 0.2 does this. The load branch below checks and says so
# rather than letting it fail inside the refit loop.
#
# NOTE on ransac_seed. Stage 1 saves a parameter of that name, and the Step 3.3
# parameter block declares one too, so by the time this chunk runs the Stage 3
# value has overwritten Stage 1's. It is therefore NOT saved here: recording 33
# as the seed Stage 1 fitted with would be worse than recording nothing.
# Renaming the Step 3.3 one to s3_ransac_seed resolves it, after which both
# belong in the list.

# Cumulative: everything Stage 2 wrote, plus Stage 3's own products up to the
# completed ellipse fit. Inheriting .stage2_required / .stage2_optional keeps
# this in lock-step with what was loaded, so no dropped upstream parameter is
# ever requested for save.
.stage3_1_own <- c(
  "run_counts",
  "pairs_stage3_in",
  "apply_mode_rot",
  "R_xyz_solved",

  "s3_slice_width",
  "s3_ransac_distance_threshold",
  "s3_ransac_iter_per_point",
  "s3_ransac_iter_max",
  "s3_ransac_iter_min",
  "fp_s3",
  "ellipses_ax_1_raw",
  "ellipses_ax_2_raw",
  "axis_tr_1",
  "axis_tr_2",
  "s3_consensus_frac_centre",
  "s3_consensus_frac_minor",
  "s3_consensus_frac_major",
  "s3_consensus_tol_floor",

  "s3_consensus_max_gap",
  "s3_consensus_sort_axes",
  "s3_mad_minor_mult",
  "s3_mad_minor_min_n",
  "s3_run_mad_minor",
  "s3_mad_major_mult",
  "s3_mad_major_min_n",
  "s3_run_mad_major",
  "s3_run_cleaning",
  "clean1_result_ax_1",
  "clean1_result_ax_2",
  "ellipses_ax_1_valid1",
  "ellipses_ax_2_valid1",
  "cp_s3",
  "s3_run_refit",
  "s3_refit_targets",
  "s3_refit_mask_scale",
  "s3_refit_min_pts",
  "s3_refit_seed",
  "s3_refit_distance_threshold",

  "s3_refit_iter_max",

  "s3_refit_early_exit",
  "refit_flagged_ax_1",
  "refit_flagged_ax_2",
  "s3_consensus2_frac_centre",
  "s3_consensus2_frac_minor",

  "s3_consensus2_tol_cap",
  "s3_consensus2_max_gap",
  "s3_consensus2_sort_axes",
  "s3_mad2_minor_mult",
  "s3_mad2_minor_min_n",
  "s3_run_mad2_minor",
  "s3_mad2_major_mult",
  "s3_mad2_major_min_n",
  "s3_run_mad2_major",
  "s3_run_cleaning_2",
  "clean_result_ax_1",
  "clean_result_ax_2",
  "cp2_s3",
  "s3_run_trim",
  "s3_trim_run_min",
  "s3_trim_side_max",
  "s3_trim_max_iter",
  "trim_diag_ax_1",
  "trim_diag_ax_2",
  "trim_range_ax_1",

  "ellipses_ax_1_valid",
  "ellipses_ax_2_valid",
  "pairs_ax_fitted"
)

# Inherited, not required to be in scope. Loading a Stage 3.1 checkpoint
# directly skips load_Stage3 - the chunk that defines .stage2_required - and the
# whole point of a resumable checkpoint is that this must still work.
.stage3_1_required <- c(.manifest_from(".stage2_required", "required"),
                        .stage3_1_own)

.stage3_1_optional_own <- c(
  "ee_ax_1",
  "ee_ax_2",
  "clean1_summary_ax_1",
  "clean1_summary_ax_2",
  "refit_summary_ax_1",
  "refit_summary_ax_2",
  "clean2_summary_ax_1",
  "clean2_summary_ax_2",

)

.stage3_1_optional <- setdiff(c(.manifest_from(".stage2_optional", "optional"),
                                .stage3_1_optional_own),
                              .stage3_1_required)

if (stage3_1_save) {
  stage3_1_rds_written <- .stage_save(stage3_1_rds_path, .stage3_1_required,
                                      .stage3_1_optional, label = "Stage 3.1")
  cat(sprintf("Stage 3.1 checkpoint: %s\n", stage3_1_rds_written))
}

if (stage3_1_load) {
  .stage_load(stage3_1_rds_path, .stage3_1_required, .stage3_1_optional,
              label = "Stage 3.1")


  cat(sprintf("\nStage 3.1 restored: %d pair(s) fitted | %d + %d ellipse(s) kept after cleaning and trimming\n",
              nrow(pairs_ax_fitted),
              sum(vapply(ellipses_ax_1_valid, nrow, integer(1))),
              sum(vapply(ellipses_ax_2_valid, nrow, integer(1)))))
  cat(sprintf("Fit: %.2f m to %s | step %.3f m | width %.3f m | threshold %.4f m\n",
              s3_slice_bot,
              if (is.null(s3_slice_top)) "each stem's own top" else sprintf("%.2f m", s3_slice_top),
              s3_slice_step, s3_slice_width, s3_ransac_distance_threshold))
  cat(sprintf("Trim: gap %d+ empty slices, side cut at <= %d kept | stem length %.2f - %.2f m across all stems\n",
              s3_trim_run_min, s3_trim_side_max,
              min(c(trim_range_ax_1$s_lo, trim_range_ax_2$s_lo), na.rm = TRUE),
              max(c(trim_range_ax_1$s_hi, trim_range_ax_2$s_hi), na.rm = TRUE)))
  .report_pivot1()

  # What this session can and cannot re-tune, said once, up front.
  if (!exists("las_1_rot") || !exists("las_2")) {
    cat("\nPoint clouds are NOT resident. Cleaning (3.4), the second pass (3.5) and\n",
        "trimming (3.6) can be re-run as they stand. The masked refit and the\n",
        "protrusion signals need points - reload the clouds first if you intend to\n",
        "change s3_refit_* or s3_prot_*.\n", sep = "")
  }
}
```

## 3.10 Release the Point Clouds

```{r}
#| label: params-release-point-clouds
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Drop las_1 / las_2 / las_1_rot from memory – nothing downstream needs them"


# Everything from here to the end of Stage 3 works on fitted ellipse geometry
# alone: cleaning, coverage filtering, LOESS curves, detrending, peak detection
# and matching all read ellipse tables, never points. Releasing the clouds now
# frees the bulk of the session's memory before the curve-matching work, which
# is where the parallel workers are spawned (each worker would otherwise inherit
# a copy of whatever is resident).
#
# Stage 4 and Stage 5 never load point clouds at all. Stage 6 reloads them from
# disk, so nothing is lost here.

.to_release <- c("las_1", "las_2", "las_1_rot",
                 "xyz_1", "xyz_2", "xyz_1_raw", "xyz_1_centered", "xyz_1_rot",
                 "res1", "res2")

.par_apply("params-release-point-clouds")
```

```{r}
#| label: release-point-clouds
#| code-summary: "Drop las_1 / las_2 / las_1_rot from memory – nothing downstream needs them"

.present <- intersect(.to_release, ls(envir = .stage_env()))

if (length(.present) > 0L) {
  rm(list = .present, envir = .stage_env())
  cat(sprintf("Released from memory: %s\n", paste(.present, collapse = ", ")))
} else {
  cat("No point-cloud objects resident (already released, or loaded from a checkpoint).\n")
}

invisible(gc())
print(gc(verbose = FALSE))
```


## 3.11 LOESS Curves – All Signals

```{r}
#| label: params-signal-registry
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Declare the signal registry (5 ellipse signals + 8 protrusion sectors) and fit all LOESS curves"


# ── center_offset ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Computed per fitted ellipse in Step 3.9 as the perpendicular distance of the
# centre from the stem axis - exactly sqrt(x^2 + y^2) in the axis frame, since
# the axis IS the local Z axis there. It survives cleaning and trimming as an
# ordinary per-row column, so nothing is computed here; ellipses_ax_1_valid /
# ellipses_ax_2_valid already carry it.

# Map from las_2 TreeID to its paired las_1 TreeID, used downstream to look up
# the shared pair axis for a las_2 tree.
tid2_to_tid1 <- setNames(
  as.character(pairs_ax_fitted$TreeID_1),
  as.character(pairs_ax_fitted$TreeID_2)
)

# ── Span: a fixed LENGTH, not a fraction ──────────────────────────────────────
# loess() takes span as a fraction of the data, which means a fractional setting
# is a different physical smoother on every stem: 0.20 of a 4 m stack is an
# 80 cm window, and 0.20 of a 15 m stack is a 3 m window. The signals are then
# not comparable between stems, and - worse for what follows - not comparable
# between the two epochs of a pair when trimming left them different lengths.
#
# So the window is declared in METRES and converted per stem:
# span = s5_loess_span_m / (that stem's fitted stem-length range)
# Every curve is then smoothed over the same physical distance of stem, and a
# feature of a given size looks the same wherever it appears.
s5_loess_span_m <- 2.0     # smoothing window, metres of stem length

# Two clamps on the conversion, both of which report when they bind.
# A stack shorter than the window would ask for span > 1. loess accepts that and
# quietly widens its weighting further, which is meaningless here - the window
# already covers everything - so it is capped.
s5_loess_span_cap <- 1.0
# A window has to hold enough points to fit through. Below this many the fit is
# either singular or interpolating noise, so the span is widened until it holds
# them, and the widening is reported rather than applied silently.
s5_loess_min_win_pts <- 6L

# Prediction grid. 1 cm is already five times finer than the 5 cm slice step the
# data arrives at, so it resolves everything the ellipses can support; the 1 mm
# grid it replaces cost ten times the memory and prediction time for detail that
# was interpolation either way.
s5_loess_grid_m <- 0.01    # prediction grid step, metres

.par_apply("params-signal-registry")
```

```{r}
#| label: signal-registry
#| code-summary: "Declare the signal registry (5 ellipse signals + 8 protrusion sectors) and fit all LOESS curves"

# ── Signal registry ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Five ellipse-geometry signals, then one per protrusion sector. The protrusion
# entries are generated rather than written out: eight near-identical blocks is
# eight chances for one of them to carry the wrong field name.
s5_signal_registry <- list(
  area = list(
    field    = "ell_area",
    pred_col = "ell_area_pred",
    curves_1 = "curves_ax_1",        by_tid_1 = "c1_by_tid",
    curves_2 = "curves_ax_2",        by_tid_2 = "c2_by_tid",
    label    = "Ellipse Area",
    y_lab    = "Ellipse area (m\u00b2)"
  ),
  center_offset = list(
    field    = "center_offset",
    pred_col = "co_pred",
    curves_1 = "curves_co_1",        by_tid_1 = "co1_by_tid",
    curves_2 = "curves_co_2",        by_tid_2 = "co2_by_tid",
    label    = "Centre Offset",
    y_lab    = "Centre offset (m)"
  ),
  sa = list(
    field    = "semi_a",
    pred_col = "sa_pred",
    curves_1 = "curves_sa_1",        by_tid_1 = "sa1_by_tid",
    curves_2 = "curves_sa_2",        by_tid_2 = "sa2_by_tid",
    label    = "Radius A (semi_a)",
    y_lab    = "Radius a (m)"
  ),
  sb = list(
    field    = "semi_b",
    pred_col = "sb_pred",
    curves_1 = "curves_sb_1",        by_tid_1 = "sb1_by_tid",
    curves_2 = "curves_sb_2",        by_tid_2 = "sb2_by_tid",
    label    = "Radius B (semi_b)",
    y_lab    = "Radius b (m)"
  ),
  ecc = list(
    field    = "ell_ecc",
    pred_col = "ecc_pred",
    curves_1 = "curves_ecc_1",       by_tid_1 = "ecc1_by_tid",
    curves_2 = "curves_ecc_2",       by_tid_2 = "ecc2_by_tid",
    label    = "Eccentricity",
    y_lab    = "Eccentricity"
  )
)

# Sector names come from Step 3.8 when it has run, so the two can never disagree
# about which sector is which. The fallback is only for a session that reloaded
# a checkpoint written before the protrusion step existed.
.sig_sectors <- if (exists(".s3_sector_names")) .s3_sector_names else
  c("N_NE", "E_NE", "E_SE", "S_SE", "S_SW", "W_SW", "W_NW", "N_NW")

for (.sec in .sig_sectors) {
  .k <- paste0("prot_", .sec)
  s5_signal_registry[[.k]] <- list(
    field    = .k,
    pred_col = paste0(.k, "_pred"),
    curves_1 = paste0("curves_", .k, "_1"),  by_tid_1 = paste0(.k, "_1_by_tid"),
    curves_2 = paste0("curves_", .k, "_2"),  by_tid_2 = paste0(.k, "_2_by_tid"),
    label    = sprintf("Protrusion %s", gsub("_", "-", .sec)),
    y_lab    = "Fraction outside the fitted ellipse"
  )
}

# Protrusion is NA wherever a sector held fewer than s3_prot_min_pts points, and
# on a thin scan that can be most of one sector's column. Those rows are dropped
# before fitting rather than treated as zeros - a sector with no points is not a
# sector with no protrusion. The CURVE, however, is still drawn across them: see
# the fitter below.

# ── Generic LOESS fitter ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The prediction grid spans the stem's full trimmed range, and every signal is
# predicted across ALL of it. Every curve therefore shares one h axis of the
# same length, which is what lets the signals be compared, detrended and
# peak-matched together - a signal that stopped early would break the alignment
# at exactly the stems where it matters.
#
# Gaps are interpolated across rather than left as holes. A missing slice is
# missing evidence, not evidence of a change, and loess with surface = "direct"
# carries the trend of the surrounding data through it - which is the honest
```
