```{r}
# reading of an interruption in the sampling.
#
# Worth knowing: where a signal's own data stops short of the trimmed range -
# common on a protrusion sector with a thin tail - the ends of its curve are
# EXTRAPOLATED rather than interpolated, and extrapolation from a local
# smoother is only as good as the last window. The span report below says which
# stems ran short.
fit_loess_signal_curve <- function(df, tid, field, pred_col,
                                   span_m   = s5_loess_span_m,
                                   span_cap = s5_loess_span_cap,
                                   min_win  = s5_loess_min_win_pts,
                                   grid_m   = s5_loess_grid_m) {

  if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) < 4L) return(NULL)
  df <- df[order(df$stem_len), ]

  h_seq <- seq(min(df$stem_len), max(df$stem_len), by = grid_m)
  origin <- if ("stem_len_origin" %in% names(df)) df$stem_len_origin[1L] else NA_real_

  out <- tibble::tibble(TreeID = as.integer(tid), h = h_seq,
                        h_abs           = h_seq + origin,
                        stem_len_origin = origin)
  out[[pred_col]] <- NA_real_
  attr(out, "span_used") <- NA_real_
  attr(out, "span_note") <- "no fit"

  sig <- df[!is.na(df[[field]]), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(sig) < 4L) return(out)

  rng  <- range(sig$stem_len)
  span_len <- diff(rng)
  if (!is.finite(span_len) || span_len <= 0) return(out)

  # Metres -> fraction, then the two clamps.
  span  <- span_m / span_len
  note  <- "as set"
  need  <- min_win / nrow(sig)          # fraction that holds min_win points
  if (span < need)      { span <- need;     note <- "widened for point count" }
  if (span > span_cap)  { span <- span_cap; note <- "capped at whole stack" }

  fit <- tryCatch(
    suppressWarnings(loess(
      reformulate("stem_len", field), data = sig, span = span,
      control = loess.control(surface = "direct")
    )),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(fit)) return(out)

  out[[pred_col]] <- suppressWarnings(
    predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(stem_len = h_seq)))

  attr(out, "span_used")  <- span
  attr(out, "span_note")  <- note
  attr(out, "span_m_eff") <- span * span_len
  # Fraction of the stem's trimmed range this signal actually had data over.
  # Below 1 the rest of the curve is extrapolated.
  attr(out, "cover") <- span_len / max(1e-9, diff(range(df$stem_len)))
  out
}

# ── Fit curves for every signal ───────────────────────────────────────────────
cat(sprintf("LOESS span: %.2f m of stem length, converted per stem | grid %.3f m | window minimum %d point(s)\n",
            s5_loess_span_m, s5_loess_grid_m, s5_loess_min_win_pts))

loess_span_diag <- NULL

.fit_epoch <- function(valid_list, sr, epoch) {
  parts <- lapply(names(valid_list), function(tid_chr) {
    r <- fit_loess_signal_curve(valid_list[[tid_chr]], tid = tid_chr,
                                field = sr$field, pred_col = sr$pred_col)
    if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
    loess_span_diag <<- rbind(loess_span_diag, data.frame(
      signal = sr$label, epoch = epoch, TreeID = tid_chr,
      span_used = attr(r, "span_used"),
      span_m_eff = if (is.null(attr(r, "span_m_eff"))) NA_real_ else attr(r, "span_m_eff"),
      cover = if (is.null(attr(r, "cover"))) NA_real_ else attr(r, "cover"),
      note = attr(r, "span_note"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
    r
  })
  dplyr::bind_rows(parts)
}

for (sig_key in names(s5_signal_registry)) {
  sr   <- s5_signal_registry[[sig_key]]
  fit1 <- .fit_epoch(ellipses_ax_1_valid, sr, "las_1")
  fit2 <- .fit_epoch(ellipses_ax_2_valid, sr, "las_2")

  assign(sr$curves_1, fit1, envir = .stage_env())
  assign(sr$curves_2, fit2, envir = .stage_env())
  assign(sr$by_tid_1, split(fit1, fit1$TreeID), envir = .stage_env())
  assign(sr$by_tid_2, split(fit2, fit2$TreeID), envir = .stage_env())

  .n1 <- if (nrow(fit1)) sum(tapply(fit1[[sr$pred_col]], fit1$TreeID,
                                    function(v) any(!is.na(v)))) else 0L
  .n2 <- if (nrow(fit2)) sum(tapply(fit2[[sr$pred_col]], fit2$TreeID,
                                    function(v) any(!is.na(v)))) else 0L
  cat(sprintf("%-28s  las_1: %d of %d tree(s) fitted  |  las_2: %d of %d\n",
              sr$label, .n1, length(ellipses_ax_1_valid),
              .n2, length(ellipses_ax_2_valid)))
}

# ── Span report ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The effective window in metres, after the clamps. Where it differs from
# s5_loess_span_m the smoother is NOT doing what was asked, and the stems it
# happened to on are the short or sparse ones - which are also the ones whose
# curves carry least weight later, so it is worth knowing rather than assuming.
if (!is.null(loess_span_diag)) {
  rownames(loess_span_diag) <- NULL
  cat(sprintf("\nEffective span: %.2f - %.2f m (median %.2f) against the %.2f m requested\n",
              min(loess_span_diag$span_m_eff, na.rm = TRUE),
              max(loess_span_diag$span_m_eff, na.rm = TRUE),
              median(loess_span_diag$span_m_eff, na.rm = TRUE),
              s5_loess_span_m))
  .nt <- table(loess_span_diag$note)
  cat(sprintf("  %s\n", paste(sprintf("%s: %d", names(.nt), as.integer(.nt)),
                              collapse = " | ")))
  .wide <- loess_span_diag[loess_span_diag$note != "as set", , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(.wide) > 0L) {
    cat(sprintf("  affected stems: %s\n",
                paste(sort(unique(.wide$TreeID)), collapse = ", ")))
  }

  # How much of each curve is interpolation rather than extrapolation. A curve
  # covering well under 1 has ends carried out beyond its own data - readable,
  # but not measured.
  .short <- loess_span_diag[!is.na(loess_span_diag$cover) &
                            loess_span_diag$cover < 0.95, , drop = FALSE]
  cat(sprintf("  data coverage of the trimmed range: median %.2f | %d curve(s) below 0.95\n",
              median(loess_span_diag$cover, na.rm = TRUE), nrow(.short)))
  if (nrow(.short) > 0L) {
    .ss <- sort(table(.short$signal), decreasing = TRUE)
    cat(sprintf("    worst signals: %s\n",
                paste(sprintf("%s (%d)", names(.ss), as.integer(.ss))[seq_len(min(4L, length(.ss)))],
                      collapse = " | ")))
  }
}

# ── Export the pair set to every signal ───────────────────────────────────────
# One object per signal, so the per-signal manual removal in Step 3.12 can
# diverge from it without touching the others.
.pairs_for_signals <- if (exists("pairs_coverage_ok")) pairs_coverage_ok else {
  # The coverage filter that produced pairs_coverage_ok is not present in this
  # document. Falling back to the fitted set keeps the pipeline running and says
  # so, rather than failing here with an object-not-found several steps away
  # from the missing chunk.
  cat("\nNote: pairs_coverage_ok not found - using pairs_ax_fitted as the pair set for every signal.\n")
  pairs_ax_fitted
}
for (sig_key in names(s5_signal_registry)) {
  assign(paste0("pairs_chosen_", sig_key), .pairs_for_signals, envir = .stage_env())
}
```

### Vis - LOESS curves for all signals and pairs

```{r}
#| label: params-fig-loess-curves-all-signals
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Render LOESS curve galleries for all signals and pairs, coloured by pair outcome"


# ── Which signals to render ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The registry now holds 13 signals, not 5, and each one is a full gallery of
# ggplot panels encoded to base64 - so rendering everything is roughly three
# times the work it used to be. NULL renders all of them; name a subset while
# iterating on the geometry signals and leave the eight protrusion sectors for
# when you actually want to read them.
s5_vis_signals <- NULL      # e.g. c("area", "sa", "sb") or NULL for all

.par_apply("params-fig-loess-curves-all-signals")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-loess-curves-all-signals
#| code-summary: "Render LOESS curve galleries for all signals and pairs, coloured by pair outcome"

.vis_keys <- if (is.null(s5_vis_signals)) names(s5_signal_registry) else
               intersect(s5_vis_signals, names(s5_signal_registry))
if (length(.vis_keys) == 0L)
  stop("[vis LOESS] s5_vis_signals matched no signal in s5_signal_registry.")

# ── Pair outcome ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Derived here rather than read from pair_filter_status, which no longer exists:
# it was written by the coverage-filter step, and so were the three outcomes the
# old legend named (the 1 m invalid-range filter, the valid-range-sum MAD and
# the longest-invalid-gap MAD). Under the current pipeline a pair leaves for one
# of exactly two reasons, both recorded upstream:
#
# trimmed out - Step 3.7 cut a stem back to no ellipses at all, meaning it
# had no continuous section to protect
# no ellipses - Step 3.9 dropped the pair because one side finished with
# nothing, whether from cleaning or from trimming
#
# Deriving it here keeps the figure honest when those steps are re-tuned: change
# a trim threshold and the panel colours follow, with nothing to regenerate.
.emptied <- function(diag) if (is.null(diag)) character(0) else
              as.character(diag$TreeID[diag$kept_after == 0L])
.gone_1 <- .emptied(if (exists("trim_diag_ax_1")) trim_diag_ax_1 else NULL)
.gone_2 <- .emptied(if (exists("trim_diag_ax_2")) trim_diag_ax_2 else NULL)

.fitted_key <- paste(pairs_ax_fitted$TreeID_1, pairs_ax_fitted$TreeID_2)

pair_vis_status <- data.frame(
  TreeID_1 = pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_1,
  TreeID_2 = pairs_axis_ok$TreeID_2,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
pair_vis_status$status <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pair_vis_status)), function(i) {
  t1 <- as.character(pair_vis_status$TreeID_1[i])
  t2 <- as.character(pair_vis_status$TreeID_2[i])
  if (paste(t1, t2) %in% .fitted_key)      return("Kept")
  if (t1 %in% .gone_1 || t2 %in% .gone_2)  return("Dropped: trimmed to nothing")
  "Dropped: no surviving ellipses"
}, character(1))

s5_status_colours <- c(
  "Dropped: trimmed to nothing"    = scales::alpha("red",    0.35),
  "Dropped: no surviving ellipses" = scales::alpha("orange", 0.35),
  "Kept"                           = "white"
)

cat(sprintf("Pair outcomes: %s\n",
            paste(sprintf("%s %d", names(table(pair_vis_status$status)),
                          as.integer(table(pair_vis_status$status))),
                  collapse = " | ")))

# ── Panel builder ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
make_pair_signal_plot <- function(tid1, tid2,
                                  by_tid_1, by_tid_2,
                                  pred_col,
                                  raw_list_1, raw_list_2,
                                  field, y_lab,
                                  panel_fill = "white",
                                  y_fixed    = NULL,
                                  y_ref      = NA_real_) {

  tid1_chr <- as.character(tid1)
  tid2_chr <- as.character(tid2)

  c1 <- by_tid_1[[tid1_chr]]
  c2 <- by_tid_2[[tid2_chr]]
  if (is.null(c1) && is.null(c2)) return(NULL)

  df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    if (!is.null(c1)) tibble::tibble(h = c1$h, pred = c1[[pred_col]], cloud = "las_1"),
    if (!is.null(c2)) tibble::tibble(h = c2$h, pred = c2[[pred_col]], cloud = "las_2")
  ) |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(pred))

  raw1 <- raw_list_1[[tid1_chr]]
  raw2 <- raw_list_2[[tid2_chr]]

  pts_list <- list()
  if (!is.null(raw1) && field %in% names(raw1))
    pts_list[["1"]] <- tibble::tibble(h = raw1$stem_len, val = raw1[[field]],
                                      cloud = "las_1")
  if (!is.null(raw2) && field %in% names(raw2))
    pts_list[["2"]] <- tibble::tibble(h = raw2$stem_len, val = raw2[[field]],
                                      cloud = "las_2")

  pts <- if (length(pts_list) > 0L)
    dplyr::bind_rows(pts_list) |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(val))
  else
    tibble::tibble(h = numeric(0), val = numeric(0), cloud = character(0))

  # ── Valid-region shading, from the trim ranges ─────────────────────────────
  # trim_range_ax_* replaces the old vr1 / vr2. It is ONE interval per stem
  # rather than the several the old shading loop enumerated, because trimming
  # produces a single surviving span by construction - so the overlap is a
  # plain intersection instead of a search over region pairs.
  .band <- function(rng, tid) {
    if (is.null(rng)) return(NULL)
    r <- rng[as.character(rng$TreeID) == as.character(tid), , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(r) == 0L || is.na(r$s_lo[1]) || is.na(r$s_hi[1])) return(NULL)
    c(r$s_lo[1], r$s_hi[1])
  }
  b1 <- .band(if (exists("trim_range_ax_1")) trim_range_ax_1 else NULL, tid1)
  b2 <- .band(if (exists("trim_range_ax_2")) trim_range_ax_2 else NULL, tid2)

  shade_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    if (!is.null(b1)) tibble::tibble(bot = b1[1], top = b1[2], shade = "blue"),
    if (!is.null(b2)) tibble::tibble(bot = b2[1], top = b2[2], shade = "red")
  )
  if (!is.null(b1) && !is.null(b2)) {
    lo <- max(b1[1], b2[1]); hi <- min(b1[2], b2[2])
    if (hi > lo)
      shade_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
        shade_df, tibble::tibble(bot = lo, top = hi, shade = "purple"))
  }

  # ── Subtitle: angular difference and pair-axis tilt ────────────────────────
  ang_row <- angular_diag[angular_diag$TreeID_1 == tid1 &
                          angular_diag$TreeID_2 == tid2, ]
  ax <- pair_axis_list[[tid1_chr]]
  axis_tilt_deg <- if (!is.null(ax) && !any(is.na(ax)))
    acos(pmax(-1, pmin(1, abs(ax[3L]) / sqrt(sum(ax^2))))) * 180 / pi else NA_real_

  subtitle_str <- if (nrow(ang_row) > 0L) {
    sprintf("3D ang. diff: %s  |  tilt diff: %s  |  axis tilt: %s",
            if (is.na(ang_row$angle_deg[1L]))      "NA" else sprintf("%.3f\u00b0", ang_row$angle_deg[1L]),
            if (is.na(ang_row$tilt_angle_deg[1L])) "NA" else sprintf("%.3f\u00b0", ang_row$tilt_angle_deg[1L]),
            if (is.na(axis_tilt_deg))              "NA" else sprintf("%.3f\u00b0", axis_tilt_deg))
  } else {
    if (is.na(axis_tilt_deg)) "axis tilt: NA" else
      sprintf("axis tilt: %.3f\u00b0", axis_tilt_deg)
  }

  # Each stem's global_stem_origin: the real-world point its axis frame's
  # (0,0,0) back-projects to, so a curve read here can be located in the stand.
  .fmt_origin <- function(raw, lab) {
    if (!is.null(raw) && nrow(raw) > 0L &&
        all(c("global_stem_origin_x", "global_stem_origin_y",
              "global_stem_origin_z") %in% names(raw)))
      sprintf("%s origin: (%.3f, %.3f, %.3f)", lab,
              raw$global_stem_origin_x[1L], raw$global_stem_origin_y[1L],
              raw$global_stem_origin_z[1L])
    else sprintf("%s origin: NA", lab)
  }
  origin_caption <- paste(.fmt_origin(raw1, "las_1"),
                          .fmt_origin(raw2, "las_2"), sep = "   |   ")

  p <- ggplot() +
    { if (nrow(shade_df) > 0L)
        geom_rect(data = shade_df,
                  aes(xmin = bot, xmax = top, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = shade),
                  alpha = 0.25)
    } +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("blue"   = scales::alpha(COL_1,    0.35),
                 "red"    = scales::alpha(COL_2,    0.35),
                 "purple" = scales::alpha("purple", 0.35)),
      name = "Kept range") +
    { if (is.finite(y_ref))
        geom_hline(yintercept = y_ref, linetype = "dashed",
                   colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4)
    } +
    geom_point(data = pts, aes(h, val, colour = cloud),
               size = 1.0, alpha = 0.25, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_line(data = df, aes(h, pred, colour = cloud),
              linewidth = 0.85, na.rm = TRUE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("las_1" = COL_1, "las_2" = COL_2), name = NULL) +
    labs(title    = sprintf("Pair %s / %s", tid1, tid2),
         subtitle = subtitle_str,
         caption  = origin_caption,
         x = "distance from per stem origin, along axis (m)", y = y_lab) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      plot.title       = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", colour = "grey20"),
      plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 8,  colour = "grey40"),
      plot.caption     = element_text(size = 7,  colour = "grey40"),
      plot.background  = element_rect(fill = panel_fill, colour = NA),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA)
    )

  # coord_cartesian, not scale limits: it clips the view without dropping rows,
  # so a curve that leaves the range still runs to the panel edge rather than
  # breaking.
  if (!is.null(y_fixed)) p <- p + coord_cartesian(ylim = y_fixed)
  p
}

# ── Render one gallery per signal ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Panel background: white = kept, orange = the pair lost its ellipses, red = a
# stem was trimmed to nothing. Excluded pairs are still drawn, because the point
# of showing them is to see WHY they went.
for (sig_key in .vis_keys) {
  sr  <- s5_signal_registry[[sig_key]]
  bt1 <- get(sr$by_tid_1)
  bt2 <- get(sr$by_tid_2)

  # Protrusion sectors share one fixed 0-1 axis and a common baseline line.
  # On a free scale every sector looks equally dramatic - the axis rescales to
  # whatever variation is there - so a genuine bulge cannot be told from normal
  # scatter. The baseline is the stand-wide median of that sector: at
  # s3_prot_outside_tol = 0 it sits near 0.5, because the fit puts the ellipse
  # THROUGH the shell and about half of it falls marginally outside.
  .is_prot <- startsWith(sig_key, "prot_")
  .y_fixed <- if (.is_prot) c(0, 1) else NULL
  .y_ref   <- if (.is_prot) {
    vv <- unlist(c(lapply(ellipses_ax_1_valid, function(d) d[[sr$field]]),
                   lapply(ellipses_ax_2_valid, function(d) d[[sr$field]])))
    suppressWarnings(median(vv, na.rm = TRUE))
  } else NA_real_

  plots_all <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(pair_vis_status)), function(i) {
    make_pair_signal_plot(
      pair_vis_status$TreeID_1[i], pair_vis_status$TreeID_2[i],
      bt1, bt2, sr$pred_col,
      ellipses_ax_1_valid, ellipses_ax_2_valid,
      sr$field, sr$y_lab,
      panel_fill = s5_status_colours[[pair_vis_status$status[i]]],
      y_fixed    = .y_fixed,
      y_ref      = .y_ref)
  })
  names(plots_all) <- paste0("Pair ", pair_vis_status$TreeID_1,
                             "/", pair_vis_status$TreeID_2)

  # A pair with no curve on either side yields NULL. Passing that to the
  # gallery leaves a hole with a label and no picture; dropping it is clearer.
  plots_all <- plots_all[!vapply(plots_all, is.null, logical(1))]
  if (length(plots_all) == 0L) {
    cat(sprintf("%-28s  no renderable pairs.\n", sr$label)); next
  }

  print(browsable(tagList(
    h3(sprintf("LOESS curves \u2014 %s", sr$label)),
    h4(sprintf("%d pair(s) | white = kept, orange = no surviving ellipses, red = trimmed to nothing%s",
               length(plots_all),
               if (.is_prot && is.finite(.y_ref))
                 sprintf(" | dashed = stand median %.2f", .y_ref) else "")),
    render_panel_gallery(plots_all, paste0("s54_", sig_key), ncols = 2L)
  )))
}
```



## 3.12 PM Peak/Trough Identification

```{r}
#| label: params-peaks
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Identify peaks AND troughs on every LOESS curve, filtered by prominence and majesty"


# ── What this does ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# BOTH SIGNS. A trough is as much a feature of a stem as a peak - a hollow, a
# scar, a gap between buttresses - and just as matchable between epochs. Peaks
# and troughs are found together, carry the same fields, and are returned in one
# table with a `type` column, so matching downstream can weigh both kinds of
# candidate at once.
#
# FILTER FIRST, THEN MEASURE. Candidates are screened on a PRELIMINARY majesty -
# the drop, on the raw curve, to the saddle separating them from the nearest
# LARGER extremum of their own kind. Only the survivors are then measured, and
# the measurement is redone using the surviving features ALONE:
# majesty - recomputed from the kept peaks/troughs only, so a feature
# whose larger same-type neighbour was filtered away is
# re-judged against the structure that actually remains.
# major_prominence - the classic prominence: the smaller of the two drops to
# the nearest opposite-type KEPT feature on each side (a
# trough for a peak, a peak for a trough), falling back to
# the curve's opposite global extreme when neither side has
# one. This is exactly what `prominence` used to be.
# minor_prominence - the drop on the OTHER side (the one major_prominence did
# not take). Where that side carries no opposite-type
# feature, the drop to the curve's own minimum (for a peak)
# / maximum (for a trough) over that side.
# majesty, major_prominence and minor_prominence are the quantities the
# candidate scoring in Step 3.13 consumes; majesty_preliminary is retained only
# so the screen that produced the kept set can be audited.
#
# WITHIN TYPE THROUGHOUT. Peaks are judged against peaks and troughs against
# troughs - for the preliminary-majesty screen, for the recomputed majesty, and
# for the separation rule. (Prominence is the one cross-type quantity: a peak's
# prominence is measured to troughs, by definition.)
#
# NO CAP ON THE COUNT. A curve keeps as many candidates as it has that are worth
# keeping.

# ── 1. Parameters ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The majesty threshold is a FRACTION OF THE STRONGEST FEATURE OF THE SAME KIND
# ON THAT CURVE, not an absolute value. The signals are on wildly different
# scales - areas in m^2, offsets in m, protrusion as a fraction - and a curve
# with big features should not be judged by the same absolute bar as a flat one.
# The screen is majesty-only now: the old prominence pre-filter is gone, since
# prominence is no longer computed until after the kept set is settled.
s3_pk_edge_m     <- 0.75   # candidates within this of either end are discarded
s3_pk_maj_frac   <- 0.02   # min PRELIMINARY majesty, as a fraction of that type's best
s3_pk_min_dist_m <- 0.10   # closer than this, the lower-majesty one of a type goes

# Adjacent extrema differing by less than this fraction of the curve's own y
# range are numerical ripple rather than structure. See the pruning step in
# .find_extrema for why this is not optional. 0.002 sits roughly two orders of
# magnitude above the observed jitter and two below the smallest real feature,
# so there is a wide band of settings that behave identically - which is what a
# threshold separating two populations should look like.
s3_pk_ripple_frac <- 0.002

s59_use_parallel <- TRUE

# Seconds to wait for PSOCK workers to call home before giving up and running
# serially. The default (no timeout in the old code) is what turned a failed
# handshake into a stalled run rather than a slow one.
s3_pk_cluster_timeout <- 60

.par_apply("params-peaks")
```

```{r}
#| label: peaks
#| code-summary: "Identify peaks AND troughs on every LOESS curve, filtered by prominence and majesty"

s59_n_cores      <- max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 1L)

p_pm <- list(edge_m      = s3_pk_edge_m,
             maj_frac    = s3_pk_maj_frac,
             min_dist_m  = s3_pk_min_dist_m,
             ripple_frac = s3_pk_ripple_frac)

# R caches the session temp dir path, but Windows (and cleaners) can delete the
# directory itself mid-session; the next thing that writes there - here, a PSOCK
# worker opening its log file - then dies with "cannot open the connection". This
# recreates the cached tempdir if it has gone missing, so the path R hands out is
# always backed by a real directory. tempdir(check = TRUE) does this on R >= 3.5;
# the dir.create is a belt-and-braces fallback for older versions and races.
.ensure_tempdir <- function() {
  td <- tryCatch(tempdir(check = TRUE), error = function(e) tempdir())
  if (!dir.exists(td)) dir.create(td, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  td
}

# ── 2. The extremum finder ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Self-contained: it takes two vectors and a parameter list and references
# nothing else, so it can be shipped to a worker without exporting half the
# environment.
.find_extrema <- function(h, y, p) {

  ok <- is.finite(h) & is.finite(y)
  h <- h[ok]; y <- y[ok]
  n <- length(y)
  empty <- tibble::tibble(type = character(0), h = numeric(0), value = numeric(0),
                          majesty_preliminary = numeric(0), majesty = numeric(0),
                          major_prominence = numeric(0), minor_prominence = numeric(0),
                          residual = numeric(0))
  if (n < 5L) return(empty)

  # ---- candidates: strictly above / below both immediate neighbours ---------
  # The rule as stated, and nothing more. A run of exactly equal values yields
  # no candidate, which is correct by this definition - a flat top is not higher
  # than both its neighbours.
  i_int <- seq.int(2L, n - 1L)
  pk_i  <- i_int[y[i_int] > y[i_int - 1L] & y[i_int] > y[i_int + 1L]]
  tr_i  <- i_int[y[i_int] < y[i_int - 1L] & y[i_int] < y[i_int + 1L]]
  if (length(pk_i) + length(tr_i) == 0L) return(empty)

  ex <- data.frame(idx  = c(pk_i, tr_i),
                   type = c(rep("peak", length(pk_i)), rep("trough", length(tr_i))),
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  ex <- ex[order(ex$idx), , drop = FALSE]
  ex$h     <- h[ex$idx]
  ex$value <- y[ex$idx]
  n_raw <- nrow(ex)

  # ---- collapse numerical ripples ------------------------------------------
  # predict.loess with surface = "direct" evaluates each grid point on its own,
  # and at 1 cm spacing that leaves alternating ripples of order 1e-5 on a
  # signal whose real features are 1e-2. A 15 m curve produces dozens of them.
  #
  # Leaving them in does far more than clutter the output. Prominence is the
  # drop to the NEAREST opposite-type extremum, so a ripple three centimetres
  # from a genuine peak becomes that peak's reference and its prominence
  # collapses from centimetres to microns. Every real feature then fails a bar
  # set by whichever one happened to have no ripple beside it. Majesty is immune
  # - it walks the whole curve to find larger terrain - which is why a curve can
  # show a peak with majesty 1.7e-2 and prominence 5e-5 at the same time. That
  # disagreement is the signature of this problem.
  #
  # Adjacent pairs are removed smallest-difference-first until nothing below the
  # floor remains. Removing a PAIR is what makes this correct rather than a
  # smoothing hack: deleting a peak together with its neighbouring trough leaves
  # the alternation intact and reconnects the two real features the ripple was
  # sitting between - which is exactly the relationship prominence needs.
  .rip <- p$ripple_frac * diff(range(y))
  repeat {
    if (nrow(ex) < 2L) break
    d <- abs(diff(ex$value))
    j <- which.min(d)
    if (d[j] >= .rip) break
    ex <- ex[-c(j, j + 1L), , drop = FALSE]
  }
  if (nrow(ex) == 0L) return(empty)
  n_pruned <- nrow(ex)

  # ---- edge exclusion ------------------------------------------------------
  # Before anything is measured. A candidate within edge_m of either end is not
  # a candidate at all, so it takes no part in the prominence or majesty of the
  # ones that remain: with it gone, its neighbour's nearest opposite-type
  # extremum is the next one inward.
  span <- range(h)
  ex <- ex[ex$h - span[1] >= p$edge_m & span[2] - ex$h >= p$edge_m, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(ex) == 0L) return(empty)

  # The curve's own global extremes are still taken from the WHOLE curve. They
  # are properties of the signal, not of the candidate pool, and majesty's
  # fallback is defined against them.
  y_min <- min(y); y_max <- max(y)

  # ---- majesty_preliminary (screening only) --------------------------------
  # The screen that decides which candidates survive. Walk out from the extremum
  # along the RAW curve until it is exceeded - a taller peak for a peak, a deeper
  # trough for a trough - and take the most extreme point of the terrain crossed
  # on the way as the saddle. That is what separates this feature from the larger
  # one. Where larger terrain lies on BOTH sides, take the higher saddle for a
  # peak (the lower for a trough): the smaller, conservative answer, and the
  # standard topographic convention. With no larger peer in either direction the
  # extremum is the curve's own global one, and majesty is measured to the
  # opposite global extreme.
  #
  # This is the SAME calculation the old `majesty` performed. It is now only a
  # screen: the majesty carried on each kept row (below) is recomputed from the
  # survivors, so it is renamed to make the two roles unmistakable.
  m <- nrow(ex)
  ex$majesty_preliminary <- vapply(seq_len(m), function(i) {
    k  <- ex$idx[i]; v <- y[k]
    up <- ex$type[i] == "peak"

    j_l <- if (k > 1L)  { w <- which(if (up) y[1:(k - 1L)] > v else y[1:(k - 1L)] < v)
                          if (length(w)) max(w) else NA_integer_ } else NA_integer_
    j_r <- if (k < n)   { w <- which(if (up) y[(k + 1L):n] > v else y[(k + 1L):n] < v)
                          if (length(w)) k + min(w) else NA_integer_ } else NA_integer_

    col_l <- if (!is.na(j_l)) (if (up) min(y[j_l:k]) else max(y[j_l:k])) else NA_real_
    col_r <- if (!is.na(j_r)) (if (up) min(y[k:j_r]) else max(y[k:j_r])) else NA_real_

    cols <- c(col_l, col_r); cols <- cols[!is.na(cols)]
    key <- if (!length(cols)) (if (up) y_min else y_max)
           else if (up) max(cols) else min(cols)
    abs(v - key)
  }, numeric(1))

  # ---- relative threshold, WITHIN each type --------------------------------
  # Peaks are judged against the strongest peak, troughs against the deepest
  # trough, on preliminary majesty. Pooling the two would let one type set the
  # bar for the other, and they are not on comparable footing: a curve with one
  # dominant peak and a set of shallow troughs would see every trough measured
  # against that peak and struck out, even though those troughs are the whole
  # trough structure the curve has.
  #
  # The consequence, stated plainly: a curve with even one weak trough keeps at
  # least that trough, because it is by definition 100% of the greatest trough
  # on the curve. Same for peaks. This threshold decides which features of a
  # kind are worth keeping, not whether a kind is present at all.
  .keep_type <- function(d) {
    if (nrow(d) == 0L) return(d)
    mm <- max(d$majesty_preliminary, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (!is.finite(mm) || mm <= 0) return(d)
    d[d$majesty_preliminary >= p$maj_frac * mm, , drop = FALSE]
  }
  ex <- rbind(.keep_type(ex[ex$type == "peak",   , drop = FALSE]),
              .keep_type(ex[ex$type == "trough", , drop = FALSE]))
  if (nrow(ex) == 0L) return(empty)
  ex <- ex[order(ex$h), , drop = FALSE]

  # ---- separation, WITHIN each type ----------------------------------------
  # Greedy by preliminary majesty: the most majestic candidate of a type is
  # taken, others of the SAME type within min_dist_m are dropped, and so on down.
  #
  # Peaks and troughs are separated independently, so a peak and a trough close
  # together both survive. They are different features - a narrow notch beside a
  # ridge is a notch and a ridge - and they will be matched against different
  # candidates downstream, so suppressing one because the other is nearby would
  # discard a real observation rather than a duplicate.
  .thin <- function(d) {
    if (nrow(d) <= 1L) return(d)
    d <- d[order(-d$majesty_preliminary), , drop = FALSE]
    keep <- logical(nrow(d))
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(d)))
      if (!any(keep) || all(abs(d$h[keep] - d$h[i]) >= p$min_dist_m)) keep[i] <- TRUE
    d[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  }
  ex <- rbind(.thin(ex[ex$type == "peak", , drop = FALSE]),
              .thin(ex[ex$type == "trough", , drop = FALSE]))
  ex <- ex[order(ex$h), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(ex) == 0L) return(empty)

  # ==========================================================================
  # `ex` is now the KEPT set. majesty, major_prominence and minor_prominence are
  # (re)computed from these survivors alone - the values Step 3.13 scores on.
  # ==========================================================================
  m    <- nrow(ex)
  vals <- ex$value
  typ  <- ex$type

  # ---- majesty (kept-only) -------------------------------------------------
  # The same notion as the preliminary majesty, but the "terrain" is now just
  # the kept features rather than the raw curve: walk out along the kept
  # sequence until a LARGER same-type feature is met, taking the most extreme
  # kept feature crossed on the way (a trough for a peak) as the saddle. A
  # feature whose larger neighbour was filtered out is therefore re-judged
  # against what survives. With no larger same-type peer on a side, that side
  # offers no saddle; with none on either side, fall back to the deepest kept
  # trough (peak) / highest kept peak (trough), or the curve's global extreme
  # if the opposite type is absent from the kept set entirely.
  ex$majesty <- vapply(seq_len(m), function(i) {
    up <- typ[i] == "peak"; v <- vals[i]
    opp     <- vals[typ != typ[i]]
    opp_ref <- if (length(opp)) (if (up) min(opp) else max(opp))
               else (if (up) y_min else y_max)
    side_col <- function(idxs) {
      run <- NA_real_; found <- FALSE
      for (k in idxs) {
        taller <- if (up) vals[k] > v else vals[k] < v
        if (taller) { found <- TRUE; break }
        run <- if (is.na(run)) vals[k] else if (up) min(run, vals[k]) else max(run, vals[k])
      }
      if (found) run else NA_real_   # NA: no larger peer, or an adjacent one with nothing between
    }
    cl   <- side_col(rev(seq_len(i - 1L)))
    cr   <- side_col(if (i < m) seq.int(i + 1L, m) else integer(0))
    cols <- c(cl, cr); cols <- cols[!is.na(cols)]
    key  <- if (length(cols)) (if (up) max(cols) else min(cols)) else opp_ref
    abs(v - key)
  }, numeric(1))

  # ---- major & minor prominence (kept-only) --------------------------------
  # major_prominence: the classic prominence - the lesser of the drops to the
  # nearest opposite-type KEPT feature on each side; the side achieving that
  # lesser drop is the "major" side. When only one side carries an opposite-type
  # feature, that side's drop is used; when neither does, the drop to the curve's
  # opposite global extreme.
  #
  # minor_prominence: the drop on the OTHER side. When that other side carries an
  # opposite-type feature, the drop to it; otherwise the drop to the curve's own
  # minimum (peak) / maximum (trough) over that side. When neither side carries
  # an opposite-type feature, minor_prominence equals major_prominence.
  .prom <- t(vapply(seq_len(m), function(i) {
    up <- typ[i] == "peak"; v <- vals[i]; k <- ex$idx[i]
    opp <- which(typ != typ[i])
    lft <- opp[ex$h[opp] < ex$h[i]]; rgt <- opp[ex$h[opp] > ex$h[i]]
    nl  <- if (length(lft)) lft[which.max(ex$h[lft])] else NA_integer_
    nr  <- if (length(rgt)) rgt[which.min(ex$h[rgt])] else NA_integer_
    drop_l <- if (!is.na(nl)) abs(v - vals[nl]) else NA_real_
    drop_r <- if (!is.na(nr)) abs(v - vals[nr]) else NA_real_

    if (!is.na(drop_l) || !is.na(drop_r)) {
      if (is.na(drop_r) || (!is.na(drop_l) && drop_l <= drop_r)) {
        major <- drop_l; major_side <- "left"
      } else {
        major <- drop_r; major_side <- "right"
      }
    } else {
      major <- abs(v - if (up) y_min else y_max); major_side <- NA_character_
    }

    minor <- if (is.na(major_side)) {
      major
    } else if (major_side == "left") {
      if (!is.na(drop_r)) drop_r else abs(v - if (up) min(y[k:n]) else max(y[k:n]))
    } else {
      if (!is.na(drop_l)) drop_l else abs(v - if (up) min(y[1:k]) else max(y[1:k]))
    }
    c(major, minor)
  }, numeric(2)))
  ex$major_prominence <- .prom[, 1]
  ex$minor_prominence <- .prom[, 2]

  # ---- record --------------------------------------------------------------
  # residual is the signed departure from the curve's arithmetic mean, which
  # says whether a feature sits above or below the stem's typical value - a peak
  # can be a peak and still lie below the mean.
  out <- tibble::tibble(
    type                = ex$type,
    h                   = ex$h,
    value               = ex$value,
    majesty_preliminary = ex$majesty_preliminary,
    majesty             = ex$majesty,
    major_prominence    = ex$major_prominence,
    minor_prominence    = ex$minor_prominence,
    residual            = ex$value - mean(y)
  )
  # Carried so the pruning can be audited in aggregate rather than trusted.
  attr(out, "n_raw")    <- n_raw
  attr(out, "n_pruned") <- n_pruned
  out
}

# ── 3. Self-contained worker ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
.run_peak_job <- function(job) {
  tryCatch({
    run_one <- function(curve, pred_col, origin_z, az) {
      if (is.null(curve) || !(pred_col %in% names(curve))) return(NULL)
      ex <- .find_extrema(curve$h, curve[[pred_col]], job$p)
      keep_attr <- attributes(ex)[c("n_raw", "n_pruned")]
      if (nrow(ex) == 0L) return(ex)
      origin <- if ("stem_len_origin" %in% names(curve))
                  curve$stem_len_origin[1L] else NA_real_
      ex$h_abs <- ex$h + origin
      # Global Z of the feature: the stem origin's Z plus the along-axis
      # distance projected onto vertical. az is the pair axis's Z component,
      # and the axis always points upward, so az is cos(tilt) directly.
      ex$global_z <- if (!is.na(origin_z) && !is.na(az)) origin_z + ex$h * az
                     else NA_real_
      attributes(ex)[names(keep_attr)] <- keep_attr
      ex
    }
    list(e1 = run_one(job$c1, job$pred_col, job$origin1_z, job$az),
         e2 = run_one(job$c2, job$pred_col, job$origin2_z, job$az))
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
}

#' Is a PSOCK cluster safe to start in THIS session?
#'
#' It is not, under the batch driver, and that is what hung a run at signal 1 of
#' 13 with no error and no progress. makeCluster(outfile = "") on Windows hands
#' the workers this process's stdout/stderr; the driver holds a sink() on both,
#' so there is no console for them to attach to and the master waits for a
#' handshake that never arrives. No timeout, no error - just a stopped run.
#'
#' The gate is therefore: only cluster when nothing is sunk. A batch pays for
#' this in wall time on one step; a stalled overnight run costs the whole thing.
.pk_cluster_ok <- function() {
  isTRUE(s59_use_parallel) && s59_n_cores > 1L &&
    sink.number() == 0L && sink.number(type = "message") == 0L
}

#' One cluster for the whole chunk, not one per signal.
#'
#' The old code started and stopped a cluster inside every call - thirteen
#' start-ups per epoch, each costing seconds and each another chance to hang.
.pk_cl <- NULL
.pk_cluster <- function() {
  if (!is.null(.pk_cl)) return(.pk_cl)
  .ensure_tempdir()
  # A real file, not "": worker output has somewhere to go that does not depend
  # on a console this process may not own. The path is printed so a worker error
  # can still be read afterwards.
  .of <- file.path(tempdir(), "peaks_workers.log")
  cl  <- tryCatch(
    parallel::makeCluster(s59_n_cores, outfile = .of,
                          setup_timeout = s3_pk_cluster_timeout),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(cl)) {
    cat(sprintf("  [3.12] cluster start-up failed - running serially. Worker log: %s\n", .of))
    return(NULL)
  }
  parallel::clusterExport(cl, varlist = c(".run_peak_job", ".find_extrema"),
                          envir = .stage_env())
  cat(sprintf("  [3.12] cluster up: %d worker(s) | worker log: %s\n", s59_n_cores, .of))
  .pk_cl <<- cl
  cl
}

.apply_peaks_parallel <- function(X, FUN) {
  if (length(X) == 0L) return(list())
  if (!.pk_cluster_ok()) return(lapply(X, FUN))
  .ensure_tempdir()

  if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") {
    cl <- .pk_cluster()
    if (is.null(cl)) return(lapply(X, FUN))
    tryCatch(parallel::parLapply(cl, X, FUN),
             error = function(e) {
               cat(sprintf("  [3.12] parLapply failed (%s) - running serially.\n",
                           conditionMessage(e)))
               lapply(X, FUN)
             })
  } else {
    parallel::mclapply(X, FUN, mc.cores = s59_n_cores)
  }
}

# ── 4. Run over every signal ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
if (!requireNamespace("cli", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("cli")

# Guard the temp dir once up front too, so anything in this chunk that writes to
# tempdir() (cli, tibble, the workers) has a real directory to write into.
.ensure_tempdir()

# kept_pairs came from the manual-removal step, which has been removed. The
# fitted pair set is the current equivalent.
.pk_pairs <- if (exists("kept_pairs")) kept_pairs else pairs_ax_fitted

n_signals <- length(s5_signal_registry)
# cat, not cli: cli writes to stderr, which the batch driver sinks to the log -
# so under a batch this header, and the PAIR COUNT in it, were invisible exactly
# when they were wanted. The signal count and the pair count are different
# numbers and easy to confuse: the progress bar below counts SIGNALS.
cat(sprintf(paste0("\n3.12 Peak and trough identification\n",
                   "  %d signal(s) x %d pair(s) | %s\n",
                   "  ripple floor %.0f%% of range | edge %.2f m | preliminary majesty >= %.0f%% | separation %.2f m\n"),
            n_signals, nrow(.pk_pairs),
            if (.pk_cluster_ok()) sprintf("%d core(s)", s59_n_cores)
            else sprintf("serial (%s)", if (isTRUE(s59_use_parallel))
                           "output is redirected - see .pk_cluster_ok()" else "s59_use_parallel = FALSE"),
            100 * s3_pk_ripple_frac, s3_pk_edge_m, 100 * s3_pk_maj_frac,
            s3_pk_min_dist_m))

pm_extrema_summary <- NULL

# One tick per SIGNAL, not per pair: the inner apply is handed to
# parallel::mclapply, and a worker cannot update a bar in the parent process.
# Thirteen ticks is coarse, but it is the finest granularity that reports
# honestly rather than jumping to 100% the moment the jobs are dispatched.
.pb_pk <- .pb_new(length(s5_signal_registry), "3.12 peaks/troughs")

for (sig_key in names(s5_signal_registry)) {

  .pb_tick(.pb_pk)

  sr  <- s5_signal_registry[[sig_key]]
  bt1 <- get(sr$by_tid_1, envir = .stage_env())
  bt2 <- get(sr$by_tid_2, envir = .stage_env())

  tids_1  <- as.character(.pk_pairs$TreeID_1)
  tids_2  <- as.character(.pk_pairs$TreeID_2)
  n_pairs <- nrow(.pk_pairs)

  peak_jobs <- lapply(seq_len(n_pairs), function(i) {
    t1c <- tids_1[i]; t2c <- tids_2[i]
    ax_i <- pair_axis_list[[t1c]]
    az_i <- if (!is.null(ax_i) && !any(is.na(ax_i))) ax_i[3L] else NA_real_
    e1 <- ellipses_ax_1_valid[[t1c]]; e2 <- ellipses_ax_2_valid[[t2c]]
    .oz <- function(e) if (!is.null(e) && nrow(e) > 0L &&
                           "global_stem_origin_z" %in% names(e))
                         e$global_stem_origin_z[1L] else NA_real_
    list(c1 = bt1[[t1c]], c2 = bt2[[t2c]], pred_col = sr$pred_col,
         p = p_pm, az = az_i, origin1_z = .oz(e1), origin2_z = .oz(e2))
  })

  results <- .apply_peaks_parallel(peak_jobs, .run_peak_job)

  peaks_1 <- setNames(lapply(results, function(r) if (is.null(r)) NULL else r$e1), tids_1)
  peaks_2 <- setNames(lapply(results, function(r) if (is.null(r)) NULL else r$e2), tids_2)

  assign(paste0("peaks_1_", sig_key), peaks_1, envir = .stage_env())
  assign(paste0("peaks_2_", sig_key), peaks_2, envir = .stage_env())

  .count <- function(lst, ty) sum(vapply(lst, function(d)
    if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L) 0L else sum(d$type == ty), integer(1)))
  .withany <- function(lst) sum(vapply(lst, function(d)
    !is.null(d) && nrow(d) > 0L, logical(1)))
  .att <- function(lst, a) sum(vapply(lst, function(d) {
    v <- attr(d, a); if (is.null(v)) 0L else as.integer(v) }, integer(1)))

  pm_extrema_summary <- rbind(pm_extrema_summary, data.frame(
    signal    = sr$label,
    key       = sig_key,
    raw       = .att(peaks_1, "n_raw")    + .att(peaks_2, "n_raw"),
    depruned  = .att(peaks_1, "n_pruned") + .att(peaks_2, "n_pruned"),
    trees_1   = .withany(peaks_1), trees_2 = .withany(peaks_2),
    peaks_1   = .count(peaks_1, "peak"),   troughs_1 = .count(peaks_1, "trough"),
    peaks_2   = .count(peaks_2, "peak"),   troughs_2 = .count(peaks_2, "trough"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
}

.pb_done(.pb_pk)

# One cluster for the chunk means one place to shut it down. Left running, its
# workers would hold their share of memory for the rest of the pair.
if (!is.null(.pk_cl)) { try(parallel::stopCluster(.pk_cl), silent = TRUE); .pk_cl <- NULL }

rownames(pm_extrema_summary) <- NULL
cat("\nExtrema found per signal (raw = before ripple pruning, depruned = after):\n")
print(pm_extrema_summary, row.names = FALSE)

# The raw-to-depruned drop is the check that matters most here. A large drop is
# expected and healthy - it is the loess grid jitter being removed. A drop of
# near zero means the ripple floor is doing nothing and prominence is still
# being measured against jitter; a drop that also takes the final counts to
# almost nothing means the floor has been set above the real features.
.tot <- with(pm_extrema_summary, peaks_1 + troughs_1 + peaks_2 + troughs_2)
cat(sprintf("\nRipple pruning removed %d of %d raw candidate(s) (%.0f%%), leaving %d after filtering\n",
            sum(pm_extrema_summary$raw) - sum(pm_extrema_summary$depruned),
            sum(pm_extrema_summary$raw),
            100 * (1 - sum(pm_extrema_summary$depruned) / max(1L, sum(pm_extrema_summary$raw))),
            sum(.tot)))
cat(sprintf("Total %d extremum/extrema | %.1f per curve on average | peak:trough %d:%d\n",
            sum(.tot),
            sum(.tot) / max(1L, 2L * nrow(.pk_pairs) * nrow(pm_extrema_summary)),
            sum(pm_extrema_summary$peaks_1 + pm_extrema_summary$peaks_2),
            sum(pm_extrema_summary$troughs_1 + pm_extrema_summary$troughs_2)))
cat("Stored as peaks_{1|2}_{sig_key}: one tibble per stem with type, h, h_abs, value, majesty_preliminary, majesty, major_prominence, minor_prominence, residual, global_z.\n")
```


### Vis - Curves with peaks

```{r}
#| label: params-fig-loess-peaks-all
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Render LOESS curve galleries with detected peaks and troughs for all signals"


# ── What changed ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The detrended panel is gone: detrending has been removed from the pipeline, so
# there is no second curve to draw and no reason to interleave. One panel per
# pair, and the gallery reads as a plain grid again.
#
# Extrema are now detected ON these curves rather than on a detrended copy, so
# their y values are directly comparable with the line they sit on. The old
# version used only the x position and said so, because a detrended y meant
# nothing on a raw panel; here the marker sits exactly where the feature is.

# Peaks point up, troughs point down. Shape carries the type rather than colour,
# because colour is already spent on the epoch - and the epoch is the comparison
# this figure exists to support.
s3_pk_shape <- c(peak = 24L, trough = 25L)   # filled triangles, up and down

.par_apply("params-fig-loess-peaks-all")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-loess-peaks-all
#| standalone: true
#| fig: false
#| results: asis
#| column: page
#| code-summary: "Render LOESS curve galleries with detected peaks and troughs for all signals"

make_pair_extrema_plot <- function(tid1, tid2, bt1, bt2,
                                   pred_col, field, y_lab,
                                   ex1, ex2) {

  t1c <- as.character(tid1); t2c <- as.character(tid2)
  c1 <- bt1[[t1c]]; c2 <- bt2[[t2c]]
  if (is.null(c1) && is.null(c2)) return(NULL)

  df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    if (!is.null(c1)) tibble::tibble(h = c1$h, pred = c1[[pred_col]], cl = "las_1"),
    if (!is.null(c2)) tibble::tibble(h = c2$h, pred = c2[[pred_col]], cl = "las_2")
  ) |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(pred))
  if (nrow(df) == 0L) return(NULL)

  r1 <- ellipses_ax_1_valid[[t1c]]
  r2 <- ellipses_ax_2_valid[[t2c]]
  pts <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    if (!is.null(r1) && field %in% names(r1))
      tibble::tibble(h = r1$stem_len, val = r1[[field]], cl = "las_1"),
    if (!is.null(r2) && field %in% names(r2))
      tibble::tibble(h = r2$stem_len, val = r2[[field]], cl = "las_2")
  ) |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(val))

  # Both epochs' extrema in one frame, so a single geom draws them and the
  # shape scale is shared rather than declared twice.
  .ex <- function(ex, cl) {
    if (is.null(ex) || nrow(ex) == 0L) return(NULL)
    tibble::tibble(h = ex$h, val = ex$value, type = ex$type,
                   prom = ex$major_prominence, cl = cl)
  }
  exd <- dplyr::bind_rows(.ex(ex1, "las_1"), .ex(ex2, "las_2"))

  # The vertical rule locates the feature along the stem, which is what the
  # matching downstream works on; the marker gives its value. Keeping both means
  # a feature can be read off the x axis without tracing back to the curve.
  gg <- ggplot() +
    geom_point(data = pts, aes(h, val, colour = cl), size = 0.9, alpha = 0.2,
               na.rm = TRUE) +
    { if (!is.null(exd) && nrow(exd) > 0L)
        geom_vline(data = exd, aes(xintercept = h, colour = cl),
                   linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.35)
    } +
    geom_line(data = df, aes(h, pred, colour = cl), linewidth = 0.85,
              na.rm = TRUE) +
    { if (!is.null(exd) && nrow(exd) > 0L)
        geom_point(data = exd, aes(h, val, shape = type, fill = cl, size = prom),
                   colour = "grey20", stroke = 0.5, alpha = 0.95)
    } +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(las_1 = COL_1, las_2 = COL_2), name = NULL) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(las_1 = COL_1, las_2 = COL_2), guide = "none") +
    scale_shape_manual(values = s3_pk_shape, name = NULL,
                       labels = c(peak = "peak", trough = "trough")) +
    # Marker area tracks major prominence, so the strong features read as strong at a
    # glance. range() is deliberately narrow: this is a cue, not a measurement,
    # and a wide range would make a weak feature invisible rather than small.
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.8, 4.2), guide = "none") +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = range(df$h, na.rm = TRUE)) +
    labs(title    = sprintf("Pair %s / %s", tid1, tid2),
         subtitle = sprintf("las_1: %d peak(s), %d trough(s)  |  las_2: %d, %d",
                            sum(exd$cl == "las_1" & exd$type == "peak"),
                            sum(exd$cl == "las_1" & exd$type == "trough"),
                            sum(exd$cl == "las_2" & exd$type == "peak"),
                            sum(exd$cl == "las_2" & exd$type == "trough")),
         x = "distance from per stem origin, along axis (m)", y = y_lab) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8, colour = "grey40"),
          legend.position = "top")
  gg
}

# ── Render ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# kept_pairs came from the manual-removal step, which has been removed.
.pk_pairs_vis <- if (exists("kept_pairs")) kept_pairs else pairs_ax_fitted

# Thirteen signals is a lot of gallery. The LOESS figure's s5_vis_signals is
# reused when it exists, so both figures narrow together.
.vis_keys <- if (exists("s5_vis_signals") && !is.null(s5_vis_signals))
               intersect(s5_vis_signals, names(s5_signal_registry)) else
               names(s5_signal_registry)

for (sig_key in .vis_keys) {
  sr  <- s5_signal_registry[[sig_key]]
  bt1 <- get(sr$by_tid_1, envir = .stage_env())
  bt2 <- get(sr$by_tid_2, envir = .stage_env())
  ex1 <- get(paste0("peaks_1_", sig_key), envir = .stage_env())
  ex2 <- get(paste0("peaks_2_", sig_key), envir = .stage_env())

  plots <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(.pk_pairs_vis)), function(i) {
    t1c <- as.character(.pk_pairs_vis$TreeID_1[i])
    t2c <- as.character(.pk_pairs_vis$TreeID_2[i])
    make_pair_extrema_plot(
      .pk_pairs_vis$TreeID_1[i], .pk_pairs_vis$TreeID_2[i],
      bt1, bt2, sr$pred_col, sr$field, sr$y_lab,
      ex1 = ex1[[t1c]], ex2 = ex2[[t2c]])
  })
  names(plots) <- sprintf("Pair %s / %s",
                          .pk_pairs_vis$TreeID_1, .pk_pairs_vis$TreeID_2)
  plots <- plots[!vapply(plots, is.null, logical(1))]
  if (length(plots) == 0L) next

  .tot <- function(lst, ty) sum(vapply(lst, function(d)
    if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L) 0L else sum(d$type == ty), integer(1)))

  print(htmltools::browsable(htmltools::tagList(
    htmltools::h3(sprintf("Step 3.12 \u2014 %s: LOESS curves with detected peaks and troughs",
                          sr$label)),
    htmltools::p(sprintf(
      "Up triangle = peak, down triangle = trough, marker size = major prominence | blue = las_1, red = las_2 | %d peak(s) and %d trough(s) across %d pair(s)",
      .tot(ex1, "peak") + .tot(ex2, "peak"),
      .tot(ex1, "trough") + .tot(ex2, "trough"), length(plots))),
    render_panel_gallery(plots, paste0("s313ex_", sig_key), ncols = 2L)
  )))
}
```




## 3.13 PM Candidate Scoring

```{r}
#| label: params-peak-candidate-scoring
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Score every peak-peak and trough-trough match candidate across 12 factors (no winner picked here)"


# ── What this does ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# For every temporal pair and every signal, enumerate the match CANDIDATES:
# - each (peak in las_1) x (peak in las_2) within the same curve, and
# - each (trough in las_1) x (trough in las_2) within the same curve.
# Peaks only ever pair with peaks and troughs with troughs. Each candidate
# carries an IMPLIED SHIFT - the las_2 feature's real-world global_z minus the
# las_1 feature's - and is scored across the 12 factors below. NO candidate is
# selected here: Step 3.14 weights these scores and takes a score-weighted
# average of the implied shifts to produce the per-pair-signal shift.
#
# The 12 factors (each in [0,1], each independently clamped; the factors are
# FLAT - none is nested inside another):
# rel_maj_tot mean of the two features' majesty / their curve's max
# same-type majesty clamp [0.10,1.00]
# rel_maj_sim gaussian similarity of those two relative majesties
# (<=0.03 diff -> 1, >=0.50 diff -> ~0) clamp [0.10,1.00]
# rel_majorprom_tot as rel_maj_tot, on major_prominence clamp [0.10,1.00]
# rel_majorprom_sim as rel_maj_sim, on major_prominence clamp [0.10,1.00]
# rel_minorprom_tot as rel_maj_tot, on minor_prominence clamp [0.10,1.00]
# rel_minorprom_sim as rel_maj_sim, on minor_prominence clamp [0.10,1.00]
# pearson cor() of the two curves over +/-0.50 m around the two
# features, mapped by exp(-rate*(1-r)): r=1 -> 1, r=0 ->
# 0.1, negatives decay lower floor 0.001
# slope_agree flatness of the (las_2 - las_1) residual curve over
# +/-pearson_half_m: interpolate both curves onto a common
# grid, subtract, differentiate, and take the SD of that
# derivative - a residual that is flat (identical shapes,
# any vertical offset) has ~0 derivative. That SD is
# normalised by the curves' own mean slope-SD to stay
# scale-free, then mapped as pearson maps (1-r): ratio 0 ->
# 1, ratio 1 -> 0.1 floor 0.001
# median_prox gaussian proximity of this candidate's implied shift to
# the pool median (width = IQR floored 0.01 m; rate 3.0);
# pool < 2 -> midpoint 0.55 clamp [0.10,1.00]
# consensus how strongly other candidates corroborate this one's
# implied shift (1 cm -> 1, ~5 cm -> 0.8, ~10 cm -> ~0.4,
# >=20 cm -> 0), summed then min-max normalised in the pool
# clamp [0.05,1.00]
# left_opp similarity of the spacing to the nearest OPPOSITE-TYPE
# feature on the LEFT of each feature: for a peak candidate
# the nearest trough, for a trough candidate the nearest
# peak (1 cm -> 1, ~5 -> 0.8, ~10 -> 0.6, ~15 -> 0.4). One
# side has such a feature and the other not -> 0.1; neither
# has one -> 0.8 clamp [0.05,1.00]
# right_opp as left_opp, nearest opposite-type feature on the RIGHT
#
# The relative factors read majesty / major_prominence / minor_prominence from
# the Step 3.12 kept-set columns; the max used to normalise is that curve's own
# max of the same kind AND the same type (peaks vs peaks, troughs vs troughs).

# ── 0. Signal toggle ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Defaults to every signal in the registry (5 geometry signals + 8 protrusion
# sectors). Flip an entry FALSE to skip it.
s57_run_flags <- setNames(rep(TRUE, length(s5_signal_registry)),
                          names(s5_signal_registry))

.par_apply("params-peak-candidate-scoring")
```

```{r}
#| label: peak-candidate-scoring
#| code-summary: "Score every peak-peak and trough-trough match candidate across 12 factors (no winner picked here)"

# ── 1. Fixed scoring anchors (NOT weights - weights live in Step 3.14) ─────────
s5_pm_score_params <- list(
  pearson_half_m    = s3_pk_edge_m,    # +/- window for the local Pearson factor
  pearson_rate      = log(10), # decay on (1 - r): r=1 -> 1, r=0 -> 0.1
  pearson_floor     = 0.001,   # floor for a bad / uncomputable correlation
  slope_half_m      = s3_pk_edge_m,    # +/- window for the slope-agreement factor
  slope_rate        = log(10), # decay on the normalised residual-slope SD ratio
  slope_floor       = 0.001,   # floor for a bad / uncomputable slope score
  sim_d_one         = 0.03,   # relative-size difference scored 1
  sim_d_zero        = 0.50,   # relative-size difference scored ~0
  sim_rate          = 3.0,    # gaussian rate for the "similarity" factors
  median_prox_rate  = 3.0,    # gaussian rate for the median-proximity factor
  median_prox_floor = 0.001, median_prox_ceil = 1.00,
  consensus_floor   = 0.001, consensus_ceil = 1.00,
  spacing_floor     = 0.001, spacing_ceil = 1.00,
  rel_tot_floor     = 0.001, rel_tot_ceil = 1.00,
  rel_sim_floor     = 0.001, rel_sim_ceil = 1.00
)

.clamp <- function(x, lo, hi) pmin(hi, pmax(lo, x))

# Gaussian "similarity": flat 1 until d_one, decaying to exp(-rate) (~0.05 at
# rate 3) by d_zero, and below that thereafter. Used by the relative-size
# similarity factors.
.gauss_sim <- function(d, d_one, d_zero, rate = 3.0) {
  if (!is.finite(d)) return(NA_real_)
  if (d <= d_one) return(1)
  x <- (d - d_one) / (d_zero - d_one)
  exp(-rate * x * x)
}

# Consensus proximity decay in METRES. A gaussian fitted so 5 cm -> 0.8 (which
# also puts 10 cm at ~0.41); forced to 1 at/below 1 cm and to 0 at/above 20 cm
# to honour the stated end points. Vectorised.
.consensus_decay <- function(d) {
  k <- -log(0.8) / (0.05^2)          # ~89.26
  s <- exp(-k * d * d)
  s[d <= 0.01] <- 1
  s[d >= 0.20] <- 0
  s
}

# Spacing-similarity decay in METRES. Linear (slope 4 / m) through the stated
# anchors 5 cm -> 0.8, 10 cm -> 0.6, 15 cm -> 0.4; flat 1 at/below 1 cm; floored
# at 0 (the [0.05,1.00] clamp is applied by the caller). Vectorised.
.spacing_decay <- function(d) {
  s <- 1 - 4 * d
  s[d <= 0.01] <- 1
  pmax(0, s)
}

# Local Pearson: interpolate both curves onto a common +/- half_m grid centred on
# each feature, correlate, then map the correlation onto a score by decaying the
# distance d = 1 - r. With rate = log(10): r = 1 -> 1, r = 0 -> 0.1 (so every
# positive correlation scores above 0.1), and negatives decay further (r = -1 ->
# 0.01). floor_val is a hard lower bound for a bad or uncomputable correlation.
.local_pearson <- function(pos1, h1, y1, pos2, h2, y2, half_m, rate, floor_val) {
  hg <- seq(-half_m, half_m, by = 0.01)
  w1 <- suppressWarnings(approx(h1, y1, xout = pos1 + hg, ties = "ordered")$y)
  w2 <- suppressWarnings(approx(h2, y2, xout = pos2 + hg, ties = "ordered")$y)
  ok <- is.finite(w1) & is.finite(w2)
  if (sum(ok) < 5L) return(floor_val)
  r <- suppressWarnings(cor(w1[ok], w2[ok]))
  if (!is.finite(r)) return(floor_val)
  min(1, max(floor_val, exp(-rate * (1 - r))))
}

# Slope agreement: how FLAT the (las_2 - las_1) residual curve is over the same
# +/- window as the local Pearson. Interpolate both curves onto a common grid
# centred on each feature, subtract (las_2 - las_1) to get the residual curve,
# differentiate it, and take the SD of that derivative. A residual that is flat -
# the two curves rising and falling in lockstep, regardless of any constant
# vertical offset between them - has a near-zero derivative everywhere and so a
# near-zero SD. To keep the score meaning the same across signals on wildly
# different scales (areas in m^2, offsets in m, protrusion as a fraction), that
# SD is NORMALISED by the curves' own mean slope-SD, giving a dimensionless
# ratio: 0 when the shapes are identical, ~1 when the residual wanders as much as
# the curves themselves do. The ratio is mapped exactly as Pearson maps (1 - r):
# with rate = log(10), ratio 0 -> 1 and ratio 1 -> 0.1. Two flat curves (no slope
# either epoch) agree trivially -> 1; floor_val bounds a bad/uncomputable result.
.slope_agreement <- function(pos1, h1, y1, pos2, h2, y2, half_m, rate, floor_val) {
  hg <- seq(-half_m, half_m, by = 0.01)
  w1 <- suppressWarnings(approx(h1, y1, xout = pos1 + hg, ties = "ordered")$y)
  w2 <- suppressWarnings(approx(h2, y2, xout = pos2 + hg, ties = "ordered")$y)
  ok <- is.finite(w1) & is.finite(w2)
  if (sum(ok) < 5L) return(floor_val)
  w1 <- w1[ok]; w2 <- w2[ok]
  dx       <- 0.01
  d_resid  <- diff(w2 - w1) / dx
  sd_resid <- stats::sd(d_resid)
  norm     <- mean(c(stats::sd(diff(w1) / dx), stats::sd(diff(w2) / dx)))
  if (!is.finite(norm) || norm <= 0)
    return(if (is.finite(sd_resid) && sd_resid <= 1e-9) 1 else floor_val)
  if (!is.finite(sd_resid)) return(floor_val)
  ratio <- sd_resid / norm
  min(1, max(floor_val, exp(-rate * ratio)))
}

# Spacing from a feature at h_focal to the nearest extremum of `want_type` on the
# given side; NA when none exists that side. Always non-negative.
.nearest_spacing <- function(h_focal, ex, side, want_type) {
  if (is.null(ex) || nrow(ex) == 0L) return(NA_real_)
  hs <- ex$h[ex$type == want_type &
             (if (side == "left") ex$h < h_focal else ex$h > h_focal)]
  if (!length(hs)) return(NA_real_)
  if (side == "left") h_focal - max(hs) else min(hs) - h_focal
}

# One spacing-similarity factor for a candidate: compare the two features'
# spacings to their nearest `want_type` neighbour on `side`.
.spacing_factor <- function(h1, ex1, h2, ex2, side, want_type, sp) {
  s1 <- .nearest_spacing(h1, ex1, side, want_type)
  s2 <- .nearest_spacing(h2, ex2, side, want_type)
  raw <- if (is.na(s1) && is.na(s2)) 0.80
         else if (is.na(s1) || is.na(s2)) 0.10
         else .spacing_decay(abs(s1 - s2))
  .clamp(raw, sp$spacing_floor, sp$spacing_ceil)
}

# ── 2. Score every candidate for one pair-signal ──────────────────────────────
# e1/e2 are the Step 3.12 extrema tables for the two stems; c1/c2 are the LOESS
# curves (columns h and pred_col). Returns one row per candidate, or NULL.
.score_candidates_one <- function(e1, e2, c1, c2, pred_col, sp,
                                   sig_key, tid1, tid2) {
  if (is.null(e1) || is.null(e2) || nrow(e1) == 0L || nrow(e2) == 0L)
    return(NULL)
  h1v <- c1$h; y1v <- c1[[pred_col]]
  h2v <- c2$h; y2v <- c2[[pred_col]]

  .safe_max <- function(v) { v <- v[is.finite(v)]; if (length(v)) max(v) else NA_real_ }
  mx  <- function(e, ty, col) .safe_max(e[[col]][e$type == ty])
  .rel <- function(v, mxv) if (is.na(mxv) || mxv <= 0 || !is.finite(v)) 0 else v / mxv

  rows <- list(); k <- 0L
  for (ty in c("peak", "trough")) {
    opp_ty <- if (ty == "peak") "trough" else "peak"   # spacing neighbour to compare
    f1 <- e1[e1$type == ty, , drop = FALSE]
    f2 <- e2[e2$type == ty, , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(f1) == 0L || nrow(f2) == 0L) next

    max_maj_1  <- mx(e1, ty, "majesty");          max_maj_2  <- mx(e2, ty, "majesty")
    max_majp_1 <- mx(e1, ty, "major_prominence"); max_majp_2 <- mx(e2, ty, "major_prominence")
    max_minp_1 <- mx(e1, ty, "minor_prominence"); max_minp_2 <- mx(e2, ty, "minor_prominence")

    for (i1 in seq_len(nrow(f1))) {
      for (i2 in seq_len(nrow(f2))) {
        k <- k + 1L
        a <- f1[i1, ]; b <- f2[i2, ]

        gz1 <- if ("global_z" %in% names(a)) a$global_z[1L] else NA_real_
        gz2 <- if ("global_z" %in% names(b)) b$global_z[1L] else NA_real_
        implied_shift <- if (is.finite(gz1) && is.finite(gz2)) gz2 - gz1 else NA_real_

        r_maj_1  <- .rel(a$majesty[1L],          max_maj_1)
        r_maj_2  <- .rel(b$majesty[1L],          max_maj_2)
        r_majp_1 <- .rel(a$major_prominence[1L], max_majp_1)
        r_majp_2 <- .rel(b$major_prominence[1L], max_majp_2)
        r_minp_1 <- .rel(a$minor_prominence[1L], max_minp_1)
        r_minp_2 <- .rel(b$minor_prominence[1L], max_minp_2)

        sc_rel_maj_tot <- .clamp(mean(c(r_maj_1, r_maj_2)),
                                 sp$rel_tot_floor, sp$rel_tot_ceil)
        sc_rel_maj_sim <- .clamp(.gauss_sim(abs(r_maj_1 - r_maj_2),
                                            sp$sim_d_one, sp$sim_d_zero, sp$sim_rate),
                                 sp$rel_sim_floor, sp$rel_sim_ceil)
        sc_rel_majorprom_tot <- .clamp(mean(c(r_majp_1, r_majp_2)),
                                       sp$rel_tot_floor, sp$rel_tot_ceil)
        sc_rel_majorprom_sim <- .clamp(.gauss_sim(abs(r_majp_1 - r_majp_2),
                                                  sp$sim_d_one, sp$sim_d_zero, sp$sim_rate),
                                       sp$rel_sim_floor, sp$rel_sim_ceil)
        sc_rel_minorprom_tot <- .clamp(mean(c(r_minp_1, r_minp_2)),
                                       sp$rel_tot_floor, sp$rel_tot_ceil)
        sc_rel_minorprom_sim <- .clamp(.gauss_sim(abs(r_minp_1 - r_minp_2),
                                                  sp$sim_d_one, sp$sim_d_zero, sp$sim_rate),
                                       sp$rel_sim_floor, sp$rel_sim_ceil)

        sc_pearson <- .local_pearson(a$h[1L], h1v, y1v, b$h[1L], h2v, y2v,
                                     sp$pearson_half_m, sp$pearson_rate,
                                     sp$pearson_floor)

        sc_slope_agree <- .slope_agreement(a$h[1L], h1v, y1v, b$h[1L], h2v, y2v,
                                           sp$slope_half_m, sp$slope_rate,
                                           sp$slope_floor)

        # spacing to the nearest OPPOSITE-TYPE feature (peak<->trough), each side
        sc_left_opp  <- .spacing_factor(a$h[1L], e1, b$h[1L], e2, "left",  opp_ty, sp)
        sc_right_opp <- .spacing_factor(a$h[1L], e1, b$h[1L], e2, "right", opp_ty, sp)

        rows[[k]] <- tibble::tibble(
          signal = sig_key, TreeID_1 = tid1, TreeID_2 = tid2,
          pair = paste0(tid1, "\u2192", tid2), type = ty,
          h1 = a$h[1L], h2 = b$h[1L],
          value1 = a$value[1L], value2 = b$value[1L],
          global_z1 = gz1, global_z2 = gz2,
          implied_shift = implied_shift,
          sc_rel_maj_tot       = sc_rel_maj_tot,
          sc_rel_maj_sim       = sc_rel_maj_sim,
          sc_rel_majorprom_tot = sc_rel_majorprom_tot,
          sc_rel_majorprom_sim = sc_rel_majorprom_sim,
          sc_rel_minorprom_tot = sc_rel_minorprom_tot,
          sc_rel_minorprom_sim = sc_rel_minorprom_sim,
          sc_pearson     = sc_pearson,
          sc_slope_agree = sc_slope_agree,
          sc_median_prox = NA_real_,   # pool factor, filled below
          sc_consensus   = NA_real_,   # pool factor, filled below
          sc_left_opp    = sc_left_opp, sc_right_opp = sc_right_opp
        )
      }
    }
  }
  if (!length(rows)) return(NULL)
  cand <- dplyr::bind_rows(rows)

  # ── pool factors: median proximity + consensus, over ALL candidates for this
  #    pair-signal (peaks and troughs pooled together) ─────────────────────────
  shifts <- cand$implied_shift
  fin    <- is.finite(shifts)

  if (sum(fin) < 2L) {
    cand$sc_median_prox <- (sp$median_prox_floor + sp$median_prox_ceil) / 2
    cand$sc_median_prox[!fin] <- NA_real_
  } else {
    med <- median(shifts[fin]); s <- max(IQR(shifts[fin]), 0.01)
    raw <- exp(-sp$median_prox_rate * ((shifts - med) / s)^2)
    cand$sc_median_prox <- .clamp(raw, sp$median_prox_floor, sp$median_prox_ceil)
    cand$sc_median_prox[!fin] <- NA_real_
  }

  # consensus: sum of decay to every OTHER finite candidate, min-max normalised.
  raw_con <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(cand)), function(j) {
    if (!fin[j]) return(NA_real_)
    d <- abs(shifts[fin] - shifts[j])
    sum(.consensus_decay(d)) - 1  # drop self (distance 0 contributes decay = 1)
  }, numeric(1))
  rc <- raw_con[is.finite(raw_con)]
  norm_con <- if (length(rc) >= 1L && diff(range(rc)) > 1e-12)
                (raw_con - min(rc)) / (max(rc) - min(rc))
              else ifelse(is.finite(raw_con), 1, NA_real_)
  cand$sc_consensus <- .clamp(norm_con, sp$consensus_floor, sp$consensus_ceil)

  cand
}

# ── 3. Run over all active signals ────────────────────────────────────────────
if (!requireNamespace("cli", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("cli")

.pm_pairs      <- pairs_ax_fitted
s57_candidates <- list()

for (sig_key in names(s5_signal_registry)) {
  if (!isTRUE(s57_run_flags[[sig_key]])) next
  sr  <- s5_signal_registry[[sig_key]]
  bt1 <- get(sr$by_tid_1, envir = .stage_env())
  bt2 <- get(sr$by_tid_2, envir = .stage_env())
  ex1 <- get(paste0("peaks_1_", sig_key), envir = .stage_env())
  ex2 <- get(paste0("peaks_2_", sig_key), envir = .stage_env())

  cand_list <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(.pm_pairs)), function(i) {
    t1c <- as.character(.pm_pairs$TreeID_1[i])
    t2c <- as.character(.pm_pairs$TreeID_2[i])
    c1  <- bt1[[t1c]]; c2 <- bt2[[t2c]]
    if (is.null(c1) || is.null(c2)) return(NULL)
    .score_candidates_one(ex1[[t1c]], ex2[[t2c]], c1, c2, sr$pred_col,
                          s5_pm_score_params, sig_key,
                          .pm_pairs$TreeID_1[i], .pm_pairs$TreeID_2[i])
  })
  cand <- dplyr::bind_rows(Filter(Negate(is.null), cand_list))

  s57_candidates[[sig_key]] <- cand
  assign(paste0("pm_candidates_",  sig_key), cand, envir = .stage_env())
  # Alias under the name the (retired) export/vis diagnostics look for.
  assign(paste0("s57_combo_diag_", sig_key), cand, envir = .stage_env())
}

s57_candidates_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(s57_candidates)
s57_combo_diag     <- s57_candidates   # alias list

# ── Report ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
.sc_cols <- c("sc_rel_maj_tot","sc_rel_maj_sim","sc_rel_majorprom_tot",
              "sc_rel_majorprom_sim","sc_rel_minorprom_tot","sc_rel_minorprom_sim",
              "sc_pearson","sc_slope_agree","sc_median_prox","sc_consensus",
              "sc_left_opp","sc_right_opp")
cli::cli_h1("3.13 Candidate scoring")
if (nrow(s57_candidates_all) == 0L) {
  cli::cli_alert_warning("No candidates scored.")
} else {
  .summ <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(s57_candidates), function(sk) {
    d <- s57_candidates[[sk]]
    if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L) return(NULL)
    data.frame(signal = sk,
               pairs  = dplyr::n_distinct(d$pair),
               cand   = nrow(d),
               peak   = sum(d$type == "peak"),
               trough = sum(d$type == "trough"),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
  print(.summ, row.names = FALSE)
  cli::cli_alert_info(
    "{nrow(s57_candidates_all)} candidate{?s} across {dplyr::n_distinct(s57_candidates_all$signal)} signal{?s}. Stored as pm_candidates_<sig> with 12 factor columns; Step 3.14 weights them.")
}
```

### Diag Missing score values

```{r}
#| label: peak-score-missingness
#| code-summary: "Flag candidates whose score calculator returned NA, among pairs that produced at least one peak match candidate"

# ── What this does ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A data-quality check, run BEFORE the correlation diagnostic and before weighting.
# The scoring step should return a finite value for every one of the 13 factors on
# every candidate; an NA means the calculator could not produce a score - most
# often a missing global_z leaving the implied shift undefined, which knocks out
# the median-proximity and consensus factors. Those NAs matter because Step 3.14
# forms a weighted MEAN over the AVAILABLE factors, so a candidate silently loses
# whichever factors are NA (and its aggregate is built from fewer of them).
#
# Scope: the (signal, pair) groups that produced at least one peak match
# candidate; within those, PEAKS AND TROUGHS ARE POOLED - every candidate in a
# qualifying pair is checked, not just the peak-vs-peak ones. Nothing is dropped
# here; this only reports where, and which, scores are missing.

.score_cols <- function(d) grep("^sc_", names(d), value = TRUE)

s5_pm_missing       <- list()   # per-signal: one row per candidate carrying >=1 NA score
s5_pm_missing_bycol <- list()   # per-signal: NA count per score column

for (sig_key in names(s5_signal_registry)) {
  obj <- paste0("pm_candidates_", sig_key)
  if (!exists(obj)) next
  cand <- get(obj, envir = .stage_env())
  if (is.null(cand) || nrow(cand) == 0L) next

  # pairs (within this signal) that produced at least one peak match candidate
  peak_pairs <- unique(cand$pair[cand$type == "peak"])
  if (!length(peak_pairs)) next

  # both types pooled within the qualifying pairs
  scope <- cand[cand$pair %in% peak_pairs, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(scope) == 0L) next

  cols <- .score_cols(scope)
  Mna  <- is.na(as.matrix(scope[, cols, drop = FALSE]))

  # per-column NA tally (kept for every column, including the zeros)
  s5_pm_missing_bycol[[sig_key]] <- tibble::tibble(
    signal = sig_key, score = sub("^sc_", "", cols),
    n_na = as.integer(colSums(Mna)), n = nrow(scope)
  )

  # per-candidate rows carrying at least one NA score
  bad <- which(rowSums(Mna) > 0L)
  if (length(bad)) {
    miss_cols <- vapply(bad, function(i)
      paste(sub("^sc_", "", cols[Mna[i, ]]), collapse = ", "), character(1))
    s5_pm_missing[[sig_key]] <- tibble::tibble(
      signal        = sig_key,
      pair          = scope$pair[bad],
      type          = scope$type[bad],
      h1            = scope$h1[bad],
      h2            = scope$h2[bad],
      implied_shift = scope$implied_shift[bad],
      n_na          = as.integer(rowSums(Mna)[bad]),
      na_scores     = miss_cols
    )
  }
}

s5_pm_missing_all       <- dplyr::bind_rows(s5_pm_missing)
s5_pm_missing_bycol_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(s5_pm_missing_bycol)

# ── Report ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if (!requireNamespace("cli", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("cli")
cli::cli_h1("3.13.1 Missing score values (peaks & troughs pooled, in pairs with >=1 peak match)")
if (nrow(s5_pm_missing_all) == 0L) {
  cli::cli_alert_success("No missing scores: every factor is finite on every candidate in scope.")
} else {
  col_tot <- s5_pm_missing_bycol_all |>
    dplyr::group_by(score) |>
    dplyr::summarise(n_na = sum(n_na), n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::filter(n_na > 0) |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n_na)) |>
    as.data.frame()
  cli::cli_alert_warning("{nrow(s5_pm_missing_all)} candidate{?s} with >=1 NA score, across {dplyr::n_distinct(s5_pm_missing_all$signal)} signal{?s}.")
  cli::cli_h2("NA count by score type (summed over signals)")
  print(col_tot, row.names = FALSE)
  cli::cli_h2("affected candidates")
  print(s5_pm_missing_all |>
          dplyr::mutate(implied_shift = round(implied_shift, 4)) |>
          as.data.frame(), row.names = FALSE)
}
```

### Diag Score correlation & redundancy

```{r}
#| label: params-peak-score-correlation
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Per-signal Pearson correlation across the 13 score factors, flagging near-collinear (redundant) score types"


# ── What this does ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A standard data-exploration collinearity check, run SEPARATELY for each signal.
# For each signal's candidate pool, the 13 factor scores are correlated pairwise
# (Pearson, across candidates - peaks and troughs pooled). Two score types that
# move together across every candidate carry the same information, so one of the
# pair is redundant. Pairs whose |r| reaches the threshold are flagged as
# candidates for removal - NOTHING is removed here, this only reports.
#
# The threshold is deliberately high: the score types are all meant to reward a
# good match, so they are expected to be somewhat correlated. Only near-duplicate
# score types - the ones carrying essentially the same information - should trip
# it. A score type pinned to a constant for a signal (e.g. always at its clamp
# floor) has no variance to correlate and is reported on its own, since it gives
# that signal no discrimination.
s5_pm_corr_threshold <- 0.95   # |r| at/above this flags a pair as redundant
s5_pm_corr_min_n     <- 3L     # need at least this many candidates to correlate

.par_apply("params-peak-score-correlation")
```

```{r}
#| label: peak-score-correlation
#| code-summary: "Per-signal Pearson correlation across the 13 score factors, flagging near-collinear (redundant) score types"

# The score columns, read from whatever the scoring step actually produced, with
# the sc_ prefix dropped so the labels match the factor names used in Step 3.14.
.score_cols <- function(d) grep("^sc_", names(d), value = TRUE)

s5_pm_score_corr       <- list()   # per-signal correlation matrix
s5_pm_score_redundancy <- list()   # per-signal flagged pairs
s5_pm_score_constant   <- list()   # per-signal zero-variance (degenerate) scores

for (sig_key in names(s5_signal_registry)) {
  obj <- paste0("pm_candidates_", sig_key)
  if (!exists(obj)) next
  cand <- get(obj, envir = .stage_env())
  if (is.null(cand) || nrow(cand) < s5_pm_corr_min_n) next

  cols <- .score_cols(cand)
  M    <- as.matrix(cand[, cols, drop = FALSE])
  colnames(M) <- sub("^sc_", "", colnames(M))

  # Drop score types with no variance in this signal: cor() is undefined for a
  # constant column, and a constant score cannot be redundant WITH anything.
  sdv  <- apply(M, 2, function(x) stats::sd(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  keep <- is.finite(sdv) & sdv > 0
  s5_pm_score_constant[[sig_key]] <- colnames(M)[!keep]
  M    <- M[, keep, drop = FALSE]
  if (ncol(M) < 2L) next

  cm <- suppressWarnings(stats::cor(M, use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
  s5_pm_score_corr[[sig_key]] <- cm
  assign(paste0("pm_score_corr_", sig_key), cm, envir = .stage_env())

  # flagged pairs: upper triangle, |r| >= threshold (NA correlations excluded)
  hit <- which(upper.tri(cm) & is.finite(cm) & abs(cm) >= s5_pm_corr_threshold,
               arr.ind = TRUE)
  s5_pm_score_redundancy[[sig_key]] <- if (nrow(hit))
    tibble::tibble(signal  = sig_key,
                   score_a = rownames(cm)[hit[, 1]],
                   score_b = colnames(cm)[hit[, 2]],
```
