```{r}
                   r       = cm[hit]) |>
      dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(abs(r)))
  else
    tibble::tibble(signal = character(0), score_a = character(0),
                   score_b = character(0), r = numeric(0))
}

s5_pm_score_redundancy_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(s5_pm_score_redundancy)

# ── Report ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if (!requireNamespace("cli", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("cli")
cli::cli_h1("3.13.1 Score correlation & redundancy (|r| >= {s5_pm_corr_threshold})")
for (sig_key in names(s5_pm_score_corr)) {
  cm <- s5_pm_score_corr[[sig_key]]
  cli::cli_h2("signal: {sig_key}  (n = {nrow(get(paste0('pm_candidates_', sig_key)))} candidates)")
  print(round(cm, 2))
  cn <- s5_pm_score_constant[[sig_key]]
  if (length(cn))
    cli::cli_alert_info("constant (no variance) here, excluded: {cn}")
  fl <- s5_pm_score_redundancy[[sig_key]]
  if (nrow(fl)) {
    cli::cli_alert_warning("{nrow(fl)} redundant pair{?s} at |r| >= {s5_pm_corr_threshold}:")
    print(fl |> dplyr::mutate(r = round(r, 3)) |> as.data.frame(), row.names = FALSE)
  } else {
    cli::cli_alert_success("no pair reaches |r| >= {s5_pm_corr_threshold}")
  }
}
if (nrow(s5_pm_score_redundancy_all)) {
  cli::cli_h2("all flagged pairs, every signal")
  print(s5_pm_score_redundancy_all |> dplyr::mutate(r = round(r, 3)) |>
        as.data.frame(), row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  cli::cli_alert_success("No redundant score pairs on any signal at |r| >= {s5_pm_corr_threshold}.")
}
```


### Optim Score effect on shift residual

```{r}
#| label: params-peak-score-residual-glm
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Resolve the TRUE post-rotation Z-shift (generator truth CSV) for the residual GLM"


# ── Where the truth comes from ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The true Z-shift used to be typed in here as a constant, which meant every
# sample in a batch was scored against whichever number was last edited: a run
# on a 29.71 deg sample was reported against a truth belonging to a different
# sample entirely.
#
#   "updatedBox" (default) DERIVE the shift from the marker box, after the
#            rotation this run actually solved. The eight box-2 corners are put
#            through the same two legs Step 3.1 applied to las_1 (R_align_1
#            about align_pivot_1, then R_xyz about pivot1), and the truth Z-shift
#            is the mean of box1_z - rotated_box2_z over the eight corner pairs.
#   "csv"    read target_shift_z_m from s3_truth_csv_path (the driver supplies
#            the per-pair one-row file in a batch). Errors if it cannot.
#   "manual" use s3_true_shift_manual - for a hand-made sample with no CSV.
#   "none"   no truth exists (real data). The GLM below is skipped and every
#            later chunk falls back to "truth unavailable" - nothing errors.
#
# Why "updatedBox" is the default. target_shift_z_m is the number the GENERATOR
# put in, and it is only the Z-shift this stage should be scored against if the
# solved rotation equals the generator's rotation. It does not: any residual
# rotation error tips the cloud, and a tipped cloud needs a different Z-shift to
# seat it. Scoring the optimisation CSVs against the generator's constant
# therefore charges Step 3.13.3 for rotation error it cannot fix and did not
# cause. Re-deriving from the corners asks the question the stage can actually
# answer - "given the rotation I ended up with, what Z-shift is correct?" - and
# the difference between the two numbers is exactly the rotation-induced Z that
# Stage 6 reports separately. Note the two ARE different quantities: use "csv"
# when you specifically want to score against the generator's input.
s3_truth_source <- "updatedBox"

s3_truth_csv_path <- "C:/Users/ascsh/Documents/1_Artemis/11_PaqLab/115_TreeTimeAlign/TestSamples/Generated/SNBG_BOS_F1_Feb2020_March2026_ULS_TLS.csv"
s3_true_shift_manual <- NA_real_

s5_pm_resid_floor <- 1e-6     # keep the Gamma response strictly > 0
s5_pm_resid_dfbuf <- 5L       # required residual-df buffer: n >= k + dfbuf
s5_pm_p_keep      <- 0.05     # round 2: keep only scores with p <= this

# .par_apply MUST sit above the file read below: the driver's values have to
# land before anything validates or opens a path.
.par_apply("params-peak-score-residual-glm")

# ── Resolve ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# In a batch the driver writes a ONE-ROW truth file per pair and points
# .batch_truth_csv at it. Read here, in the chunk that uses it, for the same
# reason every other export path is: this chunk consumes the value it sets.
if (.in_batch())
  s3_truth_csv_path <- .batch_opt(".batch_truth_csv", s3_truth_csv_path)

s5_pm_true_shift <- NA_real_

# ── Nothing below may stop the run ───────────────────────────────────────────
# The truth Z-shift is a DIAGNOSTIC. It is the yardstick 3.13.3 scores the shift
# search against, and it is not an input to the alignment itself - no ellipse,
# no rotation and no exported cloud depends on it. So a missing marker box, an
# absent CSV or an unmatched sample row must never take down a run that is
# otherwise producing a valid alignment, and in a batch must never cost a pair.
# Every path here therefore degrades: the preferred source is tried, then the
# next, and if none yields a number s5_pm_true_shift stays NA. 3.13.3 is skipped,
# the error columns come out NA, and everything else carries on exactly as it
# does on real data, where no truth exists in the first place.
.s3_src <- tolower(trimws(as.character(s3_truth_source)[1]))
if (!.s3_src %in% c("updatedbox", "csv", "manual", "none")) {
  cat(sprintf(paste0("Truth: s3_truth_source '%s' is not one of \"updatedBox\", \"csv\", \"manual\", \"none\"",
                     " - using \"updatedBox\".\n"), s3_truth_source))
  .s3_src <- "updatedbox"
}

# ── Marker-box provenance, recorded for the report ───────────────────────────
s3_box_source     <- "none"
s3_box_n_corners  <- 0L
s3_box_dz_sd_m    <- NA_real_
s3_box_dz_range_m <- NA_real_
s3_truth_resolved <- "none"     # which source actually produced the number

# ── Attempt 1: re-derive from the marker box ─────────────────────────────────
# Returns NA and says why rather than raising. Wrapped whole in tryCatch so even
# an unforeseen malformation (a ragged CSV, a corrupt attribute) degrades.
.s3_try_box <- function() tryCatch({

  # Two sources for the corners, same preference order as Stage 6 6.6:
  #   csv -> box1_c1_x ... box2_c8_z, the generator's exact coordinates
  #   las -> the TargetBox / BoxCorner fields carried in las_1, quantised by the
  #          file's scale factor (sub-millimetre against a metre-scale shift)
  # Step 0.6 reads las_1 as-is, so unlike Stage 1 the marker points are still
  # present here and the las route is genuinely available as a fallback.
  .b1nm <- sprintf("box1_c%d_%s", rep(1:8, each = 3), rep(c("x", "y", "z"), 8))
  .b2nm <- sprintf("box2_c%d_%s", rep(1:8, each = 3), rep(c("x", "y", "z"), 8))

  .bx_truth <- NULL; .bx_moved <- NULL; .bx_src <- "none"

  if (!is.null(s3_truth_csv_path) && nzchar(s3_truth_csv_path) &&
      file.exists(s3_truth_csv_path)) {
    .cs <- tryCatch(utils::read.csv(s3_truth_csv_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
                    error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(.cs)) {
      if (nrow(.cs) > 1L && "sample_name" %in% names(.cs)) {
        .nm <- if (.in_batch()) .batch_opt(".batch_sample", NA_character_) else NA_character_
        if (!is.na(.nm)) .cs <- .cs[.cs$sample_name == .nm, , drop = FALSE]
      }
      if (nrow(.cs) == 1L && all(c(.b1nm, .b2nm) %in% names(.cs))) {
        .bx_truth <- matrix(as.numeric(unlist(.cs[1, .b1nm])), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
        .bx_moved <- matrix(as.numeric(unlist(.cs[1, .b2nm])), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
        .bx_src   <- "csv"
      }
    }
  }

  if (is.null(.bx_truth) && exists("las_1") &&
      all(c("TargetBox", "BoxCorner") %in% names(las_1@data))) {
    .bt <- as.data.frame(las_1@data)[, c("X", "Y", "Z", "TargetBox", "BoxCorner")]
    names(.bt) <- c("X", "Y", "Z", "box", "corner")
    .m1 <- .bt[!is.na(.bt$box) & .bt$box == 1L, ]
    .m2 <- .bt[!is.na(.bt$box) & .bt$box == 2L, ]
    # Paired on the corner ID, never on proximity: a badly wrong run is exactly
    # the case where the nearest box-1 corner to a box-2 corner is not its twin.
    if (nrow(.m1) > 0L && nrow(.m1) == nrow(.m2) &&
        !anyDuplicated(.m1$corner) && setequal(.m1$corner, .m2$corner)) {
      .m1 <- .m1[order(.m1$corner), ]; .m2 <- .m2[order(.m2$corner), ]
      .bx_truth <- as.matrix(.m1[, c("X", "Y", "Z")])
      .bx_moved <- as.matrix(.m2[, c("X", "Y", "Z")])
      dimnames(.bx_truth) <- NULL; dimnames(.bx_moved) <- NULL
      .bx_src   <- "las"
    }
  }

  if (is.null(.bx_truth)) {
    cat("Truth: no marker box found (no box1_c*/box2_c* columns, no paired TargetBox/BoxCorner in las_1).\n")
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  # The rotation legs have to exist for the corners to be moved into the frame
  # the shift search works in. They always do in a normal run; if they somehow
  # do not, that is a reason to skip the diagnostic, not to stop.
  if (!all(vapply(c("R_align_1", "align_pivot_1", "R_xyz", "pivot1"),
                  exists, logical(1)))) {
    cat("Truth: rotation legs not available yet - marker-box derivation skipped.\n")
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  # ── The box-2 corners take the SAME two legs las_1 took in Step 3.1 ────────
  # They come off disk (or out of the generator CSV) in the RAW original-scan
  # frame, so R_xyz on its own would land them in neither frame - the same trap
  # Step 3.1 documents at length. The box-1 corners are the truth and are NOT
  # transformed: they are already where the corners belong.
  .bm <- sweep(.bx_moved, 2, align_pivot_1)
  .bm <- t(R_align_1 %*% t(.bm))
  .bm <- sweep(.bm, 2, -align_pivot_1)

  .bm <- sweep(.bm, 2, pivot1)
  .bm <- if (exists("apply_mode_rot") && identical(apply_mode_rot, "custom")) {
    .apply_4x4_transform(.bm, custom_transform_matrix_rot)
  } else {
    t(R_xyz %*% t(.bm))
  }
  .bm <- sweep(.bm, 2, -pivot1)

  # The Z-shift that seats the rotated box on the truth box, averaged over the
  # corner pairs. Sign matches implied_shift: a value to ADD to the rotated cloud.
  .dz <- .bx_truth[, 3] - .bm[, 3]
  .dz <- .dz[is.finite(.dz)]
  if (!length(.dz)) {
    cat("Truth: marker-box corners gave no finite Z differences.\n")
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  s3_box_source     <<- .bx_src
  s3_box_n_corners  <<- length(.dz)
  s3_box_dz_sd_m    <<- if (length(.dz) > 1L) stats::sd(.dz) else NA_real_
  s3_box_dz_range_m <<- diff(range(.dz))

  cat(sprintf("Truth Z-shift %+.4f m (re-derived from %d rotated box corner(s), source: %s)\n",
              mean(.dz), length(.dz), .bx_src))
  cat(sprintf("  per-corner dz: sd %.4f m | range %.4f m\n",
              s3_box_dz_sd_m, s3_box_dz_range_m))

  # A pure Z-shift moves all eight corners identically. Spread across them is
  # leftover ROTATION error, tipping the box so no single Z seats every corner.
  # The mean is still the best available scalar, but a large spread means the
  # residual the GLM is fitting is partly rotation the shift search cannot fix.
  if (is.finite(s3_box_dz_range_m) && s3_box_dz_range_m > 0.05)
    cat(sprintf(paste0("  NOTE: the eight corners disagree by %.4f m. A pure Z-shift would move them\n",
                       "        identically, so this spread is residual rotation error, not shift error.\n"),
                s3_box_dz_range_m))

  mean(.dz)

}, error = function(e) {
  cat(sprintf("Truth: marker-box derivation failed (%s) - falling through.\n",
              conditionMessage(e)))
  NA_real_
})

# ── Attempt 2: the generator's target_shift_z_m ──────────────────────────────
.s3_try_csv <- function() tryCatch({

  if (is.null(s3_truth_csv_path) || !nzchar(s3_truth_csv_path) ||
      !file.exists(s3_truth_csv_path)) {
    cat(sprintf("Truth: CSV not found (%s).\n",
                if (nzchar(s3_truth_csv_path)) s3_truth_csv_path else "path empty"))
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  .tc <- utils::read.csv(s3_truth_csv_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  if (!"target_shift_z_m" %in% names(.tc)) {
    cat(sprintf("Truth: no target_shift_z_m column in %s.\n", basename(s3_truth_csv_path)))
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  # A consolidated table is fine as long as this run's sample can be identified.
  # Anything else is ambiguous and is refused rather than guessed - scoring
  # against the wrong row is exactly the failure this block exists to end.
  if (nrow(.tc) == 1L) {
    .row <- .tc
  } else {
    .nm <- if (.in_batch()) .batch_opt(".batch_sample", NA_character_) else NA_character_
    if (!"sample_name" %in% names(.tc) || is.na(.nm)) {
      cat(sprintf(paste0("Truth: the CSV holds %d rows and this run cannot be matched to one",
                         " (needs a sample_name column and a known sample).\n"), nrow(.tc)))
      return(NA_real_)
    }
    .row <- .tc[.tc$sample_name == .nm, , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(.row) != 1L) {
      cat(sprintf("Truth: %d row(s) match sample_name '%s'; expected exactly 1.\n",
                  nrow(.row), .nm))
      return(NA_real_)
    }
  }

  .v <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.row$target_shift_z_m[1]))
  if (!is.finite(.v)) {
    cat(sprintf("Truth: target_shift_z_m is not a finite number in %s.\n",
                basename(s3_truth_csv_path)))
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  cat(sprintf("Truth Z-shift %+.4f m (target_shift_z_m) <- %s\n",
              .v, basename(s3_truth_csv_path)))
  .v

}, error = function(e) {
  cat(sprintf("Truth: reading the CSV failed (%s) - falling through.\n",
              conditionMessage(e)))
  NA_real_
})

# ── Attempt 3: the hand-entered constant ─────────────────────────────────────
.s3_try_manual <- function() {
  .v <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(s3_true_shift_manual))
  if (!is.finite(.v)) {
    cat("Truth: s3_true_shift_manual is not set.\n")
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  cat(sprintf("Truth Z-shift %+.4f m (manual).\n", .v))
  .v
}

# ── The cascade ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Each source falls through to the next-best rather than failing. "none" asks
# for no truth at all and is honoured as written.
.s3_order <- switch(.s3_src,
  updatedbox = c("updatedBox", "csv", "manual"),
  csv        = c("csv", "manual"),
  manual     = c("manual"),
  character(0)
)

for (.src in .s3_order) {
  s5_pm_true_shift <- switch(.src,
    updatedBox = .s3_try_box(),
    csv        = .s3_try_csv(),
    manual     = .s3_try_manual()
  )
  if (is.finite(s5_pm_true_shift)) { s3_truth_resolved <- .src; break }
  if (!identical(.src, tail(.s3_order, 1)))
    cat(sprintf("Truth: falling back from '%s'.\n", .src))
}

if (identical(.s3_src, "none")) {
  s5_pm_true_shift  <- NA_real_
  s3_truth_resolved <- "none"
  cat("No truth Z-shift (s3_truth_source = \"none\"): error columns will be NA and 3.13.3 is skipped.\n")
} else if (!is.finite(s5_pm_true_shift)) {
  s5_pm_true_shift  <- NA_real_
  s3_truth_resolved <- "none"
  cat(paste0("No truth Z-shift could be derived from any source: 3.13.3 is skipped and the\n",
             "  error columns come out NA. The alignment itself is unaffected - it never\n",
             "  reads this value - and the optimisation CSV is still written.\n"))
} else if (!identical(tolower(s3_truth_resolved), .s3_src)) {
  cat(sprintf("Truth: resolved from '%s' rather than the requested '%s'.\n",
              s3_truth_resolved, s3_truth_source))
}

# Reported alongside, never substituted: when the shift was re-derived, the gap
# between the two definitions IS the rotation-induced Z, and it is worth seeing.
if (identical(s3_truth_resolved, "updatedBox") &&
    nzchar(s3_truth_csv_path) && file.exists(s3_truth_csv_path)) {
  .gen <- tryCatch(utils::read.csv(s3_truth_csv_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
                   error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(.gen) && nrow(.gen) == 1L && "target_shift_z_m" %in% names(.gen)) {
    .gv <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.gen$target_shift_z_m[1]))
    if (is.finite(.gv))
      cat(sprintf("  generator target_shift_z_m %+.4f m (difference %+.4f m - not used)\n",
                  .gv, s5_pm_true_shift - .gv))
  }
  rm(.gen)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: peak-score-residual-glm
#| code-summary: "Per-signal Gamma(log) GLM of |shift - truth| on the 13 scores; AIC backward-elimination for estimability, then a p<0.05 refit, then recommended weights from the slopes"

# ── What this does ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Given the TRUE post-rotation Z-shift, every candidate's accuracy is known: the
# residual is how far its implied shift lands from the truth. This asks, SEPARATELY
# for each signal, which score types predict a SMALL residual, and turns those
# slopes into a recommended weight per score for Step 3.14.
#
# Response: residual = |implied_shift - true_shift| (m) - continuous, strictly
# positive -> GAMMA GLM with a LOG link (not the canonical inverse): log keeps the
# fitted mean positive and makes each coefficient a MULTIPLICATIVE effect. Scores
# are standardised within the signal, entered as MAIN EFFECTS ONLY (no "coop"
# interactions). exp(coef) < 1 (coef < 0) => higher score, smaller residual.
#
# Two rounds of model reduction:
# Round 1 - estimability. The full 13-score model is fitted; if it cannot be
# cleanly estimated (errors, non-convergence, too few residual df, or rank
# deficiency from collinear scores, e.g. center_offset) AIC-guided backward
# elimination runs FOR THAT SIGNAL ONLY - drop-1, keep lowest AIC, repeat -
# until a clean model is found. Signals whose full model is fine keep all 13.
# Round 2 - significance. From the round-1 model, every score with p > 0.05 is
# dropped and the model refit once. This is the FINAL model.
#
# Recommended weights (from the FINAL model's standardised slopes):
# a) a score with a positive estimate -> weight 0
# b) a score with estimate + std_error > 0 -> weight 0
# c) the remaining (confidently negative) estimates -> multiplied by -1
# d) those reversed values normalised to sum to 1 -> the per-signal weights
# NB the slopes are on STANDARDISED scores, so a weight is "importance per SD of
# that score"; Step 3.14 applies them to the raw [0,1] scores, which is fine as a
# relative-importance blend. Where no score qualifies (or the model was skipped),
# equal weights are emitted as a safe fallback and flagged.
#
# Peaks and troughs are pooled; one row per candidate. Candidates from the same
# temporal pair are not independent - a pair random effect is a later refinement.

# s5_pm_true_shift, s5_pm_resid_floor, s5_pm_resid_dfbuf and s5_pm_p_keep are
# set in params-peak-score-residual-glm above; the truth is read there from the
# generator CSV's target_shift_z_m rather than typed in.

.score_cols <- function(d) grep("^sc_", names(d), value = TRUE)

.fit_resid_gamma <- function(resid, Xs, cols) {
  if (!length(cols)) return(NULL)
  dfit <- data.frame(resid = resid, as.data.frame(Xs[, cols, drop = FALSE]),
                     check.names = TRUE)
  form <- stats::reformulate(cols, response = "resid")
  tryCatch(
    suppressWarnings(stats::glm(form, family = stats::Gamma(link = "log"),
                                data = dfit, control = list(maxit = 100))),
    error = function(e) NULL)
}

.resid_model_ok <- function(fit, n, k) {
  !is.null(fit) && isTRUE(fit$converged) &&
    n >= k + s5_pm_resid_dfbuf && !anyNA(stats::coef(fit))
}

# Round 1: full model, else AIC-guided backward elimination for estimability.
.select_resid_model <- function(resid, Xs, n) {
  full <- colnames(Xs)
  fit  <- .fit_resid_gamma(resid, Xs, full)
  if (.resid_model_ok(fit, n, length(full)))
    return(list(fit = fit, cols = full, dropped = character(0), reduced = FALSE))
  current <- full
  while (length(current) > 1L) {
    children <- lapply(current, function(dropped) setdiff(current, dropped))
    fits <- lapply(children, function(cc) .fit_resid_gamma(resid, Xs, cc))
    aic  <- vapply(fits, function(f)
      if (is.null(f)) NA_real_ else tryCatch(stats::AIC(f), error = function(e) NA_real_),
      numeric(1))
    if (all(is.na(aic))) break
    bi      <- which.min(aic)
    current <- children[[bi]]
    bfit    <- fits[[bi]]
    if (.resid_model_ok(bfit, n, length(current)))
      return(list(fit = bfit, cols = current,
                  dropped = setdiff(full, current), reduced = TRUE))
  }
  list(fit = NULL, cols = current, dropped = setdiff(full, current),
       reduced = TRUE, failed = TRUE)
}

# Round 2: drop every score with p > p_keep, refit once.
.drop_insignificant <- function(fit, resid, Xs, p_keep) {
  co    <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  terms <- setdiff(rownames(co), "(Intercept)")
  if (!length(terms)) return(list(fit = fit, kept = terms, dropped = character(0)))
  p     <- co[terms, 4]
  keep  <- terms[is.finite(p) & p <= p_keep]
  if (length(keep) == length(terms))
    return(list(fit = fit, kept = keep, dropped = character(0)))
  if (!length(keep))
    return(list(fit = NULL, kept = character(0), dropped = terms))
  refit <- .fit_resid_gamma(resid, Xs, keep)
  if (is.null(refit)) return(list(fit = fit, kept = terms, dropped = character(0)))
  list(fit = refit, kept = keep, dropped = setdiff(terms, keep))
}

# Weights from the FINAL model's standardised slopes (steps a-d).
.weights_from_fit <- function(fit, all_factors) {
  w <- setNames(numeric(length(all_factors)), all_factors)
  if (is.null(fit)) return(w)
  co    <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  terms <- setdiff(rownames(co), "(Intercept)")
  if (!length(terms)) return(w)
  est <- co[terms, 1]; se <- co[terms, 2]
  raw <- ifelse((est + se) < 0, -est, 0)     # (a)+(b) zero out, (c) reverse sign
  raw[!is.finite(raw)] <- 0
  w[terms] <- raw
  s <- sum(w)
  if (s > 0) w <- w / s                        # (d) normalise to sum 1
  w
}

s5_pm_resid_glm         <- list()   # per-signal FINAL fitted model
s5_pm_resid_effect      <- list()   # per-signal tidy coefficient table (final model)
s5_pm_resid_dropped     <- list()   # zero-variance scores dropped pre-fit
s5_pm_resid_aic_dropped <- list()   # scores removed by round-1 AIC elimination
s5_pm_resid_p_dropped   <- list()   # scores removed by round-2 p>0.05
s5_pm_resid_note        <- list()   # "full" | "reduced" (round 1)
s5_pm_recommended_weights <- list() # per-signal recommended weight vector
s5_pm_weight_fallback   <- character(0)
s5_pm_resid_skip        <- character(0)

# canonical factor set (bare names, matching s5_pm_factors in Step 3.14)
.all_factors <- NULL
for (sk in names(s5_signal_registry)) {
  o <- paste0("pm_candidates_", sk)
  if (exists(o)) { cc <- get(o); if (!is.null(cc) && nrow(cc)) {
    .all_factors <- sub("^sc_", "", .score_cols(cc)); break } }
}

# No truth = no residual to model. Every signal is marked skipped and the
# equal-weight fallback below fills the recommended-weight list, so nothing
# downstream sees a half-built object. 3.14 uses the weights written into it,
# not these, so the pipeline is unaffected.
.s5_truth_ok <- is.finite(s5_pm_true_shift)
if (!.s5_truth_ok)
  cat("[3.13.3] SKIPPED - no truth Z-shift available. Recommended weights not computed.\n")

for (sig_key in names(s5_signal_registry)) {
  if (!.s5_truth_ok) { s5_pm_resid_skip <- c(s5_pm_resid_skip, sig_key); next }
  obj <- paste0("pm_candidates_", sig_key)
  if (!exists(obj)) next
  cand <- get(obj, envir = .stage_env())
  if (is.null(cand) || nrow(cand) == 0L) next

  d <- cand[is.finite(cand$implied_shift), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(d) == 0L) next

  resid <- pmax(abs(d$implied_shift - s5_pm_true_shift), s5_pm_resid_floor)

  cols  <- .score_cols(d)
  Xs    <- scale(as.matrix(d[, cols, drop = FALSE]))
  sdv   <- attr(Xs, "scaled:scale")
  keepc <- is.finite(sdv) & sdv > 0
  s5_pm_resid_dropped[[sig_key]] <- sub("^sc_", "", cols[!keepc])
  Xs    <- Xs[, keepc, drop = FALSE]
  colnames(Xs) <- sub("^sc_", "", cols[keepc])
  n <- nrow(Xs)

  if (ncol(Xs) < 1L || n < 1L + s5_pm_resid_dfbuf) {
    s5_pm_resid_skip <- c(s5_pm_resid_skip, sig_key); next
  }

  sel <- .select_resid_model(resid, Xs, n)             # round 1
  if (is.null(sel$fit)) { s5_pm_resid_skip <- c(s5_pm_resid_skip, sig_key); next }
  s5_pm_resid_aic_dropped[[sig_key]] <- sel$dropped
  s5_pm_resid_note[[sig_key]]        <- if (sel$reduced) "reduced" else "full"

  sig <- .drop_insignificant(sel$fit, resid, Xs, s5_pm_p_keep)  # round 2
  s5_pm_resid_p_dropped[[sig_key]] <- sig$dropped
  final <- if (!is.null(sig$fit)) sig$fit else sel$fit
  s5_pm_resid_glm[[sig_key]] <- final

  # coefficient table of the FINAL model
  if (!is.null(sig$fit)) {
    co <- as.data.frame(summary(final)$coefficients)
    names(co) <- c("estimate", "std_error", "t", "p")
    co$term   <- rownames(co)
    co <- co[co$term != "(Intercept)", , drop = FALSE]
    co$mult_per_sd <- exp(co$estimate)
    co <- co[order(co$p), c("term", "estimate", "mult_per_sd", "std_error", "t", "p")]
    rownames(co) <- NULL
    s5_pm_resid_effect[[sig_key]] <- tibble::add_column(tibble::as_tibble(co),
                                                        signal = sig_key, .before = 1)
  }
  assign(paste0("pm_resid_glm_", sig_key), final, envir = .stage_env())

  # recommended weights (steps a-d); fall back to equal if nothing qualifies
  wv <- .weights_from_fit(sig$fit, .all_factors)
  if (sum(wv) == 0) {
    wv <- setNames(rep(1 / length(.all_factors), length(.all_factors)), .all_factors)
    s5_pm_weight_fallback <- c(s5_pm_weight_fallback, sig_key)
  }
  s5_pm_recommended_weights[[sig_key]] <- wv
}

# every registry signal gets a weight vector; skipped/absent -> equal fallback
for (sig_key in names(s5_signal_registry)) {
  if (is.null(s5_pm_recommended_weights[[sig_key]])) {
    s5_pm_recommended_weights[[sig_key]] <-
      setNames(rep(1 / length(.all_factors), length(.all_factors)), .all_factors)
    s5_pm_weight_fallback <- union(s5_pm_weight_fallback, sig_key)
  }
}

s5_pm_resid_effect_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(s5_pm_resid_effect)

# ── Report ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if (!requireNamespace("cli", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("cli")
cli::cli_h1("3.13.3 Score effect on |shift - truth| (true = {s5_pm_true_shift} m; Gamma/log GLM, main effects)")
for (sig_key in names(s5_pm_resid_glm)) {
  fit <- s5_pm_resid_glm[[sig_key]]
  de  <- 1 - fit$deviance / fit$null.deviance
  k   <- length(stats::coef(fit)) - 1L
  cli::cli_h2("signal: {sig_key}  ({s5_pm_resid_note[[sig_key]]}, {k} score{?s} final, n = {length(fit$y)}, dev.expl = {round(100 * de, 1)}%, AIC = {round(stats::AIC(fit), 1)})")
  if (!is.null(s5_pm_resid_effect[[sig_key]])) {
    print(s5_pm_resid_effect[[sig_key]] |>
            dplyr::select(-signal) |>
            dplyr::mutate(estimate    = round(estimate, 3),
                          mult_per_sd = round(mult_per_sd, 3),
                          std_error   = round(std_error, 3),
                          t           = round(t, 2),
                          p           = signif(p, 3)) |>
            as.data.frame(), row.names = FALSE)
  } else {
    cli::cli_alert_warning("no score survived the p<={s5_pm_p_keep} refit")
  }
  ad <- s5_pm_resid_aic_dropped[[sig_key]]; if (length(ad)) cli::cli_alert_info("round 1 (AIC) removed: {ad}")
  pd <- s5_pm_resid_p_dropped[[sig_key]];   if (length(pd)) cli::cli_alert_info("round 2 (p>{s5_pm_p_keep}) removed: {pd}")
  dc <- s5_pm_resid_dropped[[sig_key]];     if (length(dc)) cli::cli_alert_info("dropped (no variance): {dc}")
}
if (length(s5_pm_resid_skip))
  cli::cli_alert_info("skipped (no clean model reachable): {unique(s5_pm_resid_skip)}")
if (length(s5_pm_weight_fallback))
  cli::cli_alert_warning("equal-weight fallback (no score qualified / model unavailable): {unique(s5_pm_weight_fallback)}")

# ── Recommended weights - copy into the s5_pm_weights block in Step 3.14 ───────
cli::cli_h2("recommended per-signal weights (paste into 3.14, after s5_pm_weights is built)")
.wlines <- vapply(names(s5_signal_registry), function(sig_key) {
  wv <- s5_pm_recommended_weights[[sig_key]]
  paste0('s5_pm_weights[["', sig_key, '"]] <- c(',
         paste(sprintf('%s = %.4f', names(wv), wv), collapse = ", "), ')')
}, character(1))
cat(.wlines, sep = "\n")
cat("\n")
```

## 3.14 PM Candidate Weighting – Per-Pair-Signal Shift

```{r}
#| label: params-peak-candidate-weighting
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Weight the 12 candidate scores per signal, then reduce to one per-pair-signal shift by either the score-weighted average or the single best-scoring candidate (toggle)"


# ── What this does ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Each candidate first gets an AGGREGATE SCORE = weighted mean of its 12 factor
# scores, with per-signal weights (default 1 for every factor). The factors are
# flat - none is nested inside another. That score then reduces the pool of
# candidates for a pair-signal to a SINGLE shift, by one of two methods:
#
# s5_pm_shift_method = "weighted" (original)
# pm_shift_z = WEIGHTED MEAN of the candidates' implied shifts, weighted by
# their aggregate scores. Every candidate contributes; the pool's consensus
# sets the answer.
#
# s5_pm_shift_method = "best"
# pm_shift_z = the implied shift of the SINGLE highest-aggregate-score
# candidate. The pool is used only to rank; one match wins outright. Chosen
# when the strongest candidate tracks the truth better than the pooled
# average does (as the 3.14 diagnostic panels show).
#
# In both modes peaks and troughs are pooled - the winner / the average is taken
# over every candidate for the pair-signal, regardless of type.

# Reduction method for the per-pair-signal shift: "best" or "weighted".
# "rf"  - weight each candidate by a random forest's PREDICTED |error|, using a
#         sharp kernel anchored on the best prediction in its own pool. See the
#         block below. This is the method the per-signal models were trained for.
s5_pm_shift_method <- "best"

# ── The random-forest match-error model (method "rf") ────────────────────────
# Trained by TrainMatchErrorRF. One forest per signal, all eight prot_* sectors
# sharing one, plus a __fallback__ for anything unseen.
s5_rf_model_path <- "C:/Users/ascsh/Documents/1_Artemis/11_PaqLab/115_TreeTimeAlign/Models/match_error_rf.rds"

# The kernel:  w_i = exp(-k * ((e_i - min_pool e) / delta)^2)
# delta is the predicted-error gap, in metres above the pool's OWN best, at
# which a candidate is effectively discarded: exp(-5) = 0.0067.
#
# The anchor is the pool minimum, never zero. A pool where every candidate is
# predicted to be 30 cm out still yields an answer weighted toward its own
# best, rather than collapsing to all-zero weights and vanishing.
#
# Measured on the first training sample, delta 0.02 / 0.05 / 0.10 landed within
# 3 cm of each other, so this is not a knife-edge.
s5_rf_delta_m <- 0.05
s5_rf_k       <- 5

# A signal with no model of its own is scored by __fallback__ AND warned about.
# The warning is the point: the fallback was trained on every signal pooled, so
# it is a reasonable stand-in and a poor specialist, and a run should not
# quietly rely on one.
s5_rf_warn_fallback <- TRUE

# ── 1. The 12 factors and their per-signal weights ────────────────────────────
s5_pm_factors <- c(
  "rel_maj_tot", "rel_maj_sim",
  "rel_majorprom_tot", "rel_majorprom_sim",
  "rel_minorprom_tot", "rel_minorprom_sim",
  "pearson", "slope_agree", "median_prox", "consensus",
  "left_opp", "right_opp"
)

.par_apply("params-peak-candidate-weighting")
```

```{r}
s5_pm_weights <- setNames(
  lapply(names(s5_signal_registry), function(sk)
    setNames(rep(1.0, length(s5_pm_factors)), s5_pm_factors)),
```
