```{r}
# ── 2. Aggregate score ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
.sc_col <- function(f) paste0("sc_", f)

.aggregate_candidates <- function(cand, w) {
  if (is.null(cand) || nrow(cand) == 0L) return(cand)
  cols <- vapply(s5_pm_factors, .sc_col, character(1))
  M    <- as.matrix(cand[, cols, drop = FALSE])
  wv   <- as.numeric(w[s5_pm_factors])
  # Per-row weighted mean over the AVAILABLE (non-NA) factors, so a factor that
  # could not be computed for a candidate neither helps nor hurts it.
  Wmat <- matrix(wv, nrow = nrow(M), ncol = length(wv), byrow = TRUE)
  Wmat[is.na(M)] <- 0
  num  <- rowSums(Wmat * M, na.rm = TRUE)
  den  <- rowSums(Wmat)
  cand$agg_score <- ifelse(den > 0, num / den, NA_real_)
  cand
}

# ── 3. Reduce a pair-signal's candidates to one shift, by the chosen method ────
# Both methods work on the SAME per-group frame (finite implied_shift and
# agg_score, agg_score > 0) so the two modes are directly comparable.
# "weighted": score-weighted mean of the implied shifts; pm_score is the mean
# aggregate score of the contributing candidates.
# "best": the implied shift of the single highest-agg_score candidate;
# pm_score is that winner's own aggregate score.
# n_cand is the number of candidates that entered the reduction, in both modes.
if (!s5_pm_shift_method %in% c("best", "weighted", "rf"))
  stop("s5_pm_shift_method must be 'best', 'weighted' or 'rf'.")

# ── Load the forests, once, before any candidate is scored ───────────────────
# Read up front rather than per signal: a missing or malformed model file should
# stop the stage here, not eight signals into the loop with half the tables
# already overwritten.
.rf <- NULL
if (identical(s5_pm_shift_method, "rf")) {
  if (!requireNamespace("ranger", quietly = TRUE))
    stop("s5_pm_shift_method = 'rf' needs the ranger package.")
  if (!file.exists(s5_rf_model_path))
    stop(sprintf("Match-error model not found:\n  %s\nTrain one with TrainMatchErrorRF, or use method 'best'.",
                 s5_rf_model_path))
  .rf <- readRDS(s5_rf_model_path)
  .need <- c("features", "models", "group_of", "fallback", "target_scale")
  if (length(setdiff(.need, names(.rf))))
    stop(sprintf("Not a match-error model file - missing: %s",
                 paste(setdiff(.need, names(.rf)), collapse = ", ")))
  # Values pulled into plain locals first: cli's glue refuses any {expression}
  # beginning with a dot - since cli 3.4 that syntax is reserved for its own
  # styles - so `{.rf$version}` is a hard error, not a formatting nuisance.
  rf_ver  <- .rf$version %||% "?"
  rf_nmod <- length(setdiff(names(.rf$models), .rf$fallback))
  rf_nrow <- .rf$training$n_rows %||% NA
  rf_nsam <- length(.rf$training$samples %||% character(0))
  cli::cli_alert_info(
    "Match-error model v{rf_ver}: {rf_nmod} signal model(s) + fallback, trained on {rf_nrow} row(s) from {rf_nsam} sample(s).")
  rm(.need, rf_ver, rf_nmod, rf_nrow, rf_nsam)
}

#' Predicted |error| in METRES for every candidate in `cand`.
#'
#' The model returns a LOG - that is what it was trained on, because raw errors
#' span millimetres to tens of metres - so this exp()s it. Skipping that step
#' would not error; it would silently produce weights computed on the wrong
#' scale, which is why target_scale is checked rather than assumed.
.rf_predict_error <- function(cand, sig_key) {
  g  <- as.character(.rf$group_of(sig_key))
  mn <- if (!is.null(.rf$models[[g]])) g else .rf$fallback
  if (!identical(mn, g) && isTRUE(s5_rf_warn_fallback))
    warning(sprintf(paste0("[3.14 rf] Signal '%s' maps to model group '%s', which is not in the ",
                           "model file - scored with '%s' instead. That model was trained on all ",
                           "signals pooled, so it is a stand-in, not a specialist. Retrain ",
                           "including this signal."), sig_key, g, .rf$fallback), call. = FALSE)

  miss <- setdiff(.rf$features, names(cand))
  if (length(miss))
    stop(sprintf("[3.14 rf] Signal '%s' is missing predictor(s) the model needs: %s",
                 sig_key, paste(miss, collapse = ", ")))

  # Columns selected BY NAME in the model's own order - ranger matches
  # positionally, so a reordered factor list would silently score nonsense.
  p <- predict(.rf$models[[mn]], cand[, .rf$features, drop = FALSE])$predictions
  if (identical(.rf$target_scale, "log")) p <- exp(p)
  attr(p, "model_used") <- mn
  p
}

#' The weight kernel. `pred` are predicted errors in metres for ONE pool.
#'
#' Anchored on min(pred) within the pool it is called on, which is what keeps
#' pools comparable when their overall difficulty differs.
.rf_weights <- function(pred) {
  ok <- is.finite(pred)
  if (!any(ok)) return(rep(NA_real_, length(pred)))
  w <- exp(-s5_rf_k * ((pred - min(pred[ok])) / s5_rf_delta_m)^2)
  w[!ok] <- 0
  w
}

.reduce_pair_shift <- function(g, method) {
  if (method == "weighted") {
    tibble::tibble(
      pm_shift_z = stats::weighted.mean(g$implied_shift, g$agg_score),
      pm_score   = mean(g$agg_score),
      n_cand     = nrow(g)
    )
  } else if (method == "rf") {
    # Weights from the PREDICTED error, anchored on this pool's own best.
    w <- .rf_weights(g$pred_err_m)
    if (!any(is.finite(w)) || sum(w, na.rm = TRUE) <= 0) {
      tibble::tibble(pm_shift_z = NA_real_, pm_score = NA_real_, n_cand = nrow(g))
    } else {
      # pm_score is reported as the pool's BEST predicted error, negated, so
      # that "higher is better" still holds for every consumer of pm_score -
      # the downstream tables and figures all assume that direction.
      tibble::tibble(
        pm_shift_z = stats::weighted.mean(g$implied_shift, w),
        pm_score   = -min(g$pred_err_m[is.finite(g$pred_err_m)]),
        n_cand     = nrow(g)
      )
    }
  } else {                                   # "best"
    bi <- which.max(g$agg_score)
    tibble::tibble(
      pm_shift_z = g$implied_shift[bi],
      pm_score   = g$agg_score[bi],
      n_cand     = nrow(g)
    )
  }
}

pm_pair_shift    <- list()
s57_results      <- list()
s5_rf_model_used <- list()

for (sig_key in names(s5_signal_registry)) {
  obj <- paste0("pm_candidates_", sig_key)
  if (!exists(obj)) next
  cand <- get(obj, envir = .stage_env())
  if (is.null(cand) || nrow(cand) == 0L) next

  w    <- s5_pm_weights[[sig_key]]
  cand <- .aggregate_candidates(cand, w)

  # Predicted error rides along on the candidate table, so it is written back
  # below with everything else and reaches the optimisation CSV - which is what
  # makes a run's weights auditable after the fact.
  if (identical(s5_pm_shift_method, "rf")) {
    cand$pred_err_m <- .rf_predict_error(cand, sig_key)
    s5_rf_model_used[[sig_key]] <- attr(cand$pred_err_m, "model_used")
  }

  # write agg_score back onto the stored candidate/diag tables
  assign(paste0("pm_candidates_",  sig_key), cand, envir = .stage_env())
  assign(paste0("s57_combo_diag_", sig_key), cand, envir = .stage_env())

  # per pair-signal: reduce to one shift by the toggled method
  # In "rf" mode the gate is a finite prediction, not a positive agg_score: a
  # candidate the hand weights happen to score 0 may still be the one the forest
  # ranks best, and dropping it here would silently reinstate the old weighting.
  ps <- cand |>
    dplyr::filter(if (identical(s5_pm_shift_method, "rf"))
                    is.finite(implied_shift) & is.finite(pred_err_m)
                  else is.finite(implied_shift) & is.finite(agg_score) & agg_score > 0) |>
    dplyr::group_by(signal, TreeID_1, TreeID_2, pair) |>
    dplyr::group_modify(~ .reduce_pair_shift(.x, s5_pm_shift_method)) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()

  pm_pair_shift[[sig_key]] <- ps
  assign(paste0("pm_pair_shift_", sig_key), ps, envir = .stage_env())

  # Compatibility object for the downstream per-signal aggregation, which reads
  # s57_results_<sig>$pm_shift_z (one row per pair).
  res <- ps |> dplyr::select(TreeID_1, TreeID_2, pm_shift_z, pm_score, n_cand)
  s57_results[[sig_key]] <- res
  assign(paste0("s57_results_", sig_key), res, envir = .stage_env())
}

s57_pair_shift <- dplyr::bind_rows(pm_pair_shift)

# ── Report ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if (!requireNamespace("cli", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("cli")
cli::cli_h1("3.14 Candidate weighting -> per-pair-signal shift  (method: {s5_pm_shift_method})")
if (nrow(s57_pair_shift) == 0L) {
  cli::cli_alert_warning("No per-pair-signal shifts produced.")
} else {
  .rep <- s57_pair_shift |>
    dplyr::group_by(signal) |>
    dplyr::summarise(pairs = dplyr::n(),
                     med   = median(pm_shift_z),
                     mean  = mean(pm_shift_z),
                     sd    = sd(pm_shift_z),
                     .groups = "drop") |>
    as.data.frame()
  print(.rep, row.names = FALSE)
  cli::cli_alert_info("Method '{s5_pm_shift_method}': per-pair-signal shifts in s57_pair_shift / pm_pair_shift_<sig>; compatibility per-pair table in s57_results_<sig> (pm_shift_z).")
}
```

### Vis - Aggregate score by shift per pair

```{r}
#| label: params-fig-pm-candidate-weight-shift
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Per signal-pair: scatter each candidate's implied z-shift (x) against its aggregate score / weight (y)"


# ── What this does ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# One panel per temporal pair, one point per match candidate. The x position is
# the candidate's IMPLIED SHIFT (las_2 global_z - las_1 global_z); the y position
# is its AGGREGATE SCORE - the weighted mean of its factor scores that Step 3.14
# used as the candidate's weight in the shift average. So height IS influence: a
# point high on the y axis pulled the pair's result toward its x. Reading a panel
# is then direct - do the heavy (high-y) candidates agree on an x, or is the
# weight spread across disagreeing shifts?
#
# Two vertical rules and a ring turn the scatter into a verdict:
# golden solid - s5_pm_true_shift, the known truth (drawn only if 3.13.3, which
# defines it, has been run).
# dashed grey - pm_shift_z, where the score-weighted average actually landed.
# black ring - the single BEST-scoring candidate (highest y).
# A good pair has its high-y points and its best candidate sitting on the golden
# line, with the dashed line landing there too. The subtitle prints the weighted
# average, the best candidate's shift, and the average's error against truth.
#
# Peaks and troughs are drawn together (they were pooled into the one shift) but
# kept visually distinct, since a shift carried mostly by troughs vs mostly by
# peaks is worth seeing at a glance.

s5_wsh_shape <- c(peak = 24L, trough = 25L)                 # up / down triangles
s5_wsh_fill  <- c(peak = "#1b9e77", trough = "#d95f02")     # green peak, orange trough
s5_wsh_gold  <- "#d4a017"                                   # truth rule

# ── What the y axis shows ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The panel's whole claim is that HEIGHT IS INFLUENCE - a point high on y pulled
# the pair's answer toward its x. That only holds if y is the quantity the
# reduction actually weighted by, so the default follows s5_pm_shift_method
# rather than being fixed to agg_score:
#
#   "auto"      -> the weight the chosen method used. In "rf" mode that is the
#                  kernel weight exp(-k*((e - min_pool e)/delta)^2); in "best"
#                  and "weighted" mode it is agg_score, as before.
#   "weight"    -> force the kernel weight (rf only; falls back to agg_score).
#   "pred_err"  -> the RAW predicted error in metres, NOT a weight. Useful for
#                  reading the model directly, but the axis then runs the OTHER
#                  WAY - low is good - so "height is influence" is inverted.
#                  The panel says so when this is chosen.
#   "agg_score" -> force the old hand-weighted score even in rf mode, to see
#                  what the previous weighting would have done.
s5_wsh_y <- "auto"

.par_apply("params-fig-pm-candidate-weight-shift")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-pm-candidate-weight-shift
#| standalone: true
#| fig: false
#| results: asis
#| column: page
#| code-summary: "Per signal-pair: scatter each candidate's implied z-shift (x) against its aggregate score / weight (y)"

# truth is optional - only present once 3.13.3 has defined it
.wsh_truth <- if (exists("s5_pm_true_shift")) s5_pm_true_shift else NA_real_

# ── What is being plotted, resolved once ─────────────────────────────────────
# Both galleries in this section must agree with the reduction about which
# candidate won and how much each one counted. Reading agg_score while the
# reduction ran on rf weights would draw a weighting that was never used - the
# most misleading kind of diagnostic, because it looks right.
# Braced. A bare top-level `if (x)\n a\nelse\n b` is a parse error in R - the
# parser closes the statement at the end of the first branch and then meets an
# orphan `else`. It is legal inside a function body, which is why it slips
# through when written by habit.
.wsh_mode <- if (identical(s5_wsh_y, "auto")) {
  if (identical(s5_pm_shift_method, "rf")) "weight" else "agg_score"
} else {
  s5_wsh_y
}
if (.wsh_mode %in% c("weight", "pred_err") && !identical(s5_pm_shift_method, "rf")) {
  message("fig 3.14: s5_wsh_y = '", .wsh_mode,
          "' needs rf predictions, which this run has none of - showing agg_score.")
  .wsh_mode <- "agg_score"
}

# Lower is better for pred_err, higher for the other two. Ring, sort and axis
# label all read this rather than re-deciding, so they cannot disagree.
.wsh_lower_better <- identical(.wsh_mode, "pred_err")

#' The y value for every candidate in ONE pair-signal pool.
#'
#' The kernel is anchored on min(pred) WITHIN this pool - the same anchoring and
#' the same grouping the reduction used, since a panel IS one pair-signal pool.
#' So the heights drawn are the weights that were actually applied.
.wsh_yvals <- function(d) {
  if (identical(.wsh_mode, "weight"))   return(.rf_weights(d$pred_err_m))
  if (identical(.wsh_mode, "pred_err")) return(d$pred_err_m)
  d$agg_score
}

.wsh_ylab <- switch(.wsh_mode,
  weight    = sprintf("kernel weight (delta = %.2f m, k = %g)", s5_rf_delta_m, s5_rf_k),
  pred_err  = "predicted |error| (m)  -  LOW is good, so height is NOT influence",
  "aggregate score (weight in shift average)")

# The column a candidate must have a finite value in to be plotted at all.
.wsh_need <- if (.wsh_mode %in% c("weight", "pred_err")) "pred_err_m" else "agg_score"

make_pair_weight_shift_plot <- function(cand_sig, ps_sig, tid1, tid2) {
  pair_str <- paste0(tid1, "\u2192", tid2)
  d <- cand_sig[cand_sig$pair == pair_str &
                is.finite(cand_sig$implied_shift) &
                is.finite(cand_sig[[.wsh_need]]), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(d) == 0L) return(NULL)

  # Computed AFTER subsetting to this pair, so the kernel anchors on this pool's
  # own best - exactly as the reduction did.
  d$wsh_y <- .wsh_yvals(d)
  d <- d[is.finite(d$wsh_y), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(d) == 0L) return(NULL)

  # the pair's final weighted shift, looked up from the 3.14 per-pair table
  pm_z <- if (!is.null(ps_sig)) {
    v <- ps_sig$pm_shift_z[ps_sig$pair == pair_str]
    if (length(v)) v[1L] else NA_real_
  } else NA_real_

  # The single strongest candidate, by whatever the reduction ranked on.
  bi        <- if (.wsh_lower_better) which.min(d$wsh_y) else which.max(d$wsh_y)
  best      <- d[bi, , drop = FALSE]
  best_z    <- best$implied_shift[1L]
  best_type <- best$type[1L]

  err_txt <- if (is.finite(pm_z) && is.finite(.wsh_truth))
    sprintf("  |  error %+.3f m", pm_z - .wsh_truth) else ""

  gg <- ggplot(d, aes(implied_shift, wsh_y)) +
    { if (is.finite(.wsh_truth))
        geom_vline(xintercept = .wsh_truth, colour = s5_wsh_gold,
                   linewidth = 0.9) } +
    { if (is.finite(pm_z))
        geom_vline(xintercept = pm_z, colour = "grey30",
                   linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) } +
    geom_point(aes(shape = type, fill = type), colour = "grey20",
               size = 2.8, stroke = 0.4, alpha = 0.85, na.rm = TRUE) +
    # ring the best-scoring candidate so it is findable in the cloud
    geom_point(data = best, aes(implied_shift, wsh_y),
               shape = 21, fill = NA, colour = "black",
               size = 5.5, stroke = 1.1) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = s5_wsh_shape, name = NULL) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = s5_wsh_fill, name = NULL) +
    # pred_err has no meaningful zero to anchor to, and forcing one squashes
    # every panel against the top of its range.
    { if (identical(.wsh_mode, "pred_err")) NULL else coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, NA)) } +
    labs(title    = sprintf("Pair %s / %s", tid1, tid2),
         subtitle = sprintf(
           "%d candidate(s)  |  %s shift %+.3f m  |  best-cand shift %+.3f m (%s)%s%s",
           nrow(d),
           if (identical(s5_pm_shift_method, "rf")) "rf-weighted" else "weighted-avg",
           if (is.finite(pm_z)) pm_z else NA_real_,
           best_z, best_type, err_txt,
           if ("pred_err_m" %in% names(best) && is.finite(best$pred_err_m[1L]))
             sprintf("  |  best predicted error %.3f m", best$pred_err_m[1L]) else ""),
         x = "implied global z-shift (m)",
         y = .wsh_ylab) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey40"),
          legend.position = "top")
  gg
}

# ── Render ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
.wsh_pairs <- pairs_ax_fitted

# Reuse the LOESS figure's signal narrowing when it exists, so the galleries stay
# in step with the rest of the section.
.wsh_keys <- if (exists("s5_vis_signals") && !is.null(s5_vis_signals))
               intersect(s5_vis_signals, names(s5_signal_registry)) else
               names(s5_signal_registry)

for (sig_key in .wsh_keys) {
  sr  <- s5_signal_registry[[sig_key]]
  obj <- paste0("pm_candidates_", sig_key)
  if (!exists(obj)) next
  cand_sig <- get(obj, envir = .stage_env())
  if (is.null(cand_sig) || nrow(cand_sig) == 0L ||
      !(.wsh_need %in% names(cand_sig))) next

  ps_obj  <- paste0("pm_pair_shift_", sig_key)
  ps_sig  <- if (exists(ps_obj)) get(ps_obj, envir = .stage_env()) else NULL

  plots <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(.wsh_pairs)), function(i) {
    make_pair_weight_shift_plot(cand_sig, ps_sig,
                                .wsh_pairs$TreeID_1[i], .wsh_pairs$TreeID_2[i])
  })
  names(plots) <- sprintf("Pair %s / %s",
                          .wsh_pairs$TreeID_1, .wsh_pairs$TreeID_2)
  plots <- plots[!vapply(plots, is.null, logical(1))]
  if (length(plots) == 0L) next

  truth_note <- if (is.finite(.wsh_truth))
    sprintf(" | golden = truth (%.3f m), dashed grey = weighted shift", .wsh_truth)
  else " | dashed grey = weighted shift (truth unavailable - run 3.13.3)"

  print(htmltools::browsable(htmltools::tagList(
    htmltools::h3(sprintf("Step 3.14 \u2014 %s: candidate weight vs implied z-shift",
                          sr$label)),
    htmltools::p(sprintf(
      "x = implied global z-shift, y = %s | black ring = %s candidate%s | up triangle = peak, down triangle = trough | %d pair(s)",
      .wsh_ylab,
      if (.wsh_lower_better) "lowest predicted error" else "highest-weighted",
      truth_note, length(plots))),
    render_panel_gallery(plots, paste0("s315wsh_", sig_key), ncols = 1L)
  )))
}
```






### Vis - LOESS curves with PM-matched peaks

```{r}
#| label: params-fig-pm-matched-peaks
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Render LOESS curve galleries with the single highest-scoring PM feature match per pair gold-lined"


# ── What this does ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# One panel per kept pair, per signal: the two epochs' LOESS curves (las_1 blue,
# las_2 red) with their raw scatter behind them. Every scored match candidate for
# the pair is marked faintly; the SINGLE highest-agg_score candidate - the best
# feature match the weighting found - is drawn in GOLD: one line at its las_1
# feature position (h1) and one at its las_2 feature position (h2). Those two
# gold lines ARE the match: the feature at h1 in epoch 1 paired with the feature
# at h2 in epoch 2, and the vertical gap between the curves at those lines is the
# implied Z-shift the pair contributed.
#
# Rebuilt for the current pipeline: detrending is gone (so there is one panel,
# not a raw/detrended pair), and the winner is read straight from the top
# agg_score row of pm_candidates_<sig> rather than from retired pm_win_idx
# columns.

COL_GOLD <- "#D4A017"   # the winning match

.par_apply("params-fig-pm-matched-peaks")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-pm-matched-peaks
#| standalone: true
#| fig: false
#| results: asis
#| column: page
#| code-summary: "Render LOESS curve galleries with the single highest-scoring PM feature match per pair gold-lined"

.mp_pairs <- if (exists("kept_pairs")) kept_pairs else pairs_ax_fitted

# ── Which quantity ranks the winner ──────────────────────────────────────────
# The same s5_wsh_y that drives the candidate-weight gallery, resolved HERE
# rather than read from that chunk's .wsh_mode. The two galleries are separate
# chunks and either can be run without the other, so borrowing a name across
# them would work by hand and fail the moment one is skipped.
#
# "weight" and "pred_err" rank identically - the kernel is monotone decreasing
# in predicted error - so the gold line is the same under both; only the
# candidate-weight panel's axis differs. That leaves two real rankings:
# rf-predicted error, or the hand-weighted agg_score.
.mp_y <- if (exists("s5_wsh_y")) s5_wsh_y else "auto"
.mp_mode <- if (identical(.mp_y, "auto")) {
  if (identical(s5_pm_shift_method, "rf")) "weight" else "agg_score"
} else {
  .mp_y
}
if (.mp_mode %in% c("weight", "pred_err") &&
    !identical(s5_pm_shift_method, "rf")) .mp_mode <- "agg_score"

# TRUE when the winner is the LOWEST value, i.e. any rf-predicted-error ranking.
.mp_rf   <- .mp_mode %in% c("weight", "pred_err")
.mp_need <- if (.mp_rf) "pred_err_m" else "agg_score"

make_pm_peaks_plot <- function(tid1, tid2, bt1, bt2,
                               pred_col, field, y_lab,
                               cand_pair) {
  t1c <- as.character(tid1); t2c <- as.character(tid2)
  c1 <- bt1[[t1c]]; c2 <- bt2[[t2c]]
  if (is.null(c1) || is.null(c2)) return(NULL)

  # curve lines
  df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    tibble::tibble(h = c1$h, pred = c1[[pred_col]], cl = "las_1"),
    tibble::tibble(h = c2$h, pred = c2[[pred_col]], cl = "las_2")
  ) |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(pred))
  if (nrow(df) == 0L) return(NULL)

  # raw scatter behind the curves
  r1 <- ellipses_ax_1_valid[[t1c]]
  r2 <- ellipses_ax_2_valid[[t2c]]
  pts <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    if (!is.null(r1) && field %in% names(r1))
      tibble::tibble(h = r1$stem_len, val = r1[[field]], cl = "las_1"),
    if (!is.null(r2) && field %in% names(r2))
      tibble::tibble(h = r2$stem_len, val = r2[[field]], cl = "las_2")
  ) |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(val))

  # ── the winner: the candidate the REDUCTION ranked first for this pair ──────
  # In rf mode that is the LOWEST predicted error, not the highest agg_score.
  # Gold-lining the agg_score winner while the shift came from the rf winner
  # would put the gold lines on a match that contributed almost nothing - on the
  # first sample tested, 2.6 m away from the one that actually set the answer.
  best <- NULL
  if (!is.null(cand_pair) && nrow(cand_pair) > 0L &&
      .mp_need %in% names(cand_pair)) {
    cp <- cand_pair[is.finite(cand_pair[[.mp_need]]), , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(cp) > 0L)
      best <- cp[if (.mp_rf) which.min(cp$pred_err_m) else which.max(cp$agg_score), ,
                 drop = FALSE]
  }

  # faint marks for every candidate feature (both epochs), so the winner reads
  # against the field of alternatives it beat
  others1 <- if (!is.null(cand_pair)) tibble::tibble(x = cand_pair$h1) else tibble::tibble(x = numeric(0))
  others2 <- if (!is.null(cand_pair)) tibble::tibble(x = cand_pair$h2) else tibble::tibble(x = numeric(0))
  win1 <- if (!is.null(best)) tibble::tibble(x = best$h1[1L]) else tibble::tibble(x = numeric(0))
  win2 <- if (!is.null(best)) tibble::tibble(x = best$h2[1L]) else tibble::tibble(x = numeric(0))

  # subtitle: the winner's type/score/implied shift, and the pair's final shift
  pm_z    <- if (!is.null(best)) best$implied_shift[1L] else NA_real_
  win_ty  <- if (!is.null(best)) best$type[1L]          else NA_character_
  win_sc  <- if (is.null(best)) NA_real_ else best[[.mp_need]][1L]
  sub_str <- sprintf(
    "best match: %s  |  %s = %s  |  implied Z = %s m",
    if (is.na(win_ty)) "none" else win_ty,
    if (.mp_rf) "predicted error (m)" else "score",
    if (is.na(win_sc)) "NA" else sprintf("%.3f", win_sc),
    if (is.na(pm_z))   "NA" else sprintf("%+.4f", pm_z)
  )

  gg <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::geom_point(data = pts, ggplot2::aes(h, val, colour = cl),
                        size = 0.9, alpha = 0.2, na.rm = TRUE) +
    # other candidate features, faint and colour-coded by epoch
    { if (nrow(others1) > 0L)
        ggplot2::geom_vline(data = others1, ggplot2::aes(xintercept = x),
                            colour = COL_1, linewidth = 0.5,
                            linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.35) } +
    { if (nrow(others2) > 0L)
        ggplot2::geom_vline(data = others2, ggplot2::aes(xintercept = x),
                            colour = COL_2, linewidth = 0.5,
                            linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.35) } +
    ggplot2::geom_line(data = df, ggplot2::aes(h, pred, colour = cl),
                       linewidth = 0.85, na.rm = TRUE) +
    # the winning match: a gold line at each epoch's feature position
    { if (nrow(win1) > 0L)
        ggplot2::geom_vline(data = win1, ggplot2::aes(xintercept = x),
                            colour = COL_GOLD, linewidth = 1.3) } +
    { if (nrow(win2) > 0L)
        ggplot2::geom_vline(data = win2, ggplot2::aes(xintercept = x),
                            colour = COL_GOLD, linewidth = 1.3,
                            linetype = "22") } +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c(las_1 = COL_1, las_2 = COL_2),
                                 name = NULL) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(xlim = range(df$h, na.rm = TRUE)) +
    ggplot2::labs(title    = sprintf("Pair %s / %s", tid1, tid2),
                  subtitle = sub_str,
                  x = "distance from per stem origin, along axis (m)",
                  y = y_lab) +
    ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.title    = ggplot2::element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", colour = "grey20"),
      plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7.5, colour = "grey40"),
      plot.background  = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA))
  gg
}

# ── Render galleries per signal ───────────────────────────────────────────────
for (sig_key in names(s5_signal_registry)[unlist(s57_run_flags)]) {

  sr  <- s5_signal_registry[[sig_key]]
  bt1 <- get(sr$by_tid_1, envir = .stage_env())
  bt2 <- get(sr$by_tid_2, envir = .stage_env())

  cand_obj <- paste0("pm_candidates_", sig_key)
  if (!exists(cand_obj)) {
    message("fig-pm-matched-peaks: ", cand_obj, " not found – skipping.")
    next
  }
  cand_sig <- get(cand_obj, envir = .stage_env())
  # .mp_need was resolved at the top of the chunk; its absence means "3.14 has
  # not run in this mode yet".
  if (is.null(cand_sig) || nrow(cand_sig) == 0L ||
      !(.mp_need %in% names(cand_sig))) {
    message("fig-pm-matched-peaks: ", cand_obj, " has no ", .mp_need,
            " (run 3.14 first) – skipping.")
    next
  }

  plots <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(.mp_pairs)), function(i) {
    tid1 <- .mp_pairs$TreeID_1[i]; tid2 <- .mp_pairs$TreeID_2[i]
    pair_str  <- paste0(tid1, "\u2192", tid2)
    cand_pair <- cand_sig[cand_sig$pair == pair_str, , drop = FALSE]
    make_pm_peaks_plot(tid1, tid2, bt1, bt2,
                       pred_col = sr$pred_col, field = sr$field, y_lab = sr$y_lab,
                       cand_pair = cand_pair)
  })
  names(plots) <- sprintf("Pair %s / %s", .mp_pairs$TreeID_1, .mp_pairs$TreeID_2)
  plots <- plots[!vapply(plots, is.null, logical(1))]
  if (length(plots) == 0L) next

  print(htmltools::browsable(htmltools::tagList(
    htmltools::h3(sprintf("3.12 \u2014 %s: %s PM feature match (kept pairs)",
                          sr$label,
                          if (.mp_rf) "lowest predicted-error" else "highest-scoring")),
    htmltools::p(htmltools::HTML(sprintf(
      "<span style='color:%s'>&#x25A0;</span> best match, las_1 feature (solid gold) &nbsp;
       <span style='color:%s'>&#x25A0;</span> best match, las_2 feature (dashed gold) &nbsp;
       <span style='color:%s'>&#x25A0;</span> las_1 curve &nbsp;
       <span style='color:%s'>&#x25A0;</span> las_2 curve &nbsp; | other candidate features shown faint/dashed",
      COL_GOLD, COL_GOLD, COL_1, COL_2))),
    render_panel_gallery(plots, paste0("s513pm_", sig_key), ncols = 2L)
  )))
}
```

## 3.14b Pool the Protrusion Sectors into One Measurement

Each `prot_*` sector is a weak signal on its own. The eight together are one
measurement of the same thing in eight directions, so they must reach Step 3.15
as a **single** vote rather than as eight - otherwise protrusion outvotes every
other signal, on the strength of being finely subdivided rather than of being
informative.

**Why not simply pool the candidates.** The obvious approach - one kernel over
the union of all eight sectors' candidates - fails, measurably. Within a single
pair the eight sectors' *best* predicted errors are spread by around 0.35 m (up
to 0.77 m on the sample this was built against), roughly seven times
`s5_rf_delta_m`. A union kernel anchored on the single global best therefore
drives seven sectors to zero weight and keeps one. That is not pooling eight
weak signals; it is picking one and discarding the rest.

Per-pair error of the pooled protrusion shift, measured on that sample:

| pooling | median | within 5 cm |
|---|---|---|
| union, one kernel over all 8 | 0.285 m | 8.3% |
| per-sector kernels, then mean | 0.651 m | 5.6% |
| per-sector kernels, then median | 0.232 m | 19.4% |
| **per-sector kernels, then MAD + mean** | **0.269 m** | **22.2%** |

The plain mean fails the other way - one wild sector drags it. Only a robust
combiner works, and MAD-then-mean is the same idiom Step 3.15 already uses at
its two levels, so this is a third instance of one pattern rather than a special
case.

Note the multiplier: **2.0, not the 3.0 used elsewhere.** At 3 the filter barely
engages on eight values and the hit rate falls to 13.9%.

```{r}
#| label: params-pool-protrusion
#| code-summary: "Parameters - collapse the prot_* sectors to one signal"

# FALSE leaves all eight sectors as separate signals, exactly as before. Pooling
# is only meaningful for a family that is a subdivision of ONE measurement,
# which is why it is keyed to a pattern rather than always on.
s3_pool_sectors     <- TRUE
s3_pool_pattern     <- "^prot_"
s3_pool_name        <- "protrusion"

# MAD multiplier across the eight sector shifts. 2.0, not 3.0 - see above.
s3_pool_mad_k       <- 2.00

# A pair needs at least this many sectors to produce a pooled shift. Below it
# the MAD has nothing to work with and the "pooled" value would be one or two
# sectors wearing the name of eight.
s3_pool_min_sectors <- 3L

.par_apply("params-pool-protrusion")
```

```{r}
#| label: pool-protrusion
#| code-summary: "Per-sector shifts -> MAD across sectors -> one protrusion shift per pair"

s3_pool_applied <- FALSE
s3_pool_tbl     <- NULL

.get_sector_tbl <- function(sk) {
  o <- paste0("pm_pair_shift_", sk)
  if (exists(o, envir = .stage_env())) get(o, envir = .stage_env()) else NULL
}

.sector_keys <- if (isTRUE(s3_pool_sectors))
  grep(s3_pool_pattern, names(s5_signal_registry), value = TRUE) else character(0)

if (length(.sector_keys) < 2L) {
  if (isTRUE(s3_pool_sectors))
    cli::cli_alert_info("3.14b: {length(.sector_keys)} sector(s) match {s3_pool_pattern} - nothing to pool.")
} else {

  .sec <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(.sector_keys, function(sk) {
    d <- .get_sector_tbl(sk)
    if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L) return(NULL)
    tibble::tibble(signal = sk, TreeID_1 = d$TreeID_1, TreeID_2 = d$TreeID_2,
                   pair = d$pair, pm_shift_z = d$pm_shift_z, pm_score = d$pm_score)
  }))

  if (is.null(.sec) || nrow(.sec) == 0L) {
    cli::cli_alert_warning("3.14b: no sector produced a shift - protrusion contributes nothing.")
  } else {

    s3_pool_tbl <- .sec |>
      dplyr::filter(is.finite(pm_shift_z)) |>
      dplyr::group_by(TreeID_1, TreeID_2, pair) |>
      dplyr::group_modify(function(g, ...) {
        n <- nrow(g)
        if (n < s3_pool_min_sectors)
          return(tibble::tibble(pm_shift_z = NA_real_, pm_score = NA_real_,
                                n_sectors = n, n_kept = 0L,
                                sector_sd = NA_real_, reason = "too few sectors"))
        md   <- stats::mad(g$pm_shift_z)
        keep <- if (!is.finite(md) || md == 0) rep(TRUE, n)
                else abs(g$pm_shift_z - stats::median(g$pm_shift_z)) <= s3_pool_mad_k * md
        # Every sector rejected means the MAD found no centre. Keep them all and
        # let Step 3.15's own filters judge the result, rather than emitting an
        # NA that would silently remove protrusion from this pair.
        if (!any(keep)) keep <- rep(TRUE, n)
        tibble::tibble(
          pm_shift_z = mean(g$pm_shift_z[keep]),
          pm_score   = mean(g$pm_score[keep]),
          n_sectors  = n, n_kept = sum(keep),
          sector_sd  = if (n > 1L) stats::sd(g$pm_shift_z) else NA_real_,
          reason     = if (all(keep)) "all kept" else "MAD filtered")
      }) |>
      dplyr::ungroup() |>
      dplyr::mutate(signal = s3_pool_name) |>
      dplyr::relocate(signal)

    .pooled <- s3_pool_tbl |>
      dplyr::filter(is.finite(pm_shift_z)) |>
      dplyr::transmute(signal, TreeID_1, TreeID_2, pair, pm_shift_z, pm_score,
                       n_cand = n_kept)

    # Published under the pooled name so Step 3.15 finds it exactly as it finds
    # any other signal. The eight sector tables are left untouched on purpose -
    # they are what the diagnostics and the optimisation CSV read.
    assign(paste0("pm_pair_shift_", s3_pool_name), .pooled, envir = .stage_env())
    assign(paste0("s57_results_",   s3_pool_name),
           dplyr::select(.pooled, TreeID_1, TreeID_2, pm_shift_z, pm_score, n_cand),
           envir = .stage_env())
    s57_run_flags[[s3_pool_name]] <- TRUE
    s3_pool_applied <- TRUE

    cli::cli_h1("3.14b Protrusion sectors -> one signal (MAD k = {s3_pool_mad_k})")
    cli::cli_alert_success(
      "{length(.sector_keys)} sector(s) pooled into '{s3_pool_name}' for {nrow(.pooled)} pair(s).")
    cli::cli_alert_info(
      "Sectors kept per pair: median {stats::median(s3_pool_tbl$n_kept)} of {stats::median(s3_pool_tbl$n_sectors)}.")
    if (any(is.finite(s3_pool_tbl$sector_sd)))
      cli::cli_alert_info(
        "Spread across sectors within a pair: median sd {round(stats::median(s3_pool_tbl$sector_sd, na.rm = TRUE), 4)} m.")
    .short <- sum(s3_pool_tbl$reason == "too few sectors")
    if (.short > 0L)
      cli::cli_alert_warning("{.short} pair(s) had fewer than {s3_pool_min_sectors} sector(s) - no protrusion shift.")
    rm(.short, .pooled)
  }
  rm(.sec)
}
rm(.sector_keys)
```

## 3.15 Per-pair Averages

```{r}
#| label: params-per-pair-averages
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Two-stage MAD outlier filter (stage 1: within a pair across signals; stage 2: within a group across pairs), then a fixed per-signal-weighted average WITHIN EACH PAIR across the surviving signals -> per-pair Z-shift"


# ── What this does ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Reduces the per-pair-signal shifts from Step 3.14 to one shift per temporal
# PAIR, through two MAD outlier passes and a fixed-weight average:
#
# STAGE 1 - within a pair, across signals. For each temporal pair, the signals'
# pm_shift_z values form a pool; a signal whose shift is a MAD outlier among
# the other signals on that same pair is dropped for that pair. Catches one
# signal misbehaving on one pair. Multiplier: s58_pair_k.
#
# STAGE 2 - within a group, across pairs. The stage-1 survivors are pooled by
# GROUP (sa + sb -> "semi_axes"; all eight prot_* -> "protrusion"; every
# other signal alone) and MAD-filtered again across all pairs in the group.
# Multiplier: s58_group_k. (Grouping is used ONLY for this cross-pair MAD
# pass; it plays no part in the averaging below.)
#
# STAGE 3 - per-PAIR weighted average across signals. For each pair, the rows
# that survived BOTH stages are averaged, WEIGHTED BY A FIXED PER-SIGNAL
# WEIGHT (s58_signal_weight), not by pm_score. Because either MAD stage can
# drop a signal on a given pair, a pair's average is taken over whatever
# signals remain for it; the weights are renormalised over exactly those
# present signals, so a pair missing some signals is not penalised.
#
# A row is (pair x signal); it must survive BOTH passes to enter its pair's
# average. Output: one Z-shift per pair (s58_pair_shift[[pair]] and the table
# s58_pair_tbl), replacing the previous per-group shift.

# ── Signal selection ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
s58_use_request <- list()   # e.g. list(prot_W_SW = FALSE) to drop a signal

# ── MAD multipliers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
s58_pair_k  <- 1.50   # STAGE 1: within-pair, across-signal (one scalar for all pairs)

s58_group_k_default <- 2.00

s58_signal_weight_default <- 1.00

.par_apply("params-per-pair-averages")
```

```{r}
#| label: per-pair-averages
#| code-summary: "Two-stage MAD outlier filter (stage 1: within a pair across signals; stage 2: within a group across pairs), then a fixed per-signal-weighted average WITHIN EACH PAIR across the surviving signals -> per-pair Z-shift"

s58_use <- setNames(
  vapply(names(s5_signal_registry), function(sk) {
    req <- s58_use_request[[sk]]
    isTRUE(s57_run_flags[[sk]]) && (is.null(req) || isTRUE(req))
  }, logical(1)),
  names(s5_signal_registry)
)

# ── Grouping (used only for the stage-2 cross-pair MAD pass) ──────────────────
s58_group_of <- function(sk) {
  if (sk %in% c("sa", "sb"))   return("semi_axes")
  if (startsWith(sk, "prot_")) return("protrusion")
  # The pooled signal IS its own group. Reaching here as "protrusion" already,
  # it falls through to the last line and returns itself - correct, and stated
  # rather than left to be rediscovered.
  sk
}

s58_group_k <- c(     # STAGE 2: within-group, across-pair (per group)
  area          = 2.00,
  center_offset = 2.00,
  semi_axes     = 2.00,
  ecc           = 1.00,
  protrusion    = 1.00
)

# ── Per-SIGNAL averaging weights (STAGE 3) ───────────────────────────────────
# The fixed weight each signal carries into its pair's cross-signal average.
# These replace pm_score as the weight. Any signal not listed here falls back to
# s58_signal_weight_default. Weights are renormalised per pair over the signals
# that actually survived both MAD stages for that pair, so only the RELATIVE
# values matter - a signal at 2.0 counts twice one at 1.0 when both are present.
s58_signal_weight <- c(
  area          = 2.00,
  center_offset = 2.00,
  sa            = 1.00,
  sb            = 1.00,
  ecc           = 0.50,
  prot_N_NE     = 0.20,
  prot_E_NE     = 0.20,
  prot_E_SE     = 0.20,
  prot_S_SE     = 0.20,
  prot_S_SW     = 0.20,
  prot_W_SW     = 0.20,
  prot_W_NW     = 0.20,
  prot_N_NW     = 0.20
)

# ── Truth (optional, from 3.13.3) ────────────────────────────────────────────
.s58_truth <- if (exists("s5_pm_true_shift")) s5_pm_true_shift else NA_real_

# ── Assemble one long table: one row per (pair, signal) ───────────────────────
.get_pairtbl <- function(sk) {
  o <- paste0("pm_pair_shift_", sk)   # signal, TreeID_1/2, pair, pm_shift_z, pm_score
  if (exists(o)) get(o, envir = .stage_env()) else NULL
}
.active_sigs <- names(s5_signal_registry)[s58_use[names(s5_signal_registry)]]

# Step 3.14b replaced the eight sectors with one pooled signal. Swap it in here,
# so the within-pair MAD below sees protrusion as ONE vote among six rather than
# as eight among thirteen. Without this the sectors would be counted twice -
# once each, and again inside the pooled value.
if (isTRUE(s3_pool_applied)) {
  .dropped     <- grep(s3_pool_pattern, .active_sigs, value = TRUE)
  .active_sigs <- c(setdiff(.active_sigs, .dropped), s3_pool_name)
  cli::cli_alert_info(
    "3.15 input: {length(.dropped)} sector(s) replaced by '{s3_pool_name}' - {length(.active_sigs)} signal(s) vote per pair.")
  rm(.dropped)
}

long <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(.active_sigs, function(sk) {
  d <- .get_pairtbl(sk)
  if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L) return(NULL)
  tibble::tibble(
    signal     = sk,
    group      = s58_group_of(sk),
    TreeID_1   = d$TreeID_1, TreeID_2 = d$TreeID_2, pair = d$pair,
    pm_shift_z = d$pm_shift_z, pm_score = d$pm_score
  )
}))

# a single MAD test: TRUE where x is an outlier vs the pool median at multiplier k
.mad_outlier <- function(x, k) {
  ok  <- is.finite(x)
  med <- median(x[ok]); md <- mad(x[ok]); if (is.na(md) || md == 0) md <- 1e-6
  out <- rep(FALSE, length(x))
  out[ok] <- abs(x[ok] - med) > k * md
  out
}

# ── STAGE 1: within each pair, across the signals on that pair ────────────────
long$stage1_out <- FALSE
if (!is.null(long) && nrow(long) > 0L) {
  long <- long |>
    dplyr::group_by(pair) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      z_pair     = { x <- pm_shift_z; ok <- is.finite(x)
                     m <- median(x[ok]); s <- mad(x[ok]); if (is.na(s) || s == 0) s <- 1e-6
                     (x - m) / s },
      stage1_out = abs(z_pair) > s58_pair_k
    ) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()
}

# ── STAGE 2: within each group, across the surviving pairs ────────────────────
s1_keep <- long[!long$stage1_out & is.finite(long$pm_shift_z), , drop = FALSE]
s1_keep$stage2_out <- FALSE
if (nrow(s1_keep) > 0L) {
  s1_keep <- s1_keep |>
    dplyr::group_by(group) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      stage2_out = {
        k <- if (!is.na(s58_group_k[dplyr::first(group)]))
               s58_group_k[[dplyr::first(group)]] else s58_group_k_default
        .mad_outlier(pm_shift_z, k)
      }
    ) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()
}

# final status back on the long table (for the pools / audit)
long$status <- "used"
long$status[long$stage1_out] <- "stage1 outlier"
key_long <- paste(long$pair, long$signal)
key_s2   <- paste(s1_keep$pair, s1_keep$signal)[s1_keep$stage2_out]
long$status[key_long %in% key_s2] <- "stage2 outlier"
long$status[!is.finite(long$pm_shift_z)] <- "missing"

# attach each row's fixed per-signal averaging weight
.sig_w <- function(sk) {
  w <- s58_signal_weight[sk]
  if (length(w) == 0L || is.na(w)) s58_signal_weight_default else as.numeric(w)
}
long$avg_weight <- vapply(long$signal, .sig_w, numeric(1))

# ── STAGE 3: per-PAIR weighted average across surviving signals ───────────────
# rows that survived both stages, carrying a finite shift and a positive weight
kept <- long[long$status == "used" &
             is.finite(long$pm_shift_z) & long$avg_weight > 0, , drop = FALSE]

s58_pair_shift    <- list()     # pair -> weighted per-pair Z-shift
s58_pair_signals  <- list()     # pair -> signals that contributed
s58_pair_rows     <- list()

for (pr in unique(long$pair)) {
  kp <- kept[kept$pair == pr, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(kp) == 0L) {
    s58_pair_shift[[pr]]   <- NA_real_
    s58_pair_signals[[pr]] <- character(0)
    next
  }
  wsum  <- sum(kp$avg_weight)
  zbar  <- if (wsum > 0) sum(kp$avg_weight * kp$pm_shift_z) / wsum else NA_real_

  s58_pair_shift[[pr]]   <- zbar
  s58_pair_signals[[pr]] <- kp$signal

  s58_pair_rows[[pr]] <- tibble::tibble(
    pair       = pr,
    TreeID_1   = kp$TreeID_1[1L], TreeID_2 = kp$TreeID_2[1L],
    n_signals  = nrow(kp),
    signals    = paste(kp$signal, collapse = "+"),
    pm_shift_z = zbar,
    truth      = .s58_truth,
    error      = if (is.finite(.s58_truth)) zbar - .s58_truth else NA_real_
  )
}

s58_pair_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(s58_pair_rows)

# Pairs that came out of Step 3.15 with a per-pair average. Not the same as the
# number that entered: a pair whose every signal was dropped by one of the two
# MAD passes contributes nothing and is absent here.
.tally(n_pairs_pair_avg = length(unique(s58_pair_tbl$pair)))

# per-pair pools kept for the diagnostics (all rows, with status + weight)
s58_pair_pool <- split(long, long$pair)

# ── Report ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if (!requireNamespace("cli", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("cli")
cli::cli_h1("3.15 Two-stage MAD filter -> per-pair fixed-weight Z-shift across signals")
if (is.null(s58_pair_tbl) || nrow(s58_pair_tbl) == 0L) {
  cli::cli_alert_warning("No per-pair shifts produced.")
} else {
  print(s58_pair_tbl |>
          dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(pm_shift_z, truth, error), ~ round(., 4))) |>
          as.data.frame(), row.names = FALSE)

  n_full <- length(.active_sigs)
  short  <- s58_pair_tbl[s58_pair_tbl$n_signals < n_full, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(short))
    cli::cli_alert_info("{nrow(short)} pair{?s} averaged over FEWER than {n_full} signals (some dropped by MAD).")
  if (is.finite(.s58_truth))
    cli::cli_alert_info("Across pairs: mean error {round(mean(s58_pair_tbl$error, na.rm = TRUE), 4)} m, RMSE {round(sqrt(mean(s58_pair_tbl$error^2, na.rm = TRUE)), 4)} m.")
  cli::cli_alert_info("Per-pair shift in s58_pair_shift[[pair]] / s58_pair_tbl; contributing signals in s58_pair_signals[[pair]]; audit pools in s58_pair_pool[[pair]] (status, avg_weight). NB: downstream (3.10) must read these per-pair objects.")
}
```


### Vis - MAD within a pair, across signals (STAGE 1)

```{r}
#| label: params-fig-mad-per-pair
#| code-summary: "Parameters - stage-1 panel styling"

# Shared with the stage-2 panel below so the two read as one pair of figures.
s58_mad_col_kept <- "#2c7fb8"
s58_mad_col_out  <- "#D7263D"

.par_apply("params-fig-mad-per-pair")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-mad-per-pair
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6
#| code-summary: "Per PAIR: every signal's Z-shift as a within-pair MAD z-score, with +/-s58_pair_k; the stage-1 cut"

# STAGE 1 of the two-stage filter, one panel per PAIR, showing EVERY signal that
# produced a shift for it. This is the cut that happens FIRST, and until now it
# was invisible: the stage-2 figure below plots only the rows that survived it,
# so a signal thrown out here simply vanished with no record of why.
#
# Left axis  : the within-pair MAD z-score across that pair's signals, dashed at
#              +/-s58_pair_k. Outside the rules is a stage-1 outlier and never
#              reaches stage 2.
# Right axis : the same points in metres, z rescaled by this PAIR's own median
#              and MAD (shift = med + z * MAD) - an exact linear inverse, so one
#              point series carries both readings, as in the stage-2 panel.
#
# z_pair and stage1_out are read STRAIGHT OFF `long`, not recomputed. The values
# drawn are therefore the ones the filter actually used, and cannot drift from
# it the way an independent recomputation can.

.p1 <- long[is.finite(long$pm_shift_z), , drop = FALSE]

if (is.null(.p1) || nrow(.p1) == 0L) {
  message("fig-mad-per-pair: no finite per-pair-signal shifts - skipping.")
} else for (pr in unique(.p1$pair)) {

  d <- .p1[.p1$pair == pr, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(d) < 1L) next

  # The median and MAD the stage-1 test used for THIS pair, recovered from the
  # stored z rather than recomputed: z = (x - m)/s, so s and m follow from any
  # two points. Falls back to a direct computation for a one-signal pair, where
  # z is degenerate and the axis is cosmetic anyway.
  m <- median(d$pm_shift_z)
  sdev <- mad(d$pm_shift_z); if (is.na(sdev) || sdev == 0) sdev <- 1e-6

  d <- d[order(d$pm_shift_z), , drop = FALSE]
  d$xr  <- seq_len(nrow(d))
  d$st1 <- ifelse(d$stage1_out, "stage1 outlier", "kept")

  gg <- ggplot(d, aes(x = xr, y = z_pair)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(-s58_pair_k, s58_pair_k), linetype = "dashed",
               colour = s58_mad_col_out, linewidth = 0.6) +
    # Only when there is something to join. A pair down to one surviving signal
    # is exactly the case worth seeing, and it should not arrive buried under a
    # "each group consists of only one observation" warning.
    { if (nrow(d) > 1L) geom_line(colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) } +
    geom_point(aes(shape = st1, size = st1, colour = st1),
               fill = "white", stroke = 1.1, alpha = 0.9) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(kept = 16, "stage1 outlier" = 4), guide = "none") +
    scale_size_manual(values  = c(kept = 2.4, "stage1 outlier" = 3.6), guide = "none") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(kept = s58_mad_col_kept,
                                   "stage1 outlier" = s58_mad_col_out), name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = d$xr, labels = d$signal) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      name     = sprintf("within-pair MAD z-score  ( |z| > %.2f = outlier )", s58_pair_k),
      sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . * sdev + m, name = "per-pair-signal Z-shift (m)")) +
    labs(title    = sprintf("Step 3.15 stage 1 \u2014 pair '%s': signals judged against each other", pr),
         subtitle = sprintf("median %.4f m | MAD %.4f | %d kept, %d flagged of %d signal(s) at mult %.2f",
                            m, sdev, sum(!d$stage1_out), sum(d$stage1_out),
                            nrow(d), s58_pair_k),
         x = "signal, ordered by Z-shift, low \u2192 high") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 8),
          axis.title.y.right = element_text(colour = "grey35"),
          legend.position = "top")
  print(gg)
}
rm(.p1)
```

### Vis - MAD within a signal group, across pairs (STAGE 2)

```{r}
#| label: fig-mad-per-group
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6
#| code-summary: "Per GROUP: stage-1-surviving pairs on x (ordered by Z-shift), stage-2 within-group MAD z-score on the left axis with +/-k; right axis = the same points read as metres"

# STAGE 2 of the two-stage filter, one panel per signal GROUP, showing only the
# rows that SURVIVED stage 1 (the kept pairs entering stage 2). Each point is one
# surviving (pair x signal) row, ordered on x by its Z-shift, low to high.
#
# Left axis : the within-group MAD z-score computed over the stage-1 survivors,
# with dashed rules at +/-k (per group) marking the cutoff; a point
# outside them is a stage-2 outlier and does not enter the average.
# Right axis : the per-pair Z-shift in metres. It is the z-score rescaled by this
# group's own median and MAD (shift = med + z * MAD) - an EXACT,
# linear inverse of the z transform, so one point series carries both
# readings. The right axis is a second way of reading the same
# points, not a second variable (matching the pass-1/pass-2 MAD
# diagnostics elsewhere in the pipeline).

# stage-1 survivors only (the kept pairs entering stage 2)
s1 <- long[long$status != "stage1 outlier" & is.finite(long$pm_shift_z), , drop = FALSE]

for (grp in unique(s1$group)) {
  d <- s1[s1$group == grp, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(d) < 1L || all(is.na(d$pm_shift_z))) next

  k <- if (!is.na(s58_group_k[grp])) s58_group_k[[grp]] else s58_group_k_default

  # within-group median / MAD over the stage-1 survivors; z is the left axis and
  # (shift = m + z * s) is the exact right-axis relabel
  m <- median(d$pm_shift_z); s <- mad(d$pm_shift_z); if (is.na(s) || s == 0) s <- 1e-6
  d$z_grp <- (d$pm_shift_z - m) / s
  d$grp_status <- ifelse(abs(d$z_grp) > k, "stage2 outlier", "kept")

  # The z-score has to be recomputed here - the filter stores a per-PAIR z, not
  # a per-GROUP one - so the flag it implies is checked against the flag the
  # filter actually recorded. A silent disagreement would mean this panel is
  # describing a cut that did not happen.
  .want <- ifelse(d$status == "stage2 outlier", "stage2 outlier", "kept")
  if (!identical(unname(d$grp_status), unname(.want)))
    warning(sprintf(paste0("[fig-mad-per-group] group '%s': the redrawn stage-2 flag disagrees ",
                           "with long$status on %d row(s). The panel is showing a different cut ",
                           "from the one the filter applied."),
                    grp, sum(d$grp_status != .want)), call. = FALSE)
  rm(.want)

  d  <- d[order(d$pm_shift_z), , drop = FALSE]
  d$xr <- seq_len(nrow(d))

  # Label pair + signal only where a pair really does appear more than once in
  # this group - decided from the DATA, not from a hardcoded group list. That
  # list said "semi_axes and protrusion", which stopped being true at Step
  # 3.14b: the eight sectors are now pooled into one protrusion signal, so
  # protrusion contributes exactly one row per pair like every other signal, and
  # only semi_axes (sa + sb) still doubles up.
  d$lab <- if (anyDuplicated(d$pair))
             paste0(d$pair, " \u00b7 ", d$signal) else d$pair

  gg <- ggplot(d, aes(x = xr, y = z_grp)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(-k, k), linetype = "dashed",
               colour = "#D7263D", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_line(colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = grp_status, size = grp_status, colour = grp_status),
               fill = "white", stroke = 1.1, alpha = 0.9) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(kept = 16, "stage2 outlier" = 4), guide = "none") +
    scale_size_manual(values  = c(kept = 2.4, "stage2 outlier" = 3.6), guide = "none") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(kept = "#2c7fb8", "stage2 outlier" = "#D7263D"),
                        name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = d$xr, labels = d$lab) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      name     = sprintf("within-group MAD z-score  ( |z| > %.2f = outlier )", k),
      sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . * s + m, name = "per-pair Z-shift (m)")) +
    labs(title    = sprintf("Step 3.15 stage 2 \u2014 group '%s': stage-1 survivors judged across the group",
                            grp),
         subtitle = sprintf("median %.4f m | MAD %.4f | %d kept, %d flagged of %d at mult %.2f",
                            m, s, sum(d$grp_status == "kept"),
                            sum(d$grp_status == "stage2 outlier"), nrow(d), k),
         x = "kept (pair \u00d7 signal), ordered by Z-shift, low \u2192 high") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 6),
          axis.title.y.right = element_text(colour = "grey35"),
          legend.position = "top")
  print(gg)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-kept-scores
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5
#| code-summary: "Per pair: surviving signals on x = per-signal Z-shift (m), fixed averaging weight on y; ring the highest-weight signal, rule at the pair's weighted-average shift and at truth"

# One panel per temporal PAIR, KEPT rows only (signals that survived both MAD
# stages in 3.15). x is each surviving signal's per-pair Z-shift in METRES; y is
# the fixed averaging weight that signal carried into this pair's cross-signal
# average (s58_signal_weight, NOT pm_score). The highest-weight surviving signal
# is ringed. Two vertical rules mark shift values at their literal x position:
# dashed grey at the pair's fixed-weight average (what 3.15 produced for this
# pair) and golden at the true Z-shift (from 3.13.3, if run). A rule landing among
# the high-weight points means the pair's answer agrees with the signals that
# carried the most weight. Point colour carries the signal name.

.s58_truth <- if (exists("s5_pm_true_shift")) s5_pm_true_shift else NA_real_

.pb_58 <- .pb_new(length(s58_pair_pool), "3.15 per-pair averages")

for (pr in names(s58_pair_pool)) {
  .pb_tick(.pb_58)
  pool   <- s58_pair_pool[[pr]]
  pshift <- s58_pair_shift[[pr]]

  kept <- pool[pool$status == "used" &
               is.finite(pool$pm_shift_z) & pool$avg_weight > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(kept) == 0L) next

  imax    <- which.max(kept$avg_weight)   # highest-weight surviving signal
  err_txt <- if (is.finite(pshift) && is.finite(.s58_truth))
    sprintf("  |  error %+.3f m", pshift - .s58_truth) else ""

  gg <- ggplot(kept, aes(x = pm_shift_z, y = avg_weight)) +
    geom_segment(aes(xend = pm_shift_z, yend = 0), colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.3) +
    { if (is.finite(.s58_truth))
        geom_vline(xintercept = .s58_truth, colour = s58_gold, linewidth = 0.9) } +
    { if (is.finite(pshift))
        geom_vline(xintercept = pshift, colour = "grey30",
                   linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) } +
    geom_point(aes(colour = signal), size = 2.6) +
    geom_point(data = kept[imax, , drop = FALSE],
               aes(x = pm_shift_z, y = avg_weight), shape = 21, fill = NA,
               colour = "black", size = 5.5, stroke = 1.1) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = signal), size = 2.6,
                             colour = "grey35", max.overlaps = Inf,
                             segment.size = 0.2, show.legend = FALSE) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, NA)) +
    labs(title    = sprintf("Step 3.15 \u2014 pair %s: surviving-signal weights vs Z-shift", pr),
         subtitle = sprintf("%d signal(s) averaged  |  weighted-avg shift %+.3f m%s%s",
                            nrow(kept),
                            if (is.finite(pshift)) pshift else NA_real_,
                            if (is.finite(.s58_truth))
                              sprintf("  |  truth %+.3f m", .s58_truth) else "",
                            err_txt),
         x = "per-signal Z-shift (m)",
         y = "fixed averaging weight (s58_signal_weight)",
         colour = NULL) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey40"),
          legend.position = "top")
  print(gg)
}

.pb_done(.pb_58)
```



## 3.16 Multi-Pair Aggregation
```{r}
#| label: params-s58-final-mean
#| code-summary: "Parameters - 3.16: MAD-filter the per-pair Z-shifts from 3.15, then collapse to one final Z-translation (mean across surviving pairs) + dual-axis diagnostic"

# ── What this does ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Step 3.15 produced one Z-shift per temporal pair (s58_pair_tbl$pm_shift_z,
# also s58_pair_shift[[pair]]). This step first rejects outlier pairs with a
# scaled-MAD filter, then reduces the survivors to the SINGLE final Z-translation
# by averaging across them. Each pair is one observation of the stand-level
# shift, so the default is a plain mean; an n-weighted variant (each pair
# weighted by how many signals survived to build it) is also reported and
# available via the toggle.
# plain : every surviving pair counts once.
# nweight: pairs built from more surviving signals count proportionally more.
s58_final_method <- "plain"   # "plain" or "nweight"

# ── MAD outlier filter (applied BEFORE any average) ───────────────────────────
# Robust, non-destructive: flag pairs whose Z-shift sits more than s58_mad_mult
# scaled MADs from the pair-set median. mad() carries the 1.4826 constant, so
# mad_z is on a z-like scale; two-sided; a no-op when the MAD is 0 (all shifts
# identical, or too few pairs). Every summary below is taken over the survivors.
s58_mad_mult <- 3                        # rejection threshold in scaled MADs

.par_apply("params-s58-final-mean")
```

```{r}
#| label: s58-final-mean
#| code-summary: "3.16: MAD-filter the per-pair Z-shifts from 3.15, then collapse to one final Z-translation (mean across surviving pairs) + dual-axis diagnostic"

.s58_truth <- if (exists("s5_pm_true_shift")) s5_pm_true_shift else NA_real_
if (!exists("s58_pair_tbl") || is.null(s58_pair_tbl) || nrow(s58_pair_tbl) == 0L)
  stop("3.16 needs s58_pair_tbl from 3.15 – run 3.15 first.")
# keep only pairs that actually produced a finite shift
pf <- s58_pair_tbl[is.finite(s58_pair_tbl$pm_shift_z), , drop = FALSE]
if (nrow(pf) == 0L) stop("3.16: no finite per-pair shifts to average.")
z   <- pf$pm_shift_z
nw  <- if ("n_signals" %in% names(pf)) pf$n_signals else rep(1, nrow(pf))

z_med  <- median(z)
z_mad  <- mad(z)                         # scaled MAD (consistent SD estimator)
mad_z  <- if (z_mad > 0) (z - z_med) / z_mad else rep(0, length(z))
mad_keep <- abs(mad_z) <= s58_mad_mult   # TRUE = kept
if (!any(mad_keep)) {                    # safety: never drop the whole set
  if (!requireNamespace("cli", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("cli")
  cli::cli_alert_warning("3.16 MAD filter would drop every pair – keeping all.")
  mad_keep <- rep(TRUE, length(z))
}
n_drop <- sum(!mad_keep)

zk  <- z[mad_keep]
nwk <- nw[mad_keep]

final_plain   <- mean(zk)
final_nweight <- stats::weighted.mean(zk, nwk)
final_median  <- median(zk)                      # reported for reference
t_trans_z <- if (identical(s58_final_method, "nweight")) final_nweight else final_plain
# spread of the SURVIVING pair estimates around the chosen final value
n_pairs <- length(zk)
n_all   <- length(z)
sd_z    <- if (n_pairs > 1L) sd(zk) else NA_real_
se_z    <- if (n_pairs > 1L) sd_z / sqrt(n_pairs) else NA_real_
# ── Report ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if (!requireNamespace("cli", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("cli")
cli::cli_h1("3.16 Final Z-shift (mean of {n_pairs}/{n_all} MAD-kept pair{?s}; method: {s58_final_method})")
.s58_final_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  pair       = pf$pair,
  n_signals  = nw,
  pm_shift_z = round(z, 4),
  mad_z      = round(mad_z, 3),
  kept       = mad_keep,
  resid_from_final = round(z - t_trans_z, 4)
)
print(as.data.frame(.s58_final_tbl), row.names = FALSE)
if (n_drop > 0L) {
  cli::cli_alert_info("MAD filter (mult {s58_mad_mult}) dropped {n_drop} pair{?s}: {paste(pf$pair[!mad_keep], collapse = ', ')}.")
} else {
  cli::cli_alert_success("MAD filter (mult {s58_mad_mult}) dropped no pairs.")
}
.summ <- tibble::tibble(
  method       = c("plain mean", "n-weighted mean", "median"),
  value_m      = round(c(final_plain, final_nweight, final_median), 4),
  selected     = c(identical(s58_final_method, "plain"),
                   identical(s58_final_method, "nweight"),
                   FALSE)
)
print(as.data.frame(.summ), row.names = FALSE)
cli::cli_alert_info("Final Z-translation t_trans_z = {round(t_trans_z, 4)} m  (n = {n_pairs} kept of {n_all}, sd {round(sd_z, 4)} m, se {round(se_z, 4)} m).")
if (is.finite(.s58_truth))
  cli::cli_alert_info("Truth {round(.s58_truth, 4)} m -> error {sprintf('%+.4f', t_trans_z - .s58_truth)} m.")
cli::cli_alert_info("t_trans_z is set here and consumed by 3.17. Also available: s58_final_plain / s58_final_nweight / s58_final_median.")

# ── Plot: MAD robust-z (left) and Z-shift (right), pairs sorted along x ────────
# Pairs ordered by Z-shift (identical to ordering by mad_z, since mad_z is an
# affine map of z) so both series read monotonically; MAD-dropped pairs orange.
ord    <- order(z)
xp     <- seq_along(z)
lab    <- as.character(pf$pair)[ord]
drop_o <- !mad_keep[ord]
col_pt <- ifelse(drop_o, "darkorange", "grey25")

op <- graphics::par(mar = c(7.5, 4.6, 3.2, 4.6))
## left axis: MAD robust z
plot(xp, mad_z[ord], type = "n", xaxt = "n", xlab = "", ylab = "",
     main = sprintf("3.16  per-pair Z-shift vs MAD filter (mult = %g)", s58_mad_mult))
abline(h = 0, col = "grey85")
abline(h = c(-1, 1) * s58_mad_mult, lty = 2, col = "darkorange")   # rejection band
lines(xp, mad_z[ord], col = "grey60")
points(xp, mad_z[ord], pch = 16, col = col_pt)
mtext("MAD robust z  (scaled MADs from median)", side = 2, line = 2.7)
axis(1, at = xp, labels = lab, las = 2, cex.axis = 0.7)
mtext("temporal pair  (sorted by Z-shift)", side = 1, line = 6)
## right axis: Z-shift in metres
graphics::par(new = TRUE)
plot(xp, z[ord], type = "b", pch = 1, col = "steelblue",
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
axis(4, col = "steelblue", col.axis = "steelblue")
mtext("Z-shift (m)", side = 4, line = 3, col = "steelblue")
abline(h = t_trans_z, lty = 3, col = "steelblue")                 # final translation (right-axis units)
legend("topleft", bty = "n", cex = 0.8,
       legend = c("robust z (kept)", "robust z (MAD-dropped)",
                  "Z-shift (m)", sprintf("final t_trans_z (%.3f m)", t_trans_z)),
       pch = c(16, 16, 1, NA), lty = c(NA, NA, 1, 3),
       col = c("grey25", "darkorange", "steelblue", "steelblue"))
graphics::par(op)

# expose the alternatives for 3.17's auto note and any downstream use
s58_final_plain   <- final_plain
s58_final_nweight <- final_nweight
s58_final_median  <- final_median
```

### Export CSV - 3.9 - 3.10

```{r}
#| label: params-pm-optim-export
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Export one CSV at candidate grain carrying every 3.13/3.14/3.15 input and output needed to optimize their parameters"


# ── What this exports ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# ONE row per match candidate (the finest grain in the pipeline: 3.13's), with
# everything needed to tune 3.13 (the 12 raw factor scores), 3.14 (the per-signal
# factor weights, each candidate's aggregate score, and the per-pair-signal shift
# the chosen reduction produced) and 3.15 (the two MAD stages, each row's status
# and averaging weight, and the final per-pair shift vs truth) joined on so a
# single row shows how a parameter change would propagate from raw score to final
# answer.
#
# Column families (see the legend chunk for full definitions):
# ids signal, pair, TreeID_1/2, type, h1, h2, implied_shift
# sc_* the 12 RAW factor scores from 3.13 (each in [0,1])
# w_* the per-signal factor WEIGHT applied to each sc_* in 3.14
# wsc_* the WEIGHTED score contribution = w_* * sc_* (pre-normalise)
# agg_score 3.14 aggregate = sum(wsc_*)/sum(w_* over available factors)
# is_best_cand TRUE for the top-agg_score candidate in its signal×pair
# ps_* the per-PAIR-SIGNAL result from 3.14 (pm_shift_z, pm_score…)
# mad_* 3.15 per-(pair,signal) MAD bookkeeping (z_pair, status, weight)
# pair_* 3.15 final per-PAIR shift, its signal set, truth and error
# par_* the scalar parameters in force (method, k's) for provenance

# ── Where it goes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# In a batch these are replaced inside the chunk by .batch_optim_dir and
# .batch_sample, so each pair gets its own file: <dir>/<sample>_fmatch_optim.csv.
# They have to be read inside the chunk rather than pushed in as an override,
# because this chunk assigns the path and writes the file in one go - an
# override applied after the chunk arrives after the write, which is how every
# pair of a batch would otherwise queue behind the one hardcoded name below.
.pm_out_dir  <- "C:/Users/ascsh/Documents/1_Artemis/11_PaqLab/115_TreeTimeAlign/Optimization"
.pm_basename <- "fmatch_optim_BOSF1_p1"

# TRUE writes the candidate-grain CSV. This is the table the peak/trough match
# weighting is tuned on, so it is on by default - it is one CSV per pair, not a
# point cloud.
pm_optim_export <- TRUE

.par_apply("params-pm-optim-export")
```

```{r}
#| label: pm-optim-export
#| code-summary: "Export one CSV at candidate grain carrying every 3.13/3.14/3.15 input and output needed to optimize their parameters"

.safe_path <- function(dir, base, ext = ".csv") {
  path <- file.path(dir, paste0(base, ext))
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(path)
  i <- 1L
  repeat {
    cand <- file.path(dir, paste0(base, "_", i, ext))
    if (!file.exists(cand)) return(cand)
    i <- i + 1L
  }
}

.factors <- if (exists("s5_pm_factors")) s5_pm_factors else c(
  "rel_maj_tot","rel_maj_sim","rel_majorprom_tot","rel_majorprom_sim",
  "rel_minorprom_tot","rel_minorprom_sim","pearson","slope_agree",
  "median_prox","consensus","left_opp","right_opp")
.sc_cols <- paste0("sc_", .factors)

# ── Per-candidate base: 3.13 scores + 3.14 agg_score, per signal ──────────────
cand_rows <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(s5_signal_registry), function(sk) {
  obj <- paste0("pm_candidates_", sk)
  if (!exists(obj)) return(NULL)
  cand <- get(obj, envir = .stage_env())
  if (is.null(cand) || nrow(cand) == 0L) return(NULL)

  # per-signal factor weights from 3.14 (default 1 if absent)
  wv <- if (exists("s5_pm_weights") && !is.null(s5_pm_weights[[sk]]))
          s5_pm_weights[[sk]][.factors] else setNames(rep(1, length(.factors)), .factors)
  wv <- as.numeric(wv); names(wv) <- .factors

  # raw scores present on the candidate table
  present <- intersect(.sc_cols, names(cand))
  M <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(cand), ncol = length(.sc_cols),
              dimnames = list(NULL, .sc_cols))
  M[, present] <- as.matrix(cand[, present, drop = FALSE])

  # weighted contribution wsc_* = w * sc  (NA where the score is NA)
  Wsc <- sweep(M, 2, wv, `*`)
  colnames(Wsc) <- paste0("wsc_", .factors)

  base <- tibble::tibble(
    signal        = sk,
    pair          = cand$pair,
    TreeID_1      = cand$TreeID_1, TreeID_2 = cand$TreeID_2,
    type          = cand$type,
    h1            = cand$h1, h2 = cand$h2,
    implied_shift = cand$implied_shift,
    agg_score     = if ("agg_score" %in% names(cand)) cand$agg_score else NA_real_
  )

  # attach raw scores, per-signal weights (broadcast), weighted contributions
  base <- dplyr::bind_cols(
    base,
    tibble::as_tibble(M),
    tibble::as_tibble(setNames(as.list(wv), paste0("w_", .factors))),
    tibble::as_tibble(Wsc)
  )

  # best candidate flag within signal×pair (matches 3.14 method = "best")
  base <- base |>
    dplyr::group_by(pair) |>
    dplyr::mutate(is_best_cand = is.finite(agg_score) &
                                 agg_score == suppressWarnings(max(agg_score, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()
  base
}))

if (is.null(cand_rows) || nrow(cand_rows) == 0L)
  stop("pm-optim-export: no candidates found – run 3.13/3.14 first.")

# ── Join 3.14 per-pair-signal result (ps_*) ───────────────────────────────────
ps_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(s5_signal_registry), function(sk) {
  o <- paste0("pm_pair_shift_", sk)
  if (!exists(o)) return(NULL)
  d <- get(o, envir = .stage_env())
  if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L) return(NULL)
  tibble::tibble(signal = sk, pair = d$pair,
                 ps_shift_z = d$pm_shift_z, ps_score = d$pm_score,
                 ps_n_cand  = if ("n_cand" %in% names(d)) d$n_cand else NA_integer_)
}))
cand_rows <- dplyr::left_join(cand_rows, ps_all, by = c("signal", "pair"))

# ── Join 3.15 per-(pair,signal) MAD bookkeeping (mad_*) ───────────────────────
if (exists("long")) {
  mad_rows <- tibble::tibble(
    signal      = long$signal, pair = long$pair,
    mad_group   = long$group,
    mad_z_pair  = if ("z_pair" %in% names(long)) long$z_pair else NA_real_,
    mad_status  = long$status,
    mad_avg_weight = if ("avg_weight" %in% names(long)) long$avg_weight else NA_real_
  )
  cand_rows <- dplyr::left_join(cand_rows, mad_rows, by = c("signal", "pair"))
} else {
  cand_rows$mad_group <- NA_character_; cand_rows$mad_z_pair <- NA_real_
  cand_rows$mad_status <- NA_character_; cand_rows$mad_avg_weight <- NA_real_
}

# ── Join 3.15 final per-PAIR shift (pair_*) ───────────────────────────────────
if (exists("s58_pair_tbl") && nrow(s58_pair_tbl) > 0L) {
  pr_rows <- tibble::tibble(
    pair            = s58_pair_tbl$pair,
    pair_shift_z    = s58_pair_tbl$pm_shift_z,
    pair_n_signals  = if ("n_signals" %in% names(s58_pair_tbl)) s58_pair_tbl$n_signals else NA_integer_,
    pair_signals    = if ("signals"   %in% names(s58_pair_tbl)) s58_pair_tbl$signals   else NA_character_,
    pair_truth      = if ("truth"     %in% names(s58_pair_tbl)) s58_pair_tbl$truth     else NA_real_,
    pair_error      = if ("error"     %in% names(s58_pair_tbl)) s58_pair_tbl$error     else NA_real_
  )
  cand_rows <- dplyr::left_join(cand_rows, pr_rows, by = "pair")
} else {
  cand_rows$pair_shift_z <- NA_real_; cand_rows$pair_n_signals <- NA_integer_
  cand_rows$pair_signals <- NA_character_
  cand_rows$pair_truth <- NA_real_; cand_rows$pair_error <- NA_real_
}

# ── Scalar parameters in force (par_*), one value repeated down the table ─────
# Carried so a stack of these CSVs from different runs stays interpretable: a
# row's scores mean nothing without knowing which reduction method and which
# MAD multipliers produced the shift beside them.
.par_scalars <- list(
  par_pm_shift_method = if (exists("s5_pm_shift_method")) as.character(s5_pm_shift_method) else NA_character_,
  par_mad_mult        = if (exists("s58_mad_mult"))       as.numeric(s58_mad_mult)         else NA_real_,
  par_sample          = if (.in_batch()) .batch_opt(".batch_sample", NA_character_) else NA_character_,
  par_exported_utc    = format(Sys.time(), tz = "UTC", usetz = TRUE),
  # Truth provenance. Without these a stack of optim CSVs is uninterpretable:
  # the same par_true_shift means a different thing depending on whether it was
  # re-derived from this run's rotation or read from the generator's input.
  par_true_shift      = if (exists("s5_pm_true_shift"))  as.numeric(s5_pm_true_shift)    else NA_real_,
  par_truth_source    = if (exists("s3_truth_source"))   as.character(s3_truth_source)   else NA_character_,
  par_box_source      = if (exists("s3_box_source"))     as.character(s3_box_source)     else NA_character_,
  par_box_dz_range    = if (exists("s3_box_dz_range_m")) as.numeric(s3_box_dz_range_m)   else NA_real_
)
for (.k in names(.par_scalars)) cand_rows[[.k]] <- .par_scalars[[.k]]

# ── Write it ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# This is the whole point of the chunk and it was missing: every version up to
# now built cand_rows, defined .safe_path, .pm_out_dir and .pm_basename, and
# then ended without calling any of them. The table was assembled correctly and
# thrown away, which is why no run has ever produced an optimisation CSV.
pm_optim_rows <- cand_rows

if (isTRUE(pm_optim_export)) {
  .pm_dir  <- if (.in_batch()) .batch_opt(".batch_optim_dir", .pm_out_dir) else .pm_out_dir
  .pm_base <- if (.in_batch())
                paste0(.batch_opt(".batch_sample", .pm_basename), "_fmatch_optim")
              else .pm_basename

  # ── Writing this file may never take down a run ────────────────────────────
  # A completed Stage 3 is an hour of work and the alignment does not depend on
  # this CSV in any way - it is a diagnostic export. An unwritable directory, a
  # locked file (the usual cause: the CSV is open in Excel), a full disk or a
  # path the OS rejects should all cost the export and nothing else. Directory
  # creation and path construction are inside the same guard, since those fail
  # for exactly the same reasons the write does.
  pm_optim_csv_path <- NA_character_
  .ok <- tryCatch({
    dir.create(.pm_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

    # By hand, never overwrite - a re-run at different weights parks itself at _1
    # beside the previous attempt, which is exactly what a tuning session wants.
    # In a batch the sample name already makes the path unique and the pair's own
    # file is replaced, so a silent _1 would just accumulate stale copies.
    pm_optim_csv_path <- if (.in_batch()) file.path(.pm_dir, paste0(.pm_base, ".csv"))
                         else .safe_path(.pm_dir, .pm_base)

    utils::write.csv(pm_optim_rows, pm_optim_csv_path, row.names = FALSE)
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat(sprintf(paste0("[3.x pm-optim-export] Could not write the optimisation CSV: %s\n",
                       "  The table is still in memory as pm_optim_rows; the run continues.\n"),
                conditionMessage(e)))
    FALSE
  })

  if (isTRUE(.ok))
    cat(sprintf("pm-optim-export: %s row(s) x %d column(s) -> %s\n",
                format(nrow(pm_optim_rows), big.mark = ","),
                ncol(pm_optim_rows), pm_optim_csv_path))

  cat(sprintf("  candidates: %d over %d signal(s) and %d pair(s) | %d flagged is_best_cand\n",
              nrow(pm_optim_rows),
              length(unique(pm_optim_rows$signal)),
              length(unique(pm_optim_rows$pair)),
              sum(pm_optim_rows$is_best_cand, na.rm = TRUE)))

  rm(.pm_dir, .pm_base, .ok)
} else {
  cat("pm-optim-export: pm_optim_export is FALSE - table built as pm_optim_rows, nothing written.\n")
}

rm(.par_scalars, .k)
```

## 3.17 Record the Final Z-Translation

```{r}
#| label: params-step3-18-transform-toggle
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Toggle: automatic Z-translation (from 3.16) vs. custom Z-shift input – records only, applies nothing"


# ── Automatic vs. custom transform ────────────────────────────────────────────
# 3.16 sets t_trans_z to the mean of the per-pair Z-shifts from 3.15. This step
# RECORDS the final Z-translation; it never applies it. Stage 4 is where
# t_trans_z is applied – to the ellipse centres and to pivot1.
#
# apply_mode_3_18 = "auto" → use t_trans_z as computed in 3.16 (default).
# apply_mode_3_18 = "custom" → override with a user-specified Z-shift.

apply_mode_3_18  <- "auto"     # "auto" or "custom"
custom_z_shift_m <- -0.7294    # meters; only used when apply_mode_3_18 == "custom"

.par_apply("params-step3-18-transform-toggle")
```

```{r}
#| label: step3-18-transform-toggle
#| code-summary: "Toggle: automatic Z-translation (from 3.16) vs. custom Z-shift input – records only, applies nothing"

if (identical(apply_mode_3_18, "custom")) {
  auto_note <- if (exists("t_trans_z"))
    sprintf("\n  (auto-selected value from 3.16 was %.4f m)", t_trans_z) else ""
  cat(sprintf(
    "Z-translation OVERRIDDEN with custom value: %.4f m%s\n",
    custom_z_shift_m, auto_note
  ))
  t_trans_z <- custom_z_shift_m
} else {
  if (!exists("t_trans_z"))
    stop("apply_mode_3_18 == 'auto' but t_trans_z does not exist – run 3.16 first.")
  cat(sprintf("Using automatically selected Z-translation from 3.16: %.4f m\n", t_trans_z))
}
```
